I had a serious problem with Excessive brake dust: "The wheels pick up dirt very quickly"

Customer reported that the vehicle has been producing a squeaking sound from the brakes after only about four weeks of ownership, and that the issue happens whenever the brake pedal is pressed. Customer stated the noise is loud and ongoing and that it makes the car unpleasant to drive. Customer emphasized that this does not seem like a normal brake sound and expressed concern about what might be causing it. Customer noted that when the car was kept overnight at the dealership and a loaner of the same model was provided, the brakes on the loaner worked fine and did not make any noise. Customer stated the dealership has not been able to identify the source of the problem even after inspecting the vehicle, and believes the brake pads should be removed and examined properly. Customer mentioned this is the fourth BMW they have owned and that none of the prior vehicles had similar issues. Customer expressed strong dissatisfaction, saying the dealership is not performing the necessary diagnostic work. Writer suggested taking the car to another dealership for a second opinion if the customer cannot reach an understanding with the current service manager. Writer also advised that high performance brakes can produce noise.

i've had a lot of 5 series bmw cars over the years. on this 2025 i wish the steering gave more road feedback, it reminds me of the very light power steering from when i was younger. i do appreciate how smooth it is on the freeway, definitely feels more upscale than my older ones. what bothers me is when i lift off the accelerator, the car hardly slows unless i actually brake, so there is almost no engine braking. i have both a 530 and 540 from the 2025 model year and they both behave that way, and honestly i can barely tell any difference in how they drive.

I had a minor problem with Brakes - Excessively sensitive: "even a gentle touch on the brakes makes the car come to a screeching stop. I end up having to keep tapping the pedal over and over until I finally come to a stop."

Customer stated he hears a loud brake noise when he applies the brakes gently. Customer stated he first noticed this in his garage, and now he occasionally hears the same loud brake sound while driving in traffic. Customer stated there are no other driving issues and no warning lights showing in the vehicle. Customer stated he has owned other BMWs and his wife has one as well, and he has never experienced this noise on those cars. Customer stated the vehicle currently has a little over 1800 miles.
Customer indicated the brakes feel a bit more sensitive than what he is used to. Writer explained the brakes are engineered to suit the vehicle's performance and offer improved stopping power.

Customer stated he observed that braking feels lighter in electric mode, while in combustion engine mode he has to press the pedal harder. Writer explained this is expected when moving between different powertrains and that the brake feel is generally lighter in electric driving than when using the engine. Customer stated that although he understands this, he would prefer a more seamless transition.
Customer stated the brakes do not feel like brand new brakes. Customer reported that when they apply the brakes, it takes a few seconds for the vehicle to fully come to a complete stop.

1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function.

in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate.

the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues.

i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix.

2. homelink garage door opener
the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then.

most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.

i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

Customer stated a grinding noise happens during slow stops, mainly from the front, probably on the driver side. Customer mentioned it began within the first 200 miles, and the car is now at around 1,100 miles. Customer rated the severity at 5.5/10, compared with 9/10 on the previous 2025 model he traded in. Customer stated it is more noticeable on level or downhill stops and does not occur on uphill stops. Customer said it only happens in normal drive mode (D), not in Sport mode, and only at low speeds when coming to a stop. Customer reported the issue as intermittent, occurring about 5 out of 10 times. Writer scheduled an RVG call to capture the noise on video, which the customer then rescheduled for 2 weeks later. Writer called back and customer stated that after the temperature dropped significantly, both the brake noise and the RMP issues disappeared.
Customer stated they appreciate how easy it is to brake.

Customer reported that the car seems to use electric braking rather than hydraulic braking, and said it is basically impossible to come to a smooth stop without the car jerking forward. Customer described that even when pressing the brake pedal very gently and gradually, the vehicle still comes to a sudden halt, almost like slamming on the brakes, with no way to get a calm, gentle stop. Customer indicated the odometer is around one to two thousand miles. Customer added that when driving in sport mode the problem shows up less often. Writer explained that during the early break-in phase, usually up to around two thousand miles, the brakes can feel especially strong and powerful, which may make the braking feel more aggressive. Writer recommended doing some firmer braking in safe locations so the brakes get more accustomed to normal stopping. Writer also suggested turning off the Auto Hold feature to check if that changes how the braking feels.

Customer stated they largely dislike this vehicle because the brakes produce a loud squeal whenever they press them and again when they let off. Customer indicated they intend to take the car to the dealer to find out what can be done.

Customer stated there is a noticeable sound when the brakes are applied. Writer advised the customer that the Brakes have a break-in period. Customer stated that when he drives in auto brake mode the brakes get a little squeaky, and he is planning to go to the dealership to check if they need to be tuned up.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

Customer stated there is a squeaking sound when coming to a stop and during initial movement. Writer explained this can be normal on a new vehicle with under roughly 700 miles, as the brake pads need time to seat correctly against the rotors. Writer suggested braking a bit harder than usual on the first drive after the car sits overnight, when safe, to help clean the rotors and warm up the pads.

I had a problem with Brakes - Excessively sensitive: "I have to begin slowing down much farther away than I did with my previous cars, otherwise it feels like I am braking way too hard. If I want a gentle, gradual stop, I need to start braking much earlier. In my view, the brakes are just a bit too tight and they make braking feel kind of unpleasent."

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

Customer mentioned they are pleased with how the car comes to a stop and are happy with the brakes overall.

Customer stated that from the very first day of ownership, the brakes have sounded noisy. Customer stated the brakes sound wet and crunchy, almost like the pads are slipping on the brake rotors. Customer stated he particularly hears this brake noise when slowing to a complete stop, and also when his foot is on the brake pedal while turning the steering wheel. Customer stated he does not hear any squeaking or squealing from the brakes. Customer stated that when the vehicle is at a full stop and he lets off the brake pedal, it takes around 3 seconds before the car starts to creep forward. Customer stated that right before the vehicle begins creeping, it sounds as if one of the brake pads lets go from the rotor like it was stuck. Customer stated he previously took the vehicle to Metro BMW, but they did not inspect the brakes and simply dismissed the issue as normal. Customer stated he does not accept this noise as normal and has scheduled a service visit with Premier BMW on 8/15. Writer scheduled a follow-up call for 8/16.
Customer stated the vehicle's braking tends to be a bit on the hard side.

the car seems fine, but the service is not good at all. after it came out of the factory, i applied for service because the brakes failed, and after they spent 2 weeks checking the breakdown, i have been waiting more than a month since then. it is now getting close to two months and i am still waiting around.

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

Customer stated they hear the brakes squeak a little bit on the vehicle.

Customer stated that on a few occasions, when he applied the brakes, it felt like the front driver-side brake was adjusting. Customer stated the brakes themselves operate fine. Customer stated there is plenty of stopping power and the response time is good. Customer stated there is no noise, but it feels as if a motor is adjusting the brake. Customer stated there is nothing felt in the steering column, only in the brake pedal. Customer stated road conditions were good at the time. Customer stated it does not occur every time and that he has only driven on rural roads. Customer stated he will bring it up with the dealership when he goes in for the mirror repair. Customer stated the brakes work perfectly overall.
Customer stated the vehicle has very nice brakes.

Customer stated the brake malfunction indicator has come on twice. Customer stated the brakes themselves feel fine and the warning clears once he starts driving, but can show up again when he restarts the vehicle. Customer commented that the front brakes seem a bit too sensitive. Vehicle is at roughly 1800-2000 miles, and customer plans to see if the dealer can adjust the front calipers. Customer noted the brakes only feel grabby when driving at low speeds.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

the tech on this car is very inconsistent, some days everything works fine and other days features just do not. the digital key will be detected sometimes, and other days it is not, making it hard for me to get into the car. once the assisted driving feature said I was not paying attention and suddenly brought the car to a stop right in the middle of the highway. the brakes also do not feel strong enough. I have had several times where I needed to stop quickly because I was cut off or the light changed suddenly, and the brakes could not bring the car to a full stop like they should. on top of that, the battery does not hold as long as I expect, so I end up charging about 3 to 4 times a week.

Customer stated the braking does not feel as smooth as he anticipated. Customer stated the brakes seem to grab a bit when he presses the pedal and are not as smooth as his previous BMW 7 Series. Customer stated he spoke with the dealer, who advised the brakes are still in their running-in period. Customer stated he expects them to smooth out once that period is over.

i was quite upset to discover the brake fluid leaking after a long drive. i had been told this issue was already taken care of before i took ownership of the vehicle, so either it never got fixed or the leak started again.
i do enjoy the car a lot, but now i feel like i need to watch it carefully to make sure the same problem does not show up again.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

Customer reported that ever since delivery he has needed to press down very firmly on the Brakes, putting the pedal all the way to the floor to bring the vehicle to a stop. Customer said he wanted the dealership to inspect this. Writer asked whether a similar issue was happening with the Accelerator pedal, and the customer replied that it was not. Writer then asked if the vehicle slowed or stopped when he applied the Brake. Customer stated the car would slow when he pressed the pedal, but would not completely stop, and reiterated that he had to press the pedal fully down to get it to stop. Customer mentioned they had taken the vehicle in for service roughly 2 days ago, and the dealership told him they did not find anything wrong with the Brakes at that time, but planned to test them further to make sure. Mileage around 1000.

i picked up the car on the 24th of august. it was meant to be ready on the 23rd and i had taken annual leave, but there was an error message on the car that they could not sort so i only collected it a day later. then on the 21st of september, as i was leaving my work address, i got a drivetrain brake fault and the car refused to let me drive. i rang bmw support at 7pm and was told nobody could come out until the following day, so i phoned rbc instead and they came the next day, saying there were several errors and to call bmw in the morning. bmw turned up the next morning, by then the hazards had been left on all night so it had switched to the second battery, which did a restart. now, fast forward to today, i have no parking brake at all and i am just about to call again.

i haven't been happy with it because i couldn't get the options i wanted. the salesman told me bmw wouldn't give a price or a delivery date, so i had to go without them. the sport seats don't have any lumbar support and i find them really uncomfortable, with my back starting to ache after only a few miles. when i did the test drive it was in a 2 series, and those seats had lumbar support, were comfortable, and i didn't get any back ache at all. this car also doesn't have any lashing straps, and the salesman said they only come if you add the luggage net option. in the details for that option it clearly says there are 3 additional lashing eyes, so i ordered the luggage net through the salesman and picked it up from the stores, but it turned up with no lashing eyes. i didn't buy it or pay for it online either. later i read an article saying all bmw 1 series 2025 models are supposed to have a lashing eye fitted as standard. on the plus side, the car itself drives really well, with no body roll and very good brakes, and it feels like a driver's car even as an auto. i still think it would be better as a manual.

i moved down from an m135 drive and the power in this one is still absolutely fine and nicely responsive for everyday driving. i much prefer the battery assisted stop/start setup, and the steering has a nice light feel that firms up as you go faster. i am a bit let down that the i-drive knob has gone, as i always thought that system was brilliant when on the move. the new screens look very smart and, once you have them configured, they work well, and the overall fascia design and materials feel excellent. my f70120 m sport drives and handles really well day to day, and i actually like how it looks more than the f40. the front electric seats are really comfy and offer very precise adjustment. i am enjoying the head-up display, its my first time using one. the sat nav reacts quickly and is really helpful when finding your way around unfamiliar routes and towns. i also really like the 'y' style wheels and the red calipers.

i've been driving bmws for more than 20 years and the move away from physical switches feels like going backwards. having to look off the road to change things seems unsafe to me. the car often ignores what i say when i try to use voice control. parking in tight spots is a pain, it keeps cutting out and stopping, so it doesnt feel as manageable as my other cars, even the automatics. the electric help when parking tends to surge, and on a small slope it is hard to drive off smoothly. my garage is narrow and uphill, and i have to creep in very slowly, but the way it surges and then cuts out makes that awkward. i have to press the accelerator to get the parking brake to release and then it leaps forward. i do actually like the car, but these parking problems kind of take the shine off it for me.

from placing the order to getting the car, the delivery was far quicker than with my previous bmws, which was a nice surprise. my recent bmws have all been diesel, so finding the 1 series f70 only offered as petrol was rather disappointing. the car itself runs well and i am gradually getting used to operating system 9. i really do not like the lack of a paper handbook, as the built-in version is very hit and miss when trying to locate information, whereas the paper one had pictures and was much simpler to navigate. the missing physical auto hold button on the centre console is also strongly felt, especially after the last software update wiped the on screen setting, leaving you either holding the brake or messing with the selector switch.

the car drives nicely and is definitely a step up from the f40. my main gripes are with the new idrive setup, it can be a bit laggy and mine has actually shut down completely twice within the first 3 months of owning it, needing bmw assistance to come out and get it working again. thats really frustrating from a brand ive been buying different models from for around twenty years and it does make me think about going elsewhere for my next car. the performance brakes are also very poor as they squeal even though the car has only done about 2000 miles. overall it is a good car but those few problems let it down.

it might not just be this particular car, but there are several points where i do not recomend bmw.

the door locking and unlocking works inconsistently, sometimes it responds and sometimes it doesn't. the tailgate kick opening is almost useless. radio reception on the highway basically doesn't happen, which support has confirmed and is very disappointing. the auto-cruise has stopped functioning while on the move. when i downshift with the paddles, the delay before engine braking comes in is far too long, and the emblem is almost pointless. the auto brake hold can't be turned on and off with a single touch. the engine start feature is treated as a subscription. the usb is only good for charging. the auto wipers don't activate at sensible times. the paid digital premium content feels very poor. the bmw app has failed to pick up driving data three times in the roughly three months since buying the car; i force a reset every time but it never fixes the root cause.

and so on.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.

title: G60 Seat belts
requirement_statement: Improve 'Seat belts' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the seat belts in the vehicle are uncomfortable. Customer stated that because she is on the shorter side, the belt tends to rest and rub against her neck, which she finds uncomfortable.
Customer explained it is difficult for them to latch the seatbelt into the receiver, so they ended up buying an extension.
Customer stated that, if that option were available, he would have gone with a seat belt featuring the M stitching.

Customer stated the salesperson called the seats luxury seats, but they do not live up to his comfort expectations. Customer explained that with luxury seats he anticipates a much higher comfort level, and these seats fall short in that regard. Customer clarified the concern is with the seat base plus the backrest and lumbar areas, and noted the seats are not awful or extremely uncomfortable, just could be improved. Writer acknowledged the comments and advised they would pass them along to engineering.

it is a really good car and the service i get from you has always been reliable. at the same time you can tell it is a fresh model, there are some small details that get a bit irritating:

1. the plastic cover you take off at a fast charger ends up swinging and knocking against the body when it is windy, it could really use some kind of simple holder so it stays put while charging.

2. the front passenger seat belt tends to tap against the b-pillar while driving, which creates an annoying knocking noise.

3. the choice for whether the car should beep when locking/unlocking keeps disappearing and i have already had to switch those beeps off four times, even though i have only had the car around 3 months.

4. the charging cable supplied with the car is too short, since the car is quite long and many chargers make you drive straight in, it would help a lot if the cable was roughly 1-1.5 meters longer.

i really enjoy how the car rides. but bmw has a lot of room to improve when it comes to tech and charging. on the tech side, bmw should really take a look at what hyundai offers, especially since their cars cost a lot less. lane assist needs to be much better, keeping the car truly centered in the lane and handling corners properly for the whole trip. the "cruise control" also needs an upgrade so it adjusts correctly for the following distance the driver selects, and can bring the car all the way to a stop when the car in front stops. the driver alerts like lane departure and car proximity warnings also need to function more reliably.

for charging, bmw should finish up a deal with tesla so bmw owners can use the tesla fast chargers, or else team up with other brands in a joint venture to build a competing fast charging network. right now the non-tesla chargers are not dependable, and even the ones that show up on the bmw map sometimes are not actually there.

after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

the car drives nicely, is comfy, engine feels strong and the steering is quite light, but getting used to all the touchscreen tech is a nightmare. the previous idrive setup was almost perfect and should have been left alone. for example, getting the preset radio stations back onto the display is almost impossible, and being forced to use a touchscreen while driving is a dangerous distraction. there is no proper written owners manual, just loads of videos, which is disappointing as even a simple booklet would have helped. not being able to choose run flat tyres is a step backwards, and with no spare tyre that could be dangerous.

it's a good car, but the way the map magnification is controlled on-screen is extremely dangerous and very distracting, and could easily cause accidents just like using mobile phones. the old setup with a central control knob meant the driver could alter map zoom without taking attention off the road, whereas this new finger-on-screen method does exactly the opposite. i do have a simple workaround that would only need software changes, not a full redesign of the car: the knurled volume wheel could be used for both volume and map zoom, switching between them with a double click on the wheel. i cannot emphasise enough how strongly i feel about this; with this stupid system it is only a matter of time before someone gets killed.

the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.

the car itself is ok but the infotainment ruins the driving feel i was hoping for. you have dropped the basics in favour of stuff that does not matter like light colours and other trivia. before every drive i spend about 5 minutes setting everything how i want, and it still goes back to the default as soon as i stop. the endless stream of messages is distracting, same with the pings and bongs whenever the car does not like what i do. for a while i really thought i had a puncture until i found out it was the car shaking through the steering wheel. there is no need for most of this info and i think some of it is distracting and maybe even lethal. i want to watch the road, not the screen. and useful things like the petrol gauge are tiny and almost hidden on the display. out of space

good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the touchscreen setup is frankly unsafe to use on the move and really needs an idrive wheel to be safer. i don't see why that was removed other than to cut costs. turning off the speed limit and the equally risky lane departure warning is too fiddly, there should be a button for each. the my modes feature in this 120 is almost useless, adding no real driving benefit, just extra complexity and probably cost. the boot is too small for a car of this size. even with these complaints, it still suits my needs perfectly right now, and despite the over-complex tech the interface is still far better than my wife's mercedes a class.

the car itself is amazing, but i find it a real issue that lots of basic functions (like the stop start function) are only reachable through the screen, which is very distracting when you're actualy driving.

overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd than a rear-biased 4wd and you can feel torque steer. dashboard controls - getting rid of the physical buttons and burying everything in the touchscreen is awkward and could even be unsafe. the ui has become a nuisance: to switch into sport mode i have to go through several steps, and since the voice control is flaky and i don't want to chat to my car, that's not an option. when using nav i have to 1) hit the mode button on the centre console, 2) pick the mode on the display, then 3) tap nav on the side of the screen to get the map back. build quality - the plastics feel low grade and there are rattles, particularly around the dash. steering wheel - this is meant to be a sporty hatch, so please stop fitting wheels sized like they belong on a boat.

it is a comfortable place to sit, even if it is not exactly glamorous. driving is mostly good. the sunroof is a let-down though, i would have preferred a larger one. the fact that you push forward for reverse and pull back for drive feels completely crazy to me, i dont understand why anyone would set it up like that. the display isnt great either, everything is tiny, and i only just noticed i was almost out of fuel because it is so hard to see the fuel level. i have almost finished setting up the heating and cooling, but working out where the air actually goes is awkward and there are loads of little controls to fiddle with. i absolutely hate the parking and reversing assist, the car is constantly yelling at me, with margins that seem far too wide. it keeps making warning sounds for no reason i can figure out, and the car has already cut out twice and then would not go either backwards or forwards. i am now about to take it in to be checked.

i am really pleased with every aspect of my bmw 120 m sport. the quality of the finish inside and outside is first class, and it is a genuinely lovely car to drive. the automatic gearbox feels very smooth, and the changes are hardly noticeable, especially once you are at higher speeds. the infotainment setup is excellent, and i really enjoy being able to customise the display. when i use the maps, the layout looks great and is easy on the eyes, with all the key info visible at a glance. i especially like the way the next turn or direction step is shown. if i were choosing again, i would go for exactly the same car, which is the strongest recommendation i can give it.

the 120 m sport is a joy to drive and you really feel connected to it on the road. there is a small hesitation when pulling away in normal drive, but switching to s mode fixes that and that is my preferred setting. the cabin is cozy and the view backwards through the side and rear mirrors is very good. the reversing camera makes parking easy. with the pro pack the car's appearance is boosted and the styling stands out even more. the main screen menu and all its options take a bit of time to learn, but it is actually enjoyable to figure it out. i used to have a 320 sport diesel which i was very fond of, and this new 120 m sport feels even more rewarding and fun to drive. the dynamic handling is very accurate and really encourages good driving. i absolutely love it.

i really like this car. it feels solidly built, quick enough, has excellent fuel economy and is great fun to drive. steering, brakes and handling are all very good. i would prefer some key physical buttons back though, like for the heating and air con. having to switch off the speed limit warning every single time i start up is irritating. the my modes setup is overcomplicated and doesnt give enough flexibility to customise, it should be simpler. i also want a proper rev counter instead of the silly "power level" display, especially on an ice car, and that ought to be selectable in the personal mode. despite those niggles im really pleased with my 1 series.

the car has excellent fuel economy, performs well and is comfortable. what i really dislike is the almost complete absence of proper buttons. why must every control go through the touchscreen? it turns simple things into a longer process, like the heated seat: with a button it is one quick press, but on the screen i have to take my eyes off the road, tap to bring up the icons, then tap again for the seat. picking a radio station is even more of a hassle. bmw used to be sold as the ultimate driving machine, yet now it feels like bmw is just copying the rest. the 123 xdrive drives very nicely, but it is let down by excessive tech and a clear push to cut costs by putting all commands on the touchscreen.

i owned an f40 before this and with the extra power it drove really well. i am not happy that the air conditioning has to be adjusted on the screen, as trying to do that while driving feels potentially dangerous. at night the ambient lighting bounces off the driver side window and blocks part of the view in the door mirror, which to me is a possible safety issue. it makes me wonder if anyone from bmw has actually driven this model in the dark. i ended up switching the ambient lighting off entirely, which makes it seem pointless to have it on during the day anyway.

i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

[controls and ui]
- removing the physical buttons and idrive dial has made operation while driving much worse.
- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.
- the ui behavior is odd, not returning to the home screen after changing modes, leaving the selection screen up.
- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

the car is generally reasonable to drive. it is my first time owning an automatic and i am still getting used to it, noticing both advantages and disadvantages with the change. being a brand new model there are some appealing improvements, but in my view there are one or two design issues (in fact i have found three, though whether others agree is just opinion). the visual warning for another vehicle in the blind spot seems like a great new idea, yet in practice it appears, at least on the nearside, to work very inconsistently. the internal light display reflects too much onto the windscreen at night and becomes a distraction. and having the fog lamp button on the indicator stalk feels odd and tends to cause accidental switching on.

ride comfort is excellent and the power is impressive for a 3-cyl engine. seats are roomy and comfy, and the options are good. road noise is very low for a smaller car, and it compares well to my other car, the m340i, in terms of ride and reduced noise. what we find almost unacceptable is the removal of the gear lever and having nearly everything run through the touchscreen. before, you could start the ventilation with one touch; now you have to aim at the screen twice while driving, which is hard and distracting. all crucial physical buttons need to come back, along with the gear lever. the controls on the previous model were ideal, and it's not clear why they were cut, although it seems obvious it was to save costs.

1. engine and general build are pretty much what i expected. 2. the climate controls look like they are dual zone, yet they are not, which feels very misleading. 3. trying to adjust the heater through the screen is awkward and, when you are moving, even feels unsafe. 4. the software update process asks for far too many actions from the driver and then the display reboots and you have to put everything in again. just overly complex. 5. personally i would rather have a bmw without all these electric so called aids, they seem pointless and far too fussy. i just want a car that drives like they did before around 2015. and because of point 2, i would actually mark it down further, as having a graphic that clearly shows two temperature zones when there is actually only one is downright dishonest to me (even if dual zone is marketed as an extra you can upgrade to).

i really do not like that so much info is pushed onto the touch screen, it should go back to dials and buttons, much less distracting. you are told not to change things while driving and i agree, the big screen with loads of functions is too distracting on the move. this is my first automatic bmw, all the others i had were manuals, and i was offered a different choice this time. the manual was far better, the auto has a noticeable lag when you try to pull away. visibility from the driver seat is worse than in my older models because of the pillar size. the passenger door mirror used to tilt down when reversing, that was really useful for parking, but it is gone now. i also dislike that you must pay extra for premium functions, and the dealer never pointed that out. the reversing camera is useless.

this must be about my 12th bmw and my 3rd 1 series. the driving quality is good and the mini hybrid setup seems to really help with petol consumption. i do miss the bigger boot space though, as the batteries take it up; in the previous one i could put my golf trolley and bag in the back without dropping the seats, now i can't. since i started using the voice function it cuts down how much i need the touch screen and helps me keep my eyes on the road. i have a head up display on this car as on the last, and the way it changed from white to orange when the speed limit was exceeded was useful. the beeping that comes with it is very annoying, and if i turn the beeping off it also stops the orange change on the head up display, which i'd like to keep. there has also been an issue with apple car play and bmw voice.

over the last few years i have owned several 5 series models, the latest being an m5 that i have had for 8 years. that m5 has a head up display and physical knobs for most of the controls, and it is a superb car to drive. i bought this 1 series for my wife, and it comes with a touchscreen. i find that touchscreen frankly dangerous, and when i drive it i would never try to change anything on that screen while the car is moving. i took it from stock because i did not want to wait for one with a head up display, which turned out to be a bad decision. my wife also dislikes the touchscreen and therefore dislikes the car. the touchscreen feels like a solution looking for a problem, whereas in my m5 your eyes stay on the road and your left hand learns where the knobs are so you do not need to look down. it is a shame, because the car itself is great to drive.

i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

my new 120 m sport has a nice colour and is a tidy little car. before this i had 5 new 3 series tourings, the last one a 330i m sport which was lovely, and the 120 is not in the same league. i notice the road noise gets quite loud once you are over about 50 mph, which makes the radio hard to hear. i also can't get my i pod to show info on the screen via usb, it only works over bluetooth now. the automatic gearbox doesn't feel as good or as smooth as the 330i's. the tech in this car is very hard to get used to for me as a retired older driver. i asked for an owners manual when the car was delivered but, roughly 3 months later, still haven't had one, first time i've had a new car without a handbook included. the 120 is a strong little car and i'm happy with how it performs. overall i'd give it 7 out of 10.

as a daily driver it is very nice and has plenty of punch when you ask for it, but as a sporty car it feels too sterile - very fast yet no character, no proper noise apart from the fake stuff. making everything run through the touch screen is a backwards step from the old rotary i-drive, it is distracting and awkward to use while moving, especially with the firm suspension on bumpy british roads. needing apple carplay just to play music is irritating, why was usb media not kept as an option? not being able to run on side lights alone is also annoying. digital premium seems pretty pointless, and when bmw pushed a forced software update overnight once the free period ended, it actually felt like a downgrade, and the update got corrupted so nothing worked and the screens were frozen the next morning. an engineer had to come out to sort it, he did a great job, but bmw did not.

this version of the 1 series feels like a major improvement in styling, design and especially the built-in tech, with the cockpit layout standing out. i'd still tell anyone shopping for this kind of car to pick a 1 series, but some of the tech is irritating and too buried in the screen. using the screen to adjust the heating and cooling fan isn't ideal, a physical button would be better. quite often the car doesn't recognise me with the digital key, and i have to lock and unlock it before it accepts me. i like having a 24 hour clock and have set it that way, yet on each new trip it drops back off 24 hour format. small things, but they're annoying. despite that, i really enjoy my 1 series.

i am really disappointed that so many functions now depend on the central screen instead of the switches/buttons i had on my previous bmws. trying to do all that while driving feels very unsafe. for example, turning on auto hold takes four different sections on the screen, and there seems to be no way to have it preset so you dont need to repeat it for every single trip. on my last new 1 series the wing mirrors folded automatically, but on this one the fold mirrors on lock/unlock option is written in very faint letters and cannot actually be activated. the climate control fan speeds for medium, high and very high all end up blowing like the low setting. looking back, the handover when i bought the car should have explained the electronics much better. engine is finebetter ride none flats.

this feels like a big step up from my old bmw 120. the seating is far more comfortable, and the steering is lighter and reacts better. as a mild hybrid the fuel use is much improved, i get more mpg which makes it cheaper to run. the standard reverse parking camera is brilliant, it really helps make parking safer and simpler in tight spots. i also love the vehicle warning lights in the side mirrors on the motorway, another very useful standard feature that makes driving and overtaking safer. overall i'm really pleased with the new car, bmw definitely seem to have upgraded the 120 m sport. it's small but still has plenty of punch. i did knock off 1 point because the central screen is tricky to use while on the move, i'm right handed so actually hitting the correct button first go can be a bit hit and miss.

overall the car is good, but my score drops because of a few things:
* the xdrive feels too front-wheel biased. a rear-wheel bias would have suited it better and been more fun, especially since this is supposed to be a semi-enthusiast car with 300hp and a price around 500 tkr.
* there are shift paddles instead of a proper gear lever. even a sequential "fake" shift lever for the dct would have felt better than paddles. the paddles come across as a gimmick and really only make sense on the highway. when you are turning or trying to drift, the paddles are basically useless.
* there are no physical controls for climate comfort like ac or seat heating. the screen is extremely clunky for the things you change all the time, such as temperature. for everything else, the screen works great.
* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.

i honestly wouldnt have gone for this car if it werent for the excellent leasing offer, about 4500 sek per month for 2 years. the choice was between leasing this or buying an old tuned volvo 740. i am happy i picked this one, but when you want to have fun driving, the gear paddles and the slightly too strong front-wheel bias do make it feel a bit limited.

last 7 cars were bmws, but because the new 1-series launch was delayed my previous car ended up being a mercedes. very pleased to be back in a bmw! overall i am really happy with this car, so the points below are in that context: 1. first time with an automatic. i also drive my partner's fiat 500ev, and i am a bit disappointed by the slight lag in acceleration. i can get around it by putting it in sport mode ahead of time, but thats not always practical, and it doesnt stack up well against the ev. i havent touched the paddles and doubt i will. 2. the display is limited compared with the mercedes. i cant show consumption, elapsed time and distance driven along with the standard info like i could on the a-class. 3. can't use a usb stick for music. 4. as usual there is more functionality than i will ever need or use, and i am still going through the online manual.

i previously test drove the older 1 series and found it very uninvolving and not at all like a typical bmw, so i chose not to buy it. later, when i read about the new version, especially the mild hybrid with 4-wheel drive, my interest came back. within the first quarter mile it felt like a proper bmw again, with great feedback through the steering, spot-on handling, real grip on the road and strong performance when you select the right mode. the cabin layout is easy to understand even for someone who has never owned a car with a touchscreen. i really appreciate that the indicator stalks are back to simple on/off switches; the old setup could be awkward to cancel and sometimes ended up signalling the other way. i have already done several long trips and felt relaxed afterwards. extremely satisfied so far!

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

i've only covered around 1500 miles in it so far, so i don't think i've fully decided how i feel about the car yet. up to now though it's been really comfy to sit in, feels dependable and it seems very good on fuel. it did take me a bit of time to work out the whole system and get everything set up how i wanted, and i was pretty irritated when an update came through to the vehicle and wiped all my settings so i had to go back and redo them from scratch. i guess it's not a massive issue, just annoying. the other downside for me is the greasy fingerprints that end up all over the infotainment screen, which stand out a lot, especially when the sun is shining. this is the first bmw i've owned and i was told that it used to be operated with a dial between the front seats, similar to how my last 3 mercedes worked. even so, at the moment it wouldn't put me off buying another bmw. overall it feels like a good all-round car.

great spec, strong performance and generally a quality feel. one thing though - the knurled button on the steering wheel feels a bit cheap to the touch. the screen layout is very thorough and the 'recently used' feature is really useful. it would be better if there were separate heating adjustments for driver and passenger. the flashing blindspot light in the driver's wing mirror is a really good safety touch. having another, less usual option word instead of just 'bmw' would make it easier not to trigger the driver assistance wake-up by accident. the lighting modes and themes are excellent; it would be good to have extra downloadable themes to keep it fresh.

my last car was a 128ti and its overall spec was much better than this new 120i. the standard equipment, both inside and outside, is superior on the 128ti. i also find the new touch screen features harder to use and navigate; on the 120i the map is very slow to show traffic, and sometimes it does not appear at all, whereas it worked better on the 128ti. compared with the 128ti the 120i is disappointing, and i was expecting a nicer driving experience. the accelerator response is poor, and i often have to tap the pedal several times just to creep the car forward a bit. i do not know if that is because of the hybrid part, but it feels dangerous when parking or in slow traffic. overall i much prefer the old 128ti and the 120i does not impress me.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

i have already had to return the car to the dealer three times because it keeps dropping its speech function. when i collected it initially, it was missing bmw assist and sat nav and it would not connect to my phone at all. it took two separate visits before those things were finally sorted. afterwards the voice function for the sat nav vanished again. sometimes the text messages show on the touch screen, sometimes they do not. the way the car drives is excellent, but the problems above really spoil it. this is my 4th 1 series and it may end up being my last.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

this is my first bmw and also the smallest car i've had in a long time, so i find it hard to directly compare with other similar brands. i would happily point this model out to anyone who wants decent lively performance and a car that lets the driver have plenty of personal input. in m sport spec it comes very well kitted out, with some extras thrown in as standard that you normally pay for on other cars. the touchscreen controls probably won't be everyone's favourite, but you get used to them fairly quickly. the only real complaint i have is that there should be a proper owner's handbook supplied, as some of us still prefer a non-digital reference. overall it's a very pleasant car and i certainly wouldn't put anyone off buying one.

the inability to properly control the driving modes is really annoying. the disappearance of buttons and the idrive wheel to manage things is a pain. the touch screen itself is very good, but it pulls your attention away too much. a simple button to turn off start stop would do, instead it's awkward to use. i want to set off, not waste time searching through menus. the centre console buttons are hard to distinguish so you have to look down, there's barely any separation. the steering wheel is excessively thick and an option for a slimmer one would be preferable. with no audible exhaust note it becomes boring to drive. you pay a high price only to be asked to pay again for premium infotainment options soon after. i only want the spotify app. the cabin is beautiful and a pleasant environment. i feel like i'm managing a machine rather than actually driving. fantastic car, no character at all.

overall the car is very good. the centre console let the interior down because the plastics feel cheap. having the climate functions only on the touchscreen isnt great, proper buttons would work better. to turn off the climate you have to dive into a sub menu on the main screen, which creates distraction. the 7 speed gearbox sometimes reacts slowly so acceleration is delayed, and that can end up in dangerous situations. maybe a software update could sort this out?

title: F70 Drivetrain

No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.

evidence.quote: its a really good car, definitely feels like an upgrade over my old f40 118i m sport. engine is strong and the mild hybrid gives a nice extra shove and helps with efficiency. it corners and rides very well and im getting better fuel economy than with the f40. some of the cabin materials feel a bit flimsier than before, not a big deal but i did notice. the new cabin layout looks great and all the digital stuff behaves properly. a few oddities though: the keyless entry/exit reacts way too easily, and sometimes the car systems seem to randomly reset, so auto hold ends up switched off in the menu even though i had it on. the speed warning feature is just irritating, even if i can switch it off each trip here in the uk.

we run two cars at the moment, the new bmw and a 6 year old mini countryman 2 litre petrol. i actually like the countryman much more, so much so that if i could have bought a new like for like countryman i would have gone for that instead of the bmw. it is far more comfortable, nicer to drive and easily quick enough, with not a huge gap in mpg between them. the dials and controls are more old school on the countryman but i find them simpler to use and they give everything a driver needs. ideally i would keep my 6 year old mini and also have a brand new one with the same specification rather than the bmw. despite that i am still generally a fan of bmw. happy to talk about it further.  mark benson.

after years of driving fairly bland everyday cars, this one has been a real breath of fresh air in terms of driving dynamics. the last car i enjoyed as much was an audi ur quattro i bought back in 1987 and kept for about 12 years. i plan to hang on to this one for a while too, though i might look at a 123 xdrive at some point, even though this car certainly isn't short on performance. i've already suggested it to a friend, although he ended up with a 220 instead. we were both unhappy that bmw deleted the m badges from the front wings on the m sport versions, so we bought the badges ourselves. it really feels like a cost-cutting move, and i hope bmw changes that decision. overall i'm very satisfied and would recommend it to anyone.

the car itself is ok but the infotainment ruins the driving feel i was hoping for. you have dropped the basics in favour of stuff that does not matter like light colours and other trivia. before every drive i spend about 5 minutes setting everything how i want, and it still goes back to the default as soon as i stop. the endless stream of messages is distracting, same with the pings and bongs whenever the car does not like what i do. for a while i really thought i had a puncture until i found out it was the car shaking through the steering wheel. there is no need for most of this info and i think some of it is distracting and maybe even lethal. i want to watch the road, not the screen. and useful things like the petrol gauge are tiny and almost hidden on the display. out of space

overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd than a rear-biased 4wd and you can feel torque steer. dashboard controls - getting rid of the physical buttons and burying everything in the touchscreen is awkward and could even be unsafe. the ui has become a nuisance: to switch into sport mode i have to go through several steps, and since the voice control is flaky and i don't want to chat to my car, that's not an option. when using nav i have to 1) hit the mode button on the centre console, 2) pick the mode on the display, then 3) tap nav on the side of the screen to get the map back. build quality - the plastics feel low grade and there are rattles, particularly around the dash. steering wheel - this is meant to be a sporty hatch, so please stop fitting wheels sized like they belong on a boat.

the car has excellent fuel economy, performs well and is comfortable. what i really dislike is the almost complete absence of proper buttons. why must every control go through the touchscreen? it turns simple things into a longer process, like the heated seat: with a button it is one quick press, but on the screen i have to take my eyes off the road, tap to bring up the icons, then tap again for the seat. picking a radio station is even more of a hassle. bmw used to be sold as the ultimate driving machine, yet now it feels like bmw is just copying the rest. the 123 xdrive drives very nicely, but it is let down by excessive tech and a clear push to cut costs by putting all commands on the touchscreen.

the sensor for unlocking the doors feels too insensitive, and roughly one out of five times the lock wont react even when touching the handle. as soon as you open the door, the audio system powers up. if you step away from the car briefly while the engine is left running, the horn starts blaring, so you basically cant use the ot-lock feature. when setting a navigation destination by voice, only a small number of options is shown and one gets picked automatically, so you are unable to choose from several candidates. with the engine running at night you cant switch on the lights, so i would at least like them to be smaller. the rear gate opener also reacts poorly, probably because that sensor isnt very sensitive either. the remote key needs to be quite close for the doors to lock, the effective distance is short.

i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

[controls and ui]
- removing the physical buttons and idrive dial has made operation while driving much worse.
- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.
- the ui behavior is odd, not returning to the home screen after changing modes, leaving the selection screen up.
- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.

- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

ride comfort is excellent and the power is impressive for a 3-cyl engine. seats are roomy and comfy, and the options are good. road noise is very low for a smaller car, and it compares well to my other car, the m340i, in terms of ride and reduced noise. what we find almost unacceptable is the removal of the gear lever and having nearly everything run through the touchscreen. before, you could start the ventilation with one touch; now you have to aim at the screen twice while driving, which is hard and distracting. all crucial physical buttons need to come back, along with the gear lever. the controls on the previous model were ideal, and it's not clear why they were cut, although it seems obvious it was to save costs.

1. engine and general build are pretty much what i expected. 2. the climate controls look like they are dual zone, yet they are not, which feels very misleading. 3. trying to adjust the heater through the screen is awkward and, when you are moving, even feels unsafe. 4. the software update process asks for far too many actions from the driver and then the display reboots and you have to put everything in again. just overly complex. 5. personally i would rather have a bmw without all these electric so called aids, they seem pointless and far too fussy. i just want a car that drives like they did before around 2015. and because of point 2, i would actually mark it down further, as having a graphic that clearly shows two temperature zones when there is actually only one is downright dishonest to me (even if dual zone is marketed as an extra you can upgrade to).

our last car was an audi a3, only about two years old, and in every respect the 120 m sport tops it. the build quality inside and out, the fuel economy, the performance and the handling are all better. for us this model really hits the sweet spot in the range, the size is exactly right and the price is too. the dealer experience was good as well. we tried a lexus lbx alongside the bmw and while the lexus was packed with tech, the bmw was as full of technology and felt properly exciting with it. the only real negative, which seems common across other makers too, is not having a proper paper handbook any more, which would be much easier to flick through and use than the electronic versions.

for us this is a major step up from the previous f40 version. the ride is noticeably smoother and the cabin much quieter, with a handy increase in acceleration performance as well. fuel economy is significantly better, the regenerative braking really shines, and together with the bigger fuel tank it gives a very useful gain in overall range. the curved screen setup for driver info, sat nav, climate and so on works really well, and in our view is far better than similar systems in many other cars.

the one negative so far is the "puddle lights" in the outer door handles, which currently do not operate, even though they are fitted in the handles. these were standard and fully working on our previous 118i m sport, so why not on this one? apart from that, the car drives exactly how a bmw should and gives the impression of being a much larger model. we absolutely love it.

i have downsized to this small car and really like the x drive, with the 2 litre engine giving enough power for everyday use. the whole 'apps' setup feels clumsy and can distract when you just want to tweak something simple like the seat heating or heated steering wheel. after a software update some settings went back to factory, which was annoying as i only noticed at night when the instrument brightness had changed. this is a car, not a mobile phone. the boot space is badly cut down by the 'hybrid lite' batteries. over 30+ years i have had 10 new bmws and this is the first one that has no anchor points in the boot, which is particularly irritating when stuff slides around. overall still a good little car.

the car is comfortable and still fun to drive, with light controls, decent performance and good economy, and it clearly shows bmw build quality. i only marked it down from a '10' because the instruments are poor and much harder to read than on my older 325 coupe, which is vastly better laid out and more ergonomic. traditional analogue gauges are far easier to glance at without looking away from the road. the lack of a proper printed handbook also makes figuring out the complicated touch screen more difficult. the on-screen 'keyboard' for entering satnav addresses is definitely better, but the male navigation voice is less clear than the female one on my previous 118. the voice-controlled satnav is a complete waste for us, it simply will not work for either me or my wife.
