i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

my new 120 m sport has a nice colour and is a tidy little car. before this i had 5 new 3 series tourings, the last one a 330i m sport which was lovely, and the 120 is not in the same league. i notice the road noise gets quite loud once you are over about 50 mph, which makes the radio hard to hear. i also can't get my i pod to show info on the screen via usb, it only works over bluetooth now. the automatic gearbox doesn't feel as good or as smooth as the 330i's. the tech in this car is very hard to get used to for me as a retired older driver. i asked for an owners manual when the car was delivered but, roughly 3 months later, still haven't had one, first time i've had a new car without a handbook included. the 120 is a strong little car and i'm happy with how it performs. overall i'd give it 7 out of 10.

overall it is a better, if slightly mixed, step up from my old 180i msport. the roadholding is more precise, the ride is improved on bad surfaces, there is a useful bit of extra power, the stop/start is far superior (the previous one was so poor i never used it), fuel economy is better and the engine runs smoother. on the downside, there is no single, easy-to-find autohold button anymore, it now needs one button then a touch on the screen. i rely on autohold for most driving, except for slow manoeuvres in tight areas where the throttle blip to release autohold can create more movement than i want. there should be a simpler, faster way to switch autohold on and off. i also miss a feature from my 180i: comfort mode used to give constant coasting. i realise regen improves efficiency, but having the option of coasting would be good for a very relaxed drive.

as a daily driver it is very nice and has plenty of punch when you ask for it, but as a sporty car it feels too sterile - very fast yet no character, no proper noise apart from the fake stuff. making everything run through the touch screen is a backwards step from the old rotary i-drive, it is distracting and awkward to use while moving, especially with the firm suspension on bumpy british roads. needing apple carplay just to play music is irritating, why was usb media not kept as an option? not being able to run on side lights alone is also annoying. digital premium seems pretty pointless, and when bmw pushed a forced software update overnight once the free period ended, it actually felt like a downgrade, and the update got corrupted so nothing worked and the screens were frozen the next morning. an engineer had to come out to sort it, he did a great job, but bmw did not.

this is the 6th bmw i have owned, a mix of new and used, and i've liked every single one of them. i feel this particular model is the best yet, it is a pleasure to drive. i was hesitant about going for an automatic at first, but i wanted this model so i went ahead, and i have absolutely no regrets. it comes with all the technology i realistically need, even though i know there are extra options available beyond what i have. the car responds quickly when you ask it to, is comfortable, and the interior layout is very well thought out. the boot is big enough to carry my band gear without issues. i picked the midnight thunder paint and friends and family often comment on how distinctive it looks. the only downside was one time when the software hadn't updated properly and i had to carefully coax the car back home, luckily i was close by and an engineer sorted it out. now i always keep an eye on the app for that.

car drives very smoothly, corners well and has enough power. it is quiet and the fuel consumption is good, though it's been mainly motorway use so far. the dashboard looks nice but really isn't practical to operate while driving. the dash lighting reflects in both outer rear view mirrors. the boot is smaller, but in fairness the tank is larger than on my previous 118i m sport, which gives better range. i miss the little storage area on the dash by the steering column. the seats are less comfortable than in my old 118i m sport and the driver's seat is already losing its shape, and i am only just over 12 stone. i also miss having an adjustable back support. the colour is perfect. sadly the car wasn't ordered to my own spec so it has extras i wouldn't normally pay for. i'm not keen on the idea of a trial period for extras and then having to pay to keep them.

i'm very pleased with my new car overall. it fits what i need and comes with lots of extra features. the performance is excellent and i really like the interior and all the functions. my favourite bits are the heated seats, the heated steering wheel, the different drive modes and being able to personalise things like the ambient lighting. the parking camera works really well, and there were plenty of choices when buying it new. on the downside, i would have rated it even higher. i paid extra to have an electric boot fitted. the car has only done around 500 miles, and i don't think i'd actually used the electric boot up to that point. i walked up to the car, pressed the boot open button on the key, and there was nothing around me, then i heard a loud bang. when i checked, the parcel shelf clearly hadn't been fitted properly, had come loose while driving, got wedged, and the auto boot mechanism snapped the clips. i took it back to the dealer, but they couldn't assist, only telling me it would be £280 to get a new parcel shelf. #really

i chose the 1 series because i have been driving bmw cars for roughly 35 years. i would have preferred to get another x1, but my budget would not stretch to the price. given my age now and the fact i drive fewer miles, i have found this car very comfortable, especially after raising the seat to give me a higher and better driving position. the engine capacity is about 25% smaller, which worried me at first, but i quickly got used to it and now i barely notice. my concern is that, when i bought the car, nobody mentioned the extra digital upgrade, which seems to be around £12 a month. i am disappointed that the sat nav without this upgrade is quite inferior. i now think the upgrade is expensive and feel rather let down.

this feels like a big step up from my old bmw 120. the seating is far more comfortable, and the steering is lighter and reacts better. as a mild hybrid the fuel use is much improved, i get more mpg which makes it cheaper to run. the standard reverse parking camera is brilliant, it really helps make parking safer and simpler in tight spots. i also love the vehicle warning lights in the side mirrors on the motorway, another very useful standard feature that makes driving and overtaking safer. overall i'm really pleased with the new car, bmw definitely seem to have upgraded the 120 m sport. it's small but still has plenty of punch. i did knock off 1 point because the central screen is tricky to use while on the move, i'm right handed so actually hitting the correct button first go can be a bit hit and miss.

last 7 cars were bmws, but because the new 1-series launch was delayed my previous car ended up being a mercedes. very pleased to be back in a bmw! overall i am really happy with this car, so the points below are in that context: 1. first time with an automatic. i also drive my partner's fiat 500ev, and i am a bit disappointed by the slight lag in acceleration. i can get around it by putting it in sport mode ahead of time, but thats not always practical, and it doesnt stack up well against the ev. i havent touched the paddles and doubt i will. 2. the display is limited compared with the mercedes. i cant show consumption, elapsed time and distance driven along with the standard info like i could on the a-class. 3. can't use a usb stick for music. 4. as usual there is more functionality than i will ever need or use, and i am still going through the online manual.

why is there a character limit? mechanically it feels cheap, rushed and badly tuned, not what i expected from bmw. my old 2010 e82 1 series was superior in every respect. the missing idrive wheel is a letdown and there is no proper replacement. mercedes puts a touch pad on the steering wheel, but here both next track buttons are inconsistent and irritating to use. the suspension needs more tuning for uk motorways and roads. the hybrid system also needs a lot of work: when you come up to a roundabout it sits in too high a gear and takes about two seconds to change down. i picked the bmw hybrid partly because it does not use a cvt, yet the gearbox fitted feels very slow to downshift when you need it. the auto wipers react too slowly to changing weather. and is there really no tire pressure sensor?

my last car was a 128ti and its overall spec was much better than this new 120i. the standard equipment, both inside and outside, is superior on the 128ti. i also find the new touch screen features harder to use and navigate; on the 120i the map is very slow to show traffic, and sometimes it does not appear at all, whereas it worked better on the 128ti. compared with the 128ti the 120i is disappointing, and i was expecting a nicer driving experience. the accelerator response is poor, and i often have to tap the pedal several times just to creep the car forward a bit. i do not know if that is because of the hybrid part, but it feels dangerous when parking or in slow traffic. overall i much prefer the old 128ti and the 120i does not impress me.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

it's a good car, but the way the map magnification is controlled on-screen is extremely dangerous and very distracting, and could easily cause accidents just like using mobile phones. the old setup with a central control knob meant the driver could alter map zoom without taking attention off the road, whereas this new finger-on-screen method does exactly the opposite. i do have a simple workaround that would only need software changes, not a full redesign of the car: the knurled volume wheel could be used for both volume and map zoom, switching between them with a double click on the wheel. i cannot emphasise enough how strongly i feel about this; with this stupid system it is only a matter of time before someone gets killed.

the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.

the car itself is ok but the infotainment ruins the driving feel i was hoping for. you have dropped the basics in favour of stuff that does not matter like light colours and other trivia. before every drive i spend about 5 minutes setting everything how i want, and it still goes back to the default as soon as i stop. the endless stream of messages is distracting, same with the pings and bongs whenever the car does not like what i do. for a while i really thought i had a puncture until i found out it was the car shaking through the steering wheel. there is no need for most of this info and i think some of it is distracting and maybe even lethal. i want to watch the road, not the screen. and useful things like the petrol gauge are tiny and almost hidden on the display. out of space

i picked up the car on the 24th of august. it was meant to be ready on the 23rd and i had taken annual leave, but there was an error message on the car that they could not sort so i only collected it a day later. then on the 21st of september, as i was leaving my work address, i got a drivetrain brake fault and the car refused to let me drive. i rang bmw support at 7pm and was told nobody could come out until the following day, so i phoned rbc instead and they came the next day, saying there were several errors and to call bmw in the morning. bmw turned up the next morning, by then the hazards had been left on all night so it had switched to the second battery, which did a restart. now, fast forward to today, i have no parking brake at all and i am just about to call again.

at the time of purchase, the negotiations dragged on and were tied up until late at night.

a lot of people i know drive bmws, and they have not had any major trouble so far.
i want them to stick to the promise to buy it back.
or i want it to be a car that works properly.

pros - the fresh design is very attractive, the interior quality is excellent and there is some new standard kit, plus the engine with its electric boost is very efficient both in economy and performance. the new infotainment is generally very good, apart from one missing feature. cons - after having 3 118i's i really miss the rotary controller and the shortcut buttons, and finding that standard air recirculation to the rear has been removed is dissapointing. (i even checked with the dealer, thinking it was a mistake, only to be told it is now part of a package) my main disappointment is the media system. when cars lost cd players years ago i copied lots of cds onto a port memory stick and could access them via the media, which is now not possible. however, it is still a very nice car.

i moved down from an m135 drive and the power in this one is still absolutely fine and nicely responsive for everyday driving. i much prefer the battery assisted stop/start setup, and the steering has a nice light feel that firms up as you go faster. i am a bit let down that the i-drive knob has gone, as i always thought that system was brilliant when on the move. the new screens look very smart and, once you have them configured, they work well, and the overall fascia design and materials feel excellent. my f70120 m sport drives and handles really well day to day, and i actually like how it looks more than the f40. the front electric seats are really comfy and offer very precise adjustment. i am enjoying the head-up display, its my first time using one. the sat nav reacts quickly and is really helpful when finding your way around unfamiliar routes and towns. i also really like the 'y' style wheels and the red calipers.

there is plenty to appreciate but also a couple of niggles. from behind the wheel the suspension feels quite firm, possibly just more noticeable because the cabin is so quiet. the software is very complex and the manual doesn't help much, particularly when i try to use it on my phone; a proper printed booklet might be better. the satnav has sent me down more single track lanes in the past 3 months than i've driven in the last 3 years, so i don't really trust it now. i do, however, like how it integrates with the guidance on the dash.

i had a bmw before so i thought i knew what it would be like, but the performance and handling are better than i expected. my only two issues are the tech, which i find not very user friendly, and the ride being a bit harsh, but i can live with both.

i basically like the car overall, but there are a few serious reservations. the ride is simply too firm even for a performance model, and although adaptive suspension is standard, you can't actually adjust it, which makes its usefulness very debatable. my biggest annoyance, though, is that everyday functions are effectively blocked because i don't own a smartphone and therefore don't use a bmw app. for example, the nearside mirror no longer dips when reversing and auto hold can't be left permanently on. when i first bought the car the salesperson configured these for me, but an ota update wiped those settings and i have no way of getting them back. so i now have a car that cost almost £50k, with features i can't use that were incredibly easy to set up on previous vehicles, which is really disappointing.

i am really pleased with every aspect of my bmw 120 m sport. the quality of the finish inside and outside is first class, and it is a genuinely lovely car to drive. the automatic gearbox feels very smooth, and the changes are hardly noticeable, especially once you are at higher speeds. the infotainment setup is excellent, and i really enjoy being able to customise the display. when i use the maps, the layout looks great and is easy on the eyes, with all the key info visible at a glance. i especially like the way the next turn or direction step is shown. if i were choosing again, i would go for exactly the same car, which is the strongest recommendation i can give it.

overall i am very pleased with my new vehicle. after around three months i am gradually getting used to the technology built into it. there are a few aspects of the idrive options i would prefer to be different. first, i would like the ability to turn off the auto headlights. at the moment the lights can only be switched off while the car is in standby, and once the engine is running the auto lights are active again. there is a control on the lighting stalk but it does not actually disable them. second, there is no way to switch off the front daytime running lights, even though i am sure they could be accessed if needed. third, both the 12v supply (cigar lighter socket) and the usb c charging points stay powered for about 5 minutes after the vehicle is shut down, which keeps my dashcam running and leads to battery discharge.

i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

[controls and ui]
- removing the physical buttons and idrive dial has made operation while driving much worse.
- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.
- the ui behavior is odd, not returning to the home screen after changing modes, leaving the selection screen up.
- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

the driving performance and fuel economy are both very good, making it an enjoyable car to use. however, i am annoyed with the electronics and software. the 'smart' key on my phone seems to need a reset every now and then, and i have to unlock the phone with face recognition before it will unlock the car, which is no better than using the normal key. it has even looked like it unlocked the car and then left me locked out again, so i end up going through the reset process. when my wife was using the smart key we shared the same profile, and the system would jump between our phones. i still have not managed to get both phones working for calls over bluetooth; they both show as connected but only one or the other actually works. there was a remote update to the system recently, and since then the auto hold function that i set as on by default in my profile will sometimes be off again the next time i drive. it does not happen every single trip, so overall i would give it a 7.

as a daily driver it is very nice and has plenty of punch when you ask for it, but as a sporty car it feels too sterile - very fast yet no character, no proper noise apart from the fake stuff. making everything run through the touch screen is a backwards step from the old rotary i-drive, it is distracting and awkward to use while moving, especially with the firm suspension on bumpy british roads. needing apple carplay just to play music is irritating, why was usb media not kept as an option? not being able to run on side lights alone is also annoying. digital premium seems pretty pointless, and when bmw pushed a forced software update overnight once the free period ended, it actually felt like a downgrade, and the update got corrupted so nothing worked and the screens were frozen the next morning. an engineer had to come out to sort it, he did a great job, but bmw did not.

this is the 6th bmw i have owned, a mix of new and used, and i've liked every single one of them. i feel this particular model is the best yet, it is a pleasure to drive. i was hesitant about going for an automatic at first, but i wanted this model so i went ahead, and i have absolutely no regrets. it comes with all the technology i realistically need, even though i know there are extra options available beyond what i have. the car responds quickly when you ask it to, is comfortable, and the interior layout is very well thought out. the boot is big enough to carry my band gear without issues. i picked the midnight thunder paint and friends and family often comment on how distinctive it looks. the only downside was one time when the software hadn't updated properly and i had to carefully coax the car back home, luckily i was close by and an engineer sorted it out. now i always keep an eye on the app for that.

from the first drive home from the dealer in my new bmw120 i felt at ease in the car. the seats are excellent, the steering is very precise, and the general feel of the interior is one of quality. the extras that come as standard are very complete. i find bmw idrive straightforward to operate, and the control display always seems to react well to what i do. this is the 5th bmw i have owned and it is the one i enjoy driving the most. only a few gripes: i am unhappy that there is no physical owners manual. i do have a pdf on my laptop and i can use the bmw app for tutorials, but i would still like a paper copy to look at. the material on the door pockets seems lower grade than the rest of the cabin. these are minor issues really, otherwise everything is good!

why is there a character limit? mechanically it feels cheap, rushed and badly tuned, not what i expected from bmw. my old 2010 e82 1 series was superior in every respect. the missing idrive wheel is a letdown and there is no proper replacement. mercedes puts a touch pad on the steering wheel, but here both next track buttons are inconsistent and irritating to use. the suspension needs more tuning for uk motorways and roads. the hybrid system also needs a lot of work: when you come up to a roundabout it sits in too high a gear and takes about two seconds to change down. i picked the bmw hybrid partly because it does not use a cvt, yet the gearbox fitted feels very slow to downshift when you need it. the auto wipers react too slowly to changing weather. and is there really no tire pressure sensor?

i've only covered around 1500 miles in it so far, so i don't think i've fully decided how i feel about the car yet. up to now though it's been really comfy to sit in, feels dependable and it seems very good on fuel. it did take me a bit of time to work out the whole system and get everything set up how i wanted, and i was pretty irritated when an update came through to the vehicle and wiped all my settings so i had to go back and redo them from scratch. i guess it's not a massive issue, just annoying. the other downside for me is the greasy fingerprints that end up all over the infotainment screen, which stand out a lot, especially when the sun is shining. this is the first bmw i've owned and i was told that it used to be operated with a dial between the front seats, similar to how my last 3 mercedes worked. even so, at the moment it wouldn't put me off buying another bmw. overall it feels like a good all-round car.

my issue is that i find modern technology hard to cope with. it all feels very complicated. it ended up taking about 3 months before i got an owner's handbook, and that only arrived after i kept on at the dealer repeatedly. it had been 11 years since i last bought a bmw, so a lot has changed. i found not having a traditional handbrake quite frightening. if i had received the handbook on the first day, that would have been far more useful. i did consider a mercedes a class, but the privacy glass in the rear window put me off. the staff at bmw wakefield were helpful. the difficulty was that i was so overwhelmed by all the new functions that it stopped me from truly enjoying the new car. the reception desk at wakefield and the parking attendant are both really good. i am beginning to like the car more now, but i still feel slightly scared of it. younger relatives would probably love it.

the car is decent to drive, comfortable, and the performance is enough for what we need. however, the connected app is unreliable, sometimes it just does not work, and the tech interface feels overly complicated, which is quite off putting when you mainly just want to drive. it also seems to need software updates again and again, and the voice instruction function is not dependable. our connected drive premium service only lasts three months, which comes across as a cynical way to take more money when the car itself is already sold at a premium price. we have owned bmw cars for about twenty years, but it is very likely this will be the last one we buy.

i have had 7 bmws so far and liked every one of them, but this one is easily the best i have owned. it is a pleasure to drive and i actually look forward to any trip. it can be calm and smooth when i want to relax, but turns into something exciting and fun when i feel like it. despite being a small car it works hard, with a practical and flexible load space. up to now, apart from a puncture, no bmw has ever let me down. it looks great, is comfortable, and the sound system is excellent. the infotainment is very intuitive and functions really well. my only gripe is that connected drive (digital premium) should not be an add-on but built into the price from the start. outstanding customer service from stratstone derby as well.

i ordered my bmw m135 as a factory build so i could get all the extras i wanted, and it's actually the 5th bmw i've bought from the same bmw dealer in oakford. to be honest, i've kind of gone off the car because i had software problems right from the start, even when i picked it up, and the dealership took ages to get it sorted, only really moving on it because i kept sending them emails every week. i then had more issues with the my bmw app, where the my trips function just stopped working. i took the car back for the bmw genius to look at it, but he couldn't figure out what was wrong, so i ended up spending hours on the phone with the connected drive team, sending them pictures of what was happening with the car so they could put together a case for the technicians to investigate. put it this way, my next new car won't be a bmw. regards neil

generally the car is good, but in my view the electronic dash totally spoils it. my wife and i have done around 3800 miles since buying it and we have decided that trying to change anything hidden in the dash while on the move is just too dangerous, because of how long your eyes are off the road. so if we are together the passenger does the adjustments, and if alone we pull over to change things. i feel this system is many times more complex than my iphone, and it is illegal to use an iphone while driving. what is wrong with simple knobs, switches and dials? i also dread to think what it will cost to replace the dash when it eventually fails.

i'm very pleased with the car overall, except for the idrive freezing, which meant taking it back to the dealer for a hard reset. we have three 1 series in the household and i actually like the previous model's idrive more, as with this one i'm having to look away from the road to change things that used to have a physical switch or button. i also feel the premium connected idrive, which is only free for three months, should stay free for the first buyer for as long as they own the car, and then be an optional extra for any later owner. when i try talking to the car, most of what i get back is "im sorry i don't understand" or "i don't know how to help with that". i'm not sure if that's down to my accent or me not asking for specific commands, but either way i would strongly suggest a list of key words that make it work best. i'd really value knowing what to ask it.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

the inability to properly control the driving modes is really annoying. the disappearance of buttons and the idrive wheel to manage things is a pain. the touch screen itself is very good, but it pulls your attention away too much. a simple button to turn off start stop would do, instead it's awkward to use. i want to set off, not waste time searching through menus. the centre console buttons are hard to distinguish so you have to look down, there's barely any separation. the steering wheel is excessively thick and an option for a slimmer one would be preferable. with no audible exhaust note it becomes boring to drive. you pay a high price only to be asked to pay again for premium infotainment options soon after. i only want the spotify app. the cabin is beautiful and a pleasant environment. i feel like i'm managing a machine rather than actually driving. fantastic car, no character at all.

this is my first petrol 1 series after having had four previous bmw 1 series sport models, and while i do enjoy how it drives, there are some things that really annoy me. the biggest frustration is the new virtual assistant, which just isn't as good as the old one. on top of that, my bmw keeps disconnecting even when the phone or the key are actually inside the car. there are bits of my previous car that i liked more, and that's all down to the newer technology that seems to be standard now, whereas i preferred the earlier setup. the actual drive and handling are excellent, and the fuel economy is fantastic for the cheaper journeys around town. but in my opinion the it side needs work, especially the speech control. for example, on my old car i could just say something like "end route guidance" and it understood, but now it only responds properly if you say "end route navigation" exactly. it can't deal with the simpler phrasing, and changing these things with every new car you make bmw is really frustrating.

the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

Customer added that the dealership had said they would call to arrange a visit to the shop to explain how to use everything, but that call has never come. Writer informed Customer that there is a Live Genius at the local dealership and recommended Customer contact them to schedule a time to sit in the car together and review all the features. Customer confirmed they prefer the Fairfax dealership because it is near their home. Customer then asked if Korean language support would be available for that experience. Writer clarified that an interpreter can be provided for phone support, but was not certain if an interpreter would be available on-site at the dealership while sitting in the vehicle. Writer offered to bring in an interpreter for the current phone discussion to answer questions. Customer responded that they would rather go directly to the dealership in person.

Customer stated they feel overwhelmed by the amount of features. Writer offered assistance, but customer stated they do not have any questions right now because they do not use the vehicle often and it will not be their daily car. Writer acknowledged and advised that our contact details are available in the MY BMW app. Customer acknowledged.

the interior feels like a step down from the previous model in both materials and equipment.

no full leather on the dash, no stitched leather on the center of the steering wheel, and there are a lot of hard plastics. the door cards look low quality, with the lower section being hard plastic.
there is no climate control for rear passengers and no led screen back there.
the sides where your knees rest should be soft leather like before.

front seats no longer have back pockets,
the door sill is missing and there is no soft close door.

overall the cabin comes across as cheap and not fitting for a car priced above about 90k.

this car ticks almost all the boxes for me. the key thing is that it is genuinely fun to drive. on top of that, the purchase price felt competitive and the overall value for a new car seemed good.

the downside is the complexity of the technology. it is not straightforward to learn, and making it simpler would be a very good objective.

the big negative so far has been getting the driver seat adjusted so i do not end up with serious pain in my lower right back and right knee. i spent hours trying to find a position that worked. my son had to set the seat for me again this week, the second time, and now i can drive for about 30 minutes without pain. i am hoping that will also hold up for my regular 2 hour trips. over the last roughly 35 years i have had teslas and e class mercedes and never ran into this problem. my last mercedes had multi contour seats. my i5 has the upgraded seat package, but i just cannot get it dialed in, there are simply too many adjustments. the current e class mercedes offers an electronic assistant to help the driver find a seat position, and maybe bmw should add something like that too.

overall the car feels basically well built, but the price is still too high for what you actually get. there are several areas where it seems things have been pared back compared to what you would expect as obvious. it is not just about the equipment list you can read through (which you really have to study carefully, because it is very hard to understand exactly what the car has as standard). in terms of perceived quality, for example, the carpet in the boot and the standard radio have clearly been economised, which is far below what you expect from a premium brand. there are also obvious gaps in the standard equipment that ought to be a given and cost nothing, like the fact there is no cigar lighter socket in the trunk. you can see lines in the doors bulging slightly where the inner plate meets the edges, which feels far under the standard you would expect and becomes a daily irritation when you notice it. in the middle of the bonnet you can see a row of marks that look like spot welds from underneath. so in the end i actually regret buying it, even though in many ways it is a nice car.

from a driving standpoint the car is excellent. for something this big and heavy the steering and handling feel sharp, and the suspension doesn't beat you up. acceleration is exactly what you'd expect from an ev with this much power, really strong. tech is also impressive, nicely integrated and straightforward to use.

where it falls short is in materials and missing features for what it costs. no massaging seats, no soft close doors, no leather dash, no led skylounge roof, and the ambient light bar doesn't continue into the rear. some of the plastics look cheap, and i really wish there was at least a bit of stitching on the doors or dashboard to make it feel more upscale. coming out of an x5 and before that a g30, this does feel like a step down, even though everything is screwed together very tightly.

i've been driving a 530 for more than 9 years now. the last 3 were leased, and this 2024 is on a select finance plan. i've had it around 3 months and i still really love the car, but it doesn't feel different enough to justify the much higher payment…about $200 more every month. the sticker price of the car is basically the same as the previous one, which seems crazy to me.
one thing i really valued before was the run flat tires, and now that feature is gone. also, on the last 3 cars i never once got a computer error, but on this one i had an engine malfunction warning in under 2 months, which really scared me. luckily it turned out to be just a glitch that needs a computer update, and i'm getting that done this week.
the ride is still fantastic and i really like the big screen. so giving it an "8" feels about right.

this is my 3rd bmw. i went to tesla in 2022 because i got tired of dropping about $90 every time i filled the gas tank. i'm really glad bmw came out with electric models. i have no plans to go back to tesla, bmw build quality feels clearly better. the i5 drives so smoothly and quietly, the audio system is excellent, and the comfort plus cornering are just fantastic. the only thing i miss is a "dog mode" like my tesla had. hopefully bmw can add some kind of auto pilot through an update and move toward autonomous driving one day, or close to it.

my i5m60 is a fantastic car overall. but i do have four complaints. 1) it's really priced too high. you do get a lot of car, yet there's zero discount for choosing an electric. 2) when ordering, i couldn't configure it with anything except summer tires, which is a silly setup for anything but a pure sports car. i've put winter tires on now, but for summer i'd much rather run all-season radials that deal with water better and fit the character of the car more. 3) the removal of physical buttons, like just having a simple switch for the heated steering wheel, is irritating. i honestly hope the eu forces bmw to reverse that choice. 4) in assisted driving the car tends to oversteer on lane changes and then has to correct itself.
i'm a big fan of the bluetooth access, and there are a lot of other things i really like too!

with this purchase i had very high expectations of the bmw brand. choosing the 530i online edition through bmw financial lease was something i thought would make us into long-term brand customers, not just one-time consumers. right now though, i am facing serious inconvenience when using android auto. we keep having the same problem where music will not play correctly when starting tmap or other navigation apps, and it is not a random glitch but a recurring, structural issue. this is clearly not just my own case either. the same complaints are constantly coming up in major communities, such as a large online cafe called 'bmw driver club' (around 650,000 members), and even though many users are reporting the same inconvenience, bmw has provided no official explanation of the cause, no plan for improvement, and no proper guidance for customers. the issue itself matters, but the way bmw is handling it feels even more disappointing. these customer inconveniences have been building up for a long time, and i think the lack of active response and communication is something that can really damage trust in a premium brand. in my view, a premium brand is defined not only by how complete its products are, but also by how it reacts when problems come up. in the present situation, trust in the brand is inevitably shaken, even if the vehicle itself is satisfying. i feel that a clear analysis of the cause, a concrete improvement plan, and formal guidance to customers are absolutely needed. instead of treating it as just a minor technical error, i strongly ask for a proactive response that looks at the whole customer experience. my survey score here is not only showing dissatisfaction, but also my expectation that bmw will improve. i hope this point is considered very carefully.

it is a really good car and the service i get from you has always been reliable. at the same time you can tell it is a fresh model, there are some small details that get a bit irritating:

1. the plastic cover you take off at a fast charger ends up swinging and knocking against the body when it is windy, it could really use some kind of simple holder so it stays put while charging.

2. the front passenger seat belt tends to tap against the b-pillar while driving, which creates an annoying knocking noise.

3. the choice for whether the car should beep when locking/unlocking keeps disappearing and i have already had to switch those beeps off four times, even though i have only had the car around 3 months.

4. the charging cable supplied with the car is too short, since the car is quite long and many chargers make you drive straight in, it would help a lot if the cable was roughly 1-1.5 meters longer.

overall the car is very nice, but i'm not a fan of losing all the buttons and knobs and having to dig through the computer to find things. auto start/stop should either be gone or at least have a way to turn it off permanently. the fact there is no automatic mode for the fan speed, so you have to keep adjusting it by hand in an 85k car, is hard to accept. the build quality in general could be better. older bmw models had a solid, satisfying "clunk" when you closed the door, but now it sounds much more tinny and lightweight. the details show the quality, and small defects jump out, like plastic pieces that don't quite fit right or don't completely wrap around what they are supposed to.

my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

no proper gear shifter, just that goofy little switch, and the controls are a pain to work with. half the settings don't stay put after i shut off the ignition. the retractable steering wheel doesn't slide back by itself when i turn the car off and open the door. ac won't hold the recirc setting, it changes once the car is turned off, same annoyance. also really dumb that the engine "off" at stops got deleted. the on/off button is crammed next to other buttons so you might kill the engine at the wrong time. simple buttons would do a better job for changing drive modes than that silly dial and the touch screen. the car feels too bulky and wide, which makes parking more of a chore. in sport mode the mpg drops from about 34 to around 28, yet the sport mode doesn't feel all that spirited. the sport seat hugging you is fantastic but it only happens in sport mode. cleaning the windshield is awkward because the wipers don't pull away far enough. the warning system for people approaching the car from any direction isn't sensitive enough, so i have to stare around a lot more. 

the good bits are the automatic backup feature, really useful given how big the car is, and the b & w stereo, miles better than the karmon-hardin setup, plus this one came with normal tires instead of run flats! that sport seat wrap that grabs you is excellent, just a shame it only "shows up" in sport mode.

i'm pleased overall but not as thrilled as i thought i would be. a few small tweaks would really help.

air conditioned seats: i can tell the car not to turn on seat heat by default, but i can't do the same for the cooling. having a cold butt is uncomfortable for me, i don't want it at all and end up switching it off every single drive. on hot days that makes me dislike the car a bit.

- garage door openers: with such a smart car, it should use geofencing to automatically open gates and garage doors as you arrive. my old model s did that and it was extremely convenient.

- alarm: again with geofencing, the car should be able to stay unlocked and disarmed automatically when parked at home. not for everyone, but it would be easy to add as a menu option so in a safe garage you don't risk setting off the alarm or hunting for a key to open the trunk.

one-pedal driving: i use aggressive energy recovery and really like it, but i'd prefer if it brought the car all the way to a stop instead of continuing to creep.

auto hold: when auto hold releases in traffic or at lights, even with a very gentle press on the pedal the car snaps out of the hold and lurches slightly. it's annoying and should be much smoother.

on the positive side, the audio system and in-car phone are excellent. i especially value the speakerphone performance.

for an ev it truly still handles like a bmw, and i'm glad for that.

the car is very comfortable to sit in and drive, and the handling is quite responsive. i haven't had a vehicle this large for many years, but this one drives and turns almost like a smaller car. the acceleration is excellent, and i don't feel any need for the m version's extra power. the suspension is also excellent, which makes every ride enjoyable, though i'd prefer an air suspension like i've experienced in the audi q8 etron or what bmw offers on the i7. the range is very good, but with the limited fast charging along my usual routes to nj on the delmarva peninsula, i find myself wishing it could go more like 450-500 miles; for long out-of-state trips we rely on a gas vehicle. for driving around virginia the range works fine and is better than my previous ev, the vw id4. the technology in this car can be overwhelming, but i'm learning it and the infotainment bit by bit. it feels solid on the road, always composed and responsive. i do miss a spare tire, and the idea of using the provided flat repair system worries me since i've never done that before; it might help if the dealer walked me through it so i'd feel less anxious. overall, i really enjoy being behind the wheel of this car, it's the best i've owned.

Customer stated the vehicle is very enjoyable behind the wheel and she is really liking the overall driving feel of her new BMW.

1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function.

in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate.

the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues.

i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix.

2. homelink garage door opener
the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then.

most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.

the car's handling is good, but with these new electric motors the instant power delivery can make it twitch side to side, almost like it's losing grip briefly on one side, for just a split second when launching hard from a stop (compared with my 2023 m5). traction control feels too intrusive unless you turn it off. performance aside, the styling and comfort are hard to beat. the downside is that practically everything is buried in menus, so even simple things take several steps, which gets annoying. lately i've been using voice commands to jump straight to what i need in the menus. overall it's a great car, and i strongly recommend it to friends when they ask about it.

i've been driving a 530 for more than 9 years now. the last 3 were leased, and this 2024 is on a select finance plan. i've had it around 3 months and i still really love the car, but it doesn't feel different enough to justify the much higher payment…about $200 more every month. the sticker price of the car is basically the same as the previous one, which seems crazy to me.
one thing i really valued before was the run flat tires, and now that feature is gone. also, on the last 3 cars i never once got a computer error, but on this one i had an engine malfunction warning in under 2 months, which really scared me. luckily it turned out to be just a glitch that needs a computer update, and i'm getting that done this week.
the ride is still fantastic and i really like the big screen. so giving it an "8" feels about right.

i really enjoy the overall driving environment, but the storage space frustrates me. my previous car was a 2012 528i, and with the back seats folded it had almost station-wagon-like room. this 530i is a letdown in that regard: the trunk is smaller and the pass-through is narrower, so larger items are harder to carry. on top of that, there is no bmw or oem trailer hitch option, which means we can't take our bikes unless i risk damaging the sky lounge roof or trunk lid with a bike rack. the online bmw configurator also confused me, and i ended up thinking both the 530i and 540i had a hybrid electric motor to boost mileage and performance. if i had known the difference, i probably would have chosen the 540i.

overall the experience has been very positive, the tech feels solid and the highway "self-driving" is much better than the last generation. i would like finer control over the sport mode settings. i also want clearer guidance on how to use the engine when coming off battery mode, including proper warm up time. on long drives, i'd like to hold back some battery for later while still using a bit during the trip for boost, but the current programming does not seem to support that. i realize that means more complexity and instructions, but i think many bmw owners are fine with that, and i want to get the most out of how the battery and engine work together. i came from an n63, now with a b58, and while i know they are different, the b58 sometimes sounds like it's really working even when i'm not revving it much. is that extra sound being pumped in, and is that really what i want to be hearing? i'd rather hear a confident engine than one that sounds like it's straining. also, instead of having to pay for an esim subscription, why can't the car just use my phone's hotspot for things like the youtube app.

i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

1. i paid extra for the remote parking option, but it often refuses to work. out of 10 attempts it seems to fail about half the time. especially in tight spaces it just won't allow remote parking at all, whether that's because of a sensor error or something else. honestly, i'd like to get my money back for this feature.

2. the body size is bigger than a mercedes-benz e-class or an audi a6, which makes it inconvenient when trying to park or drive through narrow streets. if the body is that large, the cabin should feel more spacious, but the interior doesn't really seem any bigger.

3. the hazard light button is a touch type, so you can't easily tell if it has actually been pressed. when you're in a rush, it's hard to switch it on, which raises the chance of an accident.

4. the bsi engine oil change interval is too long. i'd prefer replacing it every year or at around 15,000 km, but they set it at 20,000 km. trying to save money like that just seems like it will hurt people's impression of how durable the car is.

5. as soon as you approach the vehicle, the side mirrors fold out, which makes it awkward to squeeze between cars in a cramped parking lot. it would be better if the mirrors only opened when the door is actually opened or once the driver gets in.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

overall it is an outstanding car. there are just a couple of things that really feel like cost cutting, and i honestly do not get why those choices were made. the biggest one is that the car cannot acclimatize while on the ice and instead will only use the main hybrid battery, which makes absolutely no sense. it comes across like somebody just did not bother to push the right software update. that behavior also hurts the practicality for people who commute. you are forced to drive in a way that saves enough of the main battery so you can still use the acclimatization settings before your next trip.

the other irritation is that you cannot unlock the car using the rear passenger door handles. at close to $80,000, it feels like they could have added two more touch sensors to make locking and unlocking simpler. overall the experience is great, but there are definitely a few things that make you wonder if they were driven by engineering or by a bean counter.

Customer stated the car was sold to them as a hybrid, but in actual use it runs purely on electric power for an initial number of miles and then, once that range is depleted, which happens within the same day if they drive more than about 30 miles, it switches over to using only gas. Writer advised that this model is indeed a hybrid and includes a specific hybrid mode. Writer advised that in the Driving settings the drive mode can be set to hybrid drive so the vehicle operates in hybrid drive for the current journey. Writer advised that when navigation is active, the anticipatory hybrid mode engages to manage electric energy optimally, so the vehicle can drive electrically along the navigation route in city areas and close to the destination. Writer advised that if the high-voltage battery has sufficient charge, further parts of the route will be allocated to electric driving.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

this is my 5th bmw vehicle.
all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:
550i
540i
740i
550i
now a 530i
i realize i am now in the regular 5 series, which i chose because, in my view, quality and functionality have gone backwards overall. that is not just about this 530 compared to those older cars.
my issues are:
run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series
2) air conditioning feels downgraded and not strong enough for south texas heat
3) ac/vent fan is too noisy except on the lowest level. with the fan high, you basically cant talk on the phone.
4) auto stop/start, but the driver does not have simple, effective full control to switch it off.
5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced
6) not enough storage. the small latched compartment by the driver is gone, there is a phone charging pad instead of extra storage depth (should be removable), and the glove box is limited and does not work well.
7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

spending around £128k on a car and then being asked to pay extra for a heated steering wheel is ridiculous. i've owned bmws for many years and this one will be my last. i lodged a complaint with bmw and they did not actually address it at all. to me it's simple: this is a bmw, not some brand that should be pushing paid "add ons" on a £128k car.
i even cancelled my order for the updated i7, which was about £146k. bmw eventually added the heated steering wheel to my current car for free, but that completely misses the point. if i wanted cheap junk with chargeable extras, i'd go to a cheap brand instead. meanwhile, mercedes s class includes a heated steering wheel at no extra cost, thank you very much.
so congratulations to whoever thought tacking on another £100 for that option was a smart move. right now i have 3 bmws in the household, and every one of them will be replaced by a mercedes.

1. it makes no sense not to have a sunglass holder. my old 740 had one, and in about three months with this car i've already broken two pricey pairs of sunglasses because of this bad design.
2. the app is moody and only seems to work when it feels like it, which is extremely irritating. i plug the car in, ride the garage elevator down, then the office tower elevator up, and the app tells me the car isn't charging. so i head back down the office building, up the garage elevator to the car, and it actually is charging. then i go back down the garage elevator, up the high rise again to my office, call bmw assist, and they say i have to return to the car to troubleshoot…meaning sitting in a hot garage while they poke around and doing the elevator shuffle twice more. forget it…click…that was me ending the call.
3. the air conditioning layout is very unfriendly to use.

the car itself drives well, but there are some things that are just not acceptable, especially the sunglasses issue you've been hearing about for years. if the next one shows up without a sunglass holder, my time at that dealer will be very short before i walk out. the charging quirks are a nuisance and waste my time, so i'll probably just end up guessing when it's actually done charging.

the car drives nicely, is comfy, engine feels strong and the steering is quite light, but getting used to all the touchscreen tech is a nightmare. the previous idrive setup was almost perfect and should have been left alone. for example, getting the preset radio stations back onto the display is almost impossible, and being forced to use a touchscreen while driving is a dangerous distraction. there is no proper written owners manual, just loads of videos, which is disappointing as even a simple booklet would have helped. not being able to choose run flat tyres is a step backwards, and with no spare tyre that could be dangerous.

the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.
