i would really have liked the option of a manual gearbox, and that would have pushed my rating higher, but as with many brands it seems bmw no longer offers this to buyers. overall the car is great fun to drive when you are not manoeuvring. a few small niggles: still no intermittent setting for the windscreen wipers when they are not in auto mode; the driver seatbelt cannot be adjusted for height so i am always fiddling with it while driving; the driver seat could go lower to give extra headroom when getting in; software updates wipe out settings, especially autohold being turned on. before purchase i would have appreciated a brochure clearly listing the equipment on each model so i could compare, and when reading the handbook, to know whether my car is supposed to have a given feature. also, comfort access does not include foot boot opening even though it was shown in the app before delivery.

i've been driving bmws for more than 20 years and the move away from physical switches feels like going backwards. having to look off the road to change things seems unsafe to me. the car often ignores what i say when i try to use voice control. parking in tight spots is a pain, it keeps cutting out and stopping, so it doesnt feel as manageable as my other cars, even the automatics. the electric help when parking tends to surge, and on a small slope it is hard to drive off smoothly. my garage is narrow and uphill, and i have to creep in very slowly, but the way it surges and then cuts out makes that awkward. i have to press the accelerator to get the parking brake to release and then it leaps forward. i do actually like the car, but these parking problems kind of take the shine off it for me.

from placing the order to getting the car, the delivery was far quicker than with my previous bmws, which was a nice surprise. my recent bmws have all been diesel, so finding the 1 series f70 only offered as petrol was rather disappointing. the car itself runs well and i am gradually getting used to operating system 9. i really do not like the lack of a paper handbook, as the built-in version is very hit and miss when trying to locate information, whereas the paper one had pictures and was much simpler to navigate. the missing physical auto hold button on the centre console is also strongly felt, especially after the last software update wiped the on screen setting, leaving you either holding the brake or messing with the selector switch.

compared with my prior 118i (2022), the overall quality has clearly stepped up, especially inside the cabin and in the improved performance. externally it also looks noticeably better and seems more balanced than before. moving to standard active suspension is a real improvement and really should have been on the earlier version. the electronics now give far more ways to customise the car, but getting to those settings often means endless menu scrolling, and the handbook is not particularly clear in places. the updated lighting setup is a real bonus, with auto dip and corner lighting. taken together, this car gives me a better driving experience than my last one.

our last car was an audi a3, only about two years old, and in every respect the 120 m sport tops it. the build quality inside and out, the fuel economy, the performance and the handling are all better. for us this model really hits the sweet spot in the range, the size is exactly right and the price is too. the dealer experience was good as well. we tried a lexus lbx alongside the bmw and while the lexus was packed with tech, the bmw was as full of technology and felt properly exciting with it. the only real negative, which seems common across other makers too, is not having a proper paper handbook any more, which would be much easier to flick through and use than the electronic versions.

i really do not like that so much info is pushed onto the touch screen, it should go back to dials and buttons, much less distracting. you are told not to change things while driving and i agree, the big screen with loads of functions is too distracting on the move. this is my first automatic bmw, all the others i had were manuals, and i was offered a different choice this time. the manual was far better, the auto has a noticeable lag when you try to pull away. visibility from the driver seat is worse than in my older models because of the pillar size. the passenger door mirror used to tilt down when reversing, that was really useful for parking, but it is gone now. i also dislike that you must pay extra for premium functions, and the dealer never pointed that out. the reversing camera is useless.

the car is comfortable and still fun to drive, with light controls, decent performance and good economy, and it clearly shows bmw build quality. i only marked it down from a '10' because the instruments are poor and much harder to read than on my older 325 coupe, which is vastly better laid out and more ergonomic. traditional analogue gauges are far easier to glance at without looking away from the road. the lack of a proper printed handbook also makes figuring out the complicated touch screen more difficult. the on-screen 'keyboard' for entering satnav addresses is definitely better, but the male navigation voice is less clear than the female one on my previous 118. the voice-controlled satnav is a complete waste for us, it simply will not work for either me or my wife.

my new 120 m sport has a nice colour and is a tidy little car. before this i had 5 new 3 series tourings, the last one a 330i m sport which was lovely, and the 120 is not in the same league. i notice the road noise gets quite loud once you are over about 50 mph, which makes the radio hard to hear. i also can't get my i pod to show info on the screen via usb, it only works over bluetooth now. the automatic gearbox doesn't feel as good or as smooth as the 330i's. the tech in this car is very hard to get used to for me as a retired older driver. i asked for an owners manual when the car was delivered but, roughly 3 months later, still haven't had one, first time i've had a new car without a handbook included. the 120 is a strong little car and i'm happy with how it performs. overall i'd give it 7 out of 10.

over more than 30 years i have owned several new bmws, from 4 series through 3 and 2 and now a 1 series, and i am honestly extremely disappointed. very important things that were always included in the purchase price before are now simply left out, clearly just to cut your production costs, yet you still remove quite a few previously 'standard' extras from every series while happily pushing the price up. when i was considering the 1 series nobody bothered to point out that there is no spare wheel and no hand book, both of which i regard as essential items for an owner. i swap my car every 2 or 3 years, but i will not choose bmw again. i feel very very let down.

there are a couple of things i feel i am missing with the car.....a button inside to shut the boot would be ideal, i was honestly shocked that there isn't one. i'd also really like a proper paper handbook, even if it seems old fashioned, because there is so much tech that i'm sure lots of us never really use properly. i dont really know what connected drive actually is, i've just been told it needs renewing soon and right now it just appears like something that will end up costing me more. it would help to have someone explain what happens if i exceed the mileage allowance under the pcp agreement. like most people, i had more questions once i got the car home.....i do think the after sales support, preferably via email, has been very good considering what the car costs, even with everything i've mentioned the car itself is fine. hope this is of use.

from the first drive home from the dealer in my new bmw120 i felt at ease in the car. the seats are excellent, the steering is very precise, and the general feel of the interior is one of quality. the extras that come as standard are very complete. i find bmw idrive straightforward to operate, and the control display always seems to react well to what i do. this is the 5th bmw i have owned and it is the one i enjoy driving the most. only a few gripes: i am unhappy that there is no physical owners manual. i do have a pdf on my laptop and i can use the bmw app for tutorials, but i would still like a paper copy to look at. the material on the door pockets seems lower grade than the rest of the cabin. these are minor issues really, otherwise everything is good!

weve been getting a new 1 series every few years since 2004 and each one has felt like a step up from the last. this latest one is easily the best yet. its our first automatic, and even though ive always claimed manuals were unbeatable, this autobox is amazing. long drives are a pleasure, really relaxing, and in city stop-start traffic its simple to handle. i did more than 6 hours at the wheel in one go to reach where we were heading and could honestly have kept going another 6 hours, it was that comfortable and low stress. the driving position has always been strong, and the new interior is brilliant, puts a grin on my face whenever i get in. the seats are super comfy and the new display is straightforward to use. absolutely love it

last 7 cars were bmws, but because the new 1-series launch was delayed my previous car ended up being a mercedes. very pleased to be back in a bmw! overall i am really happy with this car, so the points below are in that context: 1. first time with an automatic. i also drive my partner's fiat 500ev, and i am a bit disappointed by the slight lag in acceleration. i can get around it by putting it in sport mode ahead of time, but thats not always practical, and it doesnt stack up well against the ev. i havent touched the paddles and doubt i will. 2. the display is limited compared with the mercedes. i cant show consumption, elapsed time and distance driven along with the standard info like i could on the a-class. 3. can't use a usb stick for music. 4. as usual there is more functionality than i will ever need or use, and i am still going through the online manual.

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

bmw refusing to provide a hard copy printed owners handbook with a new car is completely unacceptable. i have no straightforward access to the car's features to help me understand it or sort out the everyday issues that come with any new vehicle. this has ruined my whole experience and i now just use it like an old style basic car, without knowing how to use many of the features i could manage fine with other brands. the selling dealer told me to rely on a computer app, but i'm not a computer person. i was also told i must buy a paper handbook myself, even after paying tens of thousands of pounds sterling for the car. this does nothing to increase my respect for bmw.

my issue is that i find modern technology hard to cope with. it all feels very complicated. it ended up taking about 3 months before i got an owner's handbook, and that only arrived after i kept on at the dealer repeatedly. it had been 11 years since i last bought a bmw, so a lot has changed. i found not having a traditional handbrake quite frightening. if i had received the handbook on the first day, that would have been far more useful. i did consider a mercedes a class, but the privacy glass in the rear window put me off. the staff at bmw wakefield were helpful. the difficulty was that i was so overwhelmed by all the new functions that it stopped me from truly enjoying the new car. the reception desk at wakefield and the parking attendant are both really good. i am beginning to like the car more now, but i still feel slightly scared of it. younger relatives would probably love it.

i would tell family and friends to buy this car because of the build quality, the styling, the performance and the comfortable drive. but as an older person, i find the controls far too high tech and i struggle with them, and i would have liked more traditional manual control options. the "hey bmw" command responds for some functions but not others, which makes it harder, and the menu structure is overly complicated and not user friendly. the controls were shown to me when i bought the car by an excellent salesperson who was younger and very familiar with the high tech system, but it was simply too much to take in at once. looking back, if i had realised how advanced and complex the controls were, i would not have chosen this vehicle.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

title: G60 Electric Range
requirement_statement: Improve 'Electric Range' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 61 respondents complain and 34 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: for a car on a newly developed model platform, the range should have been much better. i have to drive very slowly to get a sensible distance between charges, even for 30- to 40-mile round trips, which means lots of stops. i also find it a bit stingy that with a car in this price class, basically fully equipped, you still have to buy subscriptions for things like remote parking (parking ass. prof.), welcome light animation, etc. some are one-off payments, others tie you into an annual contract period. on top of that, it wasn't really clear that these features weren't actually included when you buy the equipment packages. apart from that, it's an absolutely fantastic car, but the high weight is a small minus, because it would have been even more fun if it were at least 200-300 kg lighter

Customer stated the car suits their 20-mile daily commute well and works with their home charging arrangement.
comfortable ride with a nice electric range.
Customer stated the driving range is good.
Customer stated the hybrid range is actually greater than what was advertised and expressed total joy with how the hybrid system performs.

Customer stated the vehicle is only getting around 100 miles of range on a full charge, which is much lower than what they expected. Customer charges the car overnight at home to 100 percent using a BMW charger that is also used for their iX, and confirmed it still only shows about 100 miles of range after an overnight charge. Customer mentioned their son also drives this vehicle and has reported the same low range. Customer owns two other electric vehicles, a BMW iX and a Mercedes EQE, and stated both of those have very good range, so the i5 range issue stands out. Customer expressed this is a serious problem and said the range is very bad. Writer explained the range should normally be around 250 to 270 miles and agreed that 100 miles is very low. Writer acknowledged this is not the customer's first EV and that they appear to be charging properly. Writer recommended the customer bring the vehicle to the dealership as soon as possible for diagnosis to find out what is causing the low range.
im generally very happy, but in winter the electric range maybe isnt the greatest. some options are hard to find again in the menus.
im generally very happy, but in winter the electric range maybe isnt the greatest. some options are hard to find again in the menus.
Customer stated the range is actually better than what was quoted, averaging about 3.4-4 kw/hour.

i'm really unhappy with the range, and with this limitation on how many times you can fast charge in a 24 hour period. on top of that, bmw has basically said nothing about it, which is very disappointing.
Customer stated the plug-in system works very well for local driving around Greenville and that they use purely electric power for their daily commutes, which fits their needs perfectly.

Customer stated he is worried about how the range is estimated. Customer stated he drove a 100 mile round trip into the city and back home. Customer stated the car showed roughly 200 miles of range at departure and less than 60 miles remaining once he got back. Customer stated he used efficient mode only for part of the drive home because he began to doubt if there was enough charge to reach his house. Customer stated the average outside temperature was about 32-35 degrees. Customer stated he did not precondition the vehicle before leaving, but the car was kept in his garage overnight. Customer stated the dealership did not clearly explain how to get the best range, and that this is his first electric vehicle.

Writer advised the figure in the instrument cluster is only an estimate. Writer advised that range is affected by climate control usage, driving style, charging behavior, weather, road terrain, and some other variables. Writer advised that preconditioning the vehicle on a cold day will provide a much more accurate range prediction. Writer advised that heating the vehicle up to optimal temperature consumes a lot of battery power, and that not just the cabin but also the battery itself must be warmed to operate efficiently.
car is nice, comfy to ride in, and the battery range is good even in winter, about 7 mil or so. luggage space is much better than my previoos 5series hybrid cannon car

it is about as close as you can get to an electric car that still doesnt really appear or feel like an ev. the whole premium feel is intact. the range, though, really has to be improved, right now it is simply not good enough. on top of that there are some irritating design details. 1. the seat belts bang into plastic if you dont consciously pull them fully up. 2. the small hooks in the trunk for groceries cant actually hold a bag handle. 3. the door handles are oddly placed, so people who dont know the car cant locate them in the dark. 4. the trunk lid needs a very firm pull to shut correctly, which again is hard for people unfamiliar with the car. 5. since clever is a major player in denmark, it is pretty frustrating that their charging card isnt integrated in the infotainment, so the charging guidance is basically unusable in denmark. supposedly that will be sorted.

Customer stated he was puzzled that the range display shows different mileage estimates at 100% charge depending on where the car is charged. Customer stated that when charging on the road at an Electrify America supercharger, the screen indicates 307 miles at 100% charge. Customer stated that when charging to 100% at home, the display shows 259 or sometimes 270 miles. Customer stated he does not understand why a full charge would result in different range readings. Writer explained that the range estimate reflects how the vehicle has been driven previously. Writer explained the number continually adjusts based on factors like freeway versus city use, air conditioning or heating, driving efficiency, and other conditions. Writer explained that the system tries to predict the miles available from the current charge using past driving data. Customer acknowledged the explanation and stated this was the only issue he wanted to ask about.

i switched from an x4m competition over to a 5 series, expecting it to feel more luxurious. instead, i realized that a lot of the newer bmws are using more plastics where older cars had premium materials, and bmw was never really known for that before. i also dont like that i cant open or lock the rear door with the convenience feature, while the front passenger doors still have it. in the past couple of generations the back doors always had this option. i saw that there is no illuminated door sill anymore, and the new idrive knob does not work as nicely as the older versions. there are no physical controls for adjusting the temperature either. the steering wheel buttons are missing functions compared with previous models. on top of that, there are no visible exhaust tips, so it doesnt look sporty. the hybrid system itself is good, but the electric range is only about 40km and it takes a long time to charge it back up fully.

the driving experience is very impressive, and nearly all our local town trips are now done purely on electric. only when we travel out of town do we use the 20ltr petrol engine together with the electric power, and we are getting an excellent 60 miles on electric. very happy with it so far.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

title: G60 Seats
requirement_statement: Improve 'Seats' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 53 respondents complain and 44 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: pros: front seat is wider than i thought, very convenient and clean with no oil smell, comfy ride, nice design. cons: touch-style emergency button is hard to press if the screen has dirt, rear seat angle cannot be adjusted so that is inconvenient, and buffer speed is slower than i expected

I had a serious problem with Seat materials scuff/soil easily: "The seats seem to stain kind of easily and I'm not really sure how I'm supposed to clean them. If something wet is on the seat, it leaves residue that builds up there. I don't even have kids anymore to worry about messes, it's just from sitting and any wetness on the seats."

the interior feels like a step down from the previous model in both materials and equipment.

no full leather on the dash, no stitched leather on the center of the steering wheel, and there are a lot of hard plastics. the door cards look low quality, with the lower section being hard plastic.
there is no climate control for rear passengers and no led screen back there.
the sides where your knees rest should be soft leather like before.

we have been buying bmw cars for at least twenty years and i always feel very safe in them. i drive about 25 miles or so every day and usually replace the car every three years. this one is very comfortable and the visibility is excellent, which is one of my essential requirements. i really like the white interior, but it is not as nice as my last car where everything inside was light cream, so i was very disappointed. i even went to look at mercedes and audi to compare their interiors and was actually about to write the deposit cheque for a mercedes before changing my mind. learning all the new systems like the heating is taking me a while, probably because i am seventy one. we prefer a spacious car with good room for passengers. the boot is big and the saloon feels very secure as we travel often and do not want anything left visible. i also wonder why you removed the sleeves on the backs of the front seats, now there is no storage there.

this car ticks almost all the boxes for me. the key thing is that it is genuinely fun to drive. on top of that, the purchase price felt competitive and the overall value for a new car seemed good.

the downside is the complexity of the technology. it is not straightforward to learn, and making it simpler would be a very good objective.

the big negative so far has been getting the driver seat adjusted so i do not end up with serious pain in my lower right back and right knee. i spent hours trying to find a position that worked. my son had to set the seat for me again this week, the second time, and now i can drive for about 30 minutes without pain. i am hoping that will also hold up for my regular 2 hour trips. over the last roughly 35 years i have had teslas and e class mercedes and never ran into this problem. my last mercedes had multi contour seats. my i5 has the upgraded seat package, but i just cannot get it dialed in, there are simply too many adjustments. the current e class mercedes offers an electronic assistant to help the driver find a seat position, and maybe bmw should add something like that too.

even though i love how the car handles, there are a few things you took away that my 2021 had and i just don't get why. you removed the pockets on the back of the seats. maybe that cut production costs, but without those pockets i have to dump stuff like umbrellas and the kids' things on the rear floor. the worst part, and honestly a deal breaker when my lease is up, is the trunk size. i can't fit my grandchild's stroller in there, or a full food shop, or my mother's walker. i also dislike the silver/chrome 5s on the rear windows, it's a luxury vehicle and i don't need it shouting that it's a 5 series. the glove box is smaller now, same with the door wells, and i really don't like that i can't leave anything in the console tray since i'm no longer able to cover it. i'm forced to look away from the road to manage the controls because the knobs are gone and everything is flat. with the fan vents hidden and streamlined, i can't adjust the airflow direction anymore. i could keep going, but i'm sure the team who came up with this very modern car is pleased with what they made. for me, if these things aren't changed by the time my lease ends, i'll most likely move to another luxury brand. i genuinely hope you take this feedback on board. when i checked reviews afterwards, i saw these issues weren't just mine, a lot of people felt the same way. i really believe i'm exactly the kind of customer you target, so i hope you treat my comments seriously. my whole family drives bmws and nobody from about 35 to 70 is happy with the new design. it feels very clunky and not sleek anymore. i've already told my sales person all of this. again, i hope you truly take in and value my feedback.
anna kerr

i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

the apps built into the car really ought to be reachable from the phone, so you don't have to sit in the car and fiddle with them - you can do that in a mercedes, which was my previous car. the windows also can't be closed via the app, while mercedes manages that. if they could close themselves automatically when it rains, like mercedes does, i haven't found any sign that they do, but they should. the car has locked me out several times when i've left either the phone or the keys inside. settings in the app like folding the mirrors when locking don't actually work when it's other users, even though the option is set in the app. my wife is forced to type in a pin code and can't just pick her id, supposedly because of the risk that her phone might be stolen - but the primary user's phone can be stolen too, so that explanation doesn't make sense. the information shown in the dashboard is poor no matter which view you choose. the radio will not receive a signal while i'm driving through the limfjord tunnel, which i go through every day, and that's something i've never run into with any other car i've owned. the winter range is deeply reprehensible and honestly my biggest complaint: no more winter holiday trips, because the real range on the motorway at 130 kmh in frost is at most about 250 km. well, i guess i have to stop somewhere, but i'm left disappointed. mvh mads

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

to me this car really shows off german engineering. all the little touches, like the crystal seat adjustment, the different massage choices, all the voice and touch controls and the whole layout are fantastic. the only thing i question is the nav. when you get close to a turn it switches to a big live image of the road and those arrows keep expanding, which i find very distracting. i preferred the nav in my previous 750 that just counted down to the turn with a small picture instead of the full camera view. apart from that, i honestly have nothing to complain about.

Customer stated his car has been sitting in the dealer's service department since around 1/8, and it has basically been out of his hands this whole time. Customer stated the dealer, while running remote diagnostic checks, picked up an issue with the air and fuel mixture. Customer stated the store still does not have a clear answer on what is actually causing that air/fuel mixture problem. Customer stated he only noticed the check engine light turning on, and besides that he did not feel anything odd in the way the vehicle was driving. Customer stated the car had about 560 miles on it when he dropped it at the dealership, and now, while it is in their possession, the odometer shows roughly 902 miles. Customer stated he has no idea when he is going to get the vehicle back from the dealer.

Update from roughly 2/5/25:
Customer stated his overall experience with this vehicle so far has been poor. Customer stated the car has been tied up in service for around 24 days. Customer stated that when the vehicle only had about 100 miles, the Check Engine Light came on for the first time. Customer stated his service technician believed the concern was related to the O2 sensors. Customer stated that when the dealership contacted BMW engineering for support, engineering did not want to approve replacing those sensors at that stage and instead told service to clear the fault codes and have the customer drive the car more to see if the Check Engine Light would return. Customer stated the light did in fact come back on, and he then had to bring the vehicle back into the service department. Customer stated he ended up driving about 800 extra miles with the Check Engine Light illuminated. Customer stated that eventually service replaced the O2 sensors to resolve the issue. Customer stated they were also told the vehicle might require a software update if the Check Engine Light comes back again. Customer stated the way BMW handled the troubleshooting has been very frustrating and that BMW needs to listen more closely to what the technician on the ground is recommending. Customer stated that the second trip into service could have been avoided if BMW had listened to the technician who was diagnosing the car the first time. Writer asked how the vehicle has behaved since he picked it up after the repair. Customer stated he has had the car back for about a week and it is running OK, but he is still worried the check engine light might reappear.
Service Notes:
Mileage: 1,254
Defect Code: 1178031500
Defect Description:
Oxygen monitor sensor permanent malfunction
Complaint:
CLIENT STATES "CHECK ENGINE"/ "SERVICE ENGINE SOON" / "MIL" WARNING LIGHT IS ON.
Cause:
.PERFORMED VEHICLE TEST. ATTACHED BATTERY CHARGER. FOUND FC 034ABA HAD RETURNED. REOPENED TSARA [CASE_NO].
Correction:	
TSARA ADVISED TO REPLACE THE FAULTY OXYGEN SENSOR. REPLACED BANK 1 POST CAT O2 SENSOR. CLEARED ADAPTATIONS AND FAULTS. TEST DROVE VEHICLE. FAULT HAS NOT RETURNED, OK AFTER REPAIR.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

i have only had my bmw for a few months and already ran into several issues:
i) at just under 1,100 miles the check engine light came on, and i had to leave the car at the bmw dealer in portville so they could fix a part that had dropped into the air intake, gotten stuck there, and was making the engine run too hot.
ii) later the rear passenger seat belt got jammed up and tangled inside the retract system, so the vehicle had to go back to the same bmw dealer for repair and for them to reinstall the belt.
iii) this morning when i got in, i noticed a crack in the glass roof; i have reached out to the bmw dealer and am now waiting for an appointment to bring it in for that repair.

in just these few months the car will have been in the shop 3 times :(

i have a 750e 2026, and this is my second 7 series model. from the very first day, the car has been making a repeating knocking sound from the right rear passenger side, very much like the automatic door lock noise (da-da). the dealership has been supportive, understanding, and professional while trying to track it down, and they have traced it to a valve that is supposed to push gas vapors toward the engine when a certain buildup level is reached.
this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

this car was delivered on pirelli high-performance tires that made the ride far too harsh for a luxury sedan. i ended up paying myself to swap to oem-spec bridgestone turanza 6s, which transformed the comfort, and tire choice really should be sorted at the factory for customers who care about refinement.

the 48v mild-hybrid start/stop is still quite rough. compared to other isg/bsg systems from different brands, and to my 2024 530i with a belt starter generator, the restart from a standstill is abrupt and gives a noticeable jolt even when holding the brake, and it can feel coarse as the car comes to a stop. that takes away from the premium driving experience, especially when mercedes and range rover have virtually imperceptible stop/start.

on top of that, ota software updates arrive very late, which is disappointing versus other luxury makers. more timely updates would really help the overall ownership experience.

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

Connected charger & perf veh test & submitted FASTA data for TSARA 3053430. R&i full-flow oil filter. Cleaned oil contaminated under panels and insulation. Road tested vehicle and verified repairs. Leak eliminated. Used 1 gallon coolant.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.

with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

2024 bmw 760i, to me, is a true mix of power and elegance. as a proud owner of the 2024 bmw 760i, it's hard not to be drawn in by how commanding it looks out on the road. the sleek exterior and the luxurious cabin make this flagship sedan feel like it radiates power and sophistication.

there's a real sense of empowerment that comes with driving something so prestigious. my wife, who is 5 foot 2 and around 100 pounds, is especially taken with the way the 760i carries itself. for her, it isn't just about the car's size, it's about feeling like she's in charge of the road and in control of a serious machine.

for her it goes beyond simple transportation; it's a statement, a way of showing her presence and capability. the 760i lives up to that, with strong performance from its potent engine and advanced tech features that give real confidence behind the wheel. whether we're weaving through city streets or cruising the highway, every trip feels like a small victory.

of course, people see a car like this differently. some might think it's about a "look-at-me" syndrome, wanting attention or validation. that may be true for some, but for many others a bmw 760i represents the result of hard work and success, a reward for what they've achieved and a symbol of personal accomplishment.

for me the 2024 bmw 760i is far more than just another vehicle; it stands for power, elegance and prestige. even if opinions about what it means vary, one thing is clear to me: it brings a huge amount of joy and satisfaction to anyone lucky enough to live with it every day.

this is my 4th brand-new 7 series and my 10th new bmw. pros: the engine is fantastic, a real beast; the tech is strong; and it drives very well overall.

cons: the hvac could cool better, likely because of the hidden vents, and it only got a bit better after i put clear uv tint on the windows. you also can't set sport mode as the default, even though i drive in sport most of the time. i can't remove the red and blue colors on the display and interactive bar, and i'm not a fan of those colors. the steering feels a little soft and not as connected to the road as my previous cars. it's a big car, and adding about 5" more length wasn't a good thing. the styling is just okay; i actually think my 2017 740i looks better.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

i am happy with the new car. it is clearly more comfortable and in general more interesting than the older series i had. still, there are some drawbacks i really cannot ignore: - once the speed goes past about 110-120 km/h, the car is not well insulated anymore, wind noise becomes obvious and disturbing even though it has the special package. - at night, the driver's main rearview mirror gives a blurry picture, lights from cars behind and strong light sources look smeared, vertical lines show up and this makes driving harder. - the air conditioning will not run when the ignition is switched off. - there is no way to turn off the lights while the car is on (for example if you just want the ac working in a parking lot). - every single time you start driving you have to switch on the battery conservation function again. - the driver has no glove compartment now. before it was located to the left of the steering wheel. there is also no smaller extra glovebox like on the f01. - the driver's joystick/control stick feels very rigid when choosing left/right/up/down. - the driver's seat fails to go back to where it was before the car was shut down. - the cup holders do not offer cooling or heating at all.

this 1 series is my first ever bmw and i'm really impressed with the power, the fuel economy and how comfortable it is. the amount of standard kit is great, and the safety features make me feel confident and are a big help, especially when parking. the seats are extremely comfortable and the cabin is very quiet, so it is a very enjoyable car to drive. the materials used inside feel high quality and the os9 instruments are very detailed with lots of different display options. i would happily recommend the 1 series and i expect to stay with bmw for many years.

I had a 118i m sport before and the 120 m sport has had all the useful bits stripped out and is not a sport model at all! this is our 6th bmw and easily the worst car we've ever had. 1. no 12v socket in the boot, a ridiculous penny pinching move. 2. no phone charging points in the back. 3. no climate controls in the rear. 4. no fog lights. 5. no leather seats. 6. no visible exhaust, sport model?? 7. basic 18" alloys (19" were standard on the 118i), sport model?? 8. thin, cheap carpets with poor grip and no m sport trim. every one of these came standard on the 118i m sport and the 120 m sport is marketed as its direct replacement! the 120 m sport is about £7/8k more, plus paying again for all the things removed, making it a pricey car and the worst thing ever to come out of a bmw showroom. total rubbish!

this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

i moved down from an m135 drive and the power in this one is still absolutely fine and nicely responsive for everyday driving. i much prefer the battery assisted stop/start setup, and the steering has a nice light feel that firms up as you go faster. i am a bit let down that the i-drive knob has gone, as i always thought that system was brilliant when on the move. the new screens look very smart and, once you have them configured, they work well, and the overall fascia design and materials feel excellent. my f70120 m sport drives and handles really well day to day, and i actually like how it looks more than the f40. the front electric seats are really comfy and offer very precise adjustment. i am enjoying the head-up display, its my first time using one. the sat nav reacts quickly and is really helpful when finding your way around unfamiliar routes and towns. i also really like the 'y' style wheels and the red calipers.

reg dn75jlu goes well and looks very good, but the door panels feel really flimsy, they almost push in when i'm washing it. there is a small rough patch on the inner edge of the front door and i can't tell if it came from the factory like that or if the garage did it when they were preparing it for handover. i'm not happy that there were no printed hand books, i ended up paying just over £70 to get hard copies. i purchased the car from a dealer in northbrook as they offered a strong price, but it's more than 100 miles away so it's been awkward getting the answers i asked for. this is the bmw 1 series 123xdrive m sport and i'm let down there are no m sport seat belts and no m sport badges on the front wings. i would appreciate hearing your reply. many thanks mark turner.

i actually like this new model more than i expected. at first i wasnt keen on the new grille but over time it has grown on me. there is a problem with headroom getting in though, the driver and passengers can bang their heads quite easily on the roof or door frame. you could fit electric front seats that automatically drop when you get out and lift when you get in. there is a delay when switching from drive to reverse, and also a pause or flat spot when pulling away in drive. the rear parcel shelf feels cheap and cheerful, not really bmw quality. i also dont like not having a proper paper manual, im old fashioned and prefer one.

ride comfort is excellent and the power is impressive for a 3-cyl engine. seats are roomy and comfy, and the options are good. road noise is very low for a smaller car, and it compares well to my other car, the m340i, in terms of ride and reduced noise. what we find almost unacceptable is the removal of the gear lever and having nearly everything run through the touchscreen. before, you could start the ventilation with one touch; now you have to aim at the screen twice while driving, which is hard and distracting. all crucial physical buttons need to come back, along with the gear lever. the controls on the previous model were ideal, and it's not clear why they were cut, although it seems obvious it was to save costs.

i really do not like that so much info is pushed onto the touch screen, it should go back to dials and buttons, much less distracting. you are told not to change things while driving and i agree, the big screen with loads of functions is too distracting on the move. this is my first automatic bmw, all the others i had were manuals, and i was offered a different choice this time. the manual was far better, the auto has a noticeable lag when you try to pull away. visibility from the driver seat is worse than in my older models because of the pillar size. the passenger door mirror used to tilt down when reversing, that was really useful for parking, but it is gone now. i also dislike that you must pay extra for premium functions, and the dealer never pointed that out. the reversing camera is useless.

this must be about my 12th bmw and my 3rd 1 series. the driving quality is good and the mini hybrid setup seems to really help with petol consumption. i do miss the bigger boot space though, as the batteries take it up; in the previous one i could put my golf trolley and bag in the back without dropping the seats, now i can't. since i started using the voice function it cuts down how much i need the touch screen and helps me keep my eyes on the road. i have a head up display on this car as on the last, and the way it changed from white to orange when the speed limit was exceeded was useful. the beeping that comes with it is very annoying, and if i turn the beeping off it also stops the orange change on the head up display, which i'd like to keep. there has also been an issue with apple car play and bmw voice.

i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

a really nice small car to drive, but the electrics / electronics have been trouble. one of the driving lights has already failed, meaning it sat 2 days in the workshop. much worse though is the key system. after a lot of work by the agent the car can now be opened and started with the single key or via the app on my wife's iphone. however, unless she keeps changing one function on her app on/off, which is a pain to do all the time, when we both walk up to the car together it cannot tell who is going to drive and regularly sets the seat etc for the wrong person, always following the iphone profile because the iphone seems to send a stronger signal than the key. this has to be fixed!!! it totally spoils how we enjoy the car.

car drives very smoothly, corners well and has enough power. it is quiet and the fuel consumption is good, though it's been mainly motorway use so far. the dashboard looks nice but really isn't practical to operate while driving. the dash lighting reflects in both outer rear view mirrors. the boot is smaller, but in fairness the tank is larger than on my previous 118i m sport, which gives better range. i miss the little storage area on the dash by the steering column. the seats are less comfortable than in my old 118i m sport and the driver's seat is already losing its shape, and i am only just over 12 stone. i also miss having an adjustable back support. the colour is perfect. sadly the car wasn't ordered to my own spec so it has extras i wouldn't normally pay for. i'm not keen on the idea of a trial period for extras and then having to pay to keep them.
