from the first drive home from the dealer in my new bmw120 i felt at ease in the car. the seats are excellent, the steering is very precise, and the general feel of the interior is one of quality. the extras that come as standard are very complete. i find bmw idrive straightforward to operate, and the control display always seems to react well to what i do. this is the 5th bmw i have owned and it is the one i enjoy driving the most. only a few gripes: i am unhappy that there is no physical owners manual. i do have a pdf on my laptop and i can use the bmw app for tutorials, but i would still like a paper copy to look at. the material on the door pockets seems lower grade than the rest of the cabin. these are minor issues really, otherwise everything is good!

i chose the 1 series because i have been driving bmw cars for roughly 35 years. i would have preferred to get another x1, but my budget would not stretch to the price. given my age now and the fact i drive fewer miles, i have found this car very comfortable, especially after raising the seat to give me a higher and better driving position. the engine capacity is about 25% smaller, which worried me at first, but i quickly got used to it and now i barely notice. my concern is that, when i bought the car, nobody mentioned the extra digital upgrade, which seems to be around £12 a month. i am disappointed that the sat nav without this upgrade is quite inferior. i now think the upgrade is expensive and feel rather let down.

hello, this is now my sixth brand new bmw - 2 x 5 series saloons, 2 x 5 series tourers and 1 x r1100s motorbike.  pros: the engine reacts quickly, the suspension really smooths out and deadens the bumps in the road, the exterior styling (it actually looks designed instead of the usual boxes you see), the instantly comfy seats and the curved display.  cons: the tech is fiddly to operate (it needs more big knobs), the supposedly helpful technology just ends up too complicated, the digital manual drowns you in information (a simpler, easy-to-find guide to the main functions would be better), build quality issues (the bonnet only secures on one side, there's no velcro under the bmw front passenger rubber mat), and there is no paper user manual. thanks, roland ross

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

i've only covered around 1500 miles in it so far, so i don't think i've fully decided how i feel about the car yet. up to now though it's been really comfy to sit in, feels dependable and it seems very good on fuel. it did take me a bit of time to work out the whole system and get everything set up how i wanted, and i was pretty irritated when an update came through to the vehicle and wiped all my settings so i had to go back and redo them from scratch. i guess it's not a massive issue, just annoying. the other downside for me is the greasy fingerprints that end up all over the infotainment screen, which stand out a lot, especially when the sun is shining. this is the first bmw i've owned and i was told that it used to be operated with a dial between the front seats, similar to how my last 3 mercedes worked. even so, at the moment it wouldn't put me off buying another bmw. overall it feels like a good all-round car.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

my son bought this car for me to replace my 18 year old mercedes-benz e-class 200 kompressor. we had been waiting quite a while for the new f70 1 series to finally be released. i picked the color i wanted with the matching interior and added a few extras like the electric seats and the electric boot lid. i think it's a pity that a rear armrest is not fitted as standard. none of the bmw new car sales staff seemed to realise that you only get the rear armrest if you order the rear split seats, which are about 175 pounds. with no proper printed brochure and a very basic online brochure, customers really can't be certain how to specify the car themselves. if we had understood that was the way to get the rear armrest, we would have paid the extra.

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.

i am very happy with my bmw 120 m sport. it replaces a previous (f40) 1 series, and the new car is clearly better in styling, engine smoothness and performance, and seating comfort. fuel economy is also much better than the last one, even with the same engine, thanks to the mild hybrid system. i was pleased that the factory order arrived in about 7 weeks, which felt relatively quick.

i really like this car overall, but there are definitely ups and downs.   pros: the way it drives in general; the new style seats are really comfy; and you can feel that classic bmw engineering in every part of this m sport 1 series.    cons: the active-lane-keeping-assistant feels dangerous on narrow roads and on uk cars you can't permanently switch it off. all the tech being buried in the screen menus and not just on a simple button is frustrating; and the turning circle is way bigger than my old mercedes so it needs a lot more steering work.

too many issues
1. the rubber gasket on the rear door, even though it is a new car, was already damaged and leaking.
2. the mirrors on this new car make a squeaky noise whenever opening or closing.
3. the key that should lock the car automatically when you walk away only works maybe 1 time out of 10.
4. the digital display also goes dark: first the navigation screen on the left side blacks out, then the speedometer side goes black while driving.
5.
when that happened, i called the bmw emergency center. they asked if there was a warning light, but with the display black i cant see any warning light.
in the end they said it was fine to keep driving
...
hey, i cant see my speed, but if i get caught they will just say it was my choice to keep going.
6. at the one month check for the water leak (and the squeaking when opening/closing), the auto lock and door mirrors,
even though i mentioned it to the dealer several times, all they did was put oil on the door mirror.
3 days later it is squeaking again!
none of the other problems have improved.
7.
even though its a brand new car, its already been back to the workshop three times.

would i recommend it?? not sure??

(im debating posting this online), but i can see the dealer is at least trying to fix it.
for now just waiting and watching.

i have had this one for about three months now, but i still don't really remember the feeling of sliding in the same model as before. what stands out is how simple it is to control and how it can cruise calmly even when i'm going fast. the price of the car itself feels quite high though. i picked this model because i was willing to pay more in order to get a comfortable drive. originally i chose a 116i f20 for my wife, and the steering on that is outstanding, you can really sense what the driver is feeling. after that, i bought a lexus is as a replacement for a 435i and that was excellent too. then came the 116i m135, which is also strong in power and easy to manage, and now i'm on an x3m competition. i use the m135 around town and the x3mc when i'm going at high speeds.

this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd than a rear-biased 4wd and you can feel torque steer. dashboard controls - getting rid of the physical buttons and burying everything in the touchscreen is awkward and could even be unsafe. the ui has become a nuisance: to switch into sport mode i have to go through several steps, and since the voice control is flaky and i don't want to chat to my car, that's not an option. when using nav i have to 1) hit the mode button on the centre console, 2) pick the mode on the display, then 3) tap nav on the side of the screen to get the map back. build quality - the plastics feel low grade and there are rattles, particularly around the dash. steering wheel - this is meant to be a sporty hatch, so please stop fitting wheels sized like they belong on a boat.

i really like my new car but i am absolutely furious about losing features that were there at the start. after about a month the high beam assist disappeared, and after roughly three months other functions were gone too, including the 3d sat nav and the live traffic information. i am not even completely sure what else has vanished yet and expect that next time i drive i will notice more things missing. to keep using what i had got used to i now have to pay a monthly subscription. the car cost enough already without having to keep shelling out more. i am really not happy about this at all. i will not be telling anyone to buy a bmw, because even though you pay more than for other cars, what you paid for does not stay and bmw want extra money for stuff that was originally on the car. honestly, i'm disgusted.

the car is generally reasonable to drive. it is my first time owning an automatic and i am still getting used to it, noticing both advantages and disadvantages with the change. being a brand new model there are some appealing improvements, but in my view there are one or two design issues (in fact i have found three, though whether others agree is just opinion). the visual warning for another vehicle in the blind spot seems like a great new idea, yet in practice it appears, at least on the nearside, to work very inconsistently. the internal light display reflects too much onto the windscreen at night and becomes a distraction. and having the fog lamp button on the indicator stalk feels odd and tends to cause accidental switching on.

for us this is a major step up from the previous f40 version. the ride is noticeably smoother and the cabin much quieter, with a handy increase in acceleration performance as well. fuel economy is significantly better, the regenerative braking really shines, and together with the bigger fuel tank it gives a very useful gain in overall range. the curved screen setup for driver info, sat nav, climate and so on works really well, and in our view is far better than similar systems in many other cars.

the one negative so far is the "puddle lights" in the outer door handles, which currently do not operate, even though they are fitted in the handles. these were standard and fully working on our previous 118i m sport, so why not on this one? apart from that, the car drives exactly how a bmw should and gives the impression of being a much larger model. we absolutely love it.

i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

over more than 30 years i have owned several new bmws, from 4 series through 3 and 2 and now a 1 series, and i am honestly extremely disappointed. very important things that were always included in the purchase price before are now simply left out, clearly just to cut your production costs, yet you still remove quite a few previously 'standard' extras from every series while happily pushing the price up. when i was considering the 1 series nobody bothered to point out that there is no spare wheel and no hand book, both of which i regard as essential items for an owner. i swap my car every 2 or 3 years, but i will not choose bmw again. i feel very very let down.

overall it is a better, if slightly mixed, step up from my old 180i msport. the roadholding is more precise, the ride is improved on bad surfaces, there is a useful bit of extra power, the stop/start is far superior (the previous one was so poor i never used it), fuel economy is better and the engine runs smoother. on the downside, there is no single, easy-to-find autohold button anymore, it now needs one button then a touch on the screen. i rely on autohold for most driving, except for slow manoeuvres in tight areas where the throttle blip to release autohold can create more movement than i want. there should be a simpler, faster way to switch autohold on and off. i also miss a feature from my 180i: comfort mode used to give constant coasting. i realise regen improves efficiency, but having the option of coasting would be good for a very relaxed drive.

the latest model is not as nicely specified as my last one. losing idrive is a real downside. the air-con does not cool as well and the lack of rear vents is unacceptable. i paid for driving assistant professional and technology pack plus, yet some of the functions only worked for 3 months as a free trial even though the tech is in the car. that didnt happen with the previous vehicle. i was never told digital premium would run out and the configurator didnt make that obvious. the plain map display and the end of traffic info on a premium car are frustrating considering the price of the packs. the car spent 2 days in the workshop because of software issues. definitely not an upgrade over the earlier model.

weve been getting a new 1 series every few years since 2004 and each one has felt like a step up from the last. this latest one is easily the best yet. its our first automatic, and even though ive always claimed manuals were unbeatable, this autobox is amazing. long drives are a pleasure, really relaxing, and in city stop-start traffic its simple to handle. i did more than 6 hours at the wheel in one go to reach where we were heading and could honestly have kept going another 6 hours, it was that comfortable and low stress. the driving position has always been strong, and the new interior is brilliant, puts a grin on my face whenever i get in. the seats are super comfy and the new display is straightforward to use. absolutely love it

i chose the 1 series because i have been driving bmw cars for roughly 35 years. i would have preferred to get another x1, but my budget would not stretch to the price. given my age now and the fact i drive fewer miles, i have found this car very comfortable, especially after raising the seat to give me a higher and better driving position. the engine capacity is about 25% smaller, which worried me at first, but i quickly got used to it and now i barely notice. my concern is that, when i bought the car, nobody mentioned the extra digital upgrade, which seems to be around £12 a month. i am disappointed that the sat nav without this upgrade is quite inferior. i now think the upgrade is expensive and feel rather let down.

love how the car drives and it really looks good, but the whole infotainment and driver interaction feels like a big step backwards with the physical buttons gone. bmw seems to think everyone wants to use their car like a smartphone now. stuff that was a single press before, like changing drive mode, is now 3 taps if i want to get back to my nav screen. thats not just annoying, it feels unsafe because you are pulled away from watching the road. same story when trying to change the fan speed. looks like this is all about saving money while the price of the car keeps going up. some of the interior plastics come across as cheap and not up to what you would expect from bmw. please bring back the buttons and the navigation wheel!

why is there a character limit? mechanically it feels cheap, rushed and badly tuned, not what i expected from bmw. my old 2010 e82 1 series was superior in every respect. the missing idrive wheel is a letdown and there is no proper replacement. mercedes puts a touch pad on the steering wheel, but here both next track buttons are inconsistent and irritating to use. the suspension needs more tuning for uk motorways and roads. the hybrid system also needs a lot of work: when you come up to a roundabout it sits in too high a gear and takes about two seconds to change down. i picked the bmw hybrid partly because it does not use a cvt, yet the gearbox fitted feels very slow to downshift when you need it. the auto wipers react too slowly to changing weather. and is there really no tire pressure sensor?

hello, this is now my sixth brand new bmw - 2 x 5 series saloons, 2 x 5 series tourers and 1 x r1100s motorbike.  pros: the engine reacts quickly, the suspension really smooths out and deadens the bumps in the road, the exterior styling (it actually looks designed instead of the usual boxes you see), the instantly comfy seats and the curved display.  cons: the tech is fiddly to operate (it needs more big knobs), the supposedly helpful technology just ends up too complicated, the digital manual drowns you in information (a simpler, easy-to-find guide to the main functions would be better), build quality issues (the bonnet only secures on one side, there's no velcro under the bmw front passenger rubber mat), and there is no paper user manual. thanks, roland ross

the car is decent to drive, comfortable, and the performance is enough for what we need. however, the connected app is unreliable, sometimes it just does not work, and the tech interface feels overly complicated, which is quite off putting when you mainly just want to drive. it also seems to need software updates again and again, and the voice instruction function is not dependable. our connected drive premium service only lasts three months, which comes across as a cynical way to take more money when the car itself is already sold at a premium price. we have owned bmw cars for about twenty years, but it is very likely this will be the last one we buy.

i have had 7 bmws so far and liked every one of them, but this one is easily the best i have owned. it is a pleasure to drive and i actually look forward to any trip. it can be calm and smooth when i want to relax, but turns into something exciting and fun when i feel like it. despite being a small car it works hard, with a practical and flexible load space. up to now, apart from a puncture, no bmw has ever let me down. it looks great, is comfortable, and the sound system is excellent. the infotainment is very intuitive and functions really well. my only gripe is that connected drive (digital premium) should not be an add-on but built into the price from the start. outstanding customer service from stratstone derby as well.

i would tell family and friends to buy this car because of the build quality, the styling, the performance and the comfortable drive. but as an older person, i find the controls far too high tech and i struggle with them, and i would have liked more traditional manual control options. the "hey bmw" command responds for some functions but not others, which makes it harder, and the menu structure is overly complicated and not user friendly. the controls were shown to me when i bought the car by an excellent salesperson who was younger and very familiar with the high tech system, but it was simply too much to take in at once. looking back, if i had realised how advanced and complex the controls were, i would not have chosen this vehicle.

great spec, strong performance and generally a quality feel. one thing though - the knurled button on the steering wheel feels a bit cheap to the touch. the screen layout is very thorough and the 'recently used' feature is really useful. it would be better if there were separate heating adjustments for driver and passenger. the flashing blindspot light in the driver's wing mirror is a really good safety touch. having another, less usual option word instead of just 'bmw' would make it easier not to trigger the driver assistance wake-up by accident. the lighting modes and themes are excellent; it would be good to have extra downloadable themes to keep it fresh.

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!

title: G60 non-contact trunk lid opening

No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the kick-to-open function is not working as smoothly as they would prefer, and even though the dealer showed them how to use it, it still does not activate every time. Writer suggested having the key in their pocket, standing about an arm's length away, and using a soccer-style kick. Customer mentioned their key is usually in a purse and asked if that setup would work. Writer advised that, depending on the type of bag, the signal may be obstructed. Customer acknowledged this.
I had a minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "Hard to figure out the exact place and movement needed to get it to activate"
Customer stated the hands free trunk only works occasionally. Writer advised using a simple poking motion with their foot under the car for better results. Customer acknowledged.

I had a very minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "It rarely works on the first try and sometimes will not work at all even after several attempts."
I had a problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "I wave my foot under the rear of the car and sometimes the trunk just does not open."

Customer reported difficulty getting the trunk to open by swinging their foot. Customer mentioned they are aware the recent software update was supposed to improve that function but still cannot open the trunk with just a foot swing. Customer asked if they should move their foot front to back or side to side and what they might be doing incorrectly. Writer went over the hands-free trunk opening steps and confirmed that the feature was turned on.

Customer stated that the kick feature to open the trunk only functions for him roughly 30 percent of the time. He mentioned that when attempting to use it, he stands a bit more than a foot away from the back of the vehicle and performs one continuous kicking motion without pausing, aimed under the center portion of the rear bumper.

Customer stated that the smart trunk function seems a bit off. Customer explained that frequently it will fail to open when he is deliberately trying to use it, but then it will randomly open by itself just when he walks past, even though he is not actively attempting to trigger it. Customer added that he is using the digital key. Writer requested that the customer compare how this feature behaves on the current vehicle versus his former BMW 5 Series, asking whether the previous car's smart trunk operated better or similarly. Customer replied that on his previous BMW the smart trunk feature worked flawlessly every single time.
I had a serious problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "the auto open using your foot only works sometimes, not every time."

I had a very minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "touchless sensor is mostly fine, works about 95% as it should, but at times I need to wave or kick my foot 2-3 times, and on other occasions it drops when I didn't mean it to."

Customer stated he is unable to get the tailgate to open using his foot, and said he just stands behind the car and waves his foot. Writer advised to stand about an arm length from the rear and do a kick under the middle of the bumper, then pull the foot back. Writer advised trying two quick kicks may help. Writer also advised that keeping the foot under the bumper will prevent it from opening.

I had a minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "I still havent managed to get the hands-free trunk sensor to work. Super frustrating trying to trigger it by swinging my leg around."

I had a minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "I've had this particular feature on a prior vehicle, but on this car it behaves inconsistently. Seems like I still haven't figured out the precise spot needed to get the trunk to open every time."

Customer stated she has not been able to get the handsfree tailgate to operate. Customer stated she turned the feature on in iDrive. Customer stated it worked one time at the dealership, but she has not gotten it to work again. Writer asked whether she was using a kick motion or waving back and forth. Customer stated she usually waves, but has also tried an in and out kick. Writer stated BMW recommends the kick motion. Writer stated that with a key on her person, she should stand at the rear center of the vehicle and use one kick in and out under the bumper directly below the BMW rondel. Writer stated if the tailgate still does not open, the customer can go to the dealership for a complete dianostics.
Customer mentioned they miss having a hands free trunk, like the one on their prior 2019 530i.
I had a very minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "Sensor not working"

Customer stated he was having issues using the foot-activated trunk function. Writer went over specific instructions, including standing in line with the emblem and using a quick front-to-back kick motion, and confirmed the necessary settings were enabled. Despite this troubleshooting, the trunk feature still did not operate.

Customer stated the touchless tailgate function was not operating. Writer used RVG and verified the settings were turned on and that the customer was aiming the foot in the right spot. Customer was keeping the foot under the sensor instead of making one quick swipe or moving the foot under and then out right away. Writer confirmed the system is working as intended.
I had a minor problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "It fails to operate reliably and at times the response is just too slow."

Customer stated she struggles using the foot trunk opener, feeling it only works when her foot is placed very precisely and that it is hard when her arms are full, making her feel goofy repeating it. Writer advised the 5 Series kick-to-open is improved and she should be able to swipe her leg to open the trunk while standing about one arm's length from the back. Customer stated she will experiment with it more.
I had a problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "just inconsistent and not reliable when you need it most."

Customer stated via email that the Touch-Free tailgate feature has never worked for him. Writer advised the customer to keep the vehicle key in-hand and make a kicking motion under the middle of the rear bumper.
I had a serious problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "when I use the foot sensor, it occasionally takes a bunch of tries before it actually activates"
I had a problem with Trunk/hatch/tailgate - Touch-free sensor doesn't work consistently/DTU: "the sensor only sporadically detects the foot movement."
Customer reported the kick-to-open trunk does not work consistently. Writer explained the correct use: position foot under the BMW roundel, move it forward smoothly, and avoid fast kicking motions.

Customer stated the foot kick opening works for him less than half the time and he finds it ineffective. Customer stated that on his previous Mercedes Benz there was a foot wave to open, which he felt was much more forgiving than the current setup.

Customer stated the trunk that opens with a foot or leg movement only works on some attempts and fails on others. Customer stated he went back to the dealership once for this issue, and a woman there tried it and had the same mixed results. Customer stated that after that visit it has worked on occasion but most of the time he ends up opening it another way. Writer confirmed the customer keeps the key fob on his body when trying to use the hands-free tailgate and does not leave it in the car.

Customer stated the tailgate foot-activated opening does not consistently function. Writer asked if she had checked the settings to confirm the feature was enabled. Customer replied no, and since she was already inside the vehicle, writer guided her to the menu. Customer indicated both open and close foot movements were checked. Writer then asked which key she uses, and customer answered she uses her Digital Key. Writer instructed her to stand centered at the rear of the vehicle, take a step back, then kick her foot straight forward and straight back like kicking a soccer ball, and then wait about 3 seconds. Customer reported it still did not work. RVG attempted while the customer tried again, and she stated it worked once she took a slightly smaller step back. Writer suggested testing it several more times to verify both opening and closing worked. Customer did so and confirmed both functions now operate properly.

Customer stated he has only been able to get the trunk to open once using the kick-to-open function. Customer stated he is using the digital key plus on his phone and holds the phone near the BMW badge on the rear of the car. Customer asked if the kick feature should operate when using his phone as the key. Writer advised that it is intended to work. Writer asked if unlock on approach was enabled. Customer stated that when he walks up to the car it unlocks automatically. Writer asked where he was kicking under the bumper. Customer stated he kicks under the middle of the bumper. Writer suggested performing two separate kicks in a row while standing about an arm's length away from the back of the vehicle. Customer stated he has a service visit at his dealership today and will have them demonstrate this feature. Writer asked if he was aware he could also close the trunk using the kick feature. Customer stated he knew that, but since he cannot reliably get the open function to work, he has not attempted the kick-to-close.

Customer commented the hands free trunk feature works really well.
Customer states the non-contact trunk opening is not operating correctly and she requires help. Writer advised her to stand a bit farther back and then move her foot forward to activate it.

Customer explained they were inside the vehicle during the call and that, even with the fan set to very high, it does not feel like a very high setting. Customer mentioned they were using max AC at the time, and while the air itself is cold, it still does not meet their expectations for overall power and cooling strength. Customer emphasized the cooling is not cold enough and the airflow is too weak, even when everything is set to the maximum.

Customer stated the vehicle does not cool the cabin or circulate the air the way he expects. Customer stated he came over to BMW from Mercedes and that Mercedes has a much better system for cooling the vehicle.

Customer stated his Air Conditioning does not feel as strong as in his 2013 7 Series and that it is getting very hot. Customer stated he currently has the Air set to MAX. Customer stated he plans to stop by the dealership when he has time to have it inspected. Writer invited the customer to contact us again if needed.
Customer stated the air conditioning does not push much air, even when set to the maximum. Customer stated he wants the cold air to blow on him more noticeably.

I had a serious problem with Air conditioner doesn't achieve/maintain desired temperature: "My vehicle has a black interior and the AC struggles to cool it properly. The fan on high needs to push more air so the cabin cools in a reasonable amount of time. The vents make it impossible for the driver to direct air to the face, so it stays hot longer. (Copied from CLMT97): The issue lies in how the air system is designed. The AC must blow harder or include additional vents, or both, to cool the car adequately."

I had a problem with Air conditioner doesn't achieve/maintain desired temperature: "(Copied from CLMT97): On auto, the AC does not jump to high speed when the cabin is hot. This is particulary noticeable when getting into a very hot car."

Customer reported that the vents are pushing out cold air, and he has to set the temperature up to about 80 degrees or higher before it starts to feel warm. Customer noted that both Auto and A/C are turned off.

my 2024 760i xdrive is just fantastic. it looks amazing, rides incredibly well, and all the tech is there without feeling too complicated. i recently drove about 220 miles and got a bit over 26 mpg overall, with 31.1 mpg for roughly the first 160 miles where the speed limit was 55 mph. the driver assist plus is a great feature, it really makes highway trips feel safer and more relaxed for me and my wife. the only two downsides i have are kind of trivial... 1) there is no spot specifically for my sunglasses, and 2) i would really prefer the hvac to stay on sync by default unless i manually change it. aside from those small things, i absolutely love this car and am already excited for my next ultimate driving experience in it. thank you!

Customer stated that both she and her husband experience the air conditioning shutting off intermittently. Customer stated she will press the air conditioning button and then a short time later it turns itself off again. Writer explained that pressing the air conditioning button will only switch the A/C on or off, and that the temperature still needs to be set if the Automatic Program is enabled. Writer stated the Automatic Program might be automatically switching off the climate control when the cabin reaches the chosen temperature. Writer stated that if this is not what she wants, the Automatic Program can be turned off so she can manually adjust the blower and other functions. Writer added that if the climate control seems abnormal, the dealer would need to further diagnose it. Customer stated she will look at the climate control settings and may visit the dealer on a different day.

Customer stated whenever he starts the vehicle the heated seats and heated steering wheel come on and he has to shut them off each time. Writer asked if the Auto function was enabled. Customer was unsure and went to the car to look. Writer, using RVG, directed him to the Climatization menu, where Auto was indeed on. Writer advised turning Auto off, then powering down the car, getting out and locking it. Customer reported he did all that, went back inside and the functions stayed off. Writer explained the system will now follow whatever settings he chooses instead of an automatic setup. Customer acknowledged.
Customer stated the air conditioning never gets cool enough to really cool her off from the Arizona heat, even when Max A/C is switched on.
Customer commented that he is happy with the climatization system.
Customer stated that with the new design of the vents they do not deliver enough airflow.

Customer mentioned she still hasnt figured out where the air vents are located. Customer said the only vent she can see is the one in the middle. Writer offered to assist, but Customer ended the call quickly to answer another call.

Customer stated he wishes the vehicle had Tesla's Dog Mode. Customer explained that Dog Mode keeps the cabin cool when the driver is out of the car but the dogs are still inside, with the duration essentially unlimited as long as there is battery power. Writer suggested using Remote Engine Start as an alternative and noted the vehicle will continue cooling for 15 minutes before turning off.
I had a very minor problem with Air conditioner doesn't achieve/maintain desired temperature: "(Copied from CLMT97): The air conditioning fan on the driver side just does not feel strong enough."

Customer reported the windshield fogs up frequently, mainly in the lower center area where the air from the dashboard hits it. Customer stated he keeps switching the wipers on to remove the fog. Writer advised using the MAX defrost button to clear the glass and noted that AUTO Climate Control also helps manage the interior conditions.
Customer reported the air conditioning is slow to cool the cabin compared to what it should do. Customer declined to give further comments or go over troubleshooting.

Customer reported that the rear air conditioning does not perform as strongly as the front air conditioning and that the weaker cooling in the rear is clearly noticeable. Customer stated that family members sitting in the back have complained about not getting enough cooling.

Customer stated he misses the climate control rules from his former 5 Series. Customer expressed he wants a way to set a specific temperature for when the heated seats, air cooled seats, and steering wheel turn on. Writer advised using iDrive and going to Climate Menu>Individual settings, then adjusting the slide bars. Customer indicated he has tried those sliders but would rather have an exact temperature setting to trigger the feature. Customer added that his air cooled seats were coming on constantly when using the sliders, so he ended up switching that function off.

Customer stated the AC seems to work well only when set to the maximum settings. Customer asked how to best configure the climate control. Writer advised typically using auto climate control and choosing a temperature for optimal results. Writer added that the only other adjustment needed would be the fan speed.
Customer stated the vehicle takes more time to cool down, and mentioned a dead area in the front center that never receives any airflow no matter how the vents are adjusted.

Customer stated the windshield keeps fogging up whenever the air conditioning or climate control is turned on, and that they have tried everything without solving it. Customer mentioned possibly returning to the dealership so staff could either demonstrate proper operation or locate the issue. Writer went over the correct procedure to turn on the air conditioner and the defrost, and advised that the IPA could be used as well. Writer was successful, and the windows no longer fogged. RVG was completed.

Customer stated there is a plastic burning odor coming from the air conditioning, particularly after driving in Sport Plus mode. Customer noted the smell is fairly strong but has not gone to the dealer yet.

Customer stated he is not pleased with how the Climate Control system behaves. Customer stated he originally relied on Auto mode, but reported that it keeps the fan running on a low setting the entire time. Customer stated that in all his prior cars he would simply put the temperature at 70 and the system would manage everything, whereas now he feels he has to go into Manual mode and crank the temperature all the way down to get the cabin to cool. Writer asked whether the fan might have been set to Level 1, but customer was unsure. RVG accepted. Customer then switched the car back to Auto mode and confirmed it was at Level 2 with the temperature set to 70 degrees while it was about 95 degrees outside. Customer stated that with the interior as hot as it is, he expects the climate to ramp up to full blast, but instead it stays gentle and he ends up sweating. Customer stated that for him to actually notice cooling, he must change to Manual mode and select Max AC. Customer stated he never had to rely on Max AC in his last vehicle, a Mercedes 560. Customer said he did not have additional time to talk and mentioned he would call again later to resume the discussion.

the car is just incredible in every respect and i really love it. i only want to highlight two things that, although clearly intended well, are flawed. first, the front passengers don't have truly adjustable ac vents. there's a tiny on knob under the vent panel to tweak the airflow a bit, but the range of adjustment is extremely limited. i understand the sleek look of a dash without the usual vents, but here it feels like form winning over function, and the ac function suffers a lot because of that choice. second, the driver's side open door button is a problem. i tend to lean my left leg against the driver door while i'm driving, and very often my knee hits that open button and the door pops open even as the car is moving. that's really frightening and unsafe. it doesn't do it when the door is locked and the speed is over roughly 10 mph, but it happens below that speed. those are the only two points i have that i think would make the car safer and better for the driver.

car is overall very good but there are a few things that really need work. the air conditioning feels weak and you can't aim it right at one person. the charger setup is awful and charging takes way too long. i do like the "hey bmw" function, but when you have to say the same command 3 times it becomes frustrating. you're not able to close the trunk with a button from inside, even though there are all kinds of ways to close the doors, which doesn't make sense. the tv screen that drops down in back completely blocks the driver's view. they should let the rearview mirror switch to a camera image so you can still see behind. the car ought to start out in efficient mode instead of one that burns more miles. the seat heating doesn't get really warm and the cooling is also weak. the moon roof lights are tied to the lights on the side panels and can't be separated, and it should be possible to mix those colors.

the car's air conditioner system is quite bad.

Customer stated she is struggling to figure out how to quickly cool the cabin when first getting into the vehicle. Writer advised that pressing "Max A/C" in the Climate Menu is an effective way to immediately set the A/C to its highest output.

Customer stated he uses the Sync function to match the Heat and Air between the driver and passenger sides, but noted that every time he gets into the vehicle he has to press sync again. Writer asked if there was a passenger in the front seat. Customer replied that most of the time there is not. Writer explained that sync will only activate when a passenger is actually seated there. Customer then asked whether he could manage the rear seat climate settings. Writer confirmed he could, and stated via RVG to tap on Climate Control>Individual settings>second row of seats>settings. Customer also wanted to know how to adjust the Air Flow toward his upper body or his feet. Writer responded via RVG to tap Climate Control>the direction tab, and said to tap the airflow animations to switch the different zones on or off. Customer further inquired about the AUTO option. Writer stated that tapping AUTO will allow the system to automatically choose settings to best reach the desired temperature.

Customer stated that the main thing they notice, especially when comparing american cars to german ones, is the air conditioning. Customer said the AC is not very quick at cooling the cabin on a hot day, so they rely on the pre conditioning feature to get around that issue.

1. it makes no sense not to have a sunglass holder. my old 740 had one, and in about three months with this car i've already broken two pricey pairs of sunglasses because of this bad design.
2. the app is moody and only seems to work when it feels like it, which is extremely irritating. i plug the car in, ride the garage elevator down, then the office tower elevator up, and the app tells me the car isn't charging. so i head back down the office building, up the garage elevator to the car, and it actually is charging. then i go back down the garage elevator, up the high rise again to my office, call bmw assist, and they say i have to return to the car to troubleshoot…meaning sitting in a hot garage while they poke around and doing the elevator shuffle twice more. forget it…click…that was me ending the call.
3. the air conditioning layout is very unfriendly to use.

the car itself drives well, but there are some things that are just not acceptable, especially the sunglasses issue you've been hearing about for years. if the next one shows up without a sunglass holder, my time at that dealer will be very short before i walk out. the charging quirks are a nuisance and waste my time, so i'll probably just end up guessing when it's actually done charging.

2. the app is moody and only seems to work when it feels like it, which is extremely irritating. i plug the car in, ride the garage elevator down, then the office tower elevator up, and the app tells me the car isn't charging. so i head back down the office building, up the garage elevator to the car, and it actually is charging. then i go back down the garage elevator, up the high rise again to my office, call bmw assist, and they say i have to return to the car to troubleshoot…meaning sitting in a hot garage while they poke around and doing the elevator shuffle twice more. forget it…click…that was me ending the call.
3. the air conditioning layout is very unfriendly to use.

the upgraded bowers wilkins stereo is awful and you should give money back to anyone who had to pay for it. in my earlier bmws with the b&w system it was great. you moved the speakers from under the seats and now it is laughable. everyone who rides in the car comments on the stereo and then i tell them it was a $4,800 upgrade... this might end up being my last bmw. when you turn it up there is basically no bass or mid at all. it sounds terrible, everything just disappears, really sad.
also, you cannot keep the ac on air recirculation or keep the whole climate system synced, it resets every single time you shut the car off. luxury should mean you do not have to keep doing things, but i have to spend about a minute every time i get in the car setting up stuff that should stay the same. ac fan level 2 is way too weak and 3 is too strong and loud. bring back proper air vents.
i am not happy with this purchase and this is my 8th 7 series in around 12 years. i will not renew to this again.

i am happy with the new car. it is clearly more comfortable and in general more interesting than the older series i had. still, there are some drawbacks i really cannot ignore: - once the speed goes past about 110-120 km/h, the car is not well insulated anymore, wind noise becomes obvious and disturbing even though it has the special package. - at night, the driver's main rearview mirror gives a blurry picture, lights from cars behind and strong light sources look smeared, vertical lines show up and this makes driving harder. - the air conditioning will not run when the ignition is switched off. - there is no way to turn off the lights while the car is on (for example if you just want the ac working in a parking lot). - every single time you start driving you have to switch on the battery conservation function again. - the driver has no glove compartment now. before it was located to the left of the steering wheel. there is also no smaller extra glovebox like on the f01. - the driver's joystick/control stick feels very rigid when choosing left/right/up/down. - the driver's seat fails to go back to where it was before the car was shut down. - the cup holders do not offer cooling or heating at all.

initial impressions were really positive, but after a few weeks there were technical issues and it had to spend half a day at the service centre in norchester. it was fine again until this month, when a similar fault occurred: the main screen went completely black, making everything it controls unusable. i took it back to the service centre, where they kept it for the day and then overnight to carry out a full reset. they did good work there in norchester, to be fair. hopefully it is now sorted, but the whole situation has definitely taken the shine off the experience of getting and driving my new car.

i really like this car. i changed from a 3 series to a new 1 series so it took a while to adapt. looking back, i would have chosen the tech pack. i feel a few things still need tweaking but overall i do love it. the side ambient lights should be dimmable on their own without dimming everything. i have a rattle behind my drivers seat that has been back twice and is booked again for january to hopefully sort it. having to pay for auto full beam and digital plus is annoying, but i still paid as they make the car feel more special. great car that in my view just needs minor adjustments.

very satisfied with the car overall, but it definitely has areas that could be improved. the gearbox is not as smooth as i would expect from a bmw, and in some situations it produces loud noises and juddering. at times it seems unsure which gear it should select. the electric driver seat also occasionally fails to go into the right position. one of the biggest disappointments is the fake engine sound, which on an m model feels like a major let down. good car, but for the price it should be a lot better.

overall this m135 is a big step down from my old 128ti, nowhere near as good. it just isnt as nice to drive, it tends to understeer and is awkward to manoeuvre slowly, especially parking, because the transmission feels very jerky. getting rid of the i-drive knob and all the physical heating buttons is backwards and i see it as a safety problem. the dashboard reflects off the windscreen, worse at night. the centre console actually flexes when you press the my modes button, which feels cheap. there is lots of wind noise from the wing mirrors on the motorway. the 128ti had door handle lights, m-sport pin stripes on the seat belts, coloured edging on the floor mats, red brake calipers and built-in digital services like spotify, all of which made it feel special, and the m135 lacks all of that. in the end the m135 feels disappointing and not worth the money.

the car itself has attractive lines and drives well, but the support from the dealership before the purchase and after collection was not acceptable. i had to go back several times with complaints before the car became easier to live with. the greater reliance on the car systems is positive, but you cant realistically grasp everything at the handover. buyers need better guidance so the advantages and joy of a new model are real, not just promised. for instance, the video they give shows a left-hand-drive car even though in the uk we drive right-hand-drive, which is confusing. i am hoping over the next few months i will learn more about the systems and use them properly, so i can get the comfort and the full experience of driving what is otherwise a remarkable car.

title: G60 Public charging / external providers
requirement_statement: Improve 'Public charging / external providers' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote:
Customer stated that some drivers keep their vehicles plugged in at Electrify America chargers even after charging is complete, which is frustrating when he needs to plug in his own car.

Customer stated some Electrify America units are often out of order or already taken by other vehicles, and this is also frustrating.

Customer stated he wishes the public charging process were more like a regular gas station, where he could drive up to a charger, stay only a few minutes, and then leave.
Customer reported that at times it is hard for her to locate a charging station that is compatible.
Customer stated that after coming from Tesla, the charging experience has been very different. Customer stated it has been hard for him to find charging stations near his area.

Customer stated the nearest Electrify America charger is about 70 miles away, and when he locates other public chargers they are usually occupied. Writer advised that BMW is actively working on expanding public charging options. Customer stated this is his first electric vehicle.

Customer stated public charging stations are not placed conveniently. Customer stated they are usually out of the way and, when he finds one, it is in a secluded area of the parking lot. Customer stated he does not feel safe using most public chargers.

the car is very comfortable to sit in and drive, and the handling is quite responsive. i haven't had a vehicle this large for many years, but this one drives and turns almost like a smaller car. the acceleration is excellent, and i don't feel any need for the m version's extra power. the suspension is also excellent, which makes every ride enjoyable, though i'd prefer an air suspension like i've experienced in the audi q8 etron or what bmw offers on the i7. the range is very good, but with the limited fast charging along my usual routes to nj on the delmarva peninsula, i find myself wishing it could go more like 450-500 miles; for long out-of-state trips we rely on a gas vehicle. for driving around virginia the range works fine and is better than my previous ev, the vw id4. the technology in this car can be overwhelming, but i'm learning it and the infotainment bit by bit. it feels solid on the road, always composed and responsive. i do miss a spare tire, and the idea of using the provided flat repair system worries me since i've never done that before; it might help if the dealer walked me through it so i'd feel less anxious. overall, i really enjoy being behind the wheel of this car, it's the best i've owned.

Customer stated that on his first attempt using a public charger, he was able to start the charger, but it would not continue charging for more than roughly 2 minutes before shutting off. Customer stated that one side of the charger was already in use when he arrived, and once the other driver left, he moved his cable to the other side of the same unit. Customer stated that using this second side allowed his vehicle to charge properly. Customer stated that, when reviewing his credit card activity, he saw three separate $30 charges from the charging operator. Customer stated it took about a week for those charges to be corrected to the proper amount.
Customer expressed anxiety about how available charging is versus regular gas stations, unsure about when and where to stop, particularly late at night.

Customer stated that calling EA for help with chargers results in hold times of about 15-20 minutes. Customer stated they are unhappy with how costly EA electricity is, noting it is 48c per kwh while other providers are closer to 20c.

Customer stated she likes that Public charging is easy to locate and operate. Customer stated she was surprised that the Public chargers are so simple to use and that this made her anxiety about using Public chargers go down a lot.

Customer stated he thought each charging session using his free credits had a time limit. Writer advised there is no per-session time limit for his offer, whereas prior promotions were limited to a 30 minute session. Writer advised his current promotion provides up to 1000 kWh in total, regardless of how long each session lasts, but the credits are only valid for two years.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

i had a bmw 3 series and then a 5 series for many years, then went to the bmw i3 as my first ev, and after that switched over to a tesla model 3. as much as tesla's new model s matches up well against the bmw i5, i feel your design, build quality, and the way it drives are exactly what the market is looking for right now. i was really glad to come back to bmw, but i have to stress that the infotainment tech and software is where companies like tesla and rivian will keep pulling customers away. if bmw keeps delivering over-the-air updates for current cars to refine and enhance the drive, you'll stay ahead of everyone else. the i5 looks fantastic and drives beautifully. at the same time, charging infrastructure is critical, and tesla is still way more convenient. can't count how many times i show up at electrify america and the units are down, or i end up waiting for hours just to get a charge on longer trips.

title: G70 Exterior
requirement_statement: Improve 'Exterior' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 38 respondents complain and 31 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
Topic and polarity come from keyword rules, not BMW labels.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the black trim on the passenger side between the front and rear passenger windows is faded. Customer stated it appears sun-faded and is almost white in color, and only the passenger side is impacted. Customer stated he was out of town and could not connect via RVG to send pictures. Customer stated the dealership already knows about the issue and he will have it repaired soon.

Customer stated the alignment of some detail parts on the vehicle appears slightly off. Customer stated a few items are just a little mis-aligned. Customer went out to the vehicle with the Writer. Writer sent RVG and captured pictures. Customer stated that along the area from the front driver-side door to the rear door, the trim pops up a bit. Customer stated you can feel this ridge with your finger. Customer stated that when he looks through the side-view window, the misalignment is visible. Writer took photos of the exterior front and rear driver-side doors. Writer attempted to take a picture from the driver side looking through the side-view mirror, but rain made it hard to see. Writer asked the customer to provide a picture from the driver seat through the side mirror when it is not raining. Customer stated there is a small gap on the hood. Writer captured photos of the slight gap at the left front of the hood where it meets the passenger-side fender.
Customer mentioned he is pleased with the overall size of the vehicle.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

2024 bmw 760i, to me, is a true mix of power and elegance. as a proud owner of the 2024 bmw 760i, it's hard not to be drawn in by how commanding it looks out on the road. the sleek exterior and the luxurious cabin make this flagship sedan feel like it radiates power and sophistication.

there's a real sense of empowerment that comes with driving something so prestigious. my wife, who is 5 foot 2 and around 100 pounds, is especially taken with the way the 760i carries itself. for her, it isn't just about the car's size, it's about feeling like she's in charge of the road and in control of a serious machine.

for her it goes beyond simple transportation; it's a statement, a way of showing her presence and capability. the 760i lives up to that, with strong performance from its potent engine and advanced tech features that give real confidence behind the wheel. whether we're weaving through city streets or cruising the highway, every trip feels like a small victory.

of course, people see a car like this differently. some might think it's about a "look-at-me" syndrome, wanting attention or validation. that may be true for some, but for many others a bmw 760i represents the result of hard work and success, a reward for what they've achieved and a symbol of personal accomplishment.

for me the 2024 bmw 760i is far more than just another vehicle; it stands for power, elegance and prestige. even if opinions about what it means vary, one thing is clear to me: it brings a huge amount of joy and satisfaction to anyone lucky enough to live with it every day.

the pricing on this car is way too high. i managed to negotiate a strong lease, but there is no chance i would spend the $190k msrp on an electric car that is bound to lose a lot of value. overall the tech is very solid, but bmw still not getting the esim to function correctly is incredibly annoying. one of the main reasons i chose this car was the theatre screen, and now it only operates if i run ugly cables to it. the seats are mostly comfortable, yet they do not give enough side bolster support, so i would really like more hold in the corners. the heated seats and heated armrests are fantastic and the infotainment works well, plus the upgraded sound system is outstanding. when using apple carplay, though, the bottom left corner with distance and time remaining is completely hidden behind my right hand while driving. if i swapped cars today i would rather be in an m5 touring.
