Customer stated that from the time he took delivery, roughly 70% of the times he starts the vehicle the eSIM icon in the iDrive menu bar shows that the Personal eSIM is not configured and not working. Customer stated that when this occurs he cannot stream anything to the Theater Screen in the rear. Customer stated that in these instances, the iDrive Tel > Mobile devices list has the Personal eSIM entry highlighted with the note "Setting up personal eSIM" beneath it, and it never progresses or finishes. Customer stated he has gone to the dealership Genius multiple times and that the Genius adjusts something in the myBMW app to get it working again. Customer stated the fix does not last and the eSIM soon goes back to not functioning. Customer stated that he has been able to connect the eSIM and stream to the Theater Screen on some occasions, but that most of the time it fails because the eSIM never fully completes setup and connection.

Writer checked AIR and confirmed vehicle integration level G070-23-03-553 is newer than the -540 level specified for AT&T Personal eSIM. Writer connected via RVG and verified the issue: the sim card symbol with an exclamation mark in the menu bar indicated an eSIM fault. Writer confirmed the customer's description that the Tel > Mobile devices screen shows Personal eSIM highlighted with "Setting up personal eSIM" that does not change. Writer confirmed the customer was signed into his BMW ID / driver profile. Customer verified in the myBMW app that the Personal eSIM was activated on AT&T and stated he has an unlimited plan for the eSIM. Writer verified the customer's iPhone 14 is on iOS 16.5.1 and that the myBMW app is current and operating correctly.

Writer guided the customer to iDrive Menu > Vehicle apps > System settings > Update apps and services. Customer selected Update apps and services, and iDrive reported the vehicle software is current. Writer then walked the customer through a 30-second iDrive reset. Writer had the customer use the myBMW app to deactivate the eSIM from the i7. Writer next directed the customer in iDrive to Menu > Apps > Personal Hotspot > Connect new device. When the QR code appeared on the Control Display, customer stated the dealership Genius had previously skipped this step and done something different in the myBMW app, though the customer could not remember the details. Writer instructed the customer to scan the QR code. Customer stated the QR code did not proceed to move his phone further through the setup flow.

Writer then advised the customer to re-activate the eSIM using the Personal eSIM section in the myBMW app. Customer entered his phone number but the process stopped, and the app indicated he needed to add service. Writer guided the customer to select the eSIM device in iDrive and choose Activate internet access. Customer followed this, and his phone was forwarded to the AT&T login page. Customer signed into his AT&T account and tried to re-activate the eSIM on the i7, then ended the RVG session. Customer reported that on the AT&T site he was being asked to add service and that he could not re-activate the eSIM this way.

Writer explained that the problem appeared to be related to the customer's AT&T account, since AT&T was requiring added service for eSIM activation. Writer recommended that the customer contact AT&T to confirm his account and eSIM plan are truly unlimited and compatible with the Personal eSIM. Customer insisted the fault was with BMW. Writer still advised the customer to perform a 70-second iDrive hard reset to restart the telematics unit, even though the symptoms pointed more toward an AT&T account issue than telematics. Writer also recommended the customer return to the dealership so the Genius could repeat the same method they had used before to start the eSIM without involving the QR code or AT&T portal. Writer encouraged the customer to ask the dealership service department to check for any possible hardware defects due to the repeated nature of the problem. Customer did not specify what he intended to do next. Writer advised that the customer could reach out again with further questions or updates, but that the immediate next steps lay with AT&T or the dealership. Customer acknowledged.

Customer stated that when they bought the vehicle they planned to use the eSIM, but were unable to do so with Spectrum, so they ended up switching to T-Mobile.

Customer stated their main complaint is that their mobile provider does not work with the BMW for hotspot. Writer asked which carrier they use. Customer stated Verizon. Writer asked if the account is personal or business. Customer stated it is personal. Writer asked if the plan is unlimited. Customer confirmed it is unlimited. Writer advised the vehicle should be eligible for a personal esim. Customer stated they have already visited 2 different Verizon stores and were told it is not. Customer stated their sales advisor also said the vehicle is not eligible. Writer apologized for the mixed messages. Writer asked if, during setup, they receive a notification from Verizon that it is not compatible. Customer confirmed. Writer advised customer to contact BMW assist to have a ticket opened to resolve the problem. Writer advised the vehicle is presently running 07-24 and needs the 11-24 software update. Writer advised the update is being pushed in batches and that they will get a notification once it is available, but if they prefer not to wait they can visit their servicing dealer to have it updated manually, as there is a known issue with activating a new esim on 07-24. Customer acknowledged.
Customer reported ongoing E sim problems that started after his remote software update. Writer advised that we are already aware of this concern and are currently working on a resolution.

Customer stated that whenever he uses Remote Engine Start, he gets into the car and an eSIM notification appears. Customer stated it shows an eSIM with an exclamation point and says the eSIM needs to be set up. Customer stated he goes through the setup and it works fine, but this happens every day with Remote Engine Start. Customer stated BMW advised him to reboot iDrive by holding the power button, which he does often. Customer stated this usually works, but he has to repeat it the next time.

Customer stated he is experiencing a problem with the Personal eSIM, explaining that it only works when his phone is physically in the vehicle. Customer stated he is the primary user on the AT&T account and set up the eSIM on his own driver profile. Customer stated he is unsure if it is simply his profile loading that makes the eSIM function. Writer advised it is more likely related to how it is configured on his driver profile. Writer recommended he try signing into his AT&T account under his wife's driver profile to see if that resolves the issue.

Customer stated her Personal eSIM is completely configured, but when she is away from the vehicle and her husband is driving, an incoming call to her phone causes him to hear the ringtone in the car, even when the vehicle is many miles away from her. At the time of the Welcome Call, the customer was not near the car and declined to troubleshoot the concern. Customer mentioned she will either call back or visit the dealer if she needs additional assistance.
Customer stated he plans to set up his personal eSim shortly and asked if this needs to be done through his mobile provider. Writer confirmed that is correct.
Customer mentioned they still need to go to the dealership to get the internet hooked up, but said they have not really had time yet. Writer offered help, however customer was busy.
Customer requested more details about how the ESIM feature works. Writer went over the requirements and how it is used with mobile devices.

Customer mentioned he is still waiting for the dealer to help get the vehicle wifi set up for the theater screen. Writer offered to assist by having the customer activate the personal esim so the car can use a wifi hotspot. Writer instructed customer to open the My BMW app, tap the profile icon in the lower right, select personal esim and then activate. Writer advised to choose the mobile provider and enter the mobile number. Writer noted that with a Verizon line, it has to be a personal account with an unlimited plan. Customer stated the process takes him to sign in to the Verizon website, but he only sees normal phone plans and no option for a personal esim. Writer advised that customer must talk to Verizon directly to add the esim, then continue the installation in the vehicle. Customer acknowledged.

Customer inquired about how to make phone calls in the vehicle without using his physical phone. Writer advised that he could set up Personal eSIM, which adds a separate line to the customer's existing cell phone plan. Writer offered to walk the customer through the setup steps. Customer acknowledged the information and declined the detailed steps.

Customer reported that a couple of times when he got into the car, the eSIM was either not connected or had no service, so his FireTV on the Theater Screen could not connect. Customer noted that when the eSIM failed to connect, he was in an area with poor cell service. Customer stated his Driver Profile was already signed in and he was using a Digital Key at the time. Customer added that once he arrived back home, he tried the eSIM again and it connected normally, and he was then able to use the Theater Screen with FireTV without issue. Customer confirmed the eSIM is currently still working normally.
Writer explained that the eSIM may have been impacted by the weak cellular reception. Writer mentioned the eSIM uses the car's antenna, which should improve reception compared to a phone, but it is still limited by areas with poor signal. Writer suggested checking for Remote Software Upgrades and for updates to Apps & Services in iDrive by going to the Apps Menu, then System Settings, then Remote Software Upgrade to look for available upgrades. Writer then advised checking for updates to Apps & Services under the same System Settings section. Customer stated he plans to check for these updates soon.

Customer stated that when he opens eSIM, the vehicle will sometimes display that it is attempting to connect to Verizon for several minutes. Customer stated the theater screen then indicates it is offline even though the eSIM shows as connected. Customer stated these issues occur often, and the vehicle currently has 1,726 miles. Customer stated he purchased a Firestick and hooked it up to his phone's hotspot. Customer stated there is no option to connect the theater screen itself to his phone's hotspot.
Customer says the process of setting up the eSIM was a nightmare.

Customer stated his Personal eSIM is active and working with his own BMW ID, but his wife is unable to access that same Personal eSIM with her BMW ID. Writer stated the BMW ID associated to the Personal eSIM must be signed in for it to function.

performance, reliability, tech, luxury, comfort - the whole package is there. i'd really like to be able to pin more apps onto that left sidebar on the home screen. i used to have the weather sitting there, then it just seemed to vanish. i rely on quick shortcuts, so i ended up putting the weather app in the shortcut section instead.
about a week after i bought the car i got a flat tire, right after a storm, and bmw connect happened to be down. i had to arrange one tow to get back home, then a second tow to reach the bmw dealer that's out of town. that meant a lot of time just waiting around for tow trucks. in that situation a spare tire would have been very useful. i was told i'd be reimbursed for the towing because bmw couldn't provide a tow, but that was in october and i still haven't received anything.
otherwise the car itself is fantastic. i really like being behind the wheel. i've always enjoyed driving, and with this being my 4th bmw - a 528 and two 740s before - this 760 tops them all. it has taken the driving experience to a completely new level for me.

Customer stated he added the eSim for a long cross-country trip, but when it was switched on it seemed to negatively impact how his phone functioned.

Customer stated he would rather have the old way of getting wi-fi in the car instead of having to deal with esim setup. Customer stated the esim setup process was an absolute nightmare and that he put in more than around 20 hours trying to sort it out. Customer stated BMW and the carrier should have some kind of stop gap, because if a customer already has a device on their line using esim you cannot have another one. Customer stated that every time he started the vehicle, it triggered a request to his provider to authorize esim, and their system would run a credit check, approve the esim and add an extra line, then charge him. Customer stated that when he looked at his Verizon bill he noticed there were over roughly 24 esim lines on the account and he was being billed for each one. Customer stated he had to pay about a $1000 phone bill up front while working with his provider afterwards to remove all the extra lines and secure a refund. Customer stated that due to this situation he also found that his Apple Watch and his daughters Apple Watch no longer operate unless they are within range of their phones.

Customer stated he activated the personal esim in the vehicle using a personal AT&T phone line, but it has never functioned for him. Customer reported a SIM card icon with an "!" continuously appearing in the upper right corner of the iDrive display. Customer stated he has been addressing this with BMW Assist and AT&T, and BMW Assist advised that the vehicle now needs to be inspected and diagnosed by the dealership. Customer mentioned an error message indicating the Esim Reader was not connected. Customer stated he is scheduled to take the vehicle in for service by the end of the week, and writer set up a follow up. Customer reported the vehicle has 226 miles and provided BMW Assist ticket iINC000049492982. Writer attempted to contact the customer to verify repair status, but the customer did not answer. No DCS or AIR Notes.

Customer stated he would prefer to connect the vehicle to his own mobile carrier instead of being stuck needing a T-Mobile plan. Customer stated he is a Verizon customer. Writer acknowleged this and advised that the feedback will be passed along to engineering.
Customer asked about using youtube and how to make it work. Writer advised an esim setup is required.

Customer stated he is experiencing issues with his personal esim and has tried to set it up several times, but it still will not work. Customer mentioned he contacted AT&T to have all the numbers removed from his account and has been planning to follow up but has not done so yet. Writer advised the vehicle currently runs software version 07-24, which has a known problem affecting the personal esim. Writer further advised that software 11-24 is being rolled out in batches and will correct this issue. Writer stated that if the customer does not wish to wait for the update to reach his vehicle, he can visit his servicing dealer and they can perform a manual update. Customer thanked the writer and acknowledged the information.

Customer said they need assistance with the eSIM. They have T-Mobile with an unlimited data plan on a personal account. Writer asked which step of the setup they were on, and customer thought maybe step 2 or 3. Writer then asked what the My BMW app shows under Personal eSIM, and customer said it shows their vehicle with an option to Activate eSIM. Writer offered to help right away if the customer could go to the car, but customer replied they did not have time. Writer advised to finish the setup in the My BMW app next time they are with the vehicle and to call back if they want more help. Customer thanked the writer.

i'm really unhappy with the self driving functions on this car. i paid more for this 7 series than for my previous one and ended up with fewer features. i believed it came with automatic traffic stop-and-go where it would handle heavy traffic on its own, and also with automatic lane change assist. right after picking up the car, i called the bmw genius for help, and after checking how the car was equipped they said those features should be there. they told me to go by a bmw dealership, so we stopped at one in riverside sc. the genius there said the car would need to stay at a dealer to be reprogrammed, but i couldn't leave it because i was only there briefly for business. i then booked service at a bmw store in bayport fl near our place in lakeside, and they held the car for 24 hours without a tech actually looking at it, then told me it was user error. during all of this i was waiting on a call from a bmw supervisor to sort things out. when i got back from fl, i left the car with my dealer in westfield ct, and after their troubleshooting they said the vehicle simply does not have those features and they can't be added. getting to that conclusion was extremely frustrating. in the end, it was my mistake for buying a car straight off the lot, not really knowing what equipment it had, and assuming i would end up with fewer features than the one i turned in.

Customer stated the eSIM connection is inconsistent. Customer stated that around half the time when they try to use the eSIM it displays, "We're Offline.". Customer stated they perform a 30 second iDrive reboot to correct the problem for that particular drive. Customer stated they have already tried deleting and reinstalling the eSIM profile, but the same issue continues. Customer stated their carrier is Verizon. Writer recommended that the customer discuss the concern with dealer service. Customer acknowledged.

overall it has been a fantastic car so far. i really like the configuration and the level of luxury, and the build feels very solid. it definitely turns heads and has a strong presence on the road, and i enjoy how it drives. my only gripes are with the software. the app itself is excellent, but idrive gives me trouble. a few things are minor but irritating, like my home screen widgets randomly vanishing so i have to re-add them. the main headache is the esim randomly refusing to activate. i do not hold this against the car itself, as it seems like something that could be fixed with an ota update rather than a hardware issue. still, it is a very frustrating bug, and the only way around it has been to cancel my ubigi plan and start over, which results in double billing. please get this fixed asap!

Customer stated he has opened an eSIM subscription through his mobile carrier, but has not connected that eSIM to the vehicle yet. Writer stated to go into iDrive, open the Apps Menu, then Mobile devices, then Personal eSIM, and follow the steps shown on the Control Display. Writer stated a QR code will appear on the display, and scanning that QR code will start activation of the eSIM. Customer stated he will most likely go to the BMW Genius at the dealership for assistance with completing the eSIM setup.
Customer said he was unsure how to enable the vehicle's wifi. Writer advised purchasing a data plan from AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon to use the personal eSIM for calls and wifi. Customer agreed.

Customer inquired about how to turn on the E-sim. Writer advised using the My BMW app, going to the profile picture, then scrolling down to select Personal E-sim and following the prompts to add the E-sim to his Verizon account. Customer then asked what else the E-sim can be used for besides the TV screen. Writer explained it provides the vehicle with its own internet connection that other devices can share, such as a tablet that has no cellular and depends on Wi-Fi. Writer also advised that the E-sim assigns the vehicle a phone number and allows it to place calls without needing a connected cell phone.

on the expressway, the autonomous driving cuts out whenever you go through a curve and basically only stays active on straight sections, so i'd like the accuracy to be improved. the rear seat monitor also has a lot of limitations and ends up being hard to use.
for driving itself, i find the ride comfort excellent, but i still crave the 760, and i would like the option of a four-wheel drive gasoline model.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

the pricing on this car is way too high. i managed to negotiate a strong lease, but there is no chance i would spend the $190k msrp on an electric car that is bound to lose a lot of value. overall the tech is very solid, but bmw still not getting the esim to function correctly is incredibly annoying. one of the main reasons i chose this car was the theatre screen, and now it only operates if i run ugly cables to it. the seats are mostly comfortable, yet they do not give enough side bolster support, so i would really like more hold in the corners. the heated seats and heated armrests are fantastic and the infotainment works well, plus the upgraded sound system is outstanding. when using apple carplay, though, the bottom left corner with distance and time remaining is completely hidden behind my right hand while driving. if i swapped cars today i would rather be in an m5 touring.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

this is a newly released model and it still has some bugs that need to be sorted out. the tech is quite overwhelming, and i am repeatedly having to reset things. the interior lighting setting i prefer keeps changing by itself to a different color. whenever i use the idrive selection tool, it drops down a presets screen each time i touch it, so when i try to choose a new radio station it pulls up those presets instead. the driving assistance functions are hard to locate and adjust, you have to hop from one screen to another. there should be a simple way to temporarily disable these features for things like traffic or going through a car wash. a basic alarm cancel or silence button would be very helpful. the seat controls on the dashboard are awkward to use because you have to lean forward to make adjustments. putting the controls on the seat or the door would be better and would let you sit properly while you fine-tune your seating position.

I still cannot manage to keep my favorite sirius/xm stations set on the radio, even though send works great. my other 7s had a massage function in the driver seat, but for some reason that feature is gone now, and oddly the salesperson said they had never heard of it.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

1. it makes no sense not to have a sunglass holder. my old 740 had one, and in about three months with this car i've already broken two pricey pairs of sunglasses because of this bad design.
2. the app is moody and only seems to work when it feels like it, which is extremely irritating. i plug the car in, ride the garage elevator down, then the office tower elevator up, and the app tells me the car isn't charging. so i head back down the office building, up the garage elevator to the car, and it actually is charging. then i go back down the garage elevator, up the high rise again to my office, call bmw assist, and they say i have to return to the car to troubleshoot…meaning sitting in a hot garage while they poke around and doing the elevator shuffle twice more. forget it…click…that was me ending the call.
3. the air conditioning layout is very unfriendly to use.

the car itself drives well, but there are some things that are just not acceptable, especially the sunglasses issue you've been hearing about for years. if the next one shows up without a sunglass holder, my time at that dealer will be very short before i walk out. the charging quirks are a nuisance and waste my time, so i'll probably just end up guessing when it's actually done charging.

the upgraded bowers wilkins stereo is awful and you should give money back to anyone who had to pay for it. in my earlier bmws with the b&w system it was great. you moved the speakers from under the seats and now it is laughable. everyone who rides in the car comments on the stereo and then i tell them it was a $4,800 upgrade... this might end up being my last bmw. when you turn it up there is basically no bass or mid at all. it sounds terrible, everything just disappears, really sad.
also, you cannot keep the ac on air recirculation or keep the whole climate system synced, it resets every single time you shut the car off. luxury should mean you do not have to keep doing things, but i have to spend about a minute every time i get in the car setting up stuff that should stay the same. ac fan level 2 is way too weak and 3 is too strong and loud. bring back proper air vents.
i am not happy with this purchase and this is my 8th 7 series in around 12 years. i will not renew to this again.

i am happy with the new car. it is clearly more comfortable and in general more interesting than the older series i had. still, there are some drawbacks i really cannot ignore: - once the speed goes past about 110-120 km/h, the car is not well insulated anymore, wind noise becomes obvious and disturbing even though it has the special package. - at night, the driver's main rearview mirror gives a blurry picture, lights from cars behind and strong light sources look smeared, vertical lines show up and this makes driving harder. - the air conditioning will not run when the ignition is switched off. - there is no way to turn off the lights while the car is on (for example if you just want the ac working in a parking lot). - every single time you start driving you have to switch on the battery conservation function again. - the driver has no glove compartment now. before it was located to the left of the steering wheel. there is also no smaller extra glovebox like on the f01. - the driver's joystick/control stick feels very rigid when choosing left/right/up/down. - the driver's seat fails to go back to where it was before the car was shut down. - the cup holders do not offer cooling or heating at all.

i have had this one for about three months now, but i still don't really remember the feeling of sliding in the same model as before. what stands out is how simple it is to control and how it can cruise calmly even when i'm going fast. the price of the car itself feels quite high though. i picked this model because i was willing to pay more in order to get a comfortable drive. originally i chose a 116i f20 for my wife, and the steering on that is outstanding, you can really sense what the driver is feeling. after that, i bought a lexus is as a replacement for a 435i and that was excellent too. then came the 116i m135, which is also strong in power and easy to manage, and now i'm on an x3m competition. i use the m135 around town and the x3mc when i'm going at high speeds.

this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

we have owned bmws for many years, so we are disappointed with our latest 120i m sport, first registered april 2025. we added extra optional kit on top of the standard packages. we have made numerous calls to the dealership about the exterior door handle lighting that is fitted, as we cannot get it programmed and the dealer says they cannot assist. we have found a matching 2025 car without the comfort package where the handles have no lights at all, which makes me think our lights were never coded from new. we have also seen, in certain sunlight, tiny speckles across the front windscreen. we asked about this and were told the dealer needs to view it, but for reasons beyond our control we have not managed to go. we will look forward to your reply.

good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the touchscreen setup is frankly unsafe to use on the move and really needs an idrive wheel to be safer. i don't see why that was removed other than to cut costs. turning off the speed limit and the equally risky lane departure warning is too fiddly, there should be a button for each. the my modes feature in this 120 is almost useless, adding no real driving benefit, just extra complexity and probably cost. the boot is too small for a car of this size. even with these complaints, it still suits my needs perfectly right now, and despite the over-complex tech the interface is still far better than my wife's mercedes a class.

ride comfort is excellent and the power is impressive for a 3-cyl engine. seats are roomy and comfy, and the options are good. road noise is very low for a smaller car, and it compares well to my other car, the m340i, in terms of ride and reduced noise. what we find almost unacceptable is the removal of the gear lever and having nearly everything run through the touchscreen. before, you could start the ventilation with one touch; now you have to aim at the screen twice while driving, which is hard and distracting. all crucial physical buttons need to come back, along with the gear lever. the controls on the previous model were ideal, and it's not clear why they were cut, although it seems obvious it was to save costs.

i have had 7 bmws so far and liked every one of them, but this one is easily the best i have owned. it is a pleasure to drive and i actually look forward to any trip. it can be calm and smooth when i want to relax, but turns into something exciting and fun when i feel like it. despite being a small car it works hard, with a practical and flexible load space. up to now, apart from a puncture, no bmw has ever let me down. it looks great, is comfortable, and the sound system is excellent. the infotainment is very intuitive and functions really well. my only gripe is that connected drive (digital premium) should not be an add-on but built into the price from the start. outstanding customer service from stratstone derby as well.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

evidence.quote: the customer commented that it is really nice being able to run the phone's navigation through wireless apple carplay.
Customer stated she feels very confident and comfortable using Apple Carplay.

Customer stated that running Apple CarPlay and iDrive at the same time is challenging because once CarPlay connects, the iDrive Home button changes into a CarPlay Home button, leaving no simple way to return to the iDrive Home Screen. Writer stated that pressing one of the iDrive shortcut buttons along the left vertical side should open an iDrive app, or if the iDrive Apps Menu button still shows along the bottom edge of the display, he can tap that to view all iDrive apps. Customer stated he wants an easier way to move back and forth between CarPlay and iDrive.

Customer stated wireless CarPlay will occasionally not connect. Customer stated he has had to reboot the phone, remove it from iDrive, then pair it again. Customer stated the issue has not appeared since the latest IOS update. Writer confirmed the phone as iPhone 12 MINI, carrier T-Mobile, IOS 17.6.1. Writer emailed additional troubleshooting steps should the problem come back.

Customer stated they were having difficulty finding their contacts in CarPlay. Writer advised that when the phone is first paired to CarPlay, an option to share contacts appears, and suggested unpairing and then re-pairing CarPlay to view and choose that option.

Customer states she occasionally has trouble connecting to Apple CarPlay. Writer advised performing an iDrive reset when this happens so it can connect properly.

Customer inquired about how to have text messages appear on the vehicle screen when using CarPlay. Writer advised this is probably controlled by a setting in CarPlay, and also noted that the BMW system can display messages. Writer referenced the owner's manual, indicating he can open the Communication menu, then More, then Messages, and choose the desired settings there.

Customer stated he has been experiencing connection problems with his iPhone 14 Pro Max on AT&T staying linked to the vehicle when using Apple CarPlay. Customer stated he plans to have his service department investigate the connection issues while the car is in for a recall. Writer advised that there are specific steps to follow that can help improve the connections. Writer advised: 1) Update the phone to the latest iOS, as phone software (iOS 16.6, 16.6.1) has been causing connection problems in the vehicle. 2) Remove the phone from the vehicle's Mobile Devices menu/app. 3) Remove the vehicle from the phone's Bluetooth menu. 4) Go into the CarPlay section in the phone's general settings and tap Forget This Car. 5) Perform a hard reset (force restart) of the iPhone by: a. pressing and quickly releasing the volume up button, b. pressing and quickly releasing the volume down button, c. pressing and holding the side button, d. releasing the side button when the Apple logo appears. 6) Restart the BMW headunit with a telecommunications reboot: a. make sure the engine or motor is turned on, b. press and hold the volume button for 70 seconds, during which the iDrive screen will turn off and on, and c. once the screen turns off the third time, release the volume button. 7) Confirm that phone Wi-Fi is turned on but not connected to another source. 8) Add the device again in the iDrive Mobile Devices menu/app and follow the prompts between the vehicle and phone. 9) Connect to Apple CarPlay when asked. Writer also emailed these instructions to the customer.

i'd tell people the car itself is worth buying, but i'd steer them away from the dealership. they just come across as pure greed. i really wish there were other choices for getting service and parts done. i tried to buy a set of tpms sensors and they wanted around $180 each, total just over $760, claiming that was basically their cost. seriously? i went online and saw the same sensors sold by other bmw dealers for roughly $100 apiece. feels like they act like they have a monopoly and squeeze you because of it.

about the car, there's some wind noise coming from around the window frame area. also, if you're going to offer the shadow line package, you should make all the exterior badging blacked out too. there's a carplay problem as well: when i play music using the apple music app, the volume is so low that i have to crank it up to around 80 to 90 percent of full just to get a normal listening level. when i use plain bluetooth instead, that issue isn't there.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

Customer stated his iPhone is currently connected to the vehicle through Bluetooth. Customer stated that when he chooses the Apple CarPlay option, a message appears warning that phone features like calls and audio will only be available via CarPlay. Customer asked what this message meant. Writer explained that changing the connection from Bluetooth to Apple CarPlay slightly alters how the system works. Writer stated that Apple CarPlay copies the phone interface but functions separately from the BMW iDrive. Writer stated the warning simply indicates that once you switch to Apple CarPlay, phone calls must be made through the CarPlay interface, not the BMW iDrive, until the connection is changed back to BMW Bluetooth. Customer acknowledged.

after cross-shopping tesla & lucid, this felt way more solidly put together.   i especially like the big range of choices for both exterior and interior.   some of the tech is maddening though - i added carplay to my profile as the secondary driver, and that somehow made my wife's setup go kind of "dead".  the trip computer also has fewer options than on our x5 or 328d - not having several separate "trips" is a real pain when i need to log some of them for work.  we have had several problems with the charge door flap locking up, which means we can't plug in to charge.  even with it set to "never lock" it still happens - this is a serius issue that almost left us stranded!

Customer stated that intermittently when wireless CarPlay connects, the skip track buttons on the steering wheel and center console do not respond. Customer stated the rotary dial will always advance to the next track with a click and never has an issue. Customer stated roughly three out of ten presses on the console and wheel will change the song, but the other seven times they must either use the touchscreen or the dial instead. Writer asked if the iPhone software was current, noting Apple updates frequently, and asked whether the customer had removed the phone from the car and deleted the car from CarPlay settings, then paired again. Customer stated this was already done and the behavior is unchanged. Writer documented that the customer uses an iPhone 16 Pro Max running iOS 26.5, which is the latest version, and the vehicle is on software 26-03-530.

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

the car is extremely smooth and quiet, unlike my earlier bmws. controls are straightforward, and the mix of performance and luxury is really well done. my other evs lacked a sun roof, so having one on the i5 is a big plus. the only real downside is the awful carplay audio behavior: most of the time i need the radio volume at max just to hear normally, then an incoming call can be super loud and the whole system ends up blaring because it is already turned up. lots of people online describe the same issue, and while some suggested fixes help for a while, the low volume problem keeps coming back.

Customer explained he uses hearing aids that pair to his phone via Bluetooth. Customer stated that sometimes when he is wearing them, they will end up connecting to the vehicle and he hears all of the vehicle sounds and audio through the hearing aids. Customer mentioned that he was not wearing the hearing aids at the time of the call.
Customer stated they appreciate having wireless Apple CarPlay, since it lets them connect without needing a cord and avoids plugging the phone in.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

the car rides amazingly smoothly, with superb handling and strong acceleration, really the ultimate driving machine. i like the styling inside and out and am glad i basically went with a fully loaded version. the kids love theater mode, and it lets me watch tv while i am at a charging station.

improvement areas are small: i would like more battery range, with around 350 miles or more on a full charge. the interactive screen setup works well but feels like it has almost too many choices, so it can take longer than i would like to get to what i need. finally, bluetooth and wifi are not always reliable, and roughly 20% of the time my phone cannot see the car wifi so carplay will not work.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

i have only had my bmw for a few months and already ran into several issues:
i) at just under 1,100 miles the check engine light came on, and i had to leave the car at the bmw dealer in portville so they could fix a part that had dropped into the air intake, gotten stuck there, and was making the engine run too hot.
ii) later the rear passenger seat belt got jammed up and tangled inside the retract system, so the vehicle had to go back to the same bmw dealer for repair and for them to reinstall the belt.
iii) this morning when i got in, i noticed a crack in the glass roof; i have reached out to the bmw dealer and am now waiting for an appointment to bring it in for that repair.

in just these few months the car will have been in the shop 3 times :(

Customer stated she had dash problems in her previous X6 and chose the 7 Series thinking a more premium model would be free of such issues, but the same type of problem is happening. Customer stated the dash display went completely black around three times before she brought the car to the dealer about a month ago, where they performed a system enhancement/update (current i-level 25-07-551, i-level ex works 25-03-536, update pending for i-level 25-03-545) and advised this would resolve the concern. Customer stated the screen still went black again about four days ago, so the vehicle is scheduled to go back to the dealer on Friday 10/24. Customer stated the screen has always come back on after each blackout, but she does not feel safe driving the vehicle, has mostly left it parked in the garage, and is nervous about taking it on trips out of town. Customer stated a $100,000 car should not be experiencing these kinds of problems and asked to be moved into another comparable vehicle that does not have them. PER SIB: 65 35 24, PROGRAMMED VEHICLE TO LATEST I-LEVEL DUE TO HEADUNIT SOFTWARE ERROR. TEST DROVE TO VERIFY REPAIR, OPERATING AS DESIGNED.

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

this is a newly released model and it still has some bugs that need to be sorted out. the tech is quite overwhelming, and i am repeatedly having to reset things. the interior lighting setting i prefer keeps changing by itself to a different color. whenever i use the idrive selection tool, it drops down a presets screen each time i touch it, so when i try to choose a new radio station it pulls up those presets instead. the driving assistance functions are hard to locate and adjust, you have to hop from one screen to another. there should be a simple way to temporarily disable these features for things like traffic or going through a car wash. a basic alarm cancel or silence button would be very helpful. the seat controls on the dashboard are awkward to use because you have to lean forward to make adjustments. putting the controls on the seat or the door would be better and would let you sit properly while you fine-tune your seating position.

the car drives really well, but i'm seeing a few software issues. the auto close and auto open funciton when using the phone as a digital key is super annoying, and there should be a way to fully shut those off at home. right now you can only turn off the "unlock" feature at home, which feels like a simple software change. other very frustrating things are needing to dig through menus and multiple screens just to adjust the seat or even change the cruise control distance. that's annoying and honestly dangerous, because you end up scrolling menus instead of using a simple physical button in the car. another bad software problem is that there's no personal, fully customizable drive mode like porsche "individual" settings, so you're stuck with whatever the default programming is. another issue is the roof glass cracking after about two weeks of owning it, confirmed by lakeside bmw, and now it's waiting for repair that will take around two months for parts and work at a body shop. meanwhile we're driving around with a cracked roof glass that feels like it could eventually shatter and drop onto everyone in the car while driving.

the car is very comfortable and feels up to date, but i have had way too many issues in a short period. i like the interior styling, yet a lot of the nice features are buried and take forever to access. there really should be simple buttons to open and close all doors. the lower door switch on the driver side is placed horribly, my knee has hit it multiple times and the door has popped open while driving. the fuel door refused to open when i was around 340 miles from home, and bmw roadside told me to just tear it off because they had no other solution. i have also gotten warning lights for the emergency contact system with no cause the dealer could identify. all of this has happened within the 3 months i have owned the car. my 2020 740ix had both keys quit working when i was roughly 70 miles from home, and nobody could explain why. i currently own 3 bmw and lease 2 more, and i am starting to lose faith in your products.

i'm really unhappy with the self driving functions on this car. i paid more for this 7 series than for my previous one and ended up with fewer features. i believed it came with automatic traffic stop-and-go where it would handle heavy traffic on its own, and also with automatic lane change assist. right after picking up the car, i called the bmw genius for help, and after checking how the car was equipped they said those features should be there. they told me to go by a bmw dealership, so we stopped at one in riverside sc. the genius there said the car would need to stay at a dealer to be reprogrammed, but i couldn't leave it because i was only there briefly for business. i then booked service at a bmw store in bayport fl near our place in lakeside, and they held the car for 24 hours without a tech actually looking at it, then told me it was user error. during all of this i was waiting on a call from a bmw supervisor to sort things out. when i got back from fl, i left the car with my dealer in westfield ct, and after their troubleshooting they said the vehicle simply does not have those features and they can't be added. getting to that conclusion was extremely frustrating. in the end, it was my mistake for buying a car straight off the lot, not really knowing what equipment it had, and assuming i would end up with fewer features than the one i turned in.

Customer stated the car has excellent technology.
Customer explained the only hiccup he has had with the car was needing to reboot iDrive by holding the radio volume knob so his phone would reconnect, which he considered just a minor inconvenience.

Customer reported that at times the screen will suddenly go black while driving. Customer indicated this occurs randomly with no prior warning. Customer stated the display typically comes back by itself after a few minutes, or he can press the Home button and the screen will return. overall it has been a fantastic car so far. i really like the configuration and the level of luxury, and the build feels very solid. it definitely turns heads and has a strong presence on the road, and i enjoy how it drives. my only gripes are with the software. the app itself is excellent, but idrive gives me trouble. a few things are minor but irritating, like my home screen widgets randomly vanishing so i have to re-add them. the main headache is the esim randomly refusing to activate. i do not hold this against the car itself, as it seems like something that could be fixed with an ota update rather than a hardware issue. still, it is a very frustrating bug, and the only way around it has been to cancel my ubigi plan and start over, which results in double billing. please get this fixed asap!

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

title: G70 Electric Range
requirement_statement: Improve 'Electric Range' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 35 respondents complain and 19 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.

evidence.quote: Customer explained he is pleased with the battery range, as it covers his weekly commuting and he only needs to charge the vehicle about once a week.
