from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

Customer stated this is their first electric vehicle, so they initially assumed they would experience range anxiety. Customer stated that being able to charge at home means they rarely ever need to visit public charging stations, as the range is adequate for their everyday driving.
Customer stated that one of the reasons for trading in his Audi e-tron was the longer electric range on this vehicle.

Customer stated that at the moment a full charge displays around 265 miles, whereas more recently it had been showing about 285 miles. Customer stated the dealer advertised a 315 mile range, and if he does not get close to that he will be upset, as he would not have bought a car that only offers around 265 miles per full charge. Writer advised that the vehicle's estimated range depends on how it is being driven. Customer stated his previous Tesla never behaved that way and would always show 350 miles whenever it was charged to full.

I had a very serious problem with EV - Range gauge is inaccurate: "The range display is unpredictable. After charging, the car showed 293 miles in efficient mode, then I drove roughly 4 miles home that evening. The next day, after the car had been parked for about 24 hours, I drove around 12 miles and the range dropped to 248. I then parked for roughly 2 1/2 hours, drove about 6 miles, parked again for another 2 1/2 hours and finally drove back home for around 15 miles. So altogether under efficient mode I drove about 37 miles, but the remaining range showed only 218 miles, which means it counted this as 76 miles driven, more than double the actual miles from the first reading after charging."

the auto time zone adjustment just does not function. the radio also fails to quiet when i give carplay voice commands. with a 291 mile range, the actual distance i can use is heavily cut because i only charge between 20% and 80%. right now the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available. every leg of a trip easily ends up with an extra hour added for each charging stop. i still dont know for sure, but if the battery life really proves to be just 8 years then this purchase will have been a poor investment. my insurance premium has shot up by about 200% even though the car has all this safety equipment. the explanation given is that repairing that safety tech after a crash costs a lot more, and the insurers claim there is not enough data yet to justify lowering the rates. sun glare or heavy rain seem to mess with the cameras trying to read the surroundings, and then the system basically chooses to shut itself off because it sees too much risk. when i drive on a road running parallel to train tracks, and a side street that crosses those tracks comes up, the railroad crossing lights aimed at the train get misread by the car as a stop light intended for my parallel road. there is also one set of traffic signals that the car reads as if they were a yield sign. the navigation does not let me set a preference for electrify america chargers when the planned distance exceeds the current charge; it just picks the first charger it finds. for at least the first 3 years, that electrify america selection option really should be there.

Customer stated it seems like the battery is dying quickly. Writer asked if he is preconditioning the vehicle before leaving for the day. Customer stated he currently does not have a home charging station because he is waiting for construction on his house to be finished. Writer advised that using climate control is probably what is hurting the range. Writer advised that once he has a home charger, it is recommended to precondition while the vehicle is plugged in before leaving, so a lot of battery is not wasted on cooling or heating the car. Writer advised this will be one factor that helps the range. Customer stated his salesperson had also explained this and several other details about the range.

Customer noted that when he first bought the vehicle, the Electric Range in the instrument cluster showed "300 miles" on a full charge, but now it shows "290 miles" fully charged. Writer explained the Electric Range is an estimate calculated by the car using past driving data. Customer stated the vehicle is trying to show him how much range he will realistically get based on his driving style and driving efficiency.

we absolutely love our i7. it rides so smoothly, looks really elegant, is packed with cool technology, and the real world range is quite good. we use it both for business and personal needs. we shuttle clients, mostly physicians at a clinic, and they are very impressed with the car and really like that it is an ev.

my spouse and i enjoy taking it everywhere. we have put close to 4800 miles on it in about 3 months, and it hardly feels like that much. it is a joy to drive on longer road trips.

there are a couple of things i would change. the subwoofer seems like it should be placed somewhere in the cabin. i think there is an upgraded diamond surround system that might add this. i owned a 2016 m5 before, and the bass in that car was just right. a friend has a 2024 ix, and i was amazed by the sound system in his.

ours is carbon black, so it gets washed often. one thing i noticed is that the rear trunk lid, especially the area under the rear bmw badge, traps a lot of water and it drains slowly. when it finally drains, it runs down onto the rear bumper and leaves water spots. we even use a blow dryer and it still causes some hassle. every car has its quirks, so i am not overly concerned.

also, i feel like the master window controls on the driver door should be moved back about 1-2 inches. even after 3 months, i still end up opening the rear windows when i mean to open the fronts. the placement feels unnatural. i'm 6 feet tall and have never really run into this in another vehicle.

overall, i really love this car and already look forward to owning another one someday. thanks for making such a gem of a vehicle.

ours is carbon black, so it gets washed often. one thing i noticed is that the rear trunk lid, especially the area under the rear bmw badge, traps a lot of water and it drains slowly. when it finally drains, it runs down onto the rear bumper and leaves water spots. we even use a blow dryer and it still causes some hassle. every car has its quirks, so i am not overly concerned.

also, i feel like the master window controls on the driver door should be moved back about 1-2 inches. even after 3 months, i still end up opening the rear windows when i mean to open the fronts. the placement feels unnatural. i'm 6 feet tall and have never really run into this in another vehicle.

overall, i really love this car and already look forward to owning another one someday. thanks for making such a gem of a vehicle.

Customer stated he would like a higher capacity battery so he could have more Electric Range and need to chareg less often.
Customer stated he would prefer the vehicle to have greater driving range.

Customer stated there is a major gap between the advertised charging range and what he actually gets in cold conditions, explaining that in cold weather operation the range drops by roughly 40 percent.

Customer stated he feels the available electric range is more than sufficient.

Customer stated he is struggling to understand what advantages the integrated electric motor actually provides. Customer reported getting just 30 miles of electric range, and said that by the time he drives to downtown the battery is already drained.
Customer mentioned he is very pleased with the amount of driving range the vehicle provides. Customer added that, on some occasions, he is able to get as much as 400 miles.

Customer stated the range seems designed more for someone who does a lot of city driving and has a short commute. Customer stated he drives a fair amount for his commute and as a result finds himself at charging stations all the time.

evidence.quote: Customer would like a way to turn off the auto start-stop permanently.

Customer indicated he wants to eliminate the auto start stop feature. Writer asked why, and Customer explained that the engine cuts out before he actually comes to a full stop at a light, which feels too early. Writer then went over how he can disable it for a drive by using sport mode and the drivetrain settings.
I had a problem with Automatic engine stop-start problem: "The auto stop/start feels harsh and jolts the whole car when it fires back up, unlike prior models that were smoother."

Customer stated that if he had the choice, he would change how the auto start-stop works. Customer commented that the system does not feel as smooth as he would like when pulling away, and that he notices the way it turns off and back on. Writer explained that besides turning off the MSA for that drive, there is also an Auto H button located near the start-stop button that the customer should try the next time he is in the car. Writer went over the Auto H, or auto hold, function and described how, when the vehicle is brought to a stop, it will remain stopped even after the driver lifts their foot off the brake pedal, and will only move once the accelerator pedal is pressed. Writer gave the example of sitting at a red light and asked the customer to see whether the car stays stationary or begins to roll ahead when the brake pedal is released before pressing the accelerator. Writer instructed the customer to check for a green light on the Auto H button and stated that a quick press will switch the feature off. Writer clarified that this feature is very useful in stop-and-go traffic, drive-throughs and similar situations where the driver wants to take their foot off the brake while the vehicle remains stopped until the accelerator is used. Writer also noted that auto hold can sometimes lead to slightly jerky movements when parking and suggested this could be playing a role in the smoothness concern the customer mentioned.
The customer mentioned he wishes there were an option to permanently turn off the engine stop start function.

I had a serious problem with Automatic engine stop-start - Controls DTU/poorly located: "I hate it and wish the car didnt even include that "feature". (Copied from FCD97): Auto start/stop really bothers me, and it is frustrating to have to switch it off every single time I get in. Also, I cant use Bimmercode like I did on my 2018 530i, which is a major issue for me. I really enjoyed being able to code settings that werent available in the dashboard menu."
I had a minor problem with Automatic engine stop-start - Controls DTU/poorly located: "I would like to shut this feature off for good but cant. I have to disable it every time I start the car. Ugh."

Customer stated she would prefer having an option to totally turn off the auto start stop function. Customer stated she drives mostly within the city, so being able to simply disable it entirely would be ideal for her.

I had a very serious problem with Automatic engine stop-start - Controls DTU/poorly located: "This feature has no off button, and when I am pulling into an intersection there is often a hesitation because it is always on. I really hate it and it is my biggest complaint about the car."

Customer stated he is unhappy with the auto engine start stop feature. Customer reported it feels rough and makes the whole car shudder when the engine comes back on. Customer acknowledged it is intended to help with fuel economy and emissions, but said he ends up using sport mode to prevent the engine from shutting off, which he feels uses more fuel. Writer recommended trying sport individual with all options set to comfort as a workaround. Customer advised he already tried that and when the engine setting is in comfort the engine still stops, so he feels the workaround is pointless. Customer commented he is so frustrated with this change that he is thinking about selling the car and switching to a different brand. Customer added that overall he really likes the car, but he strongly dislikes the way the engine turns off.

Customer stated he would prefer to have the auto engine start stop turned off permanently. Customer stated his prior vehicles always had an option to do this. Customer stated the auto engine start-stop feature leads to a not-smooth transition when the vehicle stops and then starts again. Writer explained that the vehicle is a mild hybrid with an electric motor designed to assist with those transitions, but the customer maintained it is still not as smooth as he would like.
Customer stated they would like the automatic stop/start to be disabled permanently so they do not need to shut it off each time they get in the vehicle.

Customer stated he is unhappy that there is no option to switch off the automatic engine start stop on this vehicle. Writer advised that the override is no longer included because the car is now a Mild Hybrid, with an electric motor that helps move the vehicle when the combustion engine shuts down. Customer stated he already understood the Mild Hybrid setup. Customer stated his concern with the engine turning off so often comes from having had 3 different BMWs in the past that needed motor mounts replaced. Customer stated his service center had told him the auto engine start stop feature was what caused those motor mounts to wear out faster.

Customer stated this vehicle does not have an override button for the auto engine stop start function and that he misses that feature from his 2021 5 series. Customer stated he runs the vehicle in sport mode to work around this. Writer advised that this model has an electric motor that assists when the combustion engine turns off, and that the override button was removed for that reason. Writer explained the motor helps with acceleration and should make the transition when the engine stops feel smoother than his 2021. Customer stated it does in fact feel smoother.

Customer stated her prior vehicle had a button to turn off the automatic start stop feature, and she has not found that button in this car. Writer explained that the shut off option has been removed. Writer explained the only workaround is to drive in Sport mode, which will disable automatic start stop, but it must be set to Sport mode every time the vehicle is started. Customer indicated she understood.

Customer stated that in his last BMW there was a button to turn off auto start stop, but he cannot find one in this model. Customer asked if there is any way to switch it off. Writer advised this is only possible by driving in sport mode.
Customer mentioned they would really like to have an option to completely disable MSA.

Customer stated they would prefer a specific button for MSA. Customer mentioned they do not want to switch the vehicle into Sport Mode only to turn off MSA, as they feel that could put extra stress on the drivetrain. Writer advised that Sport Mode can be personalized and that all settings within Sport can be changed to Comfort. Customer was very pleased with this guidance.

i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.

Customer stated that when he is driving in Efficient Mode, he always switches off Auto Start/Stop but it still seems like the car is shutting off. Writer asked if he notices this with any of the other Driving Modes. Customer stated no, he sets it to Efficient Mode every time he drives. Writer asked how he is turning Auto Start/Stop off. Customer stated that when he gets in, he presses the MY Modes button, selects Efficient Mode on the screen, then swipes down from the right side of the display and taps the Auto Start/Stop icon in the upper right corner to disable it. Customer was very clear that he repeats this process every time he starts a trip. Writer asked if he could go out to the car, but customer stated he could not. Writer advised that on the Instrument Cluster there is a power gauge on the right side of the display, and when Auto Start/Stop is still active and he is stopped, it will show 0 or Ready. Customer confirmed this. Customer mentioned the dealership Genius had offered to come to his home for a tutorial. Writer advised that they would normally schedule an RVG session, but in this particular case it would likely work better for the Genius to sit in the car with him so he can feel it and see it together.
Customer stated that when the auto off engages, it shuts the air-conditioning off.

no acc stop & go option in the connected drive store. i picked this car from dealer stock and really hate that it came without acc. you can tell the hardware can see traffic ahead, since it recognizes a vehicle in front while in efficient mode to trigger regen.

overall the car is very nice, but i'm not a fan of losing all the buttons and knobs and having to dig through the computer to find things. auto start/stop should either be gone or at least have a way to turn it off permanently. the fact there is no automatic mode for the fan speed, so you have to keep adjusting it by hand in an 85k car, is hard to accept. the build quality in general could be better. older bmw models had a solid, satisfying "clunk" when you closed the door, but now it sounds much more tinny and lightweight. the details show the quality, and small defects jump out, like plastic pieces that don't quite fit right or don't completely wrap around what they are supposed to.

this is my 5th bmw vehicle.
all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:
550i
540i
740i
550i
now a 530i
i realize i am now in the regular 5 series, which i chose because, in my view, quality and functionality have gone backwards overall. that is not just about this 530 compared to those older cars.
my issues are:
run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series
2) air conditioning feels downgraded and not strong enough for south texas heat
3) ac/vent fan is too noisy except on the lowest level. with the fan high, you basically cant talk on the phone.
4) auto stop/start, but the driver does not have simple, effective full control to switch it off.
5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced
6) not enough storage. the small latched compartment by the driver is gone, there is a phone charging pad instead of extra storage depth (should be removable), and the glove box is limited and does not work well.
7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

no proper gear shifter, just that goofy little switch, and the controls are a pain to work with. half the settings don't stay put after i shut off the ignition. the retractable steering wheel doesn't slide back by itself when i turn the car off and open the door. ac won't hold the recirc setting, it changes once the car is turned off, same annoyance. also really dumb that the engine "off" at stops got deleted. the on/off button is crammed next to other buttons so you might kill the engine at the wrong time. simple buttons would do a better job for changing drive modes than that silly dial and the touch screen. the car feels too bulky and wide, which makes parking more of a chore. in sport mode the mpg drops from about 34 to around 28, yet the sport mode doesn't feel all that spirited. the sport seat hugging you is fantastic but it only happens in sport mode. cleaning the windshield is awkward because the wipers don't pull away far enough. the warning system for people approaching the car from any direction isn't sensitive enough, so i have to stare around a lot more. 

the good bits are the automatic backup feature, really useful given how big the car is, and the b & w stereo, miles better than the karmon-hardin setup, plus this one came with normal tires instead of run flats! that sport seat wrap that grabs you is excellent, just a shame it only "shows up" in sport mode.

against my old 68 plate 520i, this one pulls quicker and uses less fuel. i really like the head up display and the new main screen, and the journey fuel info is handy. adaptive cruise itself works fine, but changing the gap to the car ahead while driving is awkward, especially when i want more distance in the wet. lane control helps. sat nav overall is good, yet the traffic delay icons/text are tiny and digging into that info on the move is hard, plus minor roads are shown too faintly. spotify is well integrated, simple to use and looks good. downside is the road noise, which is much louder on some surfaces and basically drowns out the audio. the speed limit warning drives me mad and is often wrong. i also want to keep the car in efficient mode without having to set it again every single journey.

i've been driving a 530 for more than 9 years now. the last 3 were leased, and this 2024 is on a select finance plan. i've had it around 3 months and i still really love the car, but it doesn't feel different enough to justify the much higher payment…about $200 more every month. the sticker price of the car is basically the same as the previous one, which seems crazy to me.
one thing i really valued before was the run flat tires, and now that feature is gone. also, on the last 3 cars i never once got a computer error, but on this one i had an engine malfunction warning in under 2 months, which really scared me. luckily it turned out to be just a glitch that needs a computer update, and i'm getting that done this week.
the ride is still fantastic and i really like the big screen. so giving it an "8" feels about right.

i'm really happy with my new bmw overall. the one thing that bothers me is trying to learn all the different options on the video screen. i also am not a fan of these door handles and liked the ones on my 2011 bmw 528i much better. another annoyance is that the driver and passenger climate controls don't automatically sync like they did in my old bmw. most of the time i'm driving alone and it's irritating that the cabin temperatures aren't synced by default. if i have someone with me, they can change their own setting, but i feel the automatic sync should be the main preference. i'm still working out how to enter navigation addresses, it was much simpler with the old dial system in my 2011 bmw. i've also found the trunk very hard to open with my foot under the rear of the car; i don't know if there's some trick to it, but it only opens maybe 10% of the times i try.

for me and my husband, who does most of the driving, the biggest negative is having nearly all the controls on the touch screen. we just can't remember every symbol for everything. a lot of them we still don't recognize and feel like we need to go back to see a genius again. we are also worried that there are no more run flat tires. we still haven't figured out how the tire flat inflator actually works. the sport vs regular gearing feels too far apart. in normal drive, the a/c airflow gets too low whenever we sit in traffic or at a red light, which is hard to deal with in southern florida where it's always hot. on the plus side, the outside and inside look very beautiful. the seats are very comfortable, but we miss having the back seat pockets and spots to store things.
the way it drives is very smooth and comfortable.

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

the car gives me the comfort, luxury, and performance i'm looking for, with just a few minor quirks that i hope can be fixed in a software update. the auto stop start setting is buried too far down in the control menus and really should be right on the home screen. also, the interior door opener handles are hard to find in the dark. the led that now lights the door armrest should be moved behind the release handle so you can easily see it in low light, or another led should be added behind the handle. smaller annoyances are not being able to set the ambient lighting to anything other than "personal" and not being able to have "sport" as the default start-up mode. and please, make a spare tire kit standard.

every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

Writer advised that by scrolling through the instrument cluster display options, one of the views shows the odometer. Customer confirmed.
Customer stated they would like the speed limit indication on their display to be more accurate, as it is wrong more often than not.

Customer stated he could not figure out how to view the vehicle mileage other than in the My BMW app. Writer advised using the steering wheel button to adjust the content shown in the instrument cluster. Writer advised pressing the gear icon and selecting vehicle status to display the mileage. Customer acknowledged.

Customer stated that when he is driving, he typically sees a very nice screen in the instrument cluster that shows how efficiently he is driving and how much range he is gaining through regenerative braking. Customer stated he has not been able to locate this particular view on his own by going through the different display layouts and content options. Writer asked where he sees this view appear. Writer also asked if the customer mainly drives in Efficient mode, and the customer confirmed that he does. Writer stated that this view is tied specifically to that driving mode. Writer stated that, to their knowledge, there is not a way to store this as a permanent view in the instrument cluster. Writer stated that it is only available while driving in Efficient mode. Customer acknowledged.

the car handles incredibly well. it feels very responsive and nimble, and the ride quality is good,
even when driving in wet weather.
i also appreciate the overall size of the vehicle - there is generous interior room in both the front and back, and the trunk is quite large.
for future upgrades, the in-car clock is really tiny - a bigger display would be better for us older drivers. also, the direction indicator (showing north, south, east, west) only appears off and on. in the cadillac i traded in, the clock face was a comfortable size and the direction display was visible all the time.
i have also found parts of the tech for the radio/sirius/spotify and car play to be difficult and a bit hard to figure out.

Customer stated she used to see the trip data and odometer by pressing the BC button on the turn signal, and now she cannot figure out how to bring them up. Customer stated the instrument cluster currently offers four different layout options for the speedometer and tachometer, but all of them use a similar vertical bar-style format. Customer stated they would prefer having other choices, such as a more traditional round speedometer disc layout implemented with LED or digital technology rather than analog. Customer stated this should be simple to achieve with modern technology and would allow for more intuitive, quick readability. Customer stated that, because the existing dashboard display is not intuitive to them, they generally avoid using it and instead depend on the heads-up display.

Customer stated that she is still becoming familiar with all the technology in the vehicle. Customer stated it took her a while to figure out where to find the vehicle's odometer.

Customer advised he was interested in viewing his total miles rather than the remaining fuel range. Writer advised she was unable to go over this with the customer at that time because he needed to end the call due to time limitations, but she set up a return call. Writer advised she attempted the callback and was not able to get in touch with the customer.
Customer asked about the two icons on the lower left of the dashboard. Writer explained one means the headlights are on, and the other shows Auto High Beams are active.

Customer stated that when he is driving in eco mode there is a bar on the instrument cluster that changes colors. Customer asked what the different colors indicate and what the bar represents. Writer advised customer that this is the efficiency trainer. Writer explained that when the number and bar are Blue he is driving efficiently. Writer explained that when it turns grey the driving is inefficient. Writer further advised that an arrow can appear to show inefficient driving, for example when accelerating too much or driving at excessive speed. Customer acknowledged.

Customer mentioned he is unclear what the combined mileage figure above the battery charge gauge represents when in efficient mode and said he was unable to locate an explanation in the owners manual. Customer also described confusion about the range indicator that only shows up in efficient mode. Writer clarified that this display represents added range gained in efficient driving mode, combining both electric and fuel range.

Customer explained they know there are multiple dash display views and intend to go back to the dealer to review the different layouts. Writer offered support. Customer added they were in a different vehicle during the conversation and will return to the dealer for help at another time.

Customer stated they had trouble viewing and resetting the trip odometer and felt the system was over-engineered for their needs. Writer explained using the steering wheel knuckle button to access and reset the trip data in the instrument panel display. Customer stated frustration that prior explanations were too complicated and required going through multiple screens.

Customer stated they had trouble finding the control for the vehicle computer data, like mileage, on the 530i, since it is not like their former i5 M60. Writer advised it is reached using the gear spinny button on the steering wheel, which opens a menu when pressed and lets them adjust the instrument cluster and dash layout.

3. steering doesn't really transmit much feel from the road.
so this is probably the last bmw i'm going to purchase.

title: G60 My Modes / driving experience
requirement_statement: Improve 'My Modes / driving experience' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 32 respondents complain and 27 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated that she really enjoys how sporty and nimble this vehicle feels, especially when she compares it to her former X5.

Customer asked what the difference is between S Mode and Sport Mode. Writer explained that S Mode is the sequential setting, where you shift manually with the paddle shifters. Writer further advised that Sport Mode keeps the automatic transmission. Customer confirmed understanding.

Customer was unsure how the various modes operate and what their purposes are. Writer explained that personal mode functions as the standard mode and is the one that provides the highest level of customization for the vehicle settings. Writer further noted that sport mode, which the customer already knew about, is geared toward delivering increased performance response. Writer then clarified that efficient mode is essentially the previous eco pro mode, intended to be the most economy focused. Writer added that the other available modes mainly adjust styling elements and are primarily aesthetic or design related.

no proper gear shifter, just that goofy little switch, and the controls are a pain to work with. half the settings don't stay put after i shut off the ignition. the retractable steering wheel doesn't slide back by itself when i turn the car off and open the door. ac won't hold the recirc setting, it changes once the car is turned off, same annoyance. also really dumb that the engine "off" at stops got deleted. the on/off button is crammed next to other buttons so you might kill the engine at the wrong time. simple buttons would do a better job for changing drive modes than that silly dial and the touch screen. the car feels too bulky and wide, which makes parking more of a chore. in sport mode the mpg drops from about 34 to around 28, yet the sport mode doesn't feel all that spirited. the sport seat hugging you is fantastic but it only happens in sport mode. cleaning the windshield is awkward because the wipers don't pull away far enough. the warning system for people approaching the car from any direction isn't sensitive enough, so i have to stare around a lot more. 

the good bits are the automatic backup feature, really useful given how big the car is, and the b & w stereo, miles better than the karmon-hardin setup, plus this one came with normal tires instead of run flats! that sport seat wrap that grabs you is excellent, just a shame it only "shows up" in sport mode.

overall i really like my new 540i xdrive, and as i'm still figuring out all the features, i'm very pleased with the size, styling, and overall design. i picked the msport package and love the sportier, more aggressive look, especially the way the lines on the front hood flow up to the bmw badge. i've been using personal mode most of the time and wish there were a more comfort-oriented setting within personal mode. i often need the car to stay running with the a/c on while i quickly go into the office or a grocery store, and i still haven't found a way to keep it on and locked without leaving the key inside. fit and finish, with the tight tolerances, are so far what i expect from bmw. the steering feels a bit lighter than the traditional bmw dna. all in all, i'm satisfied with the car so far.

really like the tech in the car and the overall fit and finish. i keep wishing there were an i4 variant that felt this quiet and this smooth (i really enjoy the i5 but it is a little on the big side for my daily commute - i chose it because it is much more comfortable. i have driven the i4 a lot and enjoy it, but it feels more like a sport car). my single design gripe is that at night the interaction light bar throws a reflection onto the driver side window, right across the line of sight to the driver side mirror - this clearly feels like an oversight. i now run the light bar at its lowest brightness at night so the problem is just bearable. the drive modes are nice, but i would really like a way to hide or delete some of the silly ones (like expressive or artistic) to make it simpler to pick the few i actually use. overall though, it is a gorgeous car and i am genuinely happy to be driving a bmw again!

for me and my husband, who does most of the driving, the biggest negative is having nearly all the controls on the touch screen. we just can't remember every symbol for everything. a lot of them we still don't recognize and feel like we need to go back to see a genius again. we are also worried that there are no more run flat tires. we still haven't figured out how the tire flat inflator actually works. the sport vs regular gearing feels too far apart. in normal drive, the a/c airflow gets too low whenever we sit in traffic or at a red light, which is hard to deal with in southern florida where it's always hot. on the plus side, the outside and inside look very beautiful. the seats are very comfortable, but we miss having the back seat pockets and spots to store things.
the way it drives is very smooth and comfortable.

overall the experience has been very positive, the tech feels solid and the highway "self-driving" is much better than the last generation. i would like finer control over the sport mode settings. i also want clearer guidance on how to use the engine when coming off battery mode, including proper warm up time. on long drives, i'd like to hold back some battery for later while still using a bit during the trip for boost, but the current programming does not seem to support that. i realize that means more complexity and instructions, but i think many bmw owners are fine with that, and i want to get the most out of how the battery and engine work together. i came from an n63, now with a b58, and while i know they are different, the b58 sometimes sounds like it's really working even when i'm not revving it much. is that extra sound being pumped in, and is that really what i want to be hearing? i'd rather hear a confident engine than one that sounds like it's straining. also, instead of having to pay for an esim subscription, why can't the car just use my phone's hotspot for things like the youtube app.

Customer stated he forgot how to engage sport mode in the vehicle. Writer advised that to use sport mode he should press the My modes button on the center console and then choose sport.

Customer asked what exactly is altered when selecting sport mode and whether the suspension would be affected. Writer advised that sport mode modifies the vehicle's performance, providing quicker acceleration and more responsive, tighter steering. Writer further stated that the suspension in this vehicle will not change.
Customer mentioned she really enjoys the various drive modes.
Customer stated he would like the option to customize the driving settings in Personal mode, in the same way adjustments can be made for Sport mode.

Customer stated they are disappointed with how the hybrid drivetrain is set up, because from a stop the car will use only full electric in Electric mode, or only the gas engine with no help from the battery unless the boost function is activated. Customer stated that in Hybrid mode it begins moving the heavy vehicle using just the battery before the engine comes on. Customer stated they would like a hybrid mode similar to the M5 that can deliver full electric and gas engine power together all the time without needing to press the boost function.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

the power, the quick response and the way this car drives are all exceptional. a trip in this m60 would probably convert even a hardcore skeptic who doubts how strong an electric car can be. i am absolutely satisfied with the cabin and with how it drives.

sadly, i placed the order without ever seeing an m60 live. i am let down by how the front grille looks. i much prefer the more "classic bmw" front of the normal i5 edrive40 models - i wanted the m60 for the all wheel drive and the dual battery setup, but i really do not care for the odd grille design. if it were possible, i would change it.

my earlier i5 had massaging seats, and that is not offered on these electric versions. that is a big disappointment because that was a feature i enjoyed a lot on my last bmw.

the car gives me the comfort, luxury, and performance i'm looking for, with just a few minor quirks that i hope can be fixed in a software update. the auto stop start setting is buried too far down in the control menus and really should be right on the home screen. also, the interior door opener handles are hard to find in the dark. the led that now lights the door armrest should be moved behind the release handle so you can easily see it in low light, or another led should be added behind the handle. smaller annoyances are not being able to set the ambient lighting to anything other than "personal" and not being able to have "sport" as the default start-up mode. and please, make a spare tire kit standard.

the "driving machine" part really is "ultimate", but the infotainment setup badly needs some refinements. bmw seems to have no real way for owners to send in feedback or ideas to fix the counterintuitive parts of the system, and the geniuses at the dealer told me there isn't any channel for that.
one specific problem is the auto lock/unlock when you come up to the car or walk away. that function is great anywhere except at home. in my garage i'm walking past the car over and over while i work, and each time it goes on and off repeatedly. that cannot be good for the car, and the only way i could stop it was to switch the entire feature off.
this exact issue shows up as a common complaint online, and i found out that i-drive 8.5 has a setting to disable the comfort access "at home" only. that would be a perfect fix, but when i tried to change my settings so i could actually enjoy the feature i paid for, i discovered it only exists on 8.5 in the 7-series, not on the same 8.5 in my 5-series.
for me that is a real "deal-breaker". bmw is aware, or absolutely should be, that this is a problem. they clearly already have a solution, but 5-series owners are blocked from using it. i have a whole list of other issues and would gladly go over them with someone who truly cares. they're simple, common-sense fixes i'd provide for free... if there were any line of communication.

this exact issue shows up as a common complaint online, and i found out that i-drive 8.5 has a setting to disable the comfort access "at home" only. that would be a perfect fix, but when i tried to change my settings so i could actually enjoy the feature i paid for, i discovered it only exists on 8.5 in the 7-series, not on the same 8.5 in my 5-series.
for me that is a real "deal-breaker". bmw is aware, or absolutely should be, that this is a problem. they clearly already have a solution, but 5-series owners are blocked from using it. i have a whole list of other issues and would gladly go over them with someone who truly cares. they're simple, common-sense fixes i'd provide for free... if there were any line of communication.

after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

i had a bmw 3 series and then a 5 series for many years, then went to the bmw i3 as my first ev, and after that switched over to a tesla model 3. as much as tesla's new model s matches up well against the bmw i5, i feel your design, build quality, and the way it drives are exactly what the market is looking for right now. i was really glad to come back to bmw, but i have to stress that the infotainment tech and software is where companies like tesla and rivian will keep pulling customers away. if bmw keeps delivering over-the-air updates for current cars to refine and enhance the drive, you'll stay ahead of everyone else. the i5 looks fantastic and drives beautifully. at the same time, charging infrastructure is critical, and tesla is still way more convenient. can't count how many times i show up at electrify america and the units are down, or i end up waiting for hours just to get a charge on longer trips.

title: G60 Operating concept, operating system
requirement_statement: Improve 'Operating concept, operating system' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 32 respondents complain and 21 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated they would prefer additional widget functionality in iDrive 8.5, more like iDrive 7. Customer stated the current setup only shows two widgets on the left side with a background and they would like performance metrics and more widgets to fill the background area when in home mode. Writer asked whether they were aware they can scroll the widgets up and down; customer replied yes but stated they still want to view more widgets simultaneously. Writer acknowledged this feedback.
Customer stated she is really enjoying the screen interface.
Customer commented that they enjoy the infotainment.
Customer asked what valet mode is used for. Writer advised it can stop a valet from accessing his driver profile or the trunk.

Customer reported that the screen layout is not very intuitive for accessing some functions, even though this is around their eighth or ninth BMW. Customer noted there are numerous manual actions required and that the system relies a lot on touchscreen interaction. Customer stated a BMW genius explained that voice commands are available, but Customer prefers more click-type controls or simpler access instead of going through several layers of menus on the display. Customer commented there are many technical features in the car and feels the system is less intuitive than prior BMW vehicles they have owned. Writer acknowledged the comments and thanked the Customer for providing their experience.
Customer stated that replacing physical buttons with more touch screens is a terrible trend, because it makes drivers take their eyes off the road.
Customer stated that it would be nice if the system offered celebrity voices or other playful features.

Customer mentioned it is difficult to use the display while driving because he has to tap through several different screens. Writer informed the customer about the quick access button along the bottom of the display. Customer added that being 6'1 and sitting farther from the screen, he occasionally hits the wrong buttons.

Customer stated that this system feels less intuitive than the one in their previous vehicle. Customer mentioned they had a Tesla before and considered that setup more user-friendly. Customer expressed that, although all the features are available here, the overall user experience is not as straightforward.

Customer stated he would like to see more physical controls return in the vehicles. Customer mentioned he understands manufacturers are moving toward more digital layouts, but he thinks it would be nice to have a good mix of analog and digital controls. Custmoer emphasized this preference.
Customer stated she is very happy with the infotainment system and described it as really cool.
Customer stated he is pleased with the system in the car and commented that it is very close to what he had in his prior vehicle.
Customer reported there were some initial system setting quirks, but they were sorted out quickly.
Customer stated he wishes the vehicle still included the physical programmable memory buttons. Customer stated that using the 1-8 buttons made pulling up menus much quicker and easier.

Customer stated he still needs to get used to where things are, since it is different from his previous BMWs. Writer offered assistance. Customer mentioned he has a lot of questions but cannot think of them right now. Customer added that in the dark it is hard to remember where one of the touch controls is and he has trouble putting his finger on the right spot. Writer recommended using the IPA, which the customer said he has just started using.
Customer stated he would have preferred to have radio presets available as physical buttons.
Customer commented the operating system is very easy to use and quite intuitive.

Customer stated that the idrive screen is challenging for him to get around. Customer stated the interface in his Cadillac was much simpler to use and felt more intuitive for both him and his spouse. Writer advised the customer that she could show him how to save his favorites into the short cuts. Customer stated he does not have time today but that he will call back to go over it.
Customer stated that the user-interface is quite complex, and it takes him some time to locate menu options. Customer stated it does not feel intuitive to him compared to Apple products.
Customer stated that the infotainment system is actually not too bad.

Customer mentioned he was uncertain how to access trip data and consumption details over a longer period. Writer explained that in the Apps menu he should select Vehicle, then Live Vehicle, then Content, and finally choose Trip data. Customer confirmed that this was exactly the information he had been looking for.
Customer stated the iDrive system feels quick and he does not notice any lag.
Customer stated the software in this vehicle is significantly better than in their i4, and that they enjoy using it.
Customer commented that having iDrive 8.5 is a nice tweak and improvement compared with iDrive 8.
Customer stated a preference for having physical switches and buttons again for commonly used features, to reduce distraction while driving and make them easier to operate.

Customer stated that before a software update his radio station appeared on the left side of the screen, but now there is only an image of the car there. Writer explained the tiles on the left can be scrolled up and down, and that the infotainment tile should be close to the top of the list. Customer asked if his available apps would still show in the center of the screen. Writer stated that tapping the apps menu will display all available apps. Customer then asked if he could add more shortcuts. Writer stated new shortcuts can be set by holding a finger on the desired item, and noted there is a maximum of eight shortcuts.

Customer stated that reaching the trip computer through the infotainment display is harder than using the former dedicated button on the turn signal stalk. Customer acknowledged BMW removed many hard buttons but felt this particular change makes the system less user-friendly.
Customer stated there are so many settings that using it is not very straightforward, but he is happy with the software itself.
Customer stated there are so many settings that using it is not very straightforward, but he is happy with the software itself.
Customer stated there are far too many menus spread across the screen. Customer stated it is a lot more complicated than he thought it was going to be.

Customer stated that switching to an almost completely touchscreen interface is too much for him. Customer stated there are some functions that would be better if they still had dedicated buttons. Customer stated he knows he can use voice to control things, but said using his voice is not really helpful when he is on a call or talking with someone in the car, it just gets confusingg.
Customer stated that the vehicle could benefit from having more physical buttons, similar to Cadillac.
Customer stated she would prefer the iDrive interface text to be larger and more distinct. Customer stated this change would help given her poor eyesight.
Customer stated the entertainment system feels clunky and requires a lot of clicks to use. Writer advised that the customer can also operate it using voice commands or the personal assistant.
Customer commented that on the home screen there are only a few widget choices available. Customer said it would be nice to edit those and decide what is shown there.

Customer advised that the vehicle feels like one big computer and he has trouble figuring out all the features. Customer stated he is uncertain how to use different functions, which of the roughly 20 to 30 icons to pick, and how to move through the various screens. Customer stated the setup is not intuitive for him or for his wife. Writer stated she offered to assist the customer, but he declined and explained that their grandsons help them instead.
Customer stated he appreciates the iDrive layout and interface, as it lets him easily locate his apps.
Customer stated he likes that he is able to place his frequently used settings into the Shortcuts menu.

Customer stated the new iDrive is mostly well designed, but feels it relies on too many individual apps for certain functions that would work better as menu entries. Customer stated the number of apps makes some features and settings harder to find and becomes distracting while driving.
Customer stated he is pleased with the user interface.
Customer stated the iDrive system is very straightforward to use.
Customer stated they consider the operating system and the vehicle's technology to be very intuitive to use.
Customer stated she would like physical buttons to store her favorite radio presets. Customer stated she wants the Programmable Memory Buttons like she had in her last BMW.

Customer stated he is pleased with the electronics in the vehicle. Customer stated he went through the owner's manual. Customer stated he spent roughly an hour sitting in the car getting familiar with the various widgets and apps. Customer stated he managed to set everything up so the car is comfortable for him and simple to operate.
Customer stated the interface is easy for them to use.
Customer stated the car offers an ideal balance between digital and physical controls, unlike Tesla, which he feels relies on too many digital controls.
Customer stated he would prefer the car to stay in Apple CarPlay when he gets in, rather than switching back to the BMW interface.
Customer stated the vehicle system has been straightforward and easy to learn.

Customer stated that from time to time, though not very often, his iPhone will disconnect from the vehicle. Customer stated the issue happens only occasionally. Writer advised that if standard troubleshooting steps do not resolve the disconnection, an idrive reset may be required in order to re-establish the connection to the phone.
Customer stated the vehicle's infotainment system is good.

Customer stated they still need to go through the various options and learn about the different features. Writer acknowledged the learning curve and provided details on the Monday-Friday corporate helpline for future assistance since the customer did not have any specific questions yet.
Customer states he is pleased with the overall infotainment aspects of the vehicle.

Customer stated he would prefer to have a seperate Valet Key. Customer stated he does not want to have to take it out of the key fob. Customer stated he is aware Valet can be turned on in the software.

the pricing on this car is way too high. i managed to negotiate a strong lease, but there is no chance i would spend the $190k msrp on an electric car that is bound to lose a lot of value. overall the tech is very solid, but bmw still not getting the esim to function correctly is incredibly annoying. one of the main reasons i chose this car was the theatre screen, and now it only operates if i run ugly cables to it. the seats are mostly comfortable, yet they do not give enough side bolster support, so i would really like more hold in the corners. the heated seats and heated armrests are fantastic and the infotainment works well, plus the upgraded sound system is outstanding. when using apple carplay, though, the bottom left corner with distance and time remaining is completely hidden behind my right hand while driving. if i swapped cars today i would rather be in an m5 touring.

this is a newly released model and it still has some bugs that need to be sorted out. the tech is quite overwhelming, and i am repeatedly having to reset things. the interior lighting setting i prefer keeps changing by itself to a different color. whenever i use the idrive selection tool, it drops down a presets screen each time i touch it, so when i try to choose a new radio station it pulls up those presets instead. the driving assistance functions are hard to locate and adjust, you have to hop from one screen to another. there should be a simple way to temporarily disable these features for things like traffic or going through a car wash. a basic alarm cancel or silence button would be very helpful. the seat controls on the dashboard are awkward to use because you have to lean forward to make adjustments. putting the controls on the seat or the door would be better and would let you sit properly while you fine-tune your seating position.

performance, reliability, tech, luxury, comfort - the whole package is there. i'd really like to be able to pin more apps onto that left sidebar on the home screen. i used to have the weather sitting there, then it just seemed to vanish. i rely on quick shortcuts, so i ended up putting the weather app in the shortcut section instead.
about a week after i bought the car i got a flat tire, right after a storm, and bmw connect happened to be down. i had to arrange one tow to get back home, then a second tow to reach the bmw dealer that's out of town. that meant a lot of time just waiting around for tow trucks. in that situation a spare tire would have been very useful. i was told i'd be reimbursed for the towing because bmw couldn't provide a tow, but that was in october and i still haven't received anything.
otherwise the car itself is fantastic. i really like being behind the wheel. i've always enjoyed driving, and with this being my 4th bmw - a 528 and two 740s before - this 760 tops them all. it has taken the driving experience to a completely new level for me.

i really enjoy this car. the ride quality is excellent and the cabin stays very quiet. the 760 has more than enough power and the tech in it is impressive. the one thing i'd change is the way the menus are laid out for the controls. i end up digging around through a bunch of apps on the screen just to find basic functions.

my other issue is that when i spec'd and ordered the car, i assumed the 760 came with active cruise and all the parking assists like my previous m850 and m5 had. it was a letdown to find out later those systems were actually part of a big option package that i hadn't realized i needed to add. my wife's lexus rx350 has all of that included as standard equipment for about half the cost.

this is my 4th brand-new 7 series and my 10th new bmw. pros: the engine is fantastic, a real beast; the tech is strong; and it drives very well overall.

cons: the hvac could cool better, likely because of the hidden vents, and it only got a bit better after i put clear uv tint on the windows. you also can't set sport mode as the default, even though i drive in sport most of the time. i can't remove the red and blue colors on the display and interactive bar, and i'm not a fan of those colors. the steering feels a little soft and not as connected to the road as my previous cars. it's a big car, and adding about 5" more length wasn't a good thing. the styling is just okay; i actually think my 2017 740i looks better.

title: G70 Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA)
requirement_statement: Improve 'Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA)' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer reported he is unhappy that the MSA off button is no longer there. Customer added he does not want to have to drive in Sport Mode for it to shut off. Customer and writer went out to the vehicle, and writer walked him through iDrive: click on "MENU", then "Vehicle apps", then "Driving settings", then "Drivetrain and chassis". Customer verified that the setting does not appear.
Customer stated that most of the time he prefers MSA disabled, but when fuel becomes a concern he likes to switch it on.
I had a very serious problem with Automatic engine stop-start problem: "when the car restarts it gives a jolt, and there's no way to shut off that economy start stop"

i really like the car itself, but i absolutely hate the auto stop-start at every light or stop sign. there is no way to shut it off permanently or at the driver's choice, other than running in sport mode. i used to be loyal to the brand, but i will not buy another car that won't let me disable this. in my previous cars there was a simple push button to turn it off. it feels dangerous in busy intersections because you sit waiting for the engine to fire, the gear to engage, and then go. my wife won't even drive it, and i'm begging you to fix this on my car. the thing has 500+ horsepower and yet you are worried about saving fuel while idling.

Customer stated he was worried about the vehicle being a Mild Hybrid. Customer stated he had an electric vehicle before that caused a lot of motion sickness. Customer asked how often the electric motor would be on and what speeds it comes on. Writer advised the electric motor assists the combustion engine, during the time the combustion engine shuts off when slowing toward a traffic light or stop sign. Writer advised it may typically come on under about 7 MPH. Writer advised it is usually not noticeable when the electric motor is operating. Writer advised the vehicle will begin to accelerate with the electric motor and then the combustion engine takes over. Customer asked if, when the vehicle is stopped in traffic for a while, the engine will turn back on to recharge the battery. Writer advised that it will, and also that the engine comes on when the climate control needs to heat or cool the cabin again.
Customer asked whether the auto start stop could be set to remain off all the time. Writer advised this is not possible.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

Customer stated he is unhappy that in the 7 Series he can only switch off MSA by putting the vehicle into Sport Mode. Writer advised that MSA can instead be turned off in the iDrive system. Writer directed him to click on "MENU">"Vehicle apps">"Driving settings">"Drivetrain and chassis">"Auto Start/Stop" and then choose the preferred setting. Writer further explained that on the Auto Start/Stop page, he should "hold your finger on the screen for a second." Writer stated that when the shortcut option appears, he should select yes. Writer added that the customer can then pull down from top to bottom on the iDrive display and select that shortcut. Writer confirmed that MSA cannot be programmed to be default off.

Customer stated they would prefer the engine not to shut off when the vehicle is stopped. Writer advised that the button for this function has been removed, but that using Sport Mode will keep MSA from engaging. Customer thanked the writer for the information.

Customer expressed that he would like a way to turn off the auto start-stop feature permanently, explaining that right now he has to go into the app and switch it off every time he drives. Customer noted that his GMC Denali pickup has a single button that disables it with one press. Customer stated he understands the 2027 models will allow a permanent shutoff, which he thinks is great, as he considers auto start-stop to be a terrible feature.

this car was delivered on pirelli high-performance tires that made the ride far too harsh for a luxury sedan. i ended up paying myself to swap to oem-spec bridgestone turanza 6s, which transformed the comfort, and tire choice really should be sorted at the factory for customers who care about refinement.

the 48v mild-hybrid start/stop is still quite rough. compared to other isg/bsg systems from different brands, and to my 2024 530i with a belt starter generator, the restart from a standstill is abrupt and gives a noticeable jolt even when holding the brake, and it can feel coarse as the car comes to a stop. that takes away from the premium driving experience, especially when mercedes and range rover have virtually imperceptible stop/start.

on top of that, ota software updates arrive very late, which is disappointing versus other luxury makers. more timely updates would really help the overall ownership experience.

this car was delivered on pirelli high-performance tires that made the ride far too harsh for a luxury sedan. i ended up paying myself to swap to oem-spec bridgestone turanza 6s, which transformed the comfort, and tire choice really should be sorted at the factory for customers who care about refinement.
