this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

Customer stated he would like to have a dedicated physical button that can switch off the Automatic Engine Start-Stop function.

Customer asked about disabling MSA. Writer explained that in Sports Mode the vehicle is not in MSA. Writer advised to go in iDrive to "MENU" then "Vehicle apps" then "Driving settings" then "Drivetrain and chassis" then "Auto Start/Stop" and choose the wanted setting. Writer further advised to create a shortcut to the MSA screen by holding a finger on the display for about a second until the popup appears, then select yes to set the shortcut. Writer stated that to use the shortcut, place a finger at the top edge of the screen and drag down so the shortcuts become visible.

Customer indicated the start-stop function is about the only feature they have a minor complaint about. Customer explained that when the engine shuts off and it is hot outside, the inside of the vehicle starts to feel warm.

Customer mentioned he considers himself a driver and a car enthusiast, and for that reason the Auto start stop function is not something he needs, as he is not worried about emissions or about fuel economy.

Customer stated he is unhappy that he cannot switch off the engine stop at lights permanently and instead has to go into the settings and disable it each time, with it only staying off for that single drive.
Customer mentioned he doesnt feel the Automatic Engine Start-Stop is any smoother than before. Customer said it remains quite noticeable when the engine shuts off and then comes back on.
Customer mentioned he would like a way to keep MSA turned off all the time.
Customer stated that the MSA makes the car shake. Customer stated that in traffic it shudders every time he comes to a stop.

Customer stated the transmission seems to clunk when pulling away from a stop or driving at about 3 to 4 mph. Customer stated he feels the transmission does not engage the gears smoothly and thinks the auto engine start/stop could be contributing to the issue. Customer stated he usually drives in efficient mode and that the vehicle currently has 2,800 miles. Customer stated he will discuss the concern with his dealer when he comes in for an oil change. Writer advised driving in sport mode to turn off auto engine start/stop and see if that helps the situation. Customer acknowledged.

i've stuck with the 7 series for a long time, and this one is a really good car overall. still, having auto start stop constantly active bothers me, and losing so many physical buttons is a negative. forcing everything through the screen and menus can be distracting and sometimes awkwardly difficult. big step up in seat comfort and in the way it rides, and the new active roll stabilization really changed the character of the car. the exterior look has grown on me, but i still like my 2020 m760i more and i'm happy i decided to keep it.

Customer stated he really hates the Auto Start-Stop function. Customer explained that whenever the engine fires back up, the car shimmies and shakes. Customer stated this Auto Start-Stop takes away from how smooth and quiet the car should be.

i'm happy with how the car looks, but there are a few things i don't like compared with my old bmws (2015 1 series and 2016 2 series). the rear view mirror feels very distorted and kind of zoomed in, so reversing with it is hard as it doesn't show a true view of what's behind. once the emergency brake suddenly activated while i was reversing even though there was absolutely nothing behind me, leaving me stuck in the road holding up traffic. my audio via apple carplay cuts out every time the car is about to do a software update. when i accelerate a bit harder the steering becomes quite jerky and doesn't feel that safe, which never happened on my 2 series m sport that was quick but smooth.

very satisfied with the car overall, but it definitely has areas that could be improved. the gearbox is not as smooth as i would expect from a bmw, and in some situations it produces loud noises and juddering. at times it seems unsure which gear it should select. the electric driver seat also occasionally fails to go into the right position. one of the biggest disappointments is the fake engine sound, which on an m model feels like a major let down. good car, but for the price it should be a lot better.

i have owned several 1 series bmws (2 f20s, 1 f40 and now this f70). build quality has been very good in all of them, though i would say the f40 was probably the best. my current bmw 120 loses out a bit because of the plastics used around the sound system speakers; my f40 had the harman kardon setup with nicer speaker facings. i do not know why bmw now only sells an automatic gearbox in the uk, but i would have liked the choice as i have always driven manuals. i notice a small lag when pulling away with the auto, which can feel unnerving at junctions. there are more things i could mention but this survey does not give enough characters!

i have had 7 bmws so far and liked every one of them, but this one is easily the best i have owned. it is a pleasure to drive and i actually look forward to any trip. it can be calm and smooth when i want to relax, but turns into something exciting and fun when i feel like it. despite being a small car it works hard, with a practical and flexible load space. up to now, apart from a puncture, no bmw has ever let me down. it looks great, is comfortable, and the sound system is excellent. the infotainment is very intuitive and functions really well. my only gripe is that connected drive (digital premium) should not be an add-on but built into the price from the start. outstanding customer service from stratstone derby as well.

the inability to properly control the driving modes is really annoying. the disappearance of buttons and the idrive wheel to manage things is a pain. the touch screen itself is very good, but it pulls your attention away too much. a simple button to turn off start stop would do, instead it's awkward to use. i want to set off, not waste time searching through menus. the centre console buttons are hard to distinguish so you have to look down, there's barely any separation. the steering wheel is excessively thick and an option for a slimmer one would be preferable. with no audible exhaust note it becomes boring to drive. you pay a high price only to be asked to pay again for premium infotainment options soon after. i only want the spotify app. the cabin is beautiful and a pleasant environment. i feel like i'm managing a machine rather than actually driving. fantastic car, no character at all.

title: G60 Vehicle, lock / unlock
requirement_statement: Improve 'Vehicle, lock / unlock' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: I had a serious problem with Door locks - DTU/controls poorly located: "When the driver door opens, the other doors dont all unlock."

Customer stated she is still trying to figure out the right way to unlock the doors, and she is usually alone when she needs to get to the back of the car. Customer stated she thought she had turned off the automatic door lock because she wants the rear door to unlock at the same time, so she does not have to lean back inside to open it. Customer stated she believed the dealer had switched that off and that when she gets into the car it locks all the doors and then unlocks them all, which is what she was looking for. Customer stated the dealer explained that for safety the back door is normally kept locked, and he did disable that for her, but when she gets out of the car and opens the doors she expects all of them to unlock again, and they do not, so she has to unlock them manually. Writer explained that the setting has to be checked in the menu and that the customer can choose whether the doors unlock when arriving at the destination or when in park. Writer asked if the customer was able to go to the car right then, but Customer stated she was in the middle of a tesing site with a friend doing some things and could not get to the vehicle. Writer advised Customer to go into Doors and Windows when she has a moment and check what she has selected, as it will show all the different options.

Customer stated he appreciates that BMW now offers the ability to unlock just the front doors instead of unlocking all of them at once, but he would prefer additional ways to customize this function. Customer stated that on his prior Prius, he could set the key fob to open only the front doors, and then by pressing a button on the door handle he could unlock the rest of the doors. Customer stated a similar setup would be useful here, or having more choices in the lock settings menu for different combinations, for example "Unlock driver's door and passenger" and similar options.
Customer indicated he is not happy with the digital lock and unlock buttons on the driver door, saying their location makes them difficult to use.

Customer stated that at present only the driver's door unlocks, but he would prefer that all doors unlock together. Writer stated that in the Apps Menu the customer should select Vehicle, then Doors and Windows, then Lock/Unlock, and finally choose "Unlock: All doors".

I had a very serious problem with Door locks - DTU/controls poorly located: "The only real downside I have with my new 2024 5 Series is the door lock behavior, which feels confusing. One time in the driveway, my wife and I were about to head out, and I realized I had left my wallet inside the house. I stepped out, let my door rest mostly closed so it clicked once but wasn't completely shut, and without noticing I left the BMW key in the cup holder. When I came back, all four doors were locked, including that door that was only partly closed but had clicked once, so I had basically locked myself out. Luckily my wife had the spare key she carries and could unlock it. This sort of thing makes me uneasy about the locks. We live in Fairview, CA, and a few years ago there was a widely reported tragedy in another city, Greenfield, when a teenager accidentally left his younger teenage sister inside a locked older BMW 3 Series in a parking lot during the summer heat, regularly over about 105 degrees. She couldn't get the doors open and she died."

Customer stated she is uncertain whether she can accidentally lock herself out of the vehicle. Customer explained that she has left her key inside the car, walked away, and then the vehicle locked itself automatically. Customer stated that she and some others tried this out in the morning and they started thinking the behavior might be due to a spare key being stored inside the house in a drawer close to the garage, with the car picking up the signal from that spare key and locking. Customer asked if she could end up locked out if she left her purse in the car that contains both her phone and her key. Writer explained that the vehicle should not lock when the key is inside and that the car is supposed to sense the key remaining in the cabin. Writer clarified that if an additional key is near the vehicle, the system may detect that second key as well, which could trigger the locking behavior. Writer suggested that the customer can use the BMW app on her phone to open the vehicle if needed and noted that there is an icon in the app specifically for unlocking. Writer confirmed that the vehicle is intended not to let the customer lock herself out because it should register that the key is inside. Customer stated she understood the explanation about the spare key being close by and causing the locking and also now knows about the BMW app unlock feature as a backup solution.

Customer stated when the driver's door unlocks, the rear doors remain locked. Writer advised going to the Apps Menu, then Vehicle, Doors and windows, lock/unlock, and choosing "Unlock: all doors" instead of "Unlock: driver's door only".

the apps built into the car really ought to be reachable from the phone, so you don't have to sit in the car and fiddle with them - you can do that in a mercedes, which was my previous car. the windows also can't be closed via the app, while mercedes manages that. if they could close themselves automatically when it rains, like mercedes does, i haven't found any sign that they do, but they should. the car has locked me out several times when i've left either the phone or the keys inside. settings in the app like folding the mirrors when locking don't actually work when it's other users, even though the option is set in the app. my wife is forced to type in a pin code and can't just pick her id, supposedly because of the risk that her phone might be stolen - but the primary user's phone can be stolen too, so that explanation doesn't make sense. the information shown in the dashboard is poor no matter which view you choose. the radio will not receive a signal while i'm driving through the limfjord tunnel, which i go through every day, and that's something i've never run into with any other car i've owned. the winter range is deeply reprehensible and honestly my biggest complaint: no more winter holiday trips, because the real range on the motorway at 130 kmh in frost is at most about 250 km. well, i guess i have to stop somewhere, but i'm left disappointed. mvh mads

overall it is an outstanding car. there are just a couple of things that really feel like cost cutting, and i honestly do not get why those choices were made. the biggest one is that the car cannot acclimatize while on the ice and instead will only use the main hybrid battery, which makes absolutely no sense. it comes across like somebody just did not bother to push the right software update. that behavior also hurts the practicality for people who commute. you are forced to drive in a way that saves enough of the main battery so you can still use the acclimatization settings before your next trip.

the other irritation is that you cannot unlock the car using the rear passenger door handles. at close to $80,000, it feels like they could have added two more touch sensors to make locking and unlocking simpler. overall the experience is great, but there are definitely a few things that make you wonder if they were driven by engineering or by a bean counter.

the "driving machine" part really is "ultimate", but the infotainment setup badly needs some refinements. bmw seems to have no real way for owners to send in feedback or ideas to fix the counterintuitive parts of the system, and the geniuses at the dealer told me there isn't any channel for that.
one specific problem is the auto lock/unlock when you come up to the car or walk away. that function is great anywhere except at home. in my garage i'm walking past the car over and over while i work, and each time it goes on and off repeatedly. that cannot be good for the car, and the only way i could stop it was to switch the entire feature off.
this exact issue shows up as a common complaint online, and i found out that i-drive 8.5 has a setting to disable the comfort access "at home" only. that would be a perfect fix, but when i tried to change my settings so i could actually enjoy the feature i paid for, i discovered it only exists on 8.5 in the 7-series, not on the same 8.5 in my 5-series.
for me that is a real "deal-breaker". bmw is aware, or absolutely should be, that this is a problem. they clearly already have a solution, but 5-series owners are blocked from using it. i have a whole list of other issues and would gladly go over them with someone who truly cares. they're simple, common-sense fixes i'd provide for free... if there were any line of communication.

this exact issue shows up as a common complaint online, and i found out that i-drive 8.5 has a setting to disable the comfort access "at home" only. that would be a perfect fix, but when i tried to change my settings so i could actually enjoy the feature i paid for, i discovered it only exists on 8.5 in the 7-series, not on the same 8.5 in my 5-series.
for me that is a real "deal-breaker". bmw is aware, or absolutely should be, that this is a problem. they clearly already have a solution, but 5-series owners are blocked from using it. i have a whole list of other issues and would gladly go over them with someone who truly cares. they're simple, common-sense fixes i'd provide for free... if there were any line of communication.

Customer stated he really likes that he can set the lock and unlock feature to just the driver door or to all doors, changing it depending on what he wants at that moment.

Customer explained she first had trouble opening the rear doors and thought she had to open the front doors before the back ones would unlock, but she eventually figured it out. Writer asked how she managed it. Customer stated she adjusted some options in the lock settings and then it worked.

Customer stated he would like the doors to automatically unlock when he parks the vehicle and is finished driving. Writer stated this can be set in the Apps menu under Vehicle, Doors and windows, Lock/unlock, and then turning on "Unlock doors at the end of trip".

evidence.quote: i'm mostly pleased with the car except for the satellite navigation. when we use it, it has taken us down tiny lanes that are only just wide enough for one vehicle so you can't get past anything coming the other way. this has happened on three trips and led to hold-ups and a lot of stress. my last 1 series let me pick between the fastest route and the shortest one but this new model doesn't offer that choice. i checked with the dealer and they confirmed this. i've chatted to other bmw drivers and they no longer rely on the idrive navigation, they just use their phones. i went for bmw as a premium brand but i'm really unhappy that the sat nav is basically not fit for purpose. simon fairclough [EMAIL]

overall it is a good car but i do have issues: drivetrain - it behaves more like a plain fwd than a rear-biased 4wd and you can feel torque steer. dashboard controls - getting rid of the physical buttons and burying everything in the touchscreen is awkward and could even be unsafe. the ui has become a nuisance: to switch into sport mode i have to go through several steps, and since the voice control is flaky and i don't want to chat to my car, that's not an option. when using nav i have to 1) hit the mode button on the centre console, 2) pick the mode on the display, then 3) tap nav on the side of the screen to get the map back. build quality - the plastics feel low grade and there are rattles, particularly around the dash. steering wheel - this is meant to be a sporty hatch, so please stop fitting wheels sized like they belong on a boat.

i moved down from an m135 drive and the power in this one is still absolutely fine and nicely responsive for everyday driving. i much prefer the battery assisted stop/start setup, and the steering has a nice light feel that firms up as you go faster. i am a bit let down that the i-drive knob has gone, as i always thought that system was brilliant when on the move. the new screens look very smart and, once you have them configured, they work well, and the overall fascia design and materials feel excellent. my f70120 m sport drives and handles really well day to day, and i actually like how it looks more than the f40. the front electric seats are really comfy and offer very precise adjustment. i am enjoying the head-up display, its my first time using one. the sat nav reacts quickly and is really helpful when finding your way around unfamiliar routes and towns. i also really like the 'y' style wheels and the red calipers.

there is plenty to appreciate but also a couple of niggles. from behind the wheel the suspension feels quite firm, possibly just more noticeable because the cabin is so quiet. the software is very complex and the manual doesn't help much, particularly when i try to use it on my phone; a proper printed booklet might be better. the satnav has sent me down more single track lanes in the past 3 months than i've driven in the last 3 years, so i don't really trust it now. i do, however, like how it integrates with the guidance on the dash.

i'm really delighted with my new bmw, it is a joy to drive. this is my first automatic after years of using manual cars and it definitely makes driving simpler and more comfortable. the auto gear changes are smooth and quiet, and the acceleration feels quick and effortless. i'm also a big fan of the automatic handbrake. the interior was a key factor in choosing this car and it has lived up to what i hoped for. the sat nav screen is easy to read and straightforward to operate, and i've had a lot of fun playing with all the different lighting options. everything feels sturdy and thought-through with the driver in mind, and i'm very pleased with the decision i made. our salesman daniel at rochdale made the whole buying process effortless and kept me well informed throughout.

i find the console display for navigation and driver info very good, and all the sensors do help with the occupant's safety. however, with my low mileage i don't really feel like i've had much of a wow factor. taking away the individual button has made the dashboard look cleaner but has also made it harder to alter settings, as you now have to work out which app to go into. some apps like 'spotify' that were on the previous car are now only there if you pay for digital premium, at extra cost. i still need to see if the 'navigation' information has been reduced since the digital premium trial finished. i think losing certain features has pushed the car more into the general mainstream hybrid market. i will definitely check other makers when it is time to swap cars.

the sensor for unlocking the doors feels too insensitive, and roughly one out of five times the lock wont react even when touching the handle. as soon as you open the door, the audio system powers up. if you step away from the car briefly while the engine is left running, the horn starts blaring, so you basically cant use the ot-lock feature. when setting a navigation destination by voice, only a small number of options is shown and one gets picked automatically, so you are unable to choose from several candidates. with the engine running at night you cant switch on the lights, so i would at least like them to be smaller. the rear gate opener also reacts poorly, probably because that sensor isnt very sensitive either. the remote key needs to be quite close for the doors to lock, the effective distance is short.

the car is comfortable and still fun to drive, with light controls, decent performance and good economy, and it clearly shows bmw build quality. i only marked it down from a '10' because the instruments are poor and much harder to read than on my older 325 coupe, which is vastly better laid out and more ergonomic. traditional analogue gauges are far easier to glance at without looking away from the road. the lack of a proper printed handbook also makes figuring out the complicated touch screen more difficult. the on-screen 'keyboard' for entering satnav addresses is definitely better, but the male navigation voice is less clear than the female one on my previous 118. the voice-controlled satnav is a complete waste for us, it simply will not work for either me or my wife.

i chose the 1 series because i have been driving bmw cars for roughly 35 years. i would have preferred to get another x1, but my budget would not stretch to the price. given my age now and the fact i drive fewer miles, i have found this car very comfortable, especially after raising the seat to give me a higher and better driving position. the engine capacity is about 25% smaller, which worried me at first, but i quickly got used to it and now i barely notice. my concern is that, when i bought the car, nobody mentioned the extra digital upgrade, which seems to be around £12 a month. i am disappointed that the sat nav without this upgrade is quite inferior. i now think the upgrade is expensive and feel rather let down.

for me, the driving feel of the car is exactly what i have associated with bmw for more than 40 years, so in that sense it is perfectly bmw. with features like mild hybrids added, i sense a new stage of evolution.
as an older driver, though, i have to work hard to get familiar with bmw os9, which has come in with the times. if you think you need some subscription functions you can sign up, but honestly, with how rarely they are used, they seem unnecessary.
out of everything, bmw navigation is the worst part. when you are just driving normally and not using the navigation guidance, it makes no sense that traffic jam information is not shown, and that it only appears if you subscribe. i really want to know the reason for that.

title: G60 ConnectedDrive and Infotainment, overall technology
requirement_statement: Improve 'ConnectedDrive and Infotainment, overall technology' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 29 respondents complain and 18 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote:
Customer stated that in the last few weeks he has experienced a few tech problems with the vehicle. Customer stated the first problem was the screen going completely black for around a day and a half. Customer stated his salesperson told him to do a software reboot on the vehicle, which made the screen come back. Customer stated he then had another issue where the music started jarring out of one speaker, and at the same time the hands-free driving feature would not work and showed it was not available. Customer stated he again did a reboot and regained functionality. Customer stated that at this time everything is working fine. Customer asked what can be done so this does not keep happening. Writer advised that if any of these issues occur again, he should reach out to the service center at his dealership to see what they recommend. Writer advised there will be a software update released within the next month that will address some software concerns.

the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

the car is very comfortable to sit in and drive, and the handling is quite responsive. i haven't had a vehicle this large for many years, but this one drives and turns almost like a smaller car. the acceleration is excellent, and i don't feel any need for the m version's extra power. the suspension is also excellent, which makes every ride enjoyable, though i'd prefer an air suspension like i've experienced in the audi q8 etron or what bmw offers on the i7. the range is very good, but with the limited fast charging along my usual routes to nj on the delmarva peninsula, i find myself wishing it could go more like 450-500 miles; for long out-of-state trips we rely on a gas vehicle. for driving around virginia the range works fine and is better than my previous ev, the vw id4. the technology in this car can be overwhelming, but i'm learning it and the infotainment bit by bit. it feels solid on the road, always composed and responsive. i do miss a spare tire, and the idea of using the provided flat repair system worries me since i've never done that before; it might help if the dealer walked me through it so i'd feel less anxious. overall, i really enjoy being behind the wheel of this car, it's the best i've owned.

Customer stated he experienced glitches with the content display, starting when the vehicle had under 200 miles. Customer stated the screen would sometimes freeze or the content would fail to load properly. Customer stated he brought the vehicle in for service and the system was reprogrammed. Customer stated the work was done by a BMW engineer at the 210 building at the Ohio office. Customer stated he was informed there is a problem with Service Pack 22 that was causing the behavior he saw. Customer stated he was also told that using Digital Key Plus instead of the key fob might be contributing to some of the issues. Customer stated he works for BMWNA, which is how he was able to have a BMW engineer examine his vehicle. Customer stated the reprogramming was completed the same day and he has not experienced any further issues.

Since service was performed at the BMW Headquarters, we do not have service notes.

1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function.

in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate.

the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues.

i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix.

2. homelink garage door opener
the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then.

most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.

i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

overall, the cars are very high quality, both in materials and in how they are put together, and also when it comes to driving feel and comfort. the software is actually really good, but there is a major but. it is almost ridiculous that you cant "talk" danish to the car. danish voice control exists even in cheap little pispotters. it comes across a bit arrogant that danish has been left out for years. that really has to be fixed if the total experience is going to feel properly high quality.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

overall it is an outstanding car. there are just a couple of things that really feel like cost cutting, and i honestly do not get why those choices were made. the biggest one is that the car cannot acclimatize while on the ice and instead will only use the main hybrid battery, which makes absolutely no sense. it comes across like somebody just did not bother to push the right software update. that behavior also hurts the practicality for people who commute. you are forced to drive in a way that saves enough of the main battery so you can still use the acclimatization settings before your next trip.

the other irritation is that you cannot unlock the car using the rear passenger door handles. at close to $80,000, it feels like they could have added two more touch sensors to make locking and unlocking simpler. overall the experience is great, but there are definitely a few things that make you wonder if they were driven by engineering or by a bean counter.

the "driving machine" part really is "ultimate", but the infotainment setup badly needs some refinements. bmw seems to have no real way for owners to send in feedback or ideas to fix the counterintuitive parts of the system, and the geniuses at the dealer told me there isn't any channel for that.
one specific problem is the auto lock/unlock when you come up to the car or walk away. that function is great anywhere except at home. in my garage i'm walking past the car over and over while i work, and each time it goes on and off repeatedly. that cannot be good for the car, and the only way i could stop it was to switch the entire feature off.
this exact issue shows up as a common complaint online, and i found out that i-drive 8.5 has a setting to disable the comfort access "at home" only. that would be a perfect fix, but when i tried to change my settings so i could actually enjoy the feature i paid for, i discovered it only exists on 8.5 in the 7-series, not on the same 8.5 in my 5-series.
for me that is a real "deal-breaker". bmw is aware, or absolutely should be, that this is a problem. they clearly already have a solution, but 5-series owners are blocked from using it. i have a whole list of other issues and would gladly go over them with someone who truly cares. they're simple, common-sense fixes i'd provide for free... if there were any line of communication.

i switched from an x4m competition over to a 5 series, expecting it to feel more luxurious. instead, i realized that a lot of the newer bmws are using more plastics where older cars had premium materials, and bmw was never really known for that before. i also dont like that i cant open or lock the rear door with the convenience feature, while the front passenger doors still have it. in the past couple of generations the back doors always had this option. i saw that there is no illuminated door sill anymore, and the new idrive knob does not work as nicely as the older versions. there are no physical controls for adjusting the temperature either. the steering wheel buttons are missing functions compared with previous models. on top of that, there are no visible exhaust tips, so it doesnt look sporty. the hybrid system itself is good, but the electric range is only about 40km and it takes a long time to charge it back up fully.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

title: G60 Door, open / close

evidence.quote: the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

Customer asked whether the i5 doors use a cable-driven door pull so you can get out if the battery dies. Writer advised that when the vehicle is stopped you should be able to pull the door handle and the door should open. Customer stated a friend had warned him about an issue with Tesla vehicles that use an electronic door opening system where you must know where the emergency release is. Customer added he heard a story about someone being trapped inside their Tesla because of that electronic door opening system. Writer advised he would look into it further and get back to the customer.
Update 3/03/25:
Writer determined the door levers on this vehicle are mechanical and do not require an emergency release lever like Tesla. Writer called the customer back and advised the doors and their levers are mechanical.

this bmw feels more like the ultimate cruising machine than the ultimate driving machine. over the years i've had several bmws, and this one is the softest and least responsive of them. it's a very nice car overall, but it doesn't have the same feel as the earlier generations. this is my third or fourth 5 series, plus a few older 7 series.

i was immediately let down that it doesn't come with a sunroof at all, which i think is a major miss. i also can't wrap my head around why you can't open or unlock the car from the rear doors. when you walk up with your hands full, those are usually the doors you go for first, so it turns into an awkward two step routine that just seems pointless.

if i had known about these things before buying this 5 series, i wouldn't have gone ahead with the purchase. and if they stay the same, i wouldn't buy another one.

i used to drive a 540 before this. the 530 does not feel like it has the same hp as the 540. in and around maple ridge we have what are called the 400 series highways, for instance the 412, 405 and 409, which are major expressways. to merge properly onto these highways it really helps to have the acceleration and horsepower of the 540. on this 530, the gas cap seems to be of much lower quality than on the 540. the whole area around where you put the gas cap back on after filling up and then close the small door also feels of much poorer quality than the other bmw vehicles i have owned. the braking on this car does not seem as good as what i had on the 540 either, wich is disappointing.

overall the car is very nice, but i'm not a fan of losing all the buttons and knobs and having to dig through the computer to find things. auto start/stop should either be gone or at least have a way to turn it off permanently. the fact there is no automatic mode for the fan speed, so you have to keep adjusting it by hand in an 85k car, is hard to accept. the build quality in general could be better. older bmw models had a solid, satisfying "clunk" when you closed the door, but now it sounds much more tinny and lightweight. the details show the quality, and small defects jump out, like plastic pieces that don't quite fit right or don't completely wrap around what they are supposed to.

the car gives me the comfort, luxury, and performance i'm looking for, with just a few minor quirks that i hope can be fixed in a software update. the auto stop start setting is buried too far down in the control menus and really should be right on the home screen. also, the interior door opener handles are hard to find in the dark. the led that now lights the door armrest should be moved behind the release handle so you can easily see it in low light, or another led should be added behind the handle. smaller annoyances are not being able to set the ambient lighting to anything other than "personal" and not being able to have "sport" as the default start-up mode. and please, make a spare tire kit standard.

i switched from an x4m competition over to a 5 series, expecting it to feel more luxurious. instead, i realized that a lot of the newer bmws are using more plastics where older cars had premium materials, and bmw was never really known for that before. i also dont like that i cant open or lock the rear door with the convenience feature, while the front passenger doors still have it. in the past couple of generations the back doors always had this option. i saw that there is no illuminated door sill anymore, and the new idrive knob does not work as nicely as the older versions. there are no physical controls for adjusting the temperature either. the steering wheel buttons are missing functions compared with previous models. on top of that, there are no visible exhaust tips, so it doesnt look sporty. the hybrid system itself is good, but the electric range is only about 40km and it takes a long time to charge it back up fully.

this is my 5th bmw vehicle.
all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:
550i
540i
740i
550i
now a 530i
i realize i am now in the regular 5 series, which i chose because, in my view, quality and functionality have gone backwards overall. that is not just about this 530 compared to those older cars.
my issues are:
run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series
2) air conditioning feels downgraded and not strong enough for south texas heat
3) ac/vent fan is too noisy except on the lowest level. with the fan high, you basically cant talk on the phone.
4) auto stop/start, but the driver does not have simple, effective full control to switch it off.
5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced
6) not enough storage. the small latched compartment by the driver is gone, there is a phone charging pad instead of extra storage depth (should be removable), and the glove box is limited and does not work well.
7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

title: G70 Door, open / close
requirement_statement: Improve 'Door, open / close' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated they would prefer the automatic door opening system to work more quickly, particularly at the beginning of the opening movement.
Customer states the doors make a squeaking sound when being opened, and the dealer has recommended replacing the hinges.

incredible luxury overall. the car looks beautiful, drives as well as our old 750i, and is wonderfully quiet. i really appreciate the interior atmosphere, the comfortable seats, and all the technology. all four seats are fully power adjustable, and the door-mounted tablets in the back are a nice detail. the electric self-opening doors initially felt like a gimmick, but now we find them very practical.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.

Customer stated the push-button door controls are positioned so they can be triggered by accident on both the front and rear doors. Customer explained his daughter opened the rear door unintentionally while the car was in motion when her knee bumped the control. Customer further noted the crystal ambient light panel is very sensitive and the doors may open by mistake while cleaning.
Customer stated he is not happy with the small button on the door panel for opening the door. Customer stated he would rather have a conventional pull door handle to open it.

Customer stated he was looking to have the self closing doors feature.

the car is just incredible in every respect and i really love it. i only want to highlight two things that, although clearly intended well, are flawed. first, the front passengers don't have truly adjustable ac vents. there's a tiny on knob under the vent panel to tweak the airflow a bit, but the range of adjustment is extremely limited. i understand the sleek look of a dash without the usual vents, but here it feels like form winning over function, and the ac function suffers a lot because of that choice. second, the driver's side open door button is a problem. i tend to lean my left leg against the driver door while i'm driving, and very often my knee hits that open button and the door pops open even as the car is moving. that's really frightening and unsafe. it doesn't do it when the door is locked and the speed is over roughly 10 mph, but it happens below that speed. those are the only two points i have that i think would make the car safer and better for the driver.

the car is very comfortable and feels up to date, but i have had way too many issues in a short period. i like the interior styling, yet a lot of the nice features are buried and take forever to access. there really should be simple buttons to open and close all doors. the lower door switch on the driver side is placed horribly, my knee has hit it multiple times and the door has popped open while driving. the fuel door refused to open when i was around 340 miles from home, and bmw roadside told me to just tear it off because they had no other solution. i have also gotten warning lights for the emergency contact system with no cause the dealer could identify. all of this has happened within the 3 months i have owned the car. my 2020 740ix had both keys quit working when i was roughly 70 miles from home, and nobody could explain why. i currently own 3 bmw and lease 2 more, and i am starting to lose faith in your products.

I had a problem with Doors - Hard to open/close: "Door is really hard to open and shut from the outside". Which Door Hard to Open/Close?: Front passenger door from the outside, Driver side rear door from the outside, Passenger side rear door from the outside, Driver door from the outside

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

i basically like the car overall, but there are a few serious reservations. the ride is simply too firm even for a performance model, and although adaptive suspension is standard, you can't actually adjust it, which makes its usefulness very debatable. my biggest annoyance, though, is that everyday functions are effectively blocked because i don't own a smartphone and therefore don't use a bmw app. for example, the nearside mirror no longer dips when reversing and auto hold can't be left permanently on. when i first bought the car the salesperson configured these for me, but an ota update wiped those settings and i have no way of getting them back. so i now have a car that cost almost £50k, with features i can't use that were incredibly easy to set up on previous vehicles, which is really disappointing.

as a daily driver it is very nice and has plenty of punch when you ask for it, but as a sporty car it feels too sterile - very fast yet no character, no proper noise apart from the fake stuff. making everything run through the touch screen is a backwards step from the old rotary i-drive, it is distracting and awkward to use while moving, especially with the firm suspension on bumpy british roads. needing apple carplay just to play music is irritating, why was usb media not kept as an option? not being able to run on side lights alone is also annoying. digital premium seems pretty pointless, and when bmw pushed a forced software update overnight once the free period ended, it actually felt like a downgrade, and the update got corrupted so nothing worked and the screens were frozen the next morning. an engineer had to come out to sort it, he did a great job, but bmw did not.

why is there a character limit? mechanically it feels cheap, rushed and badly tuned, not what i expected from bmw. my old 2010 e82 1 series was superior in every respect. the missing idrive wheel is a letdown and there is no proper replacement. mercedes puts a touch pad on the steering wheel, but here both next track buttons are inconsistent and irritating to use. the suspension needs more tuning for uk motorways and roads. the hybrid system also needs a lot of work: when you come up to a roundabout it sits in too high a gear and takes about two seconds to change down. i picked the bmw hybrid partly because it does not use a cvt, yet the gearbox fitted feels very slow to downshift when you need it. the auto wipers react too slowly to changing weather. and is there really no tire pressure sensor?

evidence.quote: Customer mentioned she is happy with the battery on her hybrid vehicle.

Customer reported the vehicle has inconsistent scheduled charging, with the car often ignoring the programmed 8:30 PM time slot. Customer noted that sometimes it begins charging immediately after being plugged in even though the settings are not set to charge right away, and at other times it will unexpectedly start charging around 5 PM or 4 PM despite being set for 8:30 PM. Customer stated the system will also change the charging configuration on its own, switching from the time slot setting to charge immediately without any action from the customer. Customer estimated this behavior occurs about half the time, with the other 50 percent working as intended. Customer indicated the issue happens whether charging from roughly 75 percent state of charge to a 90 percent target or at other battery levels, and that it was present both before and after a software update. Customer stated all charging is done at home using a 250 volt outlet in the garage. Customer mentioned the AC limit was originally at 48 amps but later reduced to 32 amps to be cautious, and the problem occurs at both limits. Customer added the outlet is capable of supporting up to 48 amps. Customer advised the vehicle was brought to the dealership, but technicians were unable to duplicate the problem even though the customer provided app screenshots showing the time slot at 8:30 PM while the car charged at 8 PM. Customer said the dealership performed tests and reached out to BMW engineers, but they were unable to resolve the issue. Customer stated the dealership did not reset the software or apply any fix, and engineers concluded there was nothing to be done. Writer suggested the customer continue to observe the charging behavior and contact the dealership again if the problem persists so they can try to reproduce and diagnose it.

Customer mentioned seeing guidance to only charge the battery to 80% and asked if that was accurate and whether he could still charge to 100%. Writer explained that routinely charging to around 80% is recommended, since the energy above that tends to run down faster, the car charges more slowly, and it helps the battery over the long term. Writer also advised that charging to 100% from time to time is acceptable when extra range is needed for a trip or similar situations.
Customer commented that charging the vehicle at home has been very convenient and has been enough to support all of their driving locally in the north suburbs of Austin as well as trips into Austin.

Customer reported the vehicle is taking longer to charge than expected, noting they are only using the level one charger that came with the car. Customer stated that, because of both the long charging time and how frequently they need to charge, they are considering switching back to a combustion vehicle.

Customer stated they are unsure about Level 2 fast charging times and are confused about what is considered fast charging. Writer explained that 0 to 80 percent can take roughly 4 to 10 hours depending on model and power allocation and confirmed three hours to reach 80 percent is typical. Writer added that Level 1 110V charging would take around a full day for a complete charge.

Customer stated he has a dedicated meter for charging their cars that was installed at their home. my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

the trunk space is really underwhelming. it will not take two normal cart golf bags unless you basically cram and jam them in there. 
during the first week with the car, i got an error warning that the emergency phone was not functioning. the service department can see that fault, but they still have not been able to correct it, even after reaching out to the home office. that feels like a serious problem if you ever actually need it. 
the a/c vents are just okay, but the airflow is not as focused or as strong as i figured it would be.
i would also like to see a sunroof offered as an option.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

i have only had my bmw for a few months and already ran into several issues:
i) at just under 1,100 miles the check engine light came on, and i had to leave the car at the bmw dealer in portville so they could fix a part that had dropped into the air intake, gotten stuck there, and was making the engine run too hot.
ii) later the rear passenger seat belt got jammed up and tangled inside the retract system, so the vehicle had to go back to the same bmw dealer for repair and for them to reinstall the belt.
iii) this morning when i got in, i noticed a crack in the glass roof; i have reached out to the bmw dealer and am now waiting for an appointment to bring it in for that repair.

in just these few months the car will have been in the shop 3 times :(

i picked up my car on may 27th from harper bmw in twin falls, id. i asked them to tint the windows, but they said their service techs are not willing to tint 7 series windows, so bmw sent me over to a tint shop called brightshield in town. i had the windows tinted there and they also suggested adding a clear coat on the front windshield and moonroof to keep uv rays from coming into the car. about a week after the install, the moonroof ended up with a big crack and bmw will not cover the repair, and brightshield is also refusing to pay for it. i bought a $130,000 bmw and within about 6 weeks there is a large crack in the moonroof that i am being told will cost a minimum of $13,000 to fix because of labor and the price of the windshield. there has been no impact or anything else done by me that would have caused this crack. so now i am driving a $130,000 car with a huge crack, trying to figure out who will actually pay for the repair. very dissatisfied customer.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.
