I had a serious problem with Sunroof/shade - DTU/controls poorly located: "Had an inital issue where the shade would not work, BMW fixed it"

Customer stated that on one occasion when she started the vehicle, the sunroof shade would not open. Customer stated when she came back to the car later, the shade opened properly and it has not given her any trouble since.

Customer stated she really misses having a sunroof on this vehicle. Customer mentioned she loves the extra ventilation a sunroof provides, especially since her area is very hot. Customer said it would have been really nice to have one on this car, and noted it might even stop her from purchasing this vehicle again in the future without it.
Customer states that he enjoys how much light the sunroof allows into the cabin.
Customer stated he likes how the sunroof looks.
Customer stated he loves the skylight and the way it opens everything up.
Customer noted they enjoy how the sunshade retracts backwards, especially compred to their prior car.
Customer mentioned he was caught off guard that the moonroof does not open.
Customer stated he would like the panorama glass roof to be able to open.
Customer enjoys driving with the moonroof screen open, but would prefer having a setting that allows it to automatically close or open depending on the vehicle's geolocation.
Customer stated he really enjoys the glass sun roof.

evidence.quote: I had a 118i m sport before and the 120 m sport has had all the useful bits stripped out and is not a sport model at all! this is our 6th bmw and easily the worst car we've ever had. 1. no 12v socket in the boot, a ridiculous penny pinching move. 2. no phone charging points in the back. 3. no climate controls in the rear. 4. no fog lights. 5. no leather seats. 6. no visible exhaust, sport model?? 7. basic 18" alloys (19" were standard on the 118i), sport model?? 8. thin, cheap carpets with poor grip and no m sport trim. every one of these came standard on the 118i m sport and the 120 m sport is marketed as its direct replacement! the 120 m sport is about £7/8k more, plus paying again for all the things removed, making it a pricey car and the worst thing ever to come out of a bmw showroom. total rubbish!

it's a good car, but the way the map magnification is controlled on-screen is extremely dangerous and very distracting, and could easily cause accidents just like using mobile phones. the old setup with a central control knob meant the driver could alter map zoom without taking attention off the road, whereas this new finger-on-screen method does exactly the opposite. i do have a simple workaround that would only need software changes, not a full redesign of the car: the knurled volume wheel could be used for both volume and map zoom, switching between them with a double click on the wheel. i cannot emphasise enough how strongly i feel about this; with this stupid system it is only a matter of time before someone gets killed.

i used to own a 118 shadow sport edition, and now have the 120m. the 120m is a pleasant car and quite economical, but i do have a few downsides when i compare it to my old one. the boot does not seem as big as before, and the new front design means dirt from the front wheels gets onto the sides of the car very easily, so it needs cleaning all the time. this was not an issue with my previous model.

love how the car drives and it really looks good, but the whole infotainment and driver interaction feels like a big step backwards with the physical buttons gone. bmw seems to think everyone wants to use their car like a smartphone now. stuff that was a single press before, like changing drive mode, is now 3 taps if i want to get back to my nav screen. thats not just annoying, it feels unsafe because you are pulled away from watching the road. same story when trying to change the fan speed. looks like this is all about saving money while the price of the car keeps going up. some of the interior plastics come across as cheap and not up to what you would expect from bmw. please bring back the buttons and the navigation wheel!

overall the car is good, but my score drops because of a few things:
* the xdrive feels too front-wheel biased. a rear-wheel bias would have suited it better and been more fun, especially since this is supposed to be a semi-enthusiast car with 300hp and a price around 500 tkr.
* there are shift paddles instead of a proper gear lever. even a sequential "fake" shift lever for the dct would have felt better than paddles. the paddles come across as a gimmick and really only make sense on the highway. when you are turning or trying to drift, the paddles are basically useless.
* there are no physical controls for climate comfort like ac or seat heating. the screen is extremely clunky for the things you change all the time, such as temperature. for everything else, the screen works great.
* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.

i honestly wouldnt have gone for this car if it werent for the excellent leasing offer, about 4500 sek per month for 2 years. the choice was between leasing this or buying an old tuned volvo 740. i am happy i picked this one, but when you want to have fun driving, the gear paddles and the slightly too strong front-wheel bias do make it feel a bit limited.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

i don't feel this is built as well as my 120i 2020 m sport. it's come with more basic tyres, not the high standard ones i had before, and i can feel vibration on certain road surfaces. some of the build spec seems cut back too - no automatic dipping mirror as standard, heating can't be adjusted separately, no rear console ports so passengers can charge phones. all of that was standard on my old 1201 m sport, and there's more plastic in the interior finish. bmw really aren't giving much away with this model.

really lovely car, very nice to drive and very comfortable. the warning lights in the wing mirrors are very useful and help keep you safe. for a petrol car hybrid car it is excellent for a petrol car. all the tech is in one place so you can watch the road instead of hunting round the cabin for buttons. with it linked to the bmw app on your phone, it gives peace of mind: it alerts you if someone tries to break in, shows how much petrol you have, how much air is in the tyres and when fluids are low, all before you even reach the car. brilliant idea, and the bmw staff are also very kind and helpful.

I had a problem with Wireless charging pad - Wrong size/poorly located: "I don't really know how to use it."

Customer stated the wireless charging pad does not charge his phone as well as plugging it into a computer or wall outlet. Customer stated that when he is playing music from the phone, it hardly charges and mostly just holds the battery level. Customer stated that if the phone is at about 57 percent when he gets in, it is usually still around 56 or 57 percent when he gets out. Customer stated that the phone will charge when it is not in use, but when it is running music or maps it basically only maintains the charge. Customer stated the phone becomes warm when using Android Auto while it is on the wireless pad. Writer explained the pad is not intended for fast charging. Writer explained the vehicle can fast charge the phone when a cable is used, and that there is a Type C cable near the cup holders that will charge much quicker. Writer explained that using Android Auto while wirelessly charging makes the phone warmer because it is doing both tasks. Writer explained that plugging the phone in is more practical, will keep it from heating too much, and will charge it faster.
I had a problem with Wireless charging pad - Broken/works inconsistently: "I have to move and wiggle my phone around before it finally makes a connection."
I had a minor problem with Wireless charging pad - Wrong size/poorly located: "wireless charging pad works fine on the driver side, but the passenger side pad does not operate"
Customer mentions he is pleased with the new wireless charging pad.

Customer stated the wireless phone charger sometimes shows slow charging without an obvious reason and that it never seems to charge at full capacity, noting this might be tied to using an iPhone 13. Writer stated the wireless charger provides 15 watts and explained it is weaker than using a cable in the USB ports, mainly intended to maintain charge rather than actively charge, especially when the phone is connected to CarPlay. Writer added that depending on the phone model and case the wireless tray may not charge at all and only hold the existing charge, though if the phone is not on CarPlay and not in use some charging can occur. Writer stated cables are much faster for charging than the wireless tray.

Customer stated the layout of the wireless charging pad is a huge mistake. Customer stated it will not properly accommodate most people's smartphones, including his iPhone 14. Customer stated this becomes a problem with the digital key, because at times his digital key plus is not recognized and he has to set the device in the tray to be able to start the car. Customer stated that with this new design, he is unable to actively use his phone when he needs it for the digital key function.

Customer reported the wireless charger had never worked since taking delivery of the vehicle and said he had to visit the dealer twice before it was corrected.

Customer advised that today they got a message telling them to remove a foreign object from the Wireless Charging Tray. Customer stated she understands that only the phone or the Digital Key Card should go in that tray. Customer reported she removed her phone from the tray but the warning message stayed on. Writer advised the customer to bring the vehicle in for service. Customer advised they will do so when they are able to.
Customer stated that their samsung s22 ultra will not fit properly in the wireless charger.
I had a very serious problem with Wireless charging pad - Broken/works inconsistently: "barely seems to charge at all and the charging is extremely slow."

Customer stated that a few weeks ago she began hearing a rattle from the phone charging tray whenever her phone is placed there. Customer confirmed she is using an iPhone 16 Pro in a hard plastic case. Customer confirmed she previously had a soft silicone case and thinks the noise may have started around the time she switched cases, but she has also tried the phone without any case and still hears the rattle. Customer stated the charging tray area and cupholders are completely empty when the sound occurs, and it happens whether the vehicle is idling or being driven. Customer stated the rattle is like a wind-up type noise, similar to a lot of coins shaking, even though the area is clear. Customer confirmed the phone itself does not move or vibrate in the tray and functions normally, and she has not yet tested with a different phone. Writer advised having the service center check this, especially if the issue also appears with other phones.

I had a minor problem with Wireless charging pad - Broken/works inconsistently: "the charging is terrible and basically won't charge my phone. the other side of the pad doesn't do anything at all, so why is it even there? i have to keep a cable charger handy if i actually need my phone to charge or if someone else does. they left that open spot making it seem like the passenger side would charge too, but it doesn't."

Customer stated the fan for the wireless charger began making a loud noise within the first week of owning the vehicle. Customer stated she could distinctly hear the fan and was sure the sound was coming from it, even making a loud whining noise herself to show what it sounded like. Customer stated she had to take the vehicle to the dealership so the fan could be replaced. Writer apologized that she already needed to bring in such a new vehicle for the wireless charger fan and acknowledged this was unfortunate. against my old 68 plate 520i, this one pulls quicker and uses less fuel. i really like the head up display and the new main screen, and the journey fuel info is handy. adaptive cruise itself works fine, but changing the gap to the car ahead while driving is awkward, especially when i want more distance in the wet. lane control helps. sat nav overall is good, yet the traffic delay icons/text are tiny and digging into that info on the move is hard, plus minor roads are shown too faintly. spotify is well integrated, simple to use and looks good. downside is the road noise, which is much louder on some surfaces and basically drowns out the audio. the speed limit warning drives me mad and is often wrong. i also want to keep the car in efficient mode without having to set it again every single journey.

Customer stated the vehicle's navigation system is much improved compared with earlier models.

Customer stated that she finds the navigation system terrible. Customer stated that she will often enter an address just to see the estimated arrival time, since she already knows how to get there and mainly uses it as a timing tool. Customer stated that for one destination the car predicted it would take 40 minutes, but in reality it took her 26 minutes to get there, and under normal conditions it usually only takes her about 20 minutes to reach that same place. Customer stated she could accept it if the system were routing her onto side roads because of traffic, but she believed taking the highway should have gotten her there closer to her usual time. Writer advised the customer to review her navigation settings and verify that the highway option is enabled so routes can factor that in, and Customer stated that she would check those settings.

with this purchase i had very high expectations of the bmw brand. choosing the 530i online edition through bmw financial lease was something i thought would make us into long-term brand customers, not just one-time consumers. right now though, i am facing serious inconvenience when using android auto. we keep having the same problem where music will not play correctly when starting tmap or other navigation apps, and it is not a random glitch but a recurring, structural issue. this is clearly not just my own case either. the same complaints are constantly coming up in major communities, such as a large online cafe called 'bmw driver club' (around 650,000 members), and even though many users are reporting the same inconvenience, bmw has provided no official explanation of the cause, no plan for improvement, and no proper guidance for customers. the issue itself matters, but the way bmw is handling it feels even more disappointing. these customer inconveniences have been building up for a long time, and i think the lack of active response and communication is something that can really damage trust in a premium brand. in my view, a premium brand is defined not only by how complete its products are, but also by how it reacts when problems come up. in the present situation, trust in the brand is inevitably shaken, even if the vehicle itself is satisfying. i feel that a clear analysis of the cause, a concrete improvement plan, and formal guidance to customers are absolutely needed. instead of treating it as just a minor technical error, i strongly ask for a proactive response that looks at the whole customer experience. my survey score here is not only showing dissatisfaction, but also my expectation that bmw will improve. i hope this point is considered very carefully.

Customer asked how to remove an incorrect address from the destination list if it is selected by mistake. Writer pointed customer to the owner's manual, noting that with the touchscreen you can press and hold the incorrect address and an option to delete that entry should appear. Writer further advised that if home or work was set to the wrong location, the customer can simply save the correct home or work address and the previous one will be deleted automatically.
Customer stated the BMW navigation system is superior to the one in the Tesla.

Customer stated the in-vehicle navigation is unreliable, and that after entering a destination the system will sometimes drop the route altogether. Customer stated this happens in the Atlanta area, where they expect to always have a signal. Customer stated that on one occasion, after navigation dropped, they used voice control to restart it, but the turn-by-turn guidance began directing them to a completely different destination until they turned the vehicle off and restarted it. Customer stated they have experienced the same problems with their current X6, so they believe it is a software issue.

while the brand itself is top-notch and the driving feel is very stable, there are letdowns in the small details. for instance, if you want to move the car forward and back for parking using the remote or a smartphone from outside, you have to pay a monthly subscription unless you switch to an iphone. when it rains there's supposed to be a heating function for the side mirrors, but it isn't actually supported, and there's talk this might also cost money. the built-in dashcam is just uncomfortable to deal with, awkward to view and operate, and getting a smartphone connected and staying connected is not easy. and the google-based navigation........... honestly, it sucks. there is android auto, but i really wish the manufacturer had partnered with a better provider for navigation instead. it's a real shame.

title: G70 My Modes / driving experience
requirement_statement: Review mixed feedback on 'My Modes / driving experience' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 26 respondents complain and 29 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer reports the vehicle drives like a dreem.
Customer asked if the M Modes could be set to default to Sport Mode. Writer stated the M Modes will always default to Personal Mode. Customer stated he would prefer Sport as the default.

Customer asked about using Sport Mode together with the booster. Writer explained Sport Mode applies the most aggressive setup. Writer added that, while moving, pressing the Boost button delivers a strong, time-limited boost to the engine.

Customer stated he normally drives in ECOPro. Customer reported that everything was fine for roughly the first few weeks, then the vehicle switched itself to comfort mode and would not allow him to change it back. Customer stated he will go to the dealership for an appointment.

Customer stated he would prefer the driving modes to be arranged like they were on his prior BMW. Customer stated he liked having separate buttons for each mode, and that setup made it simpler to turn them on and swap between them.
Customer indicated being pleased with the various driving modes available, such as sport, comfort, and efficient.
Customer stated he had an X5 M50i and before that a Mercedes S550, and said BMW is a driver's car, so he keeps coming back to the brand because there is nothing else like it.
the electric drive with no shifting is incredibly smooth and quiet. it has lots of convenience features i like, like programmable massage and heating when it is cold, etc.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

the car drives really well, but i'm seeing a few software issues. the auto close and auto open funciton when using the phone as a digital key is super annoying, and there should be a way to fully shut those off at home. right now you can only turn off the "unlock" feature at home, which feels like a simple software change. other very frustrating things are needing to dig through menus and multiple screens just to adjust the seat or even change the cruise control distance. that's annoying and honestly dangerous, because you end up scrolling menus instead of using a simple physical button in the car. another bad software problem is that there's no personal, fully customizable drive mode like porsche "individual" settings, so you're stuck with whatever the default programming is. another issue is the roof glass cracking after about two weeks of owning it, confirmed by lakeside bmw, and now it's waiting for repair that will take around two months for parts and work at a body shop. meanwhile we're driving around with a cracked roof glass that feels like it could eventually shatter and drop onto everyone in the car while driving.

the tech on this car is very inconsistent, some days everything works fine and other days features just do not. the digital key will be detected sometimes, and other days it is not, making it hard for me to get into the car. once the assisted driving feature said I was not paying attention and suddenly brought the car to a stop right in the middle of the highway. the brakes also do not feel strong enough. I have had several times where I needed to stop quickly because I was cut off or the light changed suddenly, and the brakes could not bring the car to a full stop like they should. on top of that, the battery does not hold as long as I expect, so I end up charging about 3 to 4 times a week.

Customer stated he has been seeing some odd behavior with the iDrive. Customer stated that when he changes driving modes from his personal default mode to Sports Mode, cosmetic content disappears from the center display. Customer stated he has not yet figured out any specific sequence that triggers this, but he intends to try to track it later. Customer stated it is the cluster screen where the speedometer would normally appear, directly behind the steering wheel, and that the problem does not interfere with switching modes, only with the decorative graphics tied to each mode. Customer stated the car is running the latest iDrive update, and that this has occurred twice so far. Writer asked if the customer could be at the vehicle so the issue could be observed, but customer stated it is hard to recreate, and that both times it happened he was already driving.

Customer reported wanting a way to keep a chosen My Modes setting as permanent. Customer noted the vehicle always goes back to the factory default at entry, so the preferred mode must be reselected each time.

this is my 4th brand-new 7 series and my 10th new bmw. pros: the engine is fantastic, a real beast; the tech is strong; and it drives very well overall.

cons: the hvac could cool better, likely because of the hidden vents, and it only got a bit better after i put clear uv tint on the windows. you also can't set sport mode as the default, even though i drive in sport most of the time. i can't remove the red and blue colors on the display and interactive bar, and i'm not a fan of those colors. the steering feels a little soft and not as connected to the road as my previous cars. it's a big car, and adding about 5" more length wasn't a good thing. the styling is just okay; i actually think my 2017 740i looks better.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

i'm pleased overall but not as thrilled as i thought i would be. a few small tweaks would really help.

air conditioned seats: i can tell the car not to turn on seat heat by default, but i can't do the same for the cooling. having a cold butt is uncomfortable for me, i don't want it at all and end up switching it off every single drive. on hot days that makes me dislike the car a bit.

- garage door openers: with such a smart car, it should use geofencing to automatically open gates and garage doors as you arrive. my old model s did that and it was extremely convenient.

- alarm: again with geofencing, the car should be able to stay unlocked and disarmed automatically when parked at home. not for everyone, but it would be easy to add as a menu option so in a safe garage you don't risk setting off the alarm or hunting for a key to open the trunk.

one-pedal driving: i use aggressive energy recovery and really like it, but i'd prefer if it brought the car all the way to a stop instead of continuing to creep.

auto hold: when auto hold releases in traffic or at lights, even with a very gentle press on the pedal the car snaps out of the hold and lurches slightly. it's annoying and should be much smoother.

on the positive side, the audio system and in-car phone are excellent. i especially value the speakerphone performance.

for an ev it truly still handles like a bmw, and i'm glad for that.

i've had the car for about 4 months and i'm splitting my thoughts into pros and cons.

pros:
- driving dynamics: really strong acceleration and power delivery, steering is accurate and easy, the car feels nicely planted in corners, and the steering weight is spot on.
- technology: screens have great clarity and quality, ui is fast, apps and info are solid, speakers/sound system are excellent, the iconic sounds are fun, and the mybmw app integration and features plus the ambient lighting are all big positives.
- styling: love the interior dash design and the look of the front fascia, especially the new lights and the kidney grille.

cons:
- brake pedal feel when slowing down isn't right.
- sound insulation around the b pillars is really weak; tyre/road and other cars' noises are way too loud for a 5 series, so the b pillars on both sides need extra deadening.
- rear legroom should be better for a car this long.
- not enough storage: missing rear seat pockets and nothing under the center console.
- rear lights don't look as iconic as the front, and those two silver bits on the lower bumper just seem out of place.

overall the experience has been very positive, the tech feels solid and the highway "self-driving" is much better than the last generation. i would like finer control over the sport mode settings. i also want clearer guidance on how to use the engine when coming off battery mode, including proper warm up time. on long drives, i'd like to hold back some battery for later while still using a bit during the trip for boost, but the current programming does not seem to support that. i realize that means more complexity and instructions, but i think many bmw owners are fine with that, and i want to get the most out of how the battery and engine work together. i came from an n63, now with a b58, and while i know they are different, the b58 sometimes sounds like it's really working even when i'm not revving it much. is that extra sound being pumped in, and is that really what i want to be hearing? i'd rather hear a confident engine than one that sounds like it's straining. also, instead of having to pay for an esim subscription, why can't the car just use my phone's hotspot for things like the youtube app.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

i want to be able to recommend the driving system, but with this g60 it feels like the japan spec has skipped some sound insulation, and when strong rain or big drops hit, the roof noise is like rain on an iron plate. if you snap the sun visor shut firmly, it sounds like sheet metal, like a car from the showa 40s era. even comparing the sun visor behavior on other demo cars, the current 5 just sounds cheap. i can only assume that some sound insulating material was left out when the rear electric shade and rear seat window screen were removed for the japanese version. to me that obviously drags down the status of the 5. i feel the weak yen has led to users being taken lightly, with the specs cut mainly to protect bmw japan's profit margin (and probably bmw in germany is laughing at them too).

negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

i got my first 5 series back in about 2001 and this is basically the only kind of vehicle i've driven. now i'm on my 5th 5 series and it's the best handling car i've had, which is why i rated it a 10. however, the tech is distracting and most of it i won't end up using. safety matters most to me and going into the screen takes my eyes off the road. my earlier cars were more basic, and that's what i actually like. i'm really upset that the cd player is gone. i spent just under $950 on the upgraded speakers and then found out the cg player was taken out, and the sales person never told me. i know there are other ways to play music, but i want to choose for myself. in short the car is fantastic, but it's also kind of a nuisance. less is more.

evidence.quote: Customer stated bluetooth only seems to function part of the time. Writer asked about the phone. Customer confirmed using an iPhone 15 with CarPlay and that it was just updated. Writer advised removing the phone from the vehicle, the vehicle from the phone, rebooting both, then pairing again as a fresh connection. Customer confirmed.

Customer stated that when she is using CarPlay, there are times she cannot skip tracks on Pandora and then the app will disconnect completely. Writer offered to help troubleshoot the concern, but customer stated she was heading into an appointment. Writer advised that troubleshooting instructions would be sent by email. Customer is using an iPhone XR on ios 18, and her carrier is AT&T.

Customer stated that CarPlay frequently fails to work. Writer confirmed the customer is using an iPhone 14 PRO Max on AT&T with software version 16.4. Writer advised rebooting the phone by fully powering it off and turning it back on, and also suggested un-pairing the phone, removing it from iDrive, then pairing again. Writer recommended restarting the iDrive by holding the radio power button for 30 seconds. Customer stated he has already performed those troubleshooting steps. Writer then suggested a one-time hard reboot of iDrive by holding the button for 70 seconds and recommended a visit to the dealership. Customer stated that when CarPlay acts up, he can still listen to music. Customer stated CarPlay sometimes does not appear, that the phone shows up but CarPlay is missing, and at other times he cannot select the CarPlay checkbox. Customer stated that when he cannot check the CarPlay box, he is also unable to delete the phone from iDrive. Customer stated CarPlay does work properly on some occasions.

I had a problem with Android Auto/Apple CarPlay - Not working/connectivity problems: "When I try using siri through apple carplay, it never picks up what I say and does not hear me at all.". Aspect Android Auto/Apple CarPlay Not Working: Other, What Android Auto/Apple CarPlay connection type is not working or not connecting properly: Wireless, What type of connection?: Wireless

Customer stated they noticed their phone shows as connected to the vehicle over Wi-Fi. Writer advised that this Wi-Fi link is used for Apple CarPlay and not for internet browsing. Customer acknowledged the information.
Customer stated he likes the Apple CarPlay layout, particularly the image size on the iDrive Control Display, noting it makes what is shown on the screen easy to see.

Customer stated that when he attempts to use the steering wheel button to make a phone call, the system responds that it cannot make the call with CarPlay active. Writer stated that holding the steering wheel button down will activate SIRI, and the driver can then say "Hey SIRI, call" followed by the desired contact.

Customer stated they suspect it is related to using Apple CarPlay, as when Apple CarPlay is connected the voice control button does not seem to function. Writer explained that Apple CarPlay uses its own operating system in the vehicle, which takes over voice control for communication and navigation. Writer advised that other voice commands, such as climate control, can still be used. Writer further advised that when connected to Apple CarPlay, for communication or navigation the voice control button needs to be pressed and held for about 3 seconds until the Siri tone is heard, then the request can be made through Siri. Customer thanked the writer for the information.

the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.

bmws drive very well and are great fun, but i will hold off buying another one until the bad visibility from the rearview mirror is fixed.

please, compare the mirrors with other makers and improve the rearview mirror.

i have owned many porsche 911s and caymans before, and i am still waiting for a porsche arriving this month, but their left corner visibility is very good.

in terms of driving enjoyment, bmw is more fun than porsche for me, so the mirror issue is really unfortunate.

i want to keep buying bmw in the future.
best regards.

the way the doors are shaped makes getting into the car awkward. i often end up bumping my head when climbing in. i am quite small, so i imagine someone taller would find it even harder to get in comfortably. the side wing mirrors also create a blind spot while driving. i am still familiarising myself with the car's features. if i had understood how tricky entry was before buying, i would have picked a different car. this part of the design really needs serious attention.

i owned an f40 before this and with the extra power it drove really well. i am not happy that the air conditioning has to be adjusted on the screen, as trying to do that while driving feels potentially dangerous. at night the ambient lighting bounces off the driver side window and blocks part of the view in the door mirror, which to me is a possible safety issue. it makes me wonder if anyone from bmw has actually driven this model in the dark. i ended up switching the ambient lighting off entirely, which makes it seem pointless to have it on during the day anyway.

i really do not like that so much info is pushed onto the touch screen, it should go back to dials and buttons, much less distracting. you are told not to change things while driving and i agree, the big screen with loads of functions is too distracting on the move. this is my first automatic bmw, all the others i had were manuals, and i was offered a different choice this time. the manual was far better, the auto has a noticeable lag when you try to pull away. visibility from the driver seat is worse than in my older models because of the pillar size. the passenger door mirror used to tilt down when reversing, that was really useful for parking, but it is gone now. i also dislike that you must pay extra for premium functions, and the dealer never pointed that out. the reversing camera is useless.

I cannot log into my spotify premium account, and when I rang the bmw helpline they told me my 3-month digital premium package must have run out. afterwards bmw emailed saying I now have to pay £9.95 per month for extra services, which I do not find acceptable on a luxury car. my bmw m440ix does not have this issue, nor any of the bmws my wife and I have had in recent years. the usb sockets only provide power and will not read data from memory sticks with my cds on them. since bmw removed cd players from their cars, they have made it harder to listen to the entertainment I want. this is meant to be a luxury brand. the car arrived with door mirrors that did not fold in automatically, but that has since been fixed, probably by a software update.

i am really disappointed that so many functions now depend on the central screen instead of the switches/buttons i had on my previous bmws. trying to do all that while driving feels very unsafe. for example, turning on auto hold takes four different sections on the screen, and there seems to be no way to have it preset so you dont need to repeat it for every single trip. on my last new 1 series the wing mirrors folded automatically, but on this one the fold mirrors on lock/unlock option is written in very faint letters and cannot actually be activated. the climate control fan speeds for medium, high and very high all end up blowing like the low setting. looking back, the handover when i bought the car should have explained the electronics much better. engine is finebetter ride none flats.

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!

really lovely car, very nice to drive and very comfortable. the warning lights in the wing mirrors are very useful and help keep you safe. for a petrol car hybrid car it is excellent for a petrol car. all the tech is in one place so you can watch the road instead of hunting round the cabin for buttons. with it linked to the bmw app on your phone, it gives peace of mind: it alerts you if someone tries to break in, shows how much petrol you have, how much air is in the tyres and when fluids are low, all before you even reach the car. brilliant idea, and the bmw staff are also very kind and helpful.

too many issues
1. the rubber gasket on the rear door, even though it is a new car, was already damaged and leaking.
2. the mirrors on this new car make a squeaky noise whenever opening or closing.
3. the key that should lock the car automatically when you walk away only works maybe 1 time out of 10.
4. the digital display also goes dark: first the navigation screen on the left side blacks out, then the speedometer side goes black while driving.
5.
when that happened, i called the bmw emergency center. they asked if there was a warning light, but with the display black i cant see any warning light.
in the end they said it was fine to keep driving
...
hey, i cant see my speed, but if i get caught they will just say it was my choice to keep going.
6. at the one month check for the water leak (and the squeaking when opening/closing), the auto lock and door mirrors,
even though i mentioned it to the dealer several times, all they did was put oil on the door mirror.
3 days later it is squeaking again!
none of the other problems have improved.
7.
even though its a brand new car, its already been back to the workshop three times.

would i recommend it?? not sure??

(im debating posting this online), but i can see the dealer is at least trying to fix it.
for now just waiting and watching.

i am really pleased with every aspect of my bmw 120 m sport. the quality of the finish inside and outside is first class, and it is a genuinely lovely car to drive. the automatic gearbox feels very smooth, and the changes are hardly noticeable, especially once you are at higher speeds. the infotainment setup is excellent, and i really enjoy being able to customise the display. when i use the maps, the layout looks great and is easy on the eyes, with all the key info visible at a glance. i especially like the way the next turn or direction step is shown. if i were choosing again, i would go for exactly the same car, which is the strongest recommendation i can give it.

overall this m135 is a big step down from my old 128ti, nowhere near as good. it just isnt as nice to drive, it tends to understeer and is awkward to manoeuvre slowly, especially parking, because the transmission feels very jerky. getting rid of the i-drive knob and all the physical heating buttons is backwards and i see it as a safety problem. the dashboard reflects off the windscreen, worse at night. the centre console actually flexes when you press the my modes button, which feels cheap. there is lots of wind noise from the wing mirrors on the motorway. the 128ti had door handle lights, m-sport pin stripes on the seat belts, coloured edging on the floor mats, red brake calipers and built-in digital services like spotify, all of which made it feel special, and the m135 lacks all of that. in the end the m135 feels disappointing and not worth the money.

i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

[controls and ui]
- removing the physical buttons and idrive dial has made operation while driving much worse.
- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.
- the ui behavior is odd, not returning to the home screen after changing modes, leaving the selection screen up.
- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

i have owned several 1 series bmws (2 f20s, 1 f40 and now this f70). build quality has been very good in all of them, though i would say the f40 was probably the best. my current bmw 120 loses out a bit because of the plastics used around the sound system speakers; my f40 had the harman kardon setup with nicer speaker facings. i do not know why bmw now only sells an automatic gearbox in the uk, but i would have liked the choice as i have always driven manuals. i notice a small lag when pulling away with the auto, which can feel unnerving at junctions. there are more things i could mention but this survey does not give enough characters!

my new 120 m sport has a nice colour and is a tidy little car. before this i had 5 new 3 series tourings, the last one a 330i m sport which was lovely, and the 120 is not in the same league. i notice the road noise gets quite loud once you are over about 50 mph, which makes the radio hard to hear. i also can't get my i pod to show info on the screen via usb, it only works over bluetooth now. the automatic gearbox doesn't feel as good or as smooth as the 330i's. the tech in this car is very hard to get used to for me as a retired older driver. i asked for an owners manual when the car was delivered but, roughly 3 months later, still haven't had one, first time i've had a new car without a handbook included. the 120 is a strong little car and i'm happy with how it performs. overall i'd give it 7 out of 10.

why is there a character limit? mechanically it feels cheap, rushed and badly tuned, not what i expected from bmw. my old 2010 e82 1 series was superior in every respect. the missing idrive wheel is a letdown and there is no proper replacement. mercedes puts a touch pad on the steering wheel, but here both next track buttons are inconsistent and irritating to use. the suspension needs more tuning for uk motorways and roads. the hybrid system also needs a lot of work: when you come up to a roundabout it sits in too high a gear and takes about two seconds to change down. i picked the bmw hybrid partly because it does not use a cvt, yet the gearbox fitted feels very slow to downshift when you need it. the auto wipers react too slowly to changing weather. and is there really no tire pressure sensor?

gears feel a little sluggish when shifting up, and there is a noticeable lag from pressing the accelerator to actually pulling away from a standstill.
i'm not keen that pretty much everything has to be done through the screen, and the gearbox just isn't like the other bmw models i've had before.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

after many years in a ford focus i was a bit nervous about switching to a bmw, but i needn't have been. it is a fantastic car. i've always had manual gearboxes before, yet this automatic is outstanding and incredibly smooth. for the last 15 years i was driving diesel, so going back to petrol has been a surprise in a good way. the handling matches, if not beats, my old car, so for me it really is the ultimate driving machine.

the m135x drive feels like a great all-rounder for its size, but it doesnt really give that big grin. the engine/exhaust sound isnt very inspiring, and when you slow down it tends to change down, so when you go to accelerate again it isnt ready and drops 1 or 2 gears, making the engine revvy and the car a bit jerky on re-acceleration. that said, on uk a and b roads its a lot of fun, no need to thrash it, just hold it in the higher rev band for a steady, manageable pace. id really like to experience how the x-drive with the dct gearbox behaves on slippery surfaces. nice car??

i have a 750e 2026, and this is my second 7 series model. from the very first day, the car has been making a repeating knocking sound from the right rear passenger side, very much like the automatic door lock noise (da-da). the dealership has been supportive, understanding, and professional while trying to track it down, and they have traced it to a valve that is supposed to push gas vapors toward the engine when a certain buildup level is reached.
this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

Customer stated that he is pleased with the overall door system, particularly the automatic opening and closing feature.

Customer stated he occasionally taps the button on the door by mistake and the door will open. Customer stated the car is not moving when this happens, but the door still opens while the vehicle is in drive. Customer confirmed to the writer that the gear was in drive when he pressed the button during the phone call. Customer stated he is 5'9" tall.

Customer requested guidance on opening the rear doors from the driver seat. Writer advised to go into apps, then vehicle apps, then doors and windows, and finally select automatic doors. Customer acknowledged the instructions.

Customer reported the passenger-side automatic door would not open or shut from the passenger-side control panel. Customer indicated this issue started a few weeks after purchase. Customer stated he brought the vehicle to the dealership and they managed to fix it. AIR: Owner states right front door close switch not working.

Customer reported that the automatic door opening feature feels too sensitive and also too slow. Customer explained that after pressing the button they have to step back, otherwise the door will not open, and even when they do move back there is still a long pause before the door actually opens. Customer stated this behavior makes them want to just pull the door open by hand, which defeats the purpose of having it open automatically. Customer expressed a desire for improvements to both the sensitivity and the speed of the automatic door operation. Writer advised that on the new i7 the automatic door opening has been updated and now operates about two seconds faster.

Customer stated the automatic doors function on the front passenger door and rear driver-side door is not operating because the buttons on those doors are not responding. Customer stated the dealer has ordered new parts and is waiting for them to come in. Customer stated the vehicle currently has 400 miles on it.
Customer stated his passenger-side automatic door is currently not functioning.

Customer reported that on the passenger side of the dash, the spot they press to open the door and see the temperature readout has stopped working. Customer stated they already have a dealership visit scheduled this week to have it inspected. Customer was rushing, so no additional questions were posed.
Customer stated the automatic doors take some patience to work with and would like the opening and closing to be a little quicker.

Customer stated she is very happy with the automatic doors and with being able to close the door by pressing the brake. She stated she likes that she no longer has to lean out to grab and shut the door.
Customer commented that the automatic doors are an excellent feature.

Customer reported that roughly a week ago the passenger-side doors stopped opening fully and no longer swing all the way out. Customer stated they intend to have the car checked by the dealer in the near future.
Customer indicated that the vehicle's automatic doors are very convenient and that closing the door with the brake pedal is a nice detail.

Customer mentioned he really enjoys that when he presses his foot on the pedal the door shuts on its own, so he does not have to lean out and pull it closed every time, and he described this as a feature that totally spoils you.
Customer noted she appreciates that you can press the button on the door and have it open for you automatically.
Customer commented the doors take too long to open and feel awkward.
Customer stated he finds the automatic door opening and closing feature really cool and noted that it functions entirely on its own.
Customer reported his knee occasionally bumps the automatic door switch and the door opens, no matter how fast he is going.
Customer stated he appreciates having the automatic doors.

Customer asked if the feature could be turned off. Writer, using RVG, guided her to Apps Menu, Vehicle, Doors and Windows, Automatic Doors, then Settings. Writer explained there is no way to disable the Automatic Doors themselves, only the option that makes the doors close when the Brake is pressed. Customer said he followed the steps and turned that setting off, but when he signed into his Driver Profile, the doors did it again. Writer had him go back into the menu and saw the setting was back on. Writer instructed him to switch it off once more and advised it should now stay saved under the customer Driver Profile and not repeat. Customer acknowledged.
Customer commented that she thinks it is cool that her husband can open the door for her from inside the vehicle.

Customer reported that the automatic doors can be a bit much at times, particularly for passengers or anyone who is not used to how the doors operate. Customer feels BMW may be trying to fix a problem that isn't really there.

after putting about 2600 miles on the car we already had to bring it in for service. the automatic door quit working. it's been roughly a month now, and the car is still sitting at the bmw service center waiting on a part. very bad experience.

Customer stated he likes being able to press a button to have the doors close automatically.
Customer mentioned they really enjoy the automatic doors on the car.

Customer stated a few times they got into the car, pressed the brake, and the automatic doors activated. Customer stated on a couple of occasions, while starting the vehicle and talking to someone, the door ended up hitting the person they were speaking with. Customer stated no one was hurt. Customer stated the other person was standing between the door and the customer so the sensors were not able to pick them up.
Customer stated they are impressed with the automatic doors.

Customer stated that the automatic doors sometimes have issues opening and closing and that the whole setup does not really make sense to him. Customer explained that if the button is not held long enough the door will not open, and also noted that if there is a sensor problem or if you stand in the wrong place, the system fails to operate correctly.

Customer asked how to open the driver's side Automatic Door from the outside. Writer explained that on the Automatic Door button to the left of the exterior door handle, press the lit area on the button and then step away from the door's travel path.
Customer stated she realy likes the Automatic Doors and that they open on their own.
Customer stated the automatic doors are very useful, especially during school drop-off with the kids, and he mentioned particular scenarios with young children.
Customer stated that if he rests his leg against the driver door in just the wrong spot, it accidentally presses the door open button and the door can open while he is driving at about 20 mph.

Customer stated he really appreciates the automatic doors in the vehicle. blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer reported upgrading from a Mercedes and commented it would not have felt like less of an upgrade even if the newer features were missing. Customer noted they had ordered a car at another dealership and were told about the automatic doors, theater screen, and lounge seats.

the car is truly outstanding. this is probably around my 10th 7 series, with the last one being a 2021 750, which i honestly thought was an excellent vehicle. but this new one completely outclasses that 750. even though the sticker prices weren't all that far apart, this car is on a different level in how smooth it is and how refined the luxury feels.

the seat cushions and headrests are incredibly comfortable, the crystal elements on the dash feel really opulent, and the acceleration and overall quietness are just remarkable. the dashboard layout and the whole control center setup seem extremely well thought out.

as i was turning in my 750, which i had really loved, at the dealership, the only word that came to mind to describe how i now saw that car in comparison was "archaic."

the pricing on this car is way too high. i managed to negotiate a strong lease, but there is no chance i would spend the $190k msrp on an electric car that is bound to lose a lot of value. overall the tech is very solid, but bmw still not getting the esim to function correctly is incredibly annoying. one of the main reasons i chose this car was the theatre screen, and now it only operates if i run ugly cables to it. the seats are mostly comfortable, yet they do not give enough side bolster support, so i would really like more hold in the corners. the heated seats and heated armrests are fantastic and the infotainment works well, plus the upgraded sound system is outstanding. when using apple carplay, though, the bottom left corner with distance and time remaining is completely hidden behind my right hand while driving. if i swapped cars today i would rather be in an m5 touring.

car is overall very good but there are a few things that really need work. the air conditioning feels weak and you can't aim it right at one person. the charger setup is awful and charging takes way too long. i do like the "hey bmw" function, but when you have to say the same command 3 times it becomes frustrating. you're not able to close the trunk with a button from inside, even though there are all kinds of ways to close the doors, which doesn't make sense. the tv screen that drops down in back completely blocks the driver's view. they should let the rearview mirror switch to a camera image so you can still see behind. the car ought to start out in efficient mode instead of one that burns more miles. the seat heating doesn't get really warm and the cooling is also weak. the moon roof lights are tied to the lights on the side panels and can't be separated, and it should be possible to mix those colors.

the car itself is really strong and looks gorgeous, i honestly only have compliments for it. my one big suggestion is that buyers should be told exactly which features are on the car and which are missing. after i bought mine, i found out it does not stay in its lane for hands-free driving, even though i saw ads and that feature was a main reason i picked this model. this particular build does not do that, and spending over 100,000 then feeling like i was misled makes me sad at times. still, it is a great vehicle overall.
