right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

Customer asked when the first oil change is required. Writer advised it is due at 10,000 miles or after 12 months, and customer acknowledged.
Customer stated the matte exterior paint is difficult to keep clean because he is not able to run it through a car wash.

Customer mentioned getting an offer for a track day event and asked if it could be passed on to another person. Writer advised the Customer to reach out to the performance center about this.

title: G70 Public charging / external providers
requirement_statement: Improve 'Public charging / external providers' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer expressed that the number of Electrify America charging stations on the east coast is insufficient, so the 2 years of free charging does not feel justified. Customer noted he has to drive nearly an hour just to reach one of the stations. Writer explained that BMW has teamed up with 6 other manufacturers and has started building an additional 30,000 super charges across the United States this year. Writer further advised that BMW has also partnered with Tesla and is projected to gain access to select super charges on the Tesla network in early 2025.

Customer asked why EA was charging their credit card when there is supposed to be free charging. Writer advised that charges beyond a card hold or idle fees need to be addressed directly with electrify america. Customer acknowledged this and said they would reach out to EA.

Customer stated his experience charging at Electrify America stations has been poor. Customer stated certain chargers fail to start charging, and others stop partway through a session. Customer stated he typically has to try several Electrify America chargers before locating one that will charge his vehicle.
Customer reports Electrify America has been working very well, and said the only issue is that it can be too busy at times.

Customer stated that at times this vehicle is unable to charge at the same Electrify America charging station. Customer stated she believes the problem is with that Electrify America location, since she experienced the same charging issue there with her Mercedes BEV. Customer stated she needed to end the call, and the writer did not have the chance to ask any clarifying questions. Customer requested a callback.
The writer later called the customer back and the customer stated she no longer has this car and that it was returned to the dealer. The customer then disconnected the call.

the auto time zone adjustment just does not function. the radio also fails to quiet when i give carplay voice commands. with a 291 mile range, the actual distance i can use is heavily cut because i only charge between 20% and 80%. right now the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available. every leg of a trip easily ends up with an extra hour added for each charging stop. i still dont know for sure, but if the battery life really proves to be just 8 years then this purchase will have been a poor investment. my insurance premium has shot up by about 200% even though the car has all this safety equipment. the explanation given is that repairing that safety tech after a crash costs a lot more, and the insurers claim there is not enough data yet to justify lowering the rates. sun glare or heavy rain seem to mess with the cameras trying to read the surroundings, and then the system basically chooses to shut itself off because it sees too much risk. when i drive on a road running parallel to train tracks, and a side street that crosses those tracks comes up, the railroad crossing lights aimed at the train get misread by the car as a stop light intended for my parallel road. there is also one set of traffic signals that the car reads as if they were a yield sign. the navigation does not let me set a preference for electrify america chargers when the planned distance exceeds the current charge; it just picks the first charger it finds. for at least the first 3 years, that electrify america selection option really should be there.

the car rides amazingly smoothly, with superb handling and strong acceleration, really the ultimate driving machine. i like the styling inside and out and am glad i basically went with a fully loaded version. the kids love theater mode, and it lets me watch tv while i am at a charging station.

improvement areas are small: i would like more battery range, with around 350 miles or more on a full charge. the interactive screen setup works well but feels like it has almost too many choices, so it can take longer than i would like to get to what i need. finally, bluetooth and wifi are not always reliable, and roughly 20% of the time my phone cannot see the car wifi so carplay will not work.

right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

title: G70 Rear seat entertainment
requirement_statement: Improve 'Rear seat entertainment' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 24 respondents complain and 17 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer noted she would have chosen the Home theater screen, but it obstructs the view out the rear and BMW does not offer a camera/rear-view mirror setup that could show the rear image in the mirror, so she decided not to order the screen.
Customer stated his son really enjoys watching cartoons on the Theater Screen.

During RVG customer asked what the button in the roof area is supposed to do. Writer advised that this switch is used to raise or lower the Theater Screen. Customer then stated that it is currently not operating. Writer explained that if either of the front seats is moved too far back, the Theater Screen will be blocked from coming down to prevent damage. Customer thanked the Writer for the explanation.
Customer asked whether, when using the screen, the driver seat is kept from contacting the Theater Screen. Writer confirmed that it does.

Customer asked how to activate the TV in the rear of the vehicle. Writer advised that first the E-SIM has to be activated on a cell phone plan. Customer stated he has a TelStar Mobile plan. Writer advised once the E-SIM is active through TelStar Mobile, he will need to switch on the TV to start the activation, log in to the StreamBox TV service with his ShopZone account, and enter the 6 digit code to complete activation. Writer advised that once it is activated, he can begin downloading apps to stream shows and movies.

Customer reported that whenever he folds down the theater screen, the screen powers up and the video itself works fine, but there is no sound from the vehicle speakers with that video. Customer stated he then holds the radio volume knob to restart iDrive, and after that reboot the theater audio comes through the car speakers as it should.
Customer stated this problem has been happening since he bought the car. Customer stated he ran a Remote Software Upgrade yesterday, but the concern is still there. Customer stated he already brought it up with the dealer, but they did not carry out a full diagnostic or offer a lasting repair for the audio issue.
Writer advised that the dealer will need to perform further diagnosis on the concern.

Customer shared that his kids really enjoy the Theater Screen in the rear. Writer asked whether the customer had activated the eSim. Customer replied that he has not done that. Customer stated he currently uses a Fire Stick instead and likes it that way. Writer encouraged the customer to contact if any help is needed.
Customer stated the theater screen is difficult to use. Customer mentioned the Firestick remedy and said the process was clumsy.
Customer stated that if they have a larger passenger in the front seat, they cannot fold down the theatre screen because the passenger is in the way.
Customer stated he wants the theater screen only if it can wirelessly stream content. Customer stated this would let his kids watch whatever they want in the vehicle.
Customer stated that they appreciate the large display located in the rear of the vehicle.
Customer stated it is annoying that his seat has to be moved so far forward whenever the theater screen is down.
Customer expressed that they love the theater screen and feel its quality is excellent.

Customer mentioned that her earlier 2023 model had a rear-seat TV, but her 2026 does not come with that feature. Customer said she was not aware the TV was excluded from the package, but also noted it is not a big concern for her.

Customer reported he would like to fold the Theater Screen down without having to move the front seats. Customer added his children want to use the Theater Screen while he is driving, but the driver seat slides so far forward that he is not comfortable.

Customer stated the rear TV was great and offered excellent entertainment options for passengers in the back.
Customer reported that his daughter really loves the theater screen.

Customer stated he continues to pay for an eSIM, but the Amazon Fire TV on the Theater Screen has stopped working. Customer stated the eSIM is activated, connected to his BMW ID, and has been added as a device in the vehicle under the Mobile Devices menu. Customer stated that when he turns on the Theater Screen and selects the Amazon Fire TV input, the screen displays a prompt advising him to verify that the internet connection is active and that roaming is enabled. Customer stated he has previously watched an entire football game using Amazon Fire TV on the Theater Screen.
Writer stated to go to the Apps Menu, then Vehicle Apps, and then Mobile Devices to confirm that "Personal eSIM" appears. Writer stated to open the Personal eSIM settings to make sure the data connection is permitted and roaming is switched on. Customer stated he was inside the vehicle and verified these settings are correct. Writer stated to recheck that the Theater Screen source is set to Amazon Fire TV and that the customer Amazon account is properly linked in the settings. Customer confirmed both of those settings are correct. Customer stated he did not have additional time to continue troubleshooting and that he will consult the dealer regarding this concern. The writer was not able to obtain more details about the service provider or whether the data plan is unlimited.
Customer stated he appreciates having the theater screen in the car to entertain his kids. Customer stated it is very helpful for keeping them busy during trips.

Customer stated that the large screen in the rear will not even fold down unless the front seats are moved practically all the way forward. Customer stated it feels kind of embarrassing to make the front passenger scoot up just to show off that feature. Customer stated the screen also blocks most of the sunroof, so you can't see out of the entire thing. Customer stated it seems like a major design flaw and that the car would look better if the screen just wasn't there at all.
Customer stated that the esim for the theatre screen occasionally fails to connect or does not load any content.

Customer asked about using Fire TV on the theater screen and how to stream shows and movies. Writer advised the customer to sign in with their Amazon account and then use the vehicle's 5G connection to stream the content. Customer acknowledged the information.

Customer asked how to use the theater screen and how to hook up a computer to it. Writer explained that an internet connection is required to stream amazon fire content. Writer advised the Customer to set up the eSIM and stated a computer can be connected using the HDMI Port located at the bottom of the screen. Customer acknowledged this.
Customer mentioned their kids are big fans of the screen in the back.

Customer explained he conducts a lot of meetings while in the car and feels it would be amazing to have a Microsoft Teams app built into the rear entertainment system. Customer emphasized he really, really wants this to be considered, as it would be very useful in an executive vehicle.
Customer stated he really likes the large Theater Screen in the rear of the vehicle.
Customer stated the rear seat in this vehicle is amazing. Customer added that the Theater Screen is a great feature to keep his kids entertained on long trips.

Customer stated he prefers the silver rims, saying they suit the vehicle better and make it look as if it is wearing jewelry.
Customer inquired whether her vehicle comes fitted with run-flat tires. Writer clarified that it is equipped with all season tires that are not run-flats. Customer acknowledged the information.

Customer indicated she prefers runflat tires because she does not want to risk being stranded at night. Writer advised that, if she is stranded by the roadside, she should press the SOS button to request assistance.

Customer stated they would have preferred all season tires instead of the summer tires. Customer stated the current tires do not handle that well in rain and he would not be able to drive in snow with the type of tire the vehicle comes with.

Customer expressed a wish for factory all-season tire options, explaining that the current setup forces switching between summer and winter tires when driving between Ohio and Florida. Writer acknowledged this input and agreed to pass it on for engineering review.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

fantastic vehicle, i'm a bmw fan for life and it will probably be the only brand i ever own.

Customer reported that the vehicle arrived with the wheels improperly balanced, which a third party tire shop later verified using road force balance testing. Customer stated there has been strong vibration inside the cabin at speeds around 55-70 mph. Customer indicated they used an outside tire shop because the BMW dealership was not able to assist, explaining that the customer had possessed the car long enough that they could not determine when or where the issue originated. Customer noted that every wheel needed substantial weight changes, suggesting they were far out of balance from delivery. Writer documented that after the balancing service the vibration is reduced, but some remains.

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

performance, reliability, tech, luxury, comfort - the whole package is there. i'd really like to be able to pin more apps onto that left sidebar on the home screen. i used to have the weather sitting there, then it just seemed to vanish. i rely on quick shortcuts, so i ended up putting the weather app in the shortcut section instead.
about a week after i bought the car i got a flat tire, right after a storm, and bmw connect happened to be down. i had to arrange one tow to get back home, then a second tow to reach the bmw dealer that's out of town. that meant a lot of time just waiting around for tow trucks. in that situation a spare tire would have been very useful. i was told i'd be reimbursed for the towing because bmw couldn't provide a tow, but that was in october and i still haven't received anything.
otherwise the car itself is fantastic. i really like being behind the wheel. i've always enjoyed driving, and with this being my 4th bmw - a 528 and two 740s before - this 760 tops them all. it has taken the driving experience to a completely new level for me.

otherwise the car itself is fantastic. i really like being behind the wheel. i've always enjoyed driving, and with this being my 4th bmw - a 528 and two 740s before - this 760 tops them all. it has taken the driving experience to a completely new level for me.

the refinement of the car is outstanding, and the range is surprisingly strong for a vehicle of this size. the tech is excellent as well, though a few small usability tweaks would help, like keeping the climate settings synced across trips or having auto hold stay on from one drive to the next. they seem minor, but redoing them manually every single time gets a bit annoying.

my other suggestion is to include an all season tire package with the car, or at least make sure dealers have plenty of winter tires available. i spent weeks trying to track down winter or all season tires that would fit this car. in the end i had to have them shipped from nevada by a third-party shop, because there was not a single bmw dealer within roughly 500 miles that could provide tires that matched the factory recommendations for the vehicle.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

Customer stated a tire on the new vehicle suddenly went flat with no obvious reason, and the dealer inspection did not show any damage. Writer acknowledged this was an unusual situation. Customer stated the tire was replaced, but the actual cause was never identified. Key read indicates this occurred at about 540 miles and it was the left rear tire that failed. Tire was BRIDGESTONE 459.70, TIRE SIZE: 285/40 R20 108 H.
Customer commented the car ought to be supplied with a spare tire or at least a donut.

the car itself has been a good one.
it is really frustrating that the headlights cant be switched off, and even when i turn on the air conditioner from my smartphone, the compressor doesnt run, so it just sends out air. the tires also wear out fast, and the size is so big that there are hardly any choices.
the staff member yamamoto at the coastal dealer where i bought it was one of the worst i have ever come across.
all communication was slow, i had a bad feeling already, and sure enough the response ended up being the worst i have ever experienced.
its one thing to mess up a car inspection, but you absolutely cannot make mistakes with the documents i prepared, since they are required for the procedure.
i asked them to redo the paperwork, yet there was no contact at all, and when i finally pushed, the document that was only valid for 3 months had already expired because of the negligence of the person in charge, so i had to go get the exact same document again. this should not happen with a car in the 10 million class.
i am furious with yamamoto.
since the place is far away, i almost feel it is a small blessing in misfortune that i dont have to depend on that dealer much.

title: G60 Center console, front
requirement_statement: Improve 'Center console, front' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the center console layout is terrible. Customer stated the start/stop button being so close to the other buttons makes her nervous and she feels it is not safe.
Customer stated the center console feels too small. Writer asked what she typically stores in it, and Customer replied that she usually keeps her change purse or a flashlight there.

Customer stated he would prefer the center console buttons to provide a bit of haptic feedback. Customer stated that when he is driving, it is difficult to tell if a button actually registered the press, and some haptic response would give him confirmation that the button was activated.

the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

i've had the car for about 4 months and i'm splitting my thoughts into pros and cons.

pros:
- driving dynamics: really strong acceleration and power delivery, steering is accurate and easy, the car feels nicely planted in corners, and the steering weight is spot on.
- technology: screens have great clarity and quality, ui is fast, apps and info are solid, speakers/sound system are excellent, the iconic sounds are fun, and the mybmw app integration and features plus the ambient lighting are all big positives.
- styling: love the interior dash design and the look of the front fascia, especially the new lights and the kidney grille.

cons:
- brake pedal feel when slowing down isn't right.
- sound insulation around the b pillars is really weak; tyre/road and other cars' noises are way too loud for a 5 series, so the b pillars on both sides need extra deadening.
- rear legroom should be better for a car this long.
- not enough storage: missing rear seat pockets and nothing under the center console.
- rear lights don't look as iconic as the front, and those two silver bits on the lower bumper just seem out of place.

- technology: screens have great clarity and quality, ui is fast, apps and info are solid, speakers/sound system are excellent, the iconic sounds are fun, and the mybmw app integration and features plus the ambient lighting are all big positives.
- styling: love the interior dash design and the look of the front fascia, especially the new lights and the kidney grille.

cons:
- brake pedal feel when slowing down isn't right.
- sound insulation around the b pillars is really weak; tyre/road and other cars' noises are way too loud for a 5 series, so the b pillars on both sides need extra deadening.
- rear legroom should be better for a car this long.
- not enough storage: missing rear seat pockets and nothing under the center console.
- rear lights don't look as iconic as the front, and those two silver bits on the lower bumper just seem out of place.

i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

i really enjoy how this car drives, and that was the main reason i chose it. i also like the updated exterior look. still, i was close to going with something else instead: a genesis, an audi allroad wagon, or a mercedes wagon. the genesis appealed because its interior finish seemed better than the bmw, the audi wagon because i prefer wagons and have already owned three audi avant wagons, and if audi still sold the avant i would have gone for that. the mercedes wagon was ruled out because the lease was too expensive. with this 540, the interior has been a letdown, as my previous 540 felt more upscale inside. this one makes me feel like i am sitting at an apple laptop, and it really bothers me that the retractable lid over the cup holder area is gone. without it, that spot looks like a random catch-all and ruins the console's previously nice look. the material covering the top of the dash also seems cheaper.

evidence.quote: Customer stated she would like to use the rear window shades while still being able to see out through them from the interior of the vehicle.

Customer reported that the sunshades will randomly close by themselves when the vehicle is parked and shut off, and it is annoying to come back and find them closed. Writer explained they are designed to close to protect the theater screen. Customer would like the shades to automatically open again when he re-enters the car so parking is easier.
Customer noted via email that the rear sunshade is just too dark.
Customer stated they would prefer the rear sun screen to be more see-through, as right now they cannot see through it at all.
Customer stated he would like to have one single button that could both open and close the blinds in the back.

Customer stated that with the center rear window sun shades lowered, he is unable to see out through the rear window.

Customer explained that on his previous 7 Series he could simply tap the shades button once or twice and the shades would open or close. With the current 7 Series, pressing that button now brings up a menu on the display and he has to select multiple options from the screen to open or close them.
Customer stated she really enjoys all of the window shades in the car that can be slid upward.

Customer stated that after about 1 month of using the car, the right rear window shade would no longer raise. Customer stated that she has roughly 900 miles on the car at this time.

Customer stated that when he enters the vehicle using only his Digital Key, the Driver Profile switches to the Guest profile. Customer stated he wants his personal Driver Profile to load rather than the Guest profile. Writer explained that once his own Driver Profile is signed in, he should tap the Driver Profile icon in the upper right of the screen, go to Profile Settings, then Driver Recognition, and adjust the recognition method to use both the Vehicle Key and the Digital Key.

Customer stated she feels it takes around 15 minutes to get everything configured in the car because certain settings do not seem to stay, such as the sync button and the automatic stop start. Writer advised that these particular functions are not saved in the driver profile.

Customer stated she wants to have her own digital profile, since she is still set up under her husbands name from her earlier vehicles. Writer used RVG to walk her through scanning the barcode and signing in with her BMW ID, and showed her how to connect her keys to her driver profile so she can customize seat settings, climate settings, and more.

Customer reported the car repeatedly locks and unlocks by itself while parked in the garage, even after setting the home address and trying to turn off the feature. Writer advised this may be related to phone and watch digital keys not being properly associated with the driver profile, and walked the customer through checking profile settings and connecting mobile devices. Writer told the customer to look for plus symbols in driver recognition indicating devices that still need to be linked.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

title: G60 Luggage compartment
requirement_statement: Improve 'Luggage compartment' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 22 respondents complain and 12 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: the trunk space inside is quite small considering how big the car looks from the outside.

I had a serious problem with Rear cargo/luggage cover - DTU: "The trunk looks big at first but actually feels cramped. It doesn't hold larger items well because the spare tire takes up so much space, so there isn't enough depth for big stuff."

we have been buying bmw cars for at least twenty years and i always feel very safe in them. i drive about 25 miles or so every day and usually replace the car every three years. this one is very comfortable and the visibility is excellent, which is one of my essential requirements. i really like the white interior, but it is not as nice as my last car where everything inside was light cream, so i was very disappointed. i even went to look at mercedes and audi to compare their interiors and was actually about to write the deposit cheque for a mercedes before changing my mind. learning all the new systems like the heating is taking me a while, probably because i am seventy one. we prefer a spacious car with good room for passengers. the boot is big and the saloon feels very secure as we travel often and do not want anything left visible. i also wonder why you removed the sleeves on the backs of the front seats, now there is no storage there.

even though i love how the car handles, there are a few things you took away that my 2021 had and i just don't get why. you removed the pockets on the back of the seats. maybe that cut production costs, but without those pockets i have to dump stuff like umbrellas and the kids' things on the rear floor. the worst part, and honestly a deal breaker when my lease is up, is the trunk size. i can't fit my grandchild's stroller in there, or a full food shop, or my mother's walker. i also dislike the silver/chrome 5s on the rear windows, it's a luxury vehicle and i don't need it shouting that it's a 5 series. the glove box is smaller now, same with the door wells, and i really don't like that i can't leave anything in the console tray since i'm no longer able to cover it. i'm forced to look away from the road to manage the controls because the knobs are gone and everything is flat. with the fan vents hidden and streamlined, i can't adjust the airflow direction anymore. i could keep going, but i'm sure the team who came up with this very modern car is pleased with what they made. for me, if these things aren't changed by the time my lease ends, i'll most likely move to another luxury brand. i genuinely hope you take this feedback on board. when i checked reviews afterwards, i saw these issues weren't just mine, a lot of people felt the same way. i really believe i'm exactly the kind of customer you target, so i hope you treat my comments seriously. my whole family drives bmws and nobody from about 35 to 70 is happy with the new design. it feels very clunky and not sleek anymore. i've already told my sales person all of this. again, i hope you truly take in and value my feedback.
anna kerr

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

no proper gear shifter, just that goofy little switch, and the controls are a pain to work with. half the settings don't stay put after i shut off the ignition. the retractable steering wheel doesn't slide back by itself when i turn the car off and open the door. ac won't hold the recirc setting, it changes once the car is turned off, same annoyance. also really dumb that the engine "off" at stops got deleted. the on/off button is crammed next to other buttons so you might kill the engine at the wrong time. simple buttons would do a better job for changing drive modes than that silly dial and the touch screen. the car feels too bulky and wide, which makes parking more of a chore. in sport mode the mpg drops from about 34 to around 28, yet the sport mode doesn't feel all that spirited. the sport seat hugging you is fantastic but it only happens in sport mode. cleaning the windshield is awkward because the wipers don't pull away far enough. the warning system for people approaching the car from any direction isn't sensitive enough, so i have to stare around a lot more. 

the good bits are the automatic backup feature, really useful given how big the car is, and the b & w stereo, miles better than the karmon-hardin setup, plus this one came with normal tires instead of run flats! that sport seat wrap that grabs you is excellent, just a shame it only "shows up" in sport mode.

Customer stated the heating system is excellent. Customer stated the cabin stays comfortable without him having to keep changing the climate settings.

Customer stated the Climate Control system feels complicated. Customer stated the Climate Control screen has a lot of clutter. Customer stated he would like the Climate Control to be more straightforward and easier to use.

Customer stated the air conditioning should cool the cabin more quickly and noted it takes some time before it gets cold. Customer mentioned this is especially important because the vehicle is in Florida where the heat is intense and emphasized that the air conditioning is probably more important than the motor since it is a hot car. Writer acknowledged.
Customer stated the air conditioning performs very well and mentioned they especially appreciate this feature with summer coming up in North Carolina.

Customer stated he had expected 4 zone climate control, but learned it is not available in the U.S. Customer stated he would have paid additional cost to get that feature. Customer stated that when he ordered the vehicle, he was never told it would come without rear climate controls.

Customer stated that whenever he enters the vehicle, the heated seats and heated steering wheel switch on automatically and he wants that turned off. Writer advised these features must be manually disabled by the customer. Writer further noted the vehicle is programmed to enable them automatically once the outside temperature drops below a specific level.

Customer reported the heater seems to switch on by itself even though the climate control display shows everything as off. Customer stated she can feel warm air coming out of the vents while the system indicates it is completely off. Customer noted this has happened about three times over the last month and is not a daily issue. Customer confirmed it only occurs with the heater blowing air, not with the air conditioning. Customer stated these incidents took place when it was hot outside, with the windows open, and she had not turned on the heater or A/C manually. Customer added that heat was coming from all the vents. Writer asked whether she had turned the climate controls off herself or if they were already off when this happened, and customer replied they were already off. i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

title: G70 Intelligent Personal Assistant
requirement_statement: Improve 'Intelligent Personal Assistant' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 22 respondents complain and 15 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer reported she really likes the new version of the personal assistant. Customer stated it feels slick and is helpful with whatever she needs it to do.
Customer stated giving the IPA directions on where to go is both easy and fun for them.
Customer stated IPA had stopped functioning, but after completing an iDrive reset it started working normally again.

Customer inquired whether she could use the IPA to handle navigation. Writer confirmed that navigation can be controlled through IPA and suggested using a voice command such as "Hello BMW. Open Navigation and take me to.." followed by the desired address or point of interest.

Customer stated that the voice recognition function in the vehicle is not performing well and keeps forcing them to use manual controls, which they find distracting while driving. Customer further stated that, even when trying to use the voice or hands-free options, the system still does not reliably pick up or understand their voice commands.
Customer stated the IPA would not pick up a siriusxm station just by saying the name, and he had to say the number so it would change to that station.

Customer states the Intelligent Personal Assistant does not seem to pick up on their northeastern accent. Customer states when they say, "Hey BMW. Change to SiriusXM station 102." it ends up choosing 212 instead. Customer states that when someone with more of a southern accent talks to the IPA it appears to understand them fine. Customer states that when they say "lower the screens" it does not respond, and they have to say "shades" specifically. Customer states this might be due to their accent.
Customer states they would like the Personal Assistant to be able to switch to an alternate route to the same destination while guidance is already running.

Customer inquired what the personal assistant option in the iDrive menu was for. Writer explained it is the voice assistant feature, where he can say "Hey BMW" to carry out tasks. Customer replied he knows that function, he just had not understood that was what it is called.
Customer stated the IPA is helpful for entering addresses and dialing phone numbers.
Customer stated he is very pleased with the voice command system, especially that it will lower the windows when he asks.
Customer mentioned she enjoys using the personal assistant, both for adjusting various settings and for putting in navigation destiantions.

Customer stated that about a week after getting the vehicle, the Voice Command stopped functioning. Customer reported it no longer works with the microphone button or when saying "Hello BMW". Customer mentioned they do not believe an OTA update was installed and that they are not with the vehicle right now. Writer recommended rebooting iDrive by pressing and holding the radio volume knob for 30 seconds.
Customer stated he is pleased with the IPA.

Customer stated he really likes that he can tell the personal assistant "Roll down my window" and the system automatically knows which window to lower, without him needing to specifically say "Driver's Side window."
Customer stated that the IPA was not working for him. Via RVG, writer directed the customer to tap on Apps>Personal Assistant, and then assisted through RVG in switching the feature on.
Customer stated that being able to speak to the car and have it carry out his requests is a great feature.

Customer stated the microphone for the personal assistant initially did not seem to recognize him very often, but that this issue appears to have cleared up on its own and he is now having no issues with it.

Customer stated he mainly uses Siri to make phone calls because when he asks the BMW assistant to call someone, it only pulls the numbers onto the display and he still has to start the call himself. Customer stated Siri will dial directly from the spoken command. Writer asked if his contacts were synced with the vehicle, and Customer confirmed they are.

Customer stated he has to press the microphone button on the steering wheel several times before the personal assistant responds. Writer asked how his mobile phone is connected. Customer replied that it is connected through Android Auto. Writer explained that pressing and holding the microphone button is actually activating the assistant on his mobile device. Writer advised that he would need to have hey BMW turned on in order to use the vehicle's personal assistant. Customer acknowledged this information.
Customer noted he had set his IPA name to Alfred and was upset that the assistant only has a female voice, with no other choices offered, including no masculine option.

Customer stated the intelligent voice assistant has poor understanding of their commands, especially for climate control tasks like turning on the passenger side controls. Writer went over the need for specific voice command wording, including using navigate home instead of I want to go home. Customer responded that their commands are successful only around 10% of the time.

Customer stated he feels comfortable with roughly 70 percent of the vehicle features and technology but has difficulty with the remaining 30 percent. Customer commented that the setup seems aimed at voice commands rather than using physical switches. Customer stated the voice control does not pick up a Southern accent very well and misunderstands his commands about one out of three times.
Customer stated he enjoys that he can speak to the vehicle and that it will respond back to him.
Customer stated that the IPA will open the windows, but it does not close them.
Customer sais he makes regular use of his personal assistant and finds it extremely helpful for getting around.

Customer reported that the mic button on the steering wheel only works after he presses it twice. After that, one press works normally, but every time he restarts the car he has to do the double press again.

Customer stated it is difficult for him to know what voice commands he can use to perform certain functions. Customer asked if there is anything he needs to read. Writer advised that the owner manual includes basic short commands. Customer then asked specifically for a command that would just open and close the back windshield sun shade. Writer suggested trying open/close middle rear sunshade/blind, but this command was not working. Customer stated he is able to get the rear left and rear right shades to open and close on their own, but not the back windshield sunshade. Writer advised that they will follow up with the team to see if an answer can be found, and stated that if a response is received, the writer will contact the customer.

Customer reported having some "odd problems" with the car where it seems like it is recording their phone calls, and they notice the icon that indicates it is listening for a voice command, even though they have not requested anything. Writer asked if they might be saying the wake word or saying BMW at all. Customer confirmed they are not doing that and mentioned they will take the vehicle to the dealership so they can look into it. Customer was pressed for time and unable to explain the situation further.

Customer stated he has an Android phone connected through Android Auto and when he presses the steering wheel voice button it always seems to trigger his phone. Writer advised that a short press activates the BMW system, while a long press calls up the Google assistant. Writer also advised using the BMW wake word, which by default is "Hey BMW" to speak to the car.
Customer stated he is having issues operating the IPA. Writer suggested some troubleshooting steps, but Customer declined and said he would sort it out on his own.
Customer stated he is pleased with the IPA.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

title: G60 Comfort Access
requirement_statement: Improve 'Comfort Access' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated she appreciates that when she walks away from the vehicle it will automatically lock on its own.

Customer explained that on her 2022 model she was able to lock the car and, when approaching it, she could tap the left rear door and all of the doors would unlock, but that this function no longer works on the current vehicle. Customer stated that now, when she gets close and opens the front passenger side door, all doors then open, and asked if there is any way to program it so she could touch the rear passenger door and have all doors unlock. Writer advised that on this model year the rear doors do not have comfort access and that the feature is only present on the two front doors, which is why the vehicle is operating this way. Customer thanked the writer for clarifying the issue.
Customer stated BMW's Comfort Access works well. Customer stated that whether she has the key fob or the Digital Key, the car unlocks the same way as she approaches.

Customer reported that when he walks up to the car it no longer unlocks automatically; he now needs to grab the handle. Writer offered RVG. Customer mentioned he was driving another vehicle at that time. Writer asked if he had received an RSU, and customer replied no. (G070-25-11-530) Writer recommended first verifying that the permissions had not been reset and invited the customer to get in touch again when he is with the vehicle for additional troubleshooting. Writer attempted to follow up with a detailed step-by-step, but the customer did not answer.

Customer stated that whenever he goes near the car with the key, the vehicle beeps, and said this happens every single time he approaches, which he finds a bit annoying. Writer asked the customer some questions about the situation and explained that the vehicle should have a feature called Exclude Home, and verified in the current software that this setting can turn off comfort access only when the car is at the home location. Writer offered to walk through how to use this feature either right away or at another time. Customer declined immediate support due to time constraints, saying he could either return to the dealer to review it with the salesman or arrange a callback next week, when he would be free all week. Writer set up a callback for Monday to assist the customer with the comfort access settings, and later reached out and left a voicemail requesting a return call.
Customer stated the doors only sometimes auto lock or unlock when holding the key fob for comfort access.
Customer commented he would prefer if the rear doors still offered comfort access so they could lock and unlock from the rear handles instead of only being able to use the front doors.

Customer asked if the doors are supposed to lock when a Key Fob is inside the vehicle. Customer stated she uses both the Digital Key and the physical Key Fob, especially when she plans to valet the car. Customer stated that on one occasion she walked away while the Key Fob was lying on the seat and the doors still locked. Writer stated the doors should not lock if the vehicle senses a Key Fob inside. Writer stated that since the fob was resting on the seat without anything covering it, it may be worthwhile to have the dealer look into this and also check whether the Key Fob battery is low.

this bmw feels more like the ultimate cruising machine than the ultimate driving machine. over the years i've had several bmws, and this one is the softest and least responsive of them. it's a very nice car overall, but it doesn't have the same feel as the earlier generations. this is my third or fourth 5 series, plus a few older 7 series.

i was immediately let down that it doesn't come with a sunroof at all, which i think is a major miss. i also can't wrap my head around why you can't open or unlock the car from the rear doors. when you walk up with your hands full, those are usually the doors you go for first, so it turns into an awkward two step routine that just seems pointless.

if i had known about these things before buying this 5 series, i wouldn't have gone ahead with the purchase. and if they stay the same, i wouldn't buy another one.

title: G70 Navigation
requirement_statement: Improve 'Navigation' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 21 respondents complain and 11 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.

evidence.quote: Customer commented that the augmented reality feature is excellent and gives very accurate guidance on where the car should turn.

Customer stated the BMW built-in navigation is superior and easier to use than any other manufacturer's built-in navigation system. Customer stated he appreciates having the built-in navigation and maps displayed on the large central screen.
Customer reported having issues with navigation use. Writer offered steps to troubleshoot, which the customer declined, stating he will sort it out on his own.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

this car will not suit everyone. the ride is smooth and quiet, the seats and audio are excellent, and the fuel economy and performance are impressive for such a large vehicle. the accent lighting is something I truly enjoy. the downside is the slightly isolated feel of the ride and some tech that comes across as intrusive. the accelerator pedal has a bit of a sticky feel, and the wave-your-foot trunk opener hardly ever works. the nav system is dreadful. it does not seem set up for americans, and its guidance is often inconsistent and wrong: saying "bear left" when there is no reason, then not saying it when there should be; sending me onto blocked or unfinished roads even though the map later shows them as blocked; telling me to stay on the same road ahead when nothing is actually changing; using bear left/right when you are really turning onto a different road and it should say "turn left onto...". it also does not announce when it is rerouting. there is better technology out there.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.
