I had a minor problem with Built-in navigation system - Inaccurate: "The navigation maps seem a bit outdated and are missing some newer streets that have been there for more than a year.". Aspect Navigation System Inaccurate: Address/street/city not found
Customer stated the navigation setup, including all its features, works very well. Customer stated it is far superior to the one in their Range Rover.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.

with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the entertainment setup is poor. I cannot log into my spotify premium account, and when I rang the bmw helpline they told me my 3-month digital premium package must have run out. afterwards bmw emailed saying I now have to pay £9.95 per month for extra services, which I do not find acceptable on a luxury car. my bmw m440ix does not have this issue, nor any of the bmws my wife and I have had in recent years. the usb sockets only provide power and will not read data from memory sticks with my cds on them. since bmw removed cd players from their cars, they have made it harder to listen to the entertainment I want. this is meant to be a luxury brand. the car arrived with door mirrors that did not fold in automatically, but that has since been fixed, probably by a software update.

as a daily driver it is very nice and has plenty of punch when you ask for it, but as a sporty car it feels too sterile - very fast yet no character, no proper noise apart from the fake stuff. making everything run through the touch screen is a backwards step from the old rotary i-drive, it is distracting and awkward to use while moving, especially with the firm suspension on bumpy british roads. needing apple carplay just to play music is irritating, why was usb media not kept as an option? not being able to run on side lights alone is also annoying. digital premium seems pretty pointless, and when bmw pushed a forced software update overnight once the free period ended, it actually felt like a downgrade, and the update got corrupted so nothing worked and the screens were frozen the next morning. an engineer had to come out to sort it, he did a great job, but bmw did not.

it might not just be this particular car, but there are several points where i do not recomend bmw.

the door locking and unlocking works inconsistently, sometimes it responds and sometimes it doesn't. the tailgate kick opening is almost useless. radio reception on the highway basically doesn't happen, which support has confirmed and is very disappointing. the auto-cruise has stopped functioning while on the move. when i downshift with the paddles, the delay before engine braking comes in is far too long, and the emblem is almost pointless. the auto brake hold can't be turned on and off with a single touch. the engine start feature is treated as a subscription. the usb is only good for charging. the auto wipers don't activate at sensible times. the paid digital premium content feels very poor. the bmw app has failed to pick up driving data three times in the roughly three months since buying the car; i force a reset every time but it never fixes the root cause.

the door locking and unlocking works inconsistently, sometimes it responds and sometimes it doesn't. the tailgate kick opening is almost useless. radio reception on the highway basically doesn't happen, which support has confirmed and is very disappointing. the auto-cruise has stopped functioning while on the move. when i downshift with the paddles, the delay before engine braking comes in is far too long, and the emblem is almost pointless. the auto brake hold can't be turned on and off with a single touch. the engine start feature is treated as a subscription. the usb is only good for charging. the auto wipers don't activate at sensible times. the paid digital premium content feels very poor. the bmw app has failed to pick up driving data three times in the roughly three months since buying the car; i force a reset every time but it never fixes the root cause.
other
it was delivered about 2 months later than the original date, with no progress updates. the way the dealer handles things is no different from japanese car dealers apart from the look of the building and the drinks, and the actual service is weak for an expensive car purchase.

im generally happy with the car. biggest issue is i cant play music from a usb stick, ive been told the only way is through my phone. my previous 2 series tourer didnt have that problem and taking this feature away is extremely annoying, i dont see how it saved any money. also, the cruise control has stopped working twice for several weeks. the first time i booked it in but before the visit it fixed itself, then later it failed again for weeks and again came back. i expect it may do this again. very frustrating, especially because the speed limit bong cant be disabled when cruise isnt working, and a bong at 31 mph is annoying even though i dont constantly drive over the limit.

last 7 cars were bmws, but because the new 1-series launch was delayed my previous car ended up being a mercedes. very pleased to be back in a bmw! overall i am really happy with this car, so the points below are in that context: 1. first time with an automatic. i also drive my partner's fiat 500ev, and i am a bit disappointed by the slight lag in acceleration. i can get around it by putting it in sport mode ahead of time, but thats not always practical, and it doesnt stack up well against the ev. i havent touched the paddles and doubt i will. 2. the display is limited compared with the mercedes. i cant show consumption, elapsed time and distance driven along with the standard info like i could on the a-class. 3. can't use a usb stick for music. 4. as usual there is more functionality than i will ever need or use, and i am still going through the online manual.

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!

first of all i was poorly sold this car, they pushed a basic version with options added on. within a couple of minutes of getting the keys the rearview mirror was hs, and when they fixed that they also did an update on the on-board computer. since that update, it basically doesnt work anymore. i was told i need to wait for the next update, and i still havent got it yet. the windows in the retro side that were changed dont go up on their own anymore, plus the car now uses about 1 liter more since that update. the automatic gearbox doesnt change gears quickly enough or properly, and the radio signal is weak. i am really disappointed, the after-sales is not up to standard and i do not have what i actually bought. the sales, the vehicle itself and the service are no longer at the old bmw level. if i could have just handed the key back, i would have. so what are you going to offer me? im ready to swap my car.

i am very happy with my bmw 120 m sports, this is actually my second 1 series. the first one was my wife's, i used to drive her bmw while she drove my jaguar e pace that was the top version. after my wife passed away i sold the jaguar, let my daughter have the original bmw 1, and then got this one. the car has lots of extras, but i feel some of the fun is spoiled by silly cost-cutting, like the indicator feeling really cheap and nasty, same with the car key. they took away the round control button too, just to push voice control and shave costs. you would be amazed how little things like that can influence whether you buy a car or not. i still chose it because it is small, compact, has a 360 degree camera and an opening glass sunroof, which very few small cars offer. i was looking for a small luxury car that did not trigger the luxury band road tax.

changing from my 2008 audi a3 has been far more difficult than i thought because almost every part of this car is so computerized and complex. we spent hours trying to get it to recognise my key even though i'm the owner, and the key section in the manual runs over 50 pages. i feel it would have been far better if there was some kind of simulator so i could learn about the car and its systems first. the car looks good, drives well, and is comfortable, though i've only driven it a few times in the three months so far, but i still don't feel i understand more than a small fraction of what it can actually do.

i'm very pleased with the car overall, except for the idrive freezing, which meant taking it back to the dealer for a hard reset. we have three 1 series in the household and i actually like the previous model's idrive more, as with this one i'm having to look away from the road to change things that used to have a physical switch or button. i also feel the premium connected idrive, which is only free for three months, should stay free for the first buyer for as long as they own the car, and then be an optional extra for any later owner. when i try talking to the car, most of what i get back is "im sorry i don't understand" or "i don't know how to help with that". i'm not sure if that's down to my accent or me not asking for specific commands, but either way i would strongly suggest a list of key words that make it work best. i'd really value knowing what to ask it.

too many issues
1. the rubber gasket on the rear door, even though it is a new car, was already damaged and leaking.
2. the mirrors on this new car make a squeaky noise whenever opening or closing.
3. the key that should lock the car automatically when you walk away only works maybe 1 time out of 10.
4. the digital display also goes dark: first the navigation screen on the left side blacks out, then the speedometer side goes black while driving.
5.
when that happened, i called the bmw emergency center. they asked if there was a warning light, but with the display black i cant see any warning light.
in the end they said it was fine to keep driving
...
hey, i cant see my speed, but if i get caught they will just say it was my choice to keep going.
6. at the one month check for the water leak (and the squeaking when opening/closing), the auto lock and door mirrors,
even though i mentioned it to the dealer several times, all they did was put oil on the door mirror.
3 days later it is squeaking again!
none of the other problems have improved.
7.
even though its a brand new car, its already been back to the workshop three times.

would i recommend it?? not sure??

(im debating posting this online), but i can see the dealer is at least trying to fix it.
for now just waiting and watching.

Customer stated he never has to adjust the AC because it is on auto and handles the climate settings automatically. Customer stated the experience is simply sit down and go.
Customer noted that operating the air conditioning and climate control through the infotainment screen is much easier to use than on his prior vehicle, which was a Volvo.

Customer stated that having the climate controls only on the touchscreen takes a lot of taps to adjust and is very distracting, requiring them to take their eyes off the road, while the earlier version of the same generation with physical buttons was much simpler to operate. Writer suggested using the personal assistant to change settings by voice and advised that most climate control functions can be adjusted that way.
Customer said she wished the back seat had its own rear climate controls available for passengers.
Customer mentioned he would prefer having more physical knobs for the climate control functions, rather than needing to navigate through the screen for those adjustments.

Customer inquired about how he could change the climate settings for just one side or for both sides depending on his preference. Writer used RVG to demonstrate the differences between using Auto mode and when the climate is not synced. Writer advised the customer to press the climate menu button. Writer advised the customer to activate the climate functions by pressing the power button located at the bottom left. Writer advised that if the customer turns off Auto, this will allow the multi-zone climate mode to be switched on. Writer advised that when sync is not selected in this mode, the customer can adjust the passenger or driver side individually. Customer acknowledged.

against my old 68 plate 520i, this one pulls quicker and uses less fuel. i really like the head up display and the new main screen, and the journey fuel info is handy. adaptive cruise itself works fine, but changing the gap to the car ahead while driving is awkward, especially when i want more distance in the wet. lane control helps. sat nav overall is good, yet the traffic delay icons/text are tiny and digging into that info on the move is hard, plus minor roads are shown too faintly. spotify is well integrated, simple to use and looks good. downside is the road noise, which is much louder on some surfaces and basically drowns out the audio. the speed limit warning drives me mad and is often wrong. i also want to keep the car in efficient mode without having to set it again every single journey.

we swapped a 2021 530 and a 2022 530 for two 2026 530s, and the new cars feel similar in overall quality, ride, and cabin noise. we are still learning our way around the touch screens and the menu structure, and i figure we will get the hang of it over time. i am still trying to convince myself that touch screens are truly as convenient as the old knobs and buttons, since they demand more visual attention instead of simple finger feel. the mapping functions and the heads-up display are better than before, and i really like the route graphics, especially how a real-time camera view pops up when approaching an intersection where you need to turn. nobody was able to tell me why run flat tires are no longer standard equipment. there are two letdowns for me: the removal of the small compartment to the left of the steering wheel, which used to be an ideal spot for sunglasses, and the redesign of the door storage areas into an odd shape, unlike the previous design that could hold an extra drink container. i tried the complimentary feature that lets the car pull itself into a saved parking spot, but i did not feel it was accurate enough to guide the car into my garage without risking contact with the wall on one side or the other vehicle on the opposite side.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

Customer stated he is struggling with the parking assistant and stated he plans to go to the dealership.

Customer asked how to turn on the parking assistant. Writer advised it can be started by pressing the parking button on the center console. Writer advised that once it is on, the vehicle will search for a parking space and notify the driver when it finds one the vehicle can fit in. Writer advised to then follow the prompts on the screen and let the vehicle park on its own.

Customer reported that his saved parking path did not stop the vehicle in the right place inside his garage. Customer explained that when he brought the garage door down, it came down onto the car and caused a scratch. Customer commented that he expected to be able to rely on the recorded path to stop in the proper position, but it failed to do so. Writer offered RVG to document the issue with pictures. Customer mentioned he already has several clear photos and will submit them. Customer added that the scratch is on the plastic trim around the grille.
Customer stated she likes being able to have a camera mounted on the front of her vehicle.

I had a problem with Active parking assistance - DTU: "(Copied from DRA97): On the first day, the delivery orientation felt very rushed, only around 20 minutes, so I still dont know how to switch on the parking assistance that is on my car. We test drove this same vehicle, and the salesperson used the system to park it. Same concern with the lane departure feature: it was working when I drove the car before purchase, but now it doesnt seem as strong or proactive. Maybe theres a setting causing this?"

I had a serious problem with Active parking assistance - Not working/inaccurate/inconsistent: "Sometimes it doesnt pick up the parking spots right so I end up doing it myself, and one time it almost crashed so I had to grab control, that was really scary."

Customer stated he viewed a preview of his vehicle that displayed parking assistant professional along with remote control parking and maneuver assistant. Customer stated he is interested in having those features, but noted they are not available at this time. Customer stated he would like information on when they could become available. Writer advised there have been issues with the software and, at the moment, we do not know when these features may be released.

Customer stated he likes the parking assistant feature but needed a refresher on its use. Writer advised that when nearing a parking spot, he should press the feature button and the vehicle sensors will assess if the space is sufficient, then the car will back itself into the spot.

Customer stated that while backing into a parking spot using the parking assistant, the car suddenly reversed at a very high speed, he was unable to hit the brake in time, and it failed to correct, resulting in contact with another parked vehicle. Customer added that two days after this, a message about the parking sensors appeared on the dashboard.

i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

Writer advised to push the parking button on the center console, which turns on the parking cameras and lets the vehicle begin looking for a spot while driving. Writer advised the customer needs to be traveling at around 20 miles per hour for it to search for a space. Writer advised once the system detects a suitable space it will notify the driver and an icon representing the space will show up on the display. Writer advised the customer can then stop the car when the alert appears, tap the icon on the screen, and allow the vehicle to take control and park itself. Writer advised the driver may still operate the brakes to help avoid other obstacles and slow down the maneuver if needed.
Customer stated he is pleased that this vehicle is able to park on its own.
Customer stated he would like to have a button on the steering wheel to activate the Parking Assistant.
I had a problem with Active parking assistance - DTU: "would really like more how-to videos for using it, and I find it tough to park on crowded streets"

Customer stated that even with the recent improvement, the self-parking function is still below par. Customer stated that, given the quality of the cameras and sensors on the car, the feature should be ten times better than it currently is and that it does not meet BMW standards. Customer stated the system had been worse before the latest update, and is now improved because it can also locate a parking space on the opposite side, which it could not do before, and this makes the customer feel more confident in its ability to find a spot. Customer stated that using self-park to go into a space forward is very difficult on this car. Customer stated it is hard for the system to select the actual space that is intended. Customer stated the process should be made more user-friendly, and that this has led to almost never using the function anymore to park the vehicle. Customer stated a preference for parking manually and mentioned other drivers have honked because it takes too long when trying to park with the system. Customer stated the feature is inaccurate and does not send the car where it is supposed to go. Customer stated that in normal parking situations time is often limited. Customer stated this has been a major fault. Customer stated that, as a Tesla owner as well, the BMW setup is immeasurably worse than Tesla for the same feature. Customer stated the Tesla system lets the driver press on the desired parking spot on the dashboard and the car handles it, and that it is much quicker and performs much better. Customer stated yet the optical hardware on the Tesla is inferior to BMW's, and therefore would have expected superior results from the BMW system and from German engineering.

Customer stated they would like to be able to choose specific parking spots on the screen like with Tesla and also have better parking assist at charging stations. Writer acknowledged this and said it would be shared with plant partners.
I had a serious problem with Active parking assistance - DTU: "Initially I did not know what the icons meant, and it took a while to figure them out"
Customer stated the Automatic Parking Assistant feature is nice.
Customer stated he likes the feature that helps him pull the vehicle into the garage, as it clears the garage every time and positions him close to the charger he has.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

Customer stated she is still figuring out how to use the parking assistant and is not confident about all of its functions yet. Writer suggested she practice using it on quieter streets, and the customer agreed that this sounded like a good idea.
Customer stated they really like the vehicle's parking assist features.

Customer reported he relies heavily on the recorded path function because his driveway sits at a strange angle. Customer indicated the feature only works roughly 50 percent of the time. Customer commented it feels like he has to position the car exactly right for it to trigger, which is hard. Writer asked if the system lets him start the maneuver at all or if it cancels itself after beginning. Customer replied it never gives an option to start, it only shows an option to create a new path.

Customer stated the parking assistant feature is not functioning very well and has nearly hit other cars on several occasions already. Customer stated the vehicle will begin backing in and seems to do fine at first, but sometimes it then steers directly toward the neighbor's car. Customer stated they had to step on the brake to avoid a collision. Customer stated this has happened twice and that they will not use that feature again. Writer asked whether the system attempted to stop or change direction on its own, noting that normally the system is fairly good at stopping or altering its path automatically, but Customer stated that without his intervention he believes the car would have hit the neighbor's vehicle.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

Customer asked if he really has to go into the Climate Menu every single time he wants to change the blower fan speed. Writer advised that the fan speed can be altered in the Climate Menu screen, or by telling the Intelligent Personal Assistant to adjust the fan speed instead.

Customer stated the fan noise in this vehicle is significantly louder than it was in his 2017 750i. Customer stated he has had to shut off the windshield blower because of the loudness. Customer stated that even at low or medium blower settings, the fan is still too loud.

the car is just incredible in every respect and i really love it. i only want to highlight two things that, although clearly intended well, are flawed. first, the front passengers don't have truly adjustable ac vents. there's a tiny on knob under the vent panel to tweak the airflow a bit, but the range of adjustment is extremely limited. i understand the sleek look of a dash without the usual vents, but here it feels like form winning over function, and the ac function suffers a lot because of that choice. second, the driver's side open door button is a problem. i tend to lean my left leg against the driver door while i'm driving, and very often my knee hits that open button and the door pops open even as the car is moving. that's really frightening and unsafe. it doesn't do it when the door is locked and the speed is over roughly 10 mph, but it happens below that speed. those are the only two points i have that i think would make the car safer and better for the driver.

this is an excellent car and my 5th 740i. but the air conditioning is terrible. i live in south florida, and if the car sits in the sun, it's basically undriveable for about 5 - 10 minutes until it cools down some. there needs to be a direct vent blowing at the driver's face, and the controls get so hot they are hard to touch.
that fuel economy feature is also a problem. on hot florida days, sitting at a red light, the engine shuts off and i get hot again. when it restarts, the car can lurch a bit if my foot isn't pressed firmly on the brake. unlike the older 7's, there's no switch to turn this off, other than keeping it in sport mode.
my car was supposed to come with regular tires but showed up with run flats. i had two flats in about two months and it cost me over $1,000. it shouldn't be like that; run flats are not good for florida with the heat and all the construction debris.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

cons: the hvac could cool better, likely because of the hidden vents, and it only got a bit better after i put clear uv tint on the windows. you also can't set sport mode as the default, even though i drive in sport most of the time. i can't remove the red and blue colors on the display and interactive bar, and i'm not a fan of those colors. the steering feels a little soft and not as connected to the road as my previous cars. it's a big car, and adding about 5" more length wasn't a good thing. the styling is just okay; i actually think my 2017 740i looks better.

the upgraded bowers wilkins stereo is awful and you should give money back to anyone who had to pay for it. in my earlier bmws with the b&w system it was great. you moved the speakers from under the seats and now it is laughable. everyone who rides in the car comments on the stereo and then i tell them it was a $4,800 upgrade... this might end up being my last bmw. when you turn it up there is basically no bass or mid at all. it sounds terrible, everything just disappears, really sad.
also, you cannot keep the ac on air recirculation or keep the whole climate system synced, it resets every single time you shut the car off. luxury should mean you do not have to keep doing things, but i have to spend about a minute every time i get in the car setting up stuff that should stay the same. ac fan level 2 is way too weak and 3 is too strong and loud. bring back proper air vents.
i am not happy with this purchase and this is my 8th 7 series in around 12 years. i will not renew to this again.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

Customer stated that one aspect he prefers on his Tesla is being able to initiate software updates directly from his phone without searching through menu options.

this car was delivered on pirelli high-performance tires that made the ride far too harsh for a luxury sedan. i ended up paying myself to swap to oem-spec bridgestone turanza 6s, which transformed the comfort, and tire choice really should be sorted at the factory for customers who care about refinement.

the 48v mild-hybrid start/stop is still quite rough. compared to other isg/bsg systems from different brands, and to my 2024 530i with a belt starter generator, the restart from a standstill is abrupt and gives a noticeable jolt even when holding the brake, and it can feel coarse as the car comes to a stop. that takes away from the premium driving experience, especially when mercedes and range rover have virtually imperceptible stop/start.

on top of that, ota software updates arrive very late, which is disappointing versus other luxury makers. more timely updates would really help the overall ownership experience.

Customer stated he appreciates that updates are now simpler. Customer stated he has already done one OTA software update and it was easy. Customer stated he likes not having to go to the dealership for those updates.

Customer stated they wanted assistance with downloading the software and that they follow what they believe are the right steps to get the new software, but the vehicle keeps giving reminders that it still needs to be done. Writer went through the required preconditions with the customer, and writer explained to the customer how to initiate the upgrade. The vehicle then advised the customer that he could exit, and writer informed the customer that this should resolve it.

I had a very serious problem with Over-the-air vehicle software update problem: "having a hard time getting things to connect with the software overall". Describe the over-the-air vehicle software update problem: Installation/update issue, Download issue, Which problem with RSU?: Installation/update issue, Download issue

Customer stated that a few weeks back the car could not finish a software update because it stopped at 58%. Customer stated he went to the dealer for an iDrive update and that resolved the problem. Customer stated the vehicle has 582 miles. From AIR: 301 mi
CUSTOMER STATES VEHICLE UNABLE TO PERFORM REMOTE SOFTWARE UPDATE 11/2022.44 (UPDATE GETS TO 58% AND STOPS)
Customer reported a software update notification. Using RVG, writer led him through installing it. RVG captured.
Customer noted they had some software update issues at first, but these were resolved quickly at the dealership and they did not end up finding anything wrong.

Customer stated there is a Remote Software Upgrade shown for the vehicle, but when he tries to download the RSU directly to the car it says there is no internet connection and the download fails. Writer advised trying to get the RSU via the My BMW app while his phone is on Wifi. Writer stated that next time he is in the vehicle, the phone will connect, send the update to the car and it will install. Writer stated that if this process does not work, the dealer can perform the RSU installation.

Customer stated that after bringing the vehicle home from delivery he got a notification about a software update. Customer stated he parked the car outside the garage and initiated the update. Customer stated that when he returned to the vehicle he was unable to get into it. Customer stated he contacted Roadside Assistance. Customer stated Roadside Assistance sent a tow truck, but that towing company could not move the car because it was not in neutral and there was no way to access the interior. Customer stated the local BMW arranged another style of tow truck and the vehicle was taken to the dealership. Customer stated the software update had completely frozen the car and it was totally dead. Customer stated the second towing company had to use dollies to tow it.
Customer stated the local dealer kept the car for 1 month. Customer stated that since getting it back, the vehicle has been fabulous.

overall it has been a fantastic car so far. i really like the configuration and the level of luxury, and the build feels very solid. it definitely turns heads and has a strong presence on the road, and i enjoy how it drives. my only gripes are with the software. the app itself is excellent, but idrive gives me trouble. a few things are minor but irritating, like my home screen widgets randomly vanishing so i have to re-add them. the main headache is the esim randomly refusing to activate. i do not hold this against the car itself, as it seems like something that could be fixed with an ota update rather than a hardware issue. still, it is a very frustrating bug, and the only way around it has been to cancel my ubigi plan and start over, which results in double billing. please get this fixed asap!

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

after my husband changed his phone he has not been able to load the bmw app, and even though he has asked for help he just keeps getting passed around. on the day we collected the car it was not ready because they had sprayed the roof black as they could not secure the car we had been promised. we did not get a proper hand over as we were anxious about picking up primary schoolchildren and had told the garage we would have to go. about 5 or 6 weeks later we needed an emergency technician and the car had to return to the garage because the gps in the roof fin had been damaged by rain, so the roof was resprayed. now in feb we still do not have the car we originally ordered and are waiting for a part for the black grill it should have had. the new manager martin has been trying to sort things out. we had other problems too but i am running out of spa.

after swapping my old 71 plate 1 series for this one after roughly 3 years, i was really looking forward to an updated model and hassle free, enjoyable driving. instead my new car, now a 120 rather than the 1.8 sport, feels like a much lower spec than what i had before. the seats are now basic, they do have heating but no lumbar support, there is no drivers dimming rear-view mirror, and unlike three cars ago i can no longer move it up and down with a switch. the side mirrors no longer adjust when parking, and it came with no high beam assist, which i then had to pay about £10 to get added. even the hey bmw assistant has been changed from a female voice to a male. i realise some of this can be bought as extras, but i already had these features on my previous cars, so why pay again. the car should include all that and even more, but in my view it just doesn't.

i moved down from an m135 drive and the power in this one is still absolutely fine and nicely responsive for everyday driving. i much prefer the battery assisted stop/start setup, and the steering has a nice light feel that firms up as you go faster. i am a bit let down that the i-drive knob has gone, as i always thought that system was brilliant when on the move. the new screens look very smart and, once you have them configured, they work well, and the overall fascia design and materials feel excellent. my f70120 m sport drives and handles really well day to day, and i actually like how it looks more than the f40. the front electric seats are really comfy and offer very precise adjustment. i am enjoying the head-up display, its my first time using one. the sat nav reacts quickly and is really helpful when finding your way around unfamiliar routes and towns. i also really like the 'y' style wheels and the red calipers.

i've been driving bmws for more than 20 years and the move away from physical switches feels like going backwards. having to look off the road to change things seems unsafe to me. the car often ignores what i say when i try to use voice control. parking in tight spots is a pain, it keeps cutting out and stopping, so it doesnt feel as manageable as my other cars, even the automatics. the electric help when parking tends to surge, and on a small slope it is hard to drive off smoothly. my garage is narrow and uphill, and i have to creep in very slowly, but the way it surges and then cuts out makes that awkward. i have to press the accelerator to get the parking brake to release and then it leaps forward. i do actually like the car, but these parking problems kind of take the shine off it for me.

the car handles well, which was one of the main reasons for choosing my third bmw, along with the solid build quality. there should be more time spent showing how to use the controls and software. the materials are different compared to my previous one series from 2015. i find the bmw electronic assistant poor, he does not pick up simple commands. i was also annoyed to be charged £100 for connect drive updates about 3 months after purchase, especially as i had already paid for a servicing plan and scratch insurance. when i rang bmw technical because the bmw services app would not let me pay the £100, the man i spoke to said the £100 might be refunded and put me through to customer services, but they disagreed. i have now paid the £100, but i am not happy having to pay for this within 3 months.

i really like my new car but i am absolutely furious about losing features that were there at the start. after about a month the high beam assist disappeared, and after roughly three months other functions were gone too, including the 3d sat nav and the live traffic information. i am not even completely sure what else has vanished yet and expect that next time i drive i will notice more things missing. to keep using what i had got used to i now have to pay a monthly subscription. the car cost enough already without having to keep shelling out more. i am really not happy about this at all. i will not be telling anyone to buy a bmw, because even though you pay more than for other cars, what you paid for does not stay and bmw want extra money for stuff that was originally on the car. honestly, i'm disgusted.

i really like this car overall, but there are definitely ups and downs.   pros: the way it drives in general; the new style seats are really comfy; and you can feel that classic bmw engineering in every part of this m sport 1 series.    cons: the active-lane-keeping-assistant feels dangerous on narrow roads and on uk cars you can't permanently switch it off. all the tech being buried in the screen menus and not just on a simple button is frustrating; and the turning circle is way bigger than my old mercedes so it needs a lot more steering work.

overall i'm pleased with my bmw 120 m sport. i've marked it 9 out of 10 for a couple of reasons.   1. the centre console has been glitchy, at times really sluggish and occasionally it has frozen, meaning i've had to reset it. this is annoying because it also wipes the efficient mode gained mileage reading. after the latest firmware update the console seems quicker, but the other day i got in and a message came up saying ' driver assistance restricted' and there were scrolling lines on the screen like it was rebooting ??  2. the bmw personal assistant doesn't always switch the drive mode when i ask it to.  aside from that i'm happy with the car  thanks

evidence.quote: the car drives nicely but sadly it does not meet our needs. the boot is smaller than we thought, and with the hybrid battery taking up space, which we did not realise, it is no use for trips with our dog. once the driving position is set, it has to be moved again so the smaller driver can get out of the vehicle. having almost everything run through the display screen instead of the steering wheel controls is distracting when driving and does not feel like a safe setup. apple car play is unreliable and seems to need tinkering every single time you use the car. there is no separate air conditioning for driver and passenger.

Customer stated she has not yet figured out how to change the distance setting when using Cruise Control. Writer verified the vehicle has this feature and advised that with cruise control engaged, she should press the Mode button on the left side of the steering wheel until Distance Control is selected.

against my old 68 plate 520i, this one pulls quicker and uses less fuel. i really like the head up display and the new main screen, and the journey fuel info is handy. adaptive cruise itself works fine, but changing the gap to the car ahead while driving is awkward, especially when i want more distance in the wet. lane control helps. sat nav overall is good, yet the traffic delay icons/text are tiny and digging into that info on the move is hard, plus minor roads are shown too faintly. spotify is well integrated, simple to use and looks good. downside is the road noise, which is much louder on some surfaces and basically drowns out the audio. the speed limit warning drives me mad and is often wrong. i also want to keep the car in efficient mode without having to set it again every single journey.

Customer stated that the Active Cruise Control works great.

Customer mentioned that when he is driving with ACC and presses the brake pedal, ACC switches off. Customer noted that in his earlier BMW vehicles there used to be a resume button for cruise. Writer explained that as long as ACC is active, the customer can press the set button once to resume Cruise Control, or press it twice so Cruise will align to the current speed limit including any changes set in the speed limit assistant.

Customer stated he liked how the cruise distance control worked on the i4 better. Customer stated the i4 had a toggle on the left side of the steering wheel that let him change the distance much faster and more easily. Customer stated that on the i5 he has to go into a menu to adjust it. Customer stated it feels like BMW has gone to more of a set and forget system. Customer stated he prefers to adjust the distance based on the trip or driving conditions, and having the controls on the steering wheel made changing the distance much easier while driving.

Customer reported the vehicle feels overly governed. Writer asked what he meant. Customer explained that when he goes through a corner, the car determines if it thinks he is driving too fast and then slows him down. Customer stated he wants to control how fast and how aggressively he takes curves. Customer added that he has to disable this function every time and that it takes away his ability to truly drive the car.
Customer stated he is pleased with the adaptive cruise control feature in this i5.
Customer stated the new cruise control setup is problematic and he prefers manual control. Writer acknolwedged the feedback.

Customer explained the cruise control will operate for a short period and then shut off. Customer noted the vehicle had about 500 miles on it and he was using it for a longer trip. Customer observed that after stopping and turning the vehicle off and back on, the cruise would function again for a while and then cut out. Customer stated that while traveling he called a BMW dealer for guidance, and they advised him to perform a reboot. Customer reported that after the reboot the cruise control stayed on much longer before cutting off, but it still eventually stopped working. Writer asked whether this occurred on the return portion of the trip or if it is still cutting in and out now. Customer replied it did happen on the way back, but he has not been on the highway since returning to test it further. Customer mentioned he intends to bring the vehicle to the dealer, but because he lives far away he is unsure when he will be able to go. Writer sent a follow up email to the dealer.
Customer stated he is pleased with the adaptive cruise control.
Customer commented that she appreciates how Cruise Control reduces her speed automatically when she comes up behind another vehicle that is traveling slower than she is.

I had a minor problem with Cruise control/adaptive cruise control - DTU/controls poorly located: "I eventually realized it was not really a malfunction, just a change from how I canceled cruise on my 2021 compared to this 2024. My 2021 had a RES/CAN button on the steering wheel, but the 2024 does not. Now I see that it depends on when I press the ON/Off for cruise: while actually driving it will shut cruise off, but if I am coasting after braking or coming down a highway off ramp, the same ON/Off acts like Resume. That Resume behavior made the car accelerate in the off-ramp curve when I was not expecting it. Now I know how and when to use the cruise control icon on the left side of the steering wheel and understand the difference from the 2021 to the 2024."

the pricing on this car is way too high. i managed to negotiate a strong lease, but there is no chance i would spend the $190k msrp on an electric car that is bound to lose a lot of value. overall the tech is very solid, but bmw still not getting the esim to function correctly is incredibly annoying. one of the main reasons i chose this car was the theatre screen, and now it only operates if i run ugly cables to it. the seats are mostly comfortable, yet they do not give enough side bolster support, so i would really like more hold in the corners. the heated seats and heated armrests are fantastic and the infotainment works well, plus the upgraded sound system is outstanding. when using apple carplay, though, the bottom left corner with distance and time remaining is completely hidden behind my right hand while driving. if i swapped cars today i would rather be in an m5 touring.

Customer stated they were unhappy that they did not get 2 keys and only received the card to use their phone as a key. Customer stated they have lost their single key and are now dependent on their phones until the replacement arrives, which they feel makes the vehicle harder to use.

Customer stated she wants to obtain an additional key for the driver instead of relying on the credit card style key. Customer explained that her husband's driver would prefer to have his own traditional key fob. Customer mentioned that in their family it has been common practice with previous vehicles to provide each driver with their own key. Customer went to the service department to ask about ordering another key. Service department informed her that they do not have any keys available and are not able to order them. Service department advised her to call back every month to check whether keys have come into stock. Customer expressed that this process is inconvenient and not user-friendly. Customer stated that this level of service is not acceptable for someone who has just purchased an expensive car.
Customer stated in an email that he would like the key fob to be reduced in size.

the tech on this car is very inconsistent, some days everything works fine and other days features just do not. the digital key will be detected sometimes, and other days it is not, making it hard for me to get into the car. once the assisted driving feature said I was not paying attention and suddenly brought the car to a stop right in the middle of the highway. the brakes also do not feel strong enough. I have had several times where I needed to stop quickly because I was cut off or the light changed suddenly, and the brakes could not bring the car to a full stop like they should. on top of that, the battery does not hold as long as I expect, so I end up charging about 3 to 4 times a week.

the car is very comfortable and feels up to date, but i have had way too many issues in a short period. i like the interior styling, yet a lot of the nice features are buried and take forever to access. there really should be simple buttons to open and close all doors. the lower door switch on the driver side is placed horribly, my knee has hit it multiple times and the door has popped open while driving. the fuel door refused to open when i was around 340 miles from home, and bmw roadside told me to just tear it off because they had no other solution. i have also gotten warning lights for the emergency contact system with no cause the dealer could identify. all of this has happened within the 3 months i have owned the car. my 2020 740ix had both keys quit working when i was roughly 70 miles from home, and nobody could explain why. i currently own 3 bmw and lease 2 more, and i am starting to lose faith in your products.

evidence.quote: the overall body size turned out larger than i had imagined, though the inside feels roomy, and the acceleration is good for the engine size. it is packed with lots of detailed functions, but the price came in higher than i expected, the door feels heavy, and the driver window is set high so it is hard to lean in when putting the car into the garage. i cannot switch off the front light, and i would like the air conditioner to blow only from my feet, but that option is not available. the trunk area is small, so i cannot carry as much luggage as i thought. the vibration while driving is quite strong, so it cannot really be called comfortable.

good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the touchscreen setup is frankly unsafe to use on the move and really needs an idrive wheel to be safer. i don't see why that was removed other than to cut costs. turning off the speed limit and the equally risky lane departure warning is too fiddly, there should be a button for each. the my modes feature in this 120 is almost useless, adding no real driving benefit, just extra complexity and probably cost. the boot is too small for a car of this size. even with these complaints, it still suits my needs perfectly right now, and despite the over-complex tech the interface is still far better than my wife's mercedes a class.

i used to own a 118 shadow sport edition, and now have the 120m. the 120m is a pleasant car and quite economical, but i do have a few downsides when i compare it to my old one. the boot does not seem as big as before, and the new front design means dirt from the front wheels gets onto the sides of the car very easily, so it needs cleaning all the time. this was not an issue with my previous model.

the car looks great from the outside, the styling has that typical solid bmw look. inside and on the move it has a very solid feel, no rattles, and the automatic gear changes are smooth. i like the personalisation options, and the lower compartment in the boot is really handy for keeping shopping bags and wine boxes stable.

i've had a lot of bmws over the years, but this one is easily the most comfortable, from how you sit to the steering wheel and the great all round visibility, plus it's so simple to park. the boot is huge and the space for passengers' legs is really welcome. it practically drives itself and the park assist works brilliantly. i really value the gentle suspension because my spine notices every bump now. the soft touch on the steering wheel and the whole interior look feel much more upmarket than other cars in this segment. honestly i don't think i could have picked a better car, it fits me perfectly. thank you bmw.

this must be about my 12th bmw and my 3rd 1 series. the driving quality is good and the mini hybrid setup seems to really help with petol consumption. i do miss the bigger boot space though, as the batteries take it up; in the previous one i could put my golf trolley and bag in the back without dropping the seats, now i can't. since i started using the voice function it cuts down how much i need the touch screen and helps me keep my eyes on the road. i have a head up display on this car as on the last, and the way it changed from white to orange when the speed limit was exceeded was useful. the beeping that comes with it is very annoying, and if i turn the beeping off it also stops the orange change on the head up display, which i'd like to keep. there has also been an issue with apple car play and bmw voice.

i have downsized to this small car and really like the x drive, with the 2 litre engine giving enough power for everyday use. the whole 'apps' setup feels clumsy and can distract when you just want to tweak something simple like the seat heating or heated steering wheel. after a software update some settings went back to factory, which was annoying as i only noticed at night when the instrument brightness had changed. this is a car, not a mobile phone. the boot space is badly cut down by the 'hybrid lite' batteries. over 30+ years i have had 10 new bmws and this is the first one that has no anchor points in the boot, which is particularly irritating when stuff slides around. overall still a good little car.

this is the 6th bmw i have owned, a mix of new and used, and i've liked every single one of them. i feel this particular model is the best yet, it is a pleasure to drive. i was hesitant about going for an automatic at first, but i wanted this model so i went ahead, and i have absolutely no regrets. it comes with all the technology i realistically need, even though i know there are extra options available beyond what i have. the car responds quickly when you ask it to, is comfortable, and the interior layout is very well thought out. the boot is big enough to carry my band gear without issues. i picked the midnight thunder paint and friends and family often comment on how distinctive it looks. the only downside was one time when the software hadn't updated properly and i had to carefully coax the car back home, luckily i was close by and an engineer sorted it out. now i always keep an eye on the app for that.

car drives very smoothly, corners well and has enough power. it is quiet and the fuel consumption is good, though it's been mainly motorway use so far. the dashboard looks nice but really isn't practical to operate while driving. the dash lighting reflects in both outer rear view mirrors. the boot is smaller, but in fairness the tank is larger than on my previous 118i m sport, which gives better range. i miss the little storage area on the dash by the steering column. the seats are less comfortable than in my old 118i m sport and the driver's seat is already losing its shape, and i am only just over 12 stone. i also miss having an adjustable back support. the colour is perfect. sadly the car wasn't ordered to my own spec so it has extras i wouldn't normally pay for. i'm not keen on the idea of a trial period for extras and then having to pay to keep them.

title: G60 Ambient light
requirement_statement: Review mixed feedback on 'Ambient light' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 18 respondents complain and 19 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated that they really love the ambient lighting in the vehicle.
Customer noted that the crystal casing around the ambient lighting initially felt quite loud from a design perspective, but over time he has come to really like it.
Customer stated the interaction bar lighting looks very cool and has a futuristic feel.
Customer mentioned his daughter really likes the ambient lighting and, every time she gets in, she changes it to whatever color she wants for the day.

Customer stated that red is missing from the ambient lighting color choices and expressed confusion about why both red and blue are not provided when the M package is selected, since red and blue are the recognizable signature colors of M. Customer stated they looked online and found many other owners also puzzled by this restriction. Customer stated BMW previously offered red as an option until roughly a year or two ago, when it was either removed through an over-the-air update or when the G60 model was introduced. Customer stated the current palette includes coral and pearl white and asked who would actually choose pearl white inside a car, stating these colors do not fit the character of M mode. Customer stated that when using M mode, drivers expect red and blue lighting, not coral and blue.
Customer reported the interior lights stay red in sport mode and cannot be adjusted. Customer mentioned he would like additional color choices.
Customer mentioned they miss a particular orange paint color that was offered on prior model years. Customer added they could not recall what that color was called.

Customer stated she wanted to know how to change the Ambient Lights color. Writer explained that while inside the vehicle she should open the Apps Menu, choose Interior lighting, then select Ambient lighting, and from there adjust the color.
Customer stated he is pleased with the interior lighting.
Customer stated he really likes the ambient lighting.
Customer said they would like to have more interior color choices and also wished there were additional overall lighting strips.
Customer stated they really like the interior lighting settings and the available options in the vehicle.

overall i really like my new 540i xdrive, and as i'm still figuring out all the features, i'm very pleased with the size, styling, and overall design. i picked the msport package and love the sportier, more aggressive look, especially the way the lines on the front hood flow up to the bmw badge. i've been using personal mode most of the time and wish there were a more comfort-oriented setting within personal mode. i often need the car to stay running with the a/c on while i quickly go into the office or a grocery store, and i still haven't found a way to keep it on and locked without leaving the key inside. fit and finish, with the tight tolerances, are so far what i expect from bmw. the steering feels a bit lighter than the traditional bmw dna. all in all, i'm satisfied with the car so far.

from a driving standpoint the car is excellent. for something this big and heavy the steering and handling feel sharp, and the suspension doesn't beat you up. acceleration is exactly what you'd expect from an ev with this much power, really strong. tech is also impressive, nicely integrated and straightforward to use.

where it falls short is in materials and missing features for what it costs. no massaging seats, no soft close doors, no leather dash, no led skylounge roof, and the ambient light bar doesn't continue into the rear. some of the plastics look cheap, and i really wish there was at least a bit of stitching on the doors or dashboard to make it feel more upscale. coming out of an x5 and before that a g30, this does feel like a step down, even though everything is screwed together very tightly.

i really like the 5 series bmw and have been buying bmw vehicles since 1999. i still have my 2016 535 xi and it is easily the best car i've owned, both in appearance and in the features it came with. that 2016 has massaging seats, the bmw logo lights up on the inside of the doors, and the wheels look great. overall it's just a gorgeous car.

by comparison, my current 2025 feels very generic. i custom ordered this 2025 and added every option that was available, so it's supposed to be top of the line, yet it's very disappointing. it seems like bmw cut corners on this model. there are no massaging seats, and when i chose the upgraded seats you removed the heated seats in the back. i had a 2024 before and swapped it for the 2025 only because i didn't like the color on the 2024.

back in 2016 and earlier, bmw would send a little gift like a nice keychain or a usb fob shaped like a bmw key. i got nothing with the 2024 or the 2025. the key that came with the 2024 was shiny and attractive, while the 2025 key looks very plain and generic. i don't know why it ended up like that, especially since the 2025 cost more than the 2024. overall, the 2025 has been very disappointing.

i would like to show you a video comparing the 2016 with the 2025 to explain what i mean. i've ordered an m5 and i'm hoping that will turn out better than what i'm driving now. thank you.

i'd tell people the car itself is worth buying, but i'd steer them away from the dealership. they just come across as pure greed. i really wish there were other choices for getting service and parts done. i tried to buy a set of tpms sensors and they wanted around $180 each, total just over $760, claiming that was basically their cost. seriously? i went online and saw the same sensors sold by other bmw dealers for roughly $100 apiece. feels like they act like they have a monopoly and squeeze you because of it.

about the car, there's some wind noise coming from around the window frame area. also, if you're going to offer the shadow line package, you should make all the exterior badging blacked out too. there's a carplay problem as well: when i play music using the apple music app, the volume is so low that i have to crank it up to around 80 to 90 percent of full just to get a normal listening level. when i use plain bluetooth instead, that issue isn't there.

1. i paid extra for the remote parking option, but it often refuses to work. out of 10 attempts it seems to fail about half the time. especially in tight spaces it just won't allow remote parking at all, whether that's because of a sensor error or something else. honestly, i'd like to get my money back for this feature.

2. the body size is bigger than a mercedes-benz e-class or an audi a6, which makes it inconvenient when trying to park or drive through narrow streets. if the body is that large, the cabin should feel more spacious, but the interior doesn't really seem any bigger.

3. the hazard light button is a touch type, so you can't easily tell if it has actually been pressed. when you're in a rush, it's hard to switch it on, which raises the chance of an accident.

4. the bsi engine oil change interval is too long. i'd prefer replacing it every year or at around 15,000 km, but they set it at 20,000 km. trying to save money like that just seems like it will hurt people's impression of how durable the car is.

5. as soon as you approach the vehicle, the side mirrors fold out, which makes it awkward to squeeze between cars in a cramped parking lot. it would be better if the mirrors only opened when the door is actually opened or once the driver gets in.

this is my 5th bmw vehicle.
all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:
550i
540i
740i
550i
now a 530i
i realize i am now in the regular 5 series, which i chose because, in my view, quality and functionality have gone backwards overall. that is not just about this 530 compared to those older cars.
my issues are:
run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series
2) air conditioning feels downgraded and not strong enough for south texas heat
3) ac/vent fan is too noisy except on the lowest level. with the fan high, you basically cant talk on the phone.
4) auto stop/start, but the driver does not have simple, effective full control to switch it off.
5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced
6) not enough storage. the small latched compartment by the driver is gone, there is a phone charging pad instead of extra storage depth (should be removable), and the glove box is limited and does not work well.
7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.
