from a driving standpoint the car is excellent. for something this big and heavy the steering and handling feel sharp, and the suspension doesn't beat you up. acceleration is exactly what you'd expect from an ev with this much power, really strong. tech is also impressive, nicely integrated and straightforward to use.

where it falls short is in materials and missing features for what it costs. no massaging seats, no soft close doors, no leather dash, no led skylounge roof, and the ambient light bar doesn't continue into the rear. some of the plastics look cheap, and i really wish there was at least a bit of stitching on the doors or dashboard to make it feel more upscale. coming out of an x5 and before that a g30, this does feel like a step down, even though everything is screwed together very tightly.

i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

the apps built into the car really ought to be reachable from the phone, so you don't have to sit in the car and fiddle with them - you can do that in a mercedes, which was my previous car. the windows also can't be closed via the app, while mercedes manages that. if they could close themselves automatically when it rains, like mercedes does, i haven't found any sign that they do, but they should. the car has locked me out several times when i've left either the phone or the keys inside. settings in the app like folding the mirrors when locking don't actually work when it's other users, even though the option is set in the app. my wife is forced to type in a pin code and can't just pick her id, supposedly because of the risk that her phone might be stolen - but the primary user's phone can be stolen too, so that explanation doesn't make sense. the information shown in the dashboard is poor no matter which view you choose. the radio will not receive a signal while i'm driving through the limfjord tunnel, which i go through every day, and that's something i've never run into with any other car i've owned. the winter range is deeply reprehensible and honestly my biggest complaint: no more winter holiday trips, because the real range on the motorway at 130 kmh in frost is at most about 250 km. well, i guess i have to stop somewhere, but i'm left disappointed. mvh mads

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

i really enjoy how this car drives, and that was the main reason i chose it. i also like the updated exterior look. still, i was close to going with something else instead: a genesis, an audi allroad wagon, or a mercedes wagon. the genesis appealed because its interior finish seemed better than the bmw, the audi wagon because i prefer wagons and have already owned three audi avant wagons, and if audi still sold the avant i would have gone for that. the mercedes wagon was ruled out because the lease was too expensive. with this 540, the interior has been a letdown, as my previous 540 felt more upscale inside. this one makes me feel like i am sitting at an apple laptop, and it really bothers me that the retractable lid over the cup holder area is gone. without it, that spot looks like a random catch-all and ruins the console's previously nice look. the material covering the top of the dash also seems cheaper.

overall i really like my new 540i xdrive, and as i'm still figuring out all the features, i'm very pleased with the size, styling, and overall design. i picked the msport package and love the sportier, more aggressive look, especially the way the lines on the front hood flow up to the bmw badge. i've been using personal mode most of the time and wish there were a more comfort-oriented setting within personal mode. i often need the car to stay running with the a/c on while i quickly go into the office or a grocery store, and i still haven't found a way to keep it on and locked without leaving the key inside. fit and finish, with the tight tolerances, are so far what i expect from bmw. the steering feels a bit lighter than the traditional bmw dna. all in all, i'm satisfied with the car so far.

i really like the 5 series bmw and have been buying bmw vehicles since 1999. i still have my 2016 535 xi and it is easily the best car i've owned, both in appearance and in the features it came with. that 2016 has massaging seats, the bmw logo lights up on the inside of the doors, and the wheels look great. overall it's just a gorgeous car.

by comparison, my current 2025 feels very generic. i custom ordered this 2025 and added every option that was available, so it's supposed to be top of the line, yet it's very disappointing. it seems like bmw cut corners on this model. there are no massaging seats, and when i chose the upgraded seats you removed the heated seats in the back. i had a 2024 before and swapped it for the 2025 only because i didn't like the color on the 2024.

back in 2016 and earlier, bmw would send a little gift like a nice keychain or a usb fob shaped like a bmw key. i got nothing with the 2024 or the 2025. the key that came with the 2024 was shiny and attractive, while the 2025 key looks very plain and generic. i don't know why it ended up like that, especially since the 2025 cost more than the 2024. overall, the 2025 has been very disappointing.

i would like to show you a video comparing the 2016 with the 2025 to explain what i mean. i've ordered an m5 and i'm hoping that will turn out better than what i'm driving now. thank you.

i really enjoy this car. the ride quality is excellent and the cabin stays very quiet. the 760 has more than enough power and the tech in it is impressive. the one thing i'd change is the way the menus are laid out for the controls. i end up digging around through a bunch of apps on the screen just to find basic functions.

my other issue is that when i spec'd and ordered the car, i assumed the 760 came with active cruise and all the parking assists like my previous m850 and m5 had. it was a letdown to find out later those systems were actually part of a big option package that i hadn't realized i needed to add. my wife's lexus rx350 has all of that included as standard equipment for about half the cost.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.

with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

Customer stated he misses the physical button that adjusted the distance to the car ahead. Writer recommended using the IPA by saying, "Hello BMW, increase the distance to the car in front of me."
Customer stated he appreciates that Cruise Control can set the speed either to match the road's speed limit or to whatever speed he is currently driving.
Customer mentioned that when using cruise control, he feels there should be more videos online explaining its operation. Writer advised that he can search YouTube for instructional videos.

Customer asked what the Set button for Cruise Control does.
Writer explained that switching on Cruise Control will automatically set the present driving speed.
Writer further explained that pressing Set will use the currently detected speed limit.
Customer confirmed understanding.
Customer indicated that he would like to have adaptive cruise control.

Customer stated they were unsure about the cruise control and how to switch it to active cruise control. Writer advised that it is changed using the mode button while cruise control is engaged. Customer acknowledged this.

Customer stated there was a knob on the left side of the steering wheel that he did not know the function of. Writer advised it is used to change the set speed while cruise control is on, and that it can be pressed lightly to adjust by 1 mph at a time, or held to change by 5 mph at a time. Writer explaind this was only for cruise speed.

title: G70 Digital Key
requirement_statement: Improve 'Digital Key' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 18 respondents complain and 8 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated he appreciates that his phone and Apple Watch function as vehicle keys so he does not need to carry a key fob.
Customer mentioned he really likes being able to use his phone as the key.

Customer reported the dealer tried to set up his Apple iPhone 8 Plus as a key, but they were unable to get it to connect to the car to lock and unlock. Customer indicated he can still use the app for other functions, just not for starting the vehicle. Customer explained he was able to start his Corvette and his Lexus directly from his iPhone, but the BMW will not start that way. Customer commented it is not a big problem since he can simply go to the window and use the fob to start the car from outside. Writer documented that his iPhone 8 Plus appears incompatible with the digital key feature.

Customer asked about operation of the plastic digital key card. Writer explained it uses NFC and has to be held near the door handles to lock or unlock the vehicle, and placed in the tray to start it. Writer noted it will not open the tailgate. Writer added that digital key plus allows touchless locking, unlocking, and starting the engine. Customer acknowledged.

Customer stated the digital key only fails around 1% of the time. Customer stated that when it does fail, the phone will not connect via Bluetooth to the vehicle and comfort access will not unlock the doors, so he has to unlock his phone and physically tap it on the door handle to get in. Customer stated he also keeps the digital key card with him as a backup and uses the card when handing the vehicle to valet, since he cannot give a valet his phone.
Customer stated they really enjoy using the digital key and think it is cool. Customer stated they appreciate how simple it is, particularly not having to bring the physical key fob with them.

Customer asked if his wife can also use a Digital Key when he already has one. Writer confirmed she can create a Digital Key on her phone through the My BMW app. Writer explained to open the app, go to "Vehicle Configuration", choose "BMW Digital Key", then tap the tile to add it to the Apple Wallet.

Customer stated the vehicle does not immediately recognize his iPhone when using digital key plus. Customer stated he must place the phone right next to the door handle for the car to unlock. Customer believes the vehicle eSIM is interfering with the touchless digital key feature.
Customer stated it is convenient not having to bring a physical key.

Customer stated the vehicle was purchased in Florida, shipped up to Maryland, and there was no walkthrough at delivery, so the customer has been trying to learn everything alone. Customer stated they are accustomed to receiving two keys, but with this car there is only one key and two cards, and they were unsure how to handle the two cards. Writer explained the purpose of the service cards and the activation cards.

Customer mentioned he no longer remembered how to turn on and operate the valet key card, even though the dealers had quickly demonstrated it. Writer explained to hold the key card to the door handle for locking and unlocking and place it on the wireless charging tray to start the vehicle. Writer further suggested leaving the card inactive when stored in the vehicle for security, since it serves as a key.

Customer asked whether the digital key is dependable enough to use on a daily basis without bringing the key fob. Writer advised that there are customers who rely solely on the digital key and keep their key fobs at home. Writer further advised that the digital key card can serve as a back-up if necessary.
Customer mentioned he misplaced his Key Fob for a short period, and that the Digital Key worked well as a backup during that time.

Customer stated he was next to the vehicle holding his iPhone when the digital key did not unlock the car. Customer stated he needed to restart his phone, and after doing so the problem went away. Customer stated the vehicle currently has 1,116 miles.
Customer stated he enjoys being able to use his phone as the key.

Customer stated he would like to create a second digital key for his wife. Writer explained he can add her phone using the same procedure he followed for his own phone. Writer further noted that when both phones are inside the vehicle, it will detect whichever phone arrives in the area first.
Customer stated he would have preferred to have the digital key option.
Customer stated they appreciate having the option to use their phone as a key.

the car drives really well, but i'm seeing a few software issues. the auto close and auto open funciton when using the phone as a digital key is super annoying, and there should be a way to fully shut those off at home. right now you can only turn off the "unlock" feature at home, which feels like a simple software change. other very frustrating things are needing to dig through menus and multiple screens just to adjust the seat or even change the cruise control distance. that's annoying and honestly dangerous, because you end up scrolling menus instead of using a simple physical button in the car. another bad software problem is that there's no personal, fully customizable drive mode like porsche "individual" settings, so you're stuck with whatever the default programming is. another issue is the roof glass cracking after about two weeks of owning it, confirmed by lakeside bmw, and now it's waiting for repair that will take around two months for parts and work at a body shop. meanwhile we're driving around with a cracked roof glass that feels like it could eventually shatter and drop onto everyone in the car while driving.

overall i am very pleased with my new vehicle. after around three months i am gradually getting used to the technology built into it. there are a few aspects of the idrive options i would prefer to be different. first, i would like the ability to turn off the auto headlights. at the moment the lights can only be switched off while the car is in standby, and once the engine is running the auto lights are active again. there is a control on the lighting stalk but it does not actually disable them. second, there is no way to switch off the front daytime running lights, even though i am sure they could be accessed if needed. third, both the 12v supply (cigar lighter socket) and the usb c charging points stay powered for about 5 minutes after the vehicle is shut down, which keeps my dashcam running and leads to battery discharge.

it's a good car, but i was really put off by what feels like a sneaky approach from bmw around what i thought was basic standard kit. the 120m comes with headlights that dip automatically when a car is coming towards you or is in front, but nobody explained to me that this is only a one month free trial. to keep it on permanently you have to pay about £200, which i only found out later, and i think that is underhanded and not the bmw i used to know. if they had told me this clearly when i was looking at buying, it would not have stopped me getting the car, i would just have added the £200 onto the order. for a car costing over £35k i find this almost dishonest and really unpleasant, especially when even my wifes nissan includes that feature as standard.

evidence.quote: this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

i was ready to give a full 10, as it has been a very smooth, intuitive drive with a great shape and layout and solid fuel economy. however, last week the entire left side of the dashboard suddenly stopped working for no clear reason, so i lost hands free, radio, air con and other essentials, and was anxious about how long i'd be without them and whether it was safe to keep driving, especially with an amber spanner warning showing. i ended up being bounced between the dealer and bmw assist, with neither actually owning or fixing the problem. i was expecting around 3 weeks of having to drive with things not right when, to my surprise and relief, everything started working again the next day. it really played on my worst worries and i'm left wondering when it might fail again. happy to speak with someone at bmw about it.

i find the console display for navigation and driver info very good, and all the sensors do help with the occupant's safety. however, with my low mileage i don't really feel like i've had much of a wow factor. taking away the individual button has made the dashboard look cleaner but has also made it harder to alter settings, as you now have to work out which app to go into. some apps like 'spotify' that were on the previous car are now only there if you pay for digital premium, at extra cost. i still need to see if the 'navigation' information has been reduced since the digital premium trial finished. i think losing certain features has pushed the car more into the general mainstream hybrid market. i will definitely check other makers when it is time to swap cars.

overall this m135 is a big step down from my old 128ti, nowhere near as good. it just isnt as nice to drive, it tends to understeer and is awkward to manoeuvre slowly, especially parking, because the transmission feels very jerky. getting rid of the i-drive knob and all the physical heating buttons is backwards and i see it as a safety problem. the dashboard reflects off the windscreen, worse at night. the centre console actually flexes when you press the my modes button, which feels cheap. there is lots of wind noise from the wing mirrors on the motorway. the 128ti had door handle lights, m-sport pin stripes on the seat belts, coloured edging on the floor mats, red brake calipers and built-in digital services like spotify, all of which made it feel special, and the m135 lacks all of that. in the end the m135 feels disappointing and not worth the money.

fantastic car but extremely disappointed that after only about 5 weeks with a brand new model the whole dashboard crashed and needed a new part, meaning we were without our own car for roughly another 5 weeks! (the dealer in portstewart did give us a replacement car) but our main issue is with bmw for this kind of failure on a new car! it really knocks our confidence in bmw going forward and it was embarrassing having to tell people our car had to go back to the garage for repairs!! definitely not good for bmw. it is frustrating that bmw uk do not see this as a major problem and were hesitant to even admit it was disruptive for customers, so although the dealer gave us a hotel voucher it would have been considerate for bmw to at least acknowledge the fault and give an explanation!

as a small car it is excellent overall. plenty of space, comfortable and quick off the mark, with very smooth pull through the gears and really strong grip and cornering behaviour. the keyless boot release can be a bit unreliable. the digital key setup can also be frustrating at times: with my iphone and apple watch the car unlocks as i walk up, but if i open the boot to load it, by the time i've shut it and gone round to the driver door it has locked again and i need to stand for a moment until it opens. the mirrors do not always fold when locking, and the instrument cluster sometimes drops my personal layout. aside from those small digital issues, everything else is perfect.

car drives very smoothly, corners well and has enough power. it is quiet and the fuel consumption is good, though it's been mainly motorway use so far. the dashboard looks nice but really isn't practical to operate while driving. the dash lighting reflects in both outer rear view mirrors. the boot is smaller, but in fairness the tank is larger than on my previous 118i m sport, which gives better range. i miss the little storage area on the dash by the steering column. the seats are less comfortable than in my old 118i m sport and the driver's seat is already losing its shape, and i am only just over 12 stone. i also miss having an adjustable back support. the colour is perfect. sadly the car wasn't ordered to my own spec so it has extras i wouldn't normally pay for. i'm not keen on the idea of a trial period for extras and then having to pay to keep them.

overall the car is good, but my score drops because of a few things:
* the xdrive feels too front-wheel biased. a rear-wheel bias would have suited it better and been more fun, especially since this is supposed to be a semi-enthusiast car with 300hp and a price around 500 tkr.
* there are shift paddles instead of a proper gear lever. even a sequential "fake" shift lever for the dct would have felt better than paddles. the paddles come across as a gimmick and really only make sense on the highway. when you are turning or trying to drift, the paddles are basically useless.
* there are no physical controls for climate comfort like ac or seat heating. the screen is extremely clunky for the things you change all the time, such as temperature. for everything else, the screen works great.
* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.

i honestly wouldnt have gone for this car if it werent for the excellent leasing offer, about 4500 sek per month for 2 years. the choice was between leasing this or buying an old tuned volvo 740. i am happy i picked this one, but when you want to have fun driving, the gear paddles and the slightly too strong front-wheel bias do make it feel a bit limited.

* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.

generally the car is good, but in my view the electronic dash totally spoils it. my wife and i have done around 3800 miles since buying it and we have decided that trying to change anything hidden in the dash while on the move is just too dangerous, because of how long your eyes are off the road. so if we are together the passenger does the adjustments, and if alone we pull over to change things. i feel this system is many times more complex than my iphone, and it is illegal to use an iphone while driving. what is wrong with simple knobs, switches and dials? i also dread to think what it will cost to replace the dash when it eventually fails.

this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

good car to drive, it handles well and is quick enough for what i need. interior is nice, but the touchscreen setup is frankly unsafe to use on the move and really needs an idrive wheel to be safer. i don't see why that was removed other than to cut costs. turning off the speed limit and the equally risky lane departure warning is too fiddly, there should be a button for each. the my modes feature in this 120 is almost useless, adding no real driving benefit, just extra complexity and probably cost. the boot is too small for a car of this size. even with these complaints, it still suits my needs perfectly right now, and despite the over-complex tech the interface is still far better than my wife's mercedes a class.

i've been driving an m135 for around five years now. the one i got in april is spot on - smooth, properly punchy in sport mode, very comfortable and the tech support is excellent. but back in february i took delivery of a new m135 that lasted only about four days before it failed completely and came to a total stop. nobody ever came up with a diagnosis.

i had to bring in a solicitor to get that unreliable car returned and to secure a like-for-like replacement. after weeks of hassle, worry and extra expense, i did not receive a single word of apology from bmw. that is not the kind of response i would expect when paying over 42000 pounds for a car. while i'm really pleased with the m135 i have now, i'm still very disappointed with bmw and am waiting for your apolgy.

such a fantastic car, it gives an amazing driving experience every time. it is fully loaded with equipment and has three driving modes; i have not used the economy setting yet, but will do soon as my daily commute mileage is about to increase a lot. for my needs it is ideal, the interior and exterior build quality feel truly top class, backed up by advanced electronics and security systems. the two year service intervals are a real plus, and the my bmw app is excellent. i have only owned it for a couple of months, it has just finished running in and now it is ready for some proper fun. the drive chain and gearbox are incredibly smooth, and the way it grips the road is superb, always giving me confidence on the twisty country lanes where i live. i do still wish the new regulations did not affect the exhaust sound, as i love the noise from the m series, but sadly my car does not have that same exhaust note.

the 120 m sport is a joy to drive and you really feel connected to it on the road. there is a small hesitation when pulling away in normal drive, but switching to s mode fixes that and that is my preferred setting. the cabin is cozy and the view backwards through the side and rear mirrors is very good. the reversing camera makes parking easy. with the pro pack the car's appearance is boosted and the styling stands out even more. the main screen menu and all its options take a bit of time to learn, but it is actually enjoyable to figure it out. i used to have a 320 sport diesel which i was very fond of, and this new 120 m sport feels even more rewarding and fun to drive. the dynamic handling is very accurate and really encourages good driving. i absolutely love it.

this must be about my 12th bmw and my 3rd 1 series. the driving quality is good and the mini hybrid setup seems to really help with petol consumption. i do miss the bigger boot space though, as the batteries take it up; in the previous one i could put my golf trolley and bag in the back without dropping the seats, now i can't. since i started using the voice function it cuts down how much i need the touch screen and helps me keep my eyes on the road. i have a head up display on this car as on the last, and the way it changed from white to orange when the speed limit was exceeded was useful. the beeping that comes with it is very annoying, and if i turn the beeping off it also stops the orange change on the head up display, which i'd like to keep. there has also been an issue with apple car play and bmw voice.

overall it is a better, if slightly mixed, step up from my old 180i msport. the roadholding is more precise, the ride is improved on bad surfaces, there is a useful bit of extra power, the stop/start is far superior (the previous one was so poor i never used it), fuel economy is better and the engine runs smoother. on the downside, there is no single, easy-to-find autohold button anymore, it now needs one button then a touch on the screen. i rely on autohold for most driving, except for slow manoeuvres in tight areas where the throttle blip to release autohold can create more movement than i want. there should be a simpler, faster way to switch autohold on and off. i also miss a feature from my 180i: comfort mode used to give constant coasting. i realise regen improves efficiency, but having the option of coasting would be good for a very relaxed drive.

had a 21 plate m sport which we loved, so we went for a new 25 plate. picked it up and by the 3rd day it was showing a drive train fault. there are too many failures from sytner and bmw to list, but only after long and unnecessary legal action and sheer determination did we finally get our money back. we are still out of pocket because we had to hire a car until we could find another. we now have a 75 plate m sport which is a joy to drive and proves how obviously faulty the new one was. all 3 drivers on our policy have used both and agree. we expected much better from sytner and bmw given we were legally due a refund and should not have had to battle for it. it is a shame, as the car itself is good, with better service from sytner harold's wood.

last 7 cars were bmws, but because the new 1-series launch was delayed my previous car ended up being a mercedes. very pleased to be back in a bmw! overall i am really happy with this car, so the points below are in that context: 1. first time with an automatic. i also drive my partner's fiat 500ev, and i am a bit disappointed by the slight lag in acceleration. i can get around it by putting it in sport mode ahead of time, but thats not always practical, and it doesnt stack up well against the ev. i havent touched the paddles and doubt i will. 2. the display is limited compared with the mercedes. i cant show consumption, elapsed time and distance driven along with the standard info like i could on the a-class. 3. can't use a usb stick for music. 4. as usual there is more functionality than i will ever need or use, and i am still going through the online manual.

i previously test drove the older 1 series and found it very uninvolving and not at all like a typical bmw, so i chose not to buy it. later, when i read about the new version, especially the mild hybrid with 4-wheel drive, my interest came back. within the first quarter mile it felt like a proper bmw again, with great feedback through the steering, spot-on handling, real grip on the road and strong performance when you select the right mode. the cabin layout is easy to understand even for someone who has never owned a car with a touchscreen. i really appreciate that the indicator stalks are back to simple on/off switches; the old setup could be awkward to cancel and sometimes ended up signalling the other way. i have already done several long trips and felt relaxed afterwards. extremely satisfied so far!

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.

the inability to properly control the driving modes is really annoying. the disappearance of buttons and the idrive wheel to manage things is a pain. the touch screen itself is very good, but it pulls your attention away too much. a simple button to turn off start stop would do, instead it's awkward to use. i want to set off, not waste time searching through menus. the centre console buttons are hard to distinguish so you have to look down, there's barely any separation. the steering wheel is excessively thick and an option for a slimmer one would be preferable. with no audible exhaust note it becomes boring to drive. you pay a high price only to be asked to pay again for premium infotainment options soon after. i only want the spotify app. the cabin is beautiful and a pleasant environment. i feel like i'm managing a machine rather than actually driving. fantastic car, no character at all.

this is my first petrol 1 series after having had four previous bmw 1 series sport models, and while i do enjoy how it drives, there are some things that really annoy me. the biggest frustration is the new virtual assistant, which just isn't as good as the old one. on top of that, my bmw keeps disconnecting even when the phone or the key are actually inside the car. there are bits of my previous car that i liked more, and that's all down to the newer technology that seems to be standard now, whereas i preferred the earlier setup. the actual drive and handling are excellent, and the fuel economy is fantastic for the cheaper journeys around town. but in my opinion the it side needs work, especially the speech control. for example, on my old car i could just say something like "end route guidance" and it understood, but now it only responds properly if you say "end route navigation" exactly. it can't deal with the simpler phrasing, and changing these things with every new car you make bmw is really frustrating.

overall i'm pleased with my bmw 120 m sport. i've marked it 9 out of 10 for a couple of reasons.   1. the centre console has been glitchy, at times really sluggish and occasionally it has frozen, meaning i've had to reset it. this is annoying because it also wipes the efficient mode gained mileage reading. after the latest firmware update the console seems quicker, but the other day i got in and a message came up saying ' driver assistance restricted' and there were scrolling lines on the screen like it was rebooting ??  2. the bmw personal assistant doesn't always switch the drive mode when i ask it to.  aside from that i'm happy with the car  thanks

title: G60 Blower function
requirement_statement: Improve 'Blower function' for G60 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated they have seen the air conditioning vents change position, and specifically mentioned the driver-side vent on the right sometimes ending up at zero. Customer questioned if this is happening by itself or from accidentally touching it. Writer asked if the customer could be hitting the vent while reaching for the touchscreen and advised that once the vents are set, they do not adjust automatically.

Customer mentioned the touchscreen controls for airflow are too distracting while driving and said she would prefer physical knobs to set the vent speed manually. Writer advised using the "Hey BMW" voice assistant for climate adjustments. Customer said she had noticed that feature but was not aware it could handle that function.

really solid build quality, but it should have been a true from-scratch pure electric design. the climate control setup and the air vents are terrible. should have proper analog controls with usable vents. the car doesnt feel agile or nimble, and it ought to, even if the batteries are heavy. my car keeps dropping the connection so the app is out of sync, often forcing a 70 second hard reset or a call to a genius for a forced update. still, i am interested in watching how the i5 and later versions evolve.

Customer reported hearing a knocking noise from beneath the centrally positioned climate control vents on the dash. Customer mentioned seeing on an internet forum that the knocking could be linked to the air conditioning pumps. Customer stated the noise only appears at low speeds when the air conditioning is on and is not affected by road conditions or bumps. Customer stated he has not reached out to his dealer. Writer advised that the dealer would be able to perform additional diagnosis on the knocking sound.

even though i love how the car handles, there are a few things you took away that my 2021 had and i just don't get why. you removed the pockets on the back of the seats. maybe that cut production costs, but without those pockets i have to dump stuff like umbrellas and the kids' things on the rear floor. the worst part, and honestly a deal breaker when my lease is up, is the trunk size. i can't fit my grandchild's stroller in there, or a full food shop, or my mother's walker. i also dislike the silver/chrome 5s on the rear windows, it's a luxury vehicle and i don't need it shouting that it's a 5 series. the glove box is smaller now, same with the door wells, and i really don't like that i can't leave anything in the console tray since i'm no longer able to cover it. i'm forced to look away from the road to manage the controls because the knobs are gone and everything is flat. with the fan vents hidden and streamlined, i can't adjust the airflow direction anymore. i could keep going, but i'm sure the team who came up with this very modern car is pleased with what they made. for me, if these things aren't changed by the time my lease ends, i'll most likely move to another luxury brand. i genuinely hope you take this feedback on board. when i checked reviews afterwards, i saw these issues weren't just mine, a lot of people felt the same way. i really believe i'm exactly the kind of customer you target, so i hope you treat my comments seriously. my whole family drives bmws and nobody from about 35 to 70 is happy with the new design. it feels very clunky and not sleek anymore. i've already told my sales person all of this. again, i hope you truly take in and value my feedback.
anna kerr

overall the car feels basically well built, but the price is still too high for what you actually get. there are several areas where it seems things have been pared back compared to what you would expect as obvious. it is not just about the equipment list you can read through (which you really have to study carefully, because it is very hard to understand exactly what the car has as standard). in terms of perceived quality, for example, the carpet in the boot and the standard radio have clearly been economised, which is far below what you expect from a premium brand. there are also obvious gaps in the standard equipment that ought to be a given and cost nothing, like the fact there is no cigar lighter socket in the trunk. you can see lines in the doors bulging slightly where the inner plate meets the edges, which feels far under the standard you would expect and becomes a daily irritation when you notice it. in the middle of the bonnet you can see a row of marks that look like spot welds from underneath. so in the end i actually regret buying it, even though in many ways it is a nice car.

Customer stated that when playing music from his phone, via the built-in Spotify app, or from the radio, he cannot find any way to pause it. Customer stated he would like a dedicated pause button and noted he is able to skip tracks but not actually pause them.

Customer stated she was unsure how to shut the radio off. Writer advised that the volume knob on the center console is also a button that can be pressed. Writer advised pressing it will switch off or mute the radio.

the car handles incredibly well. it feels very responsive and nimble, and the ride quality is good,
even when driving in wet weather.
i also appreciate the overall size of the vehicle - there is generous interior room in both the front and back, and the trunk is quite large.
for future upgrades, the in-car clock is really tiny - a bigger display would be better for us older drivers. also, the direction indicator (showing north, south, east, west) only appears off and on. in the cadillac i traded in, the clock face was a comfortable size and the direction display was visible all the time.
i have also found parts of the tech for the radio/sirius/spotify and car play to be difficult and a bit hard to figure out.

Customer expressed a preference for how the 540i implements the Bowers & Wilkins sound system compared to the M5. Customer stated that his 540i has speakers positioned under the seats and he likes that setup.

Customer stated that recently he tried to put the game on in his vehicle and then realized there were no AM stations available. Customer wanted to verify that the vehicle does not include AM. Writer confirmed that electric vehicles do not have AM radio because the frequencies used would affect the electric components.

Customer stated that when listening to Sirius radio he has his favorite stations stored, but once he picks a station the favorites list disappears and he has to go back into the favorites menu to see them again. Customer stated it is also frustrating that the selected station takes over the full screen, and he has to work back through the home screen to return, since he cannot just go back one step.

Customer stated he wants a way to pause XM radio in the car like his previous vehicle did. He said when there is a great interview he does not want to miss any of it and wants the system to buffer and save it so he can continue listening when he returns.

the apps built into the car really ought to be reachable from the phone, so you don't have to sit in the car and fiddle with them - you can do that in a mercedes, which was my previous car. the windows also can't be closed via the app, while mercedes manages that. if they could close themselves automatically when it rains, like mercedes does, i haven't found any sign that they do, but they should. the car has locked me out several times when i've left either the phone or the keys inside. settings in the app like folding the mirrors when locking don't actually work when it's other users, even though the option is set in the app. my wife is forced to type in a pin code and can't just pick her id, supposedly because of the risk that her phone might be stolen - but the primary user's phone can be stolen too, so that explanation doesn't make sense. the information shown in the dashboard is poor no matter which view you choose. the radio will not receive a signal while i'm driving through the limfjord tunnel, which i go through every day, and that's something i've never run into with any other car i've owned. the winter range is deeply reprehensible and honestly my biggest complaint: no more winter holiday trips, because the real range on the motorway at 130 kmh in frost is at most about 250 km. well, i guess i have to stop somewhere, but i'm left disappointed. mvh mads

Customer stated the Sirius XM Notify function no longer operates on the current 27 530i or on their prior 2024 530i. Customer explained it used to alert them when favorite songs or artists were on other channels, and now they rely on preset stations instead as a workaround. Writer advised that software updates and reboots had already been completed. Writer further explained this could be a Sirius-related problem or a feature they may have discontinued, and advised the customer to reach out to Sirius for additional details and troubleshooting.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

the car is extremely smooth and quiet, unlike my earlier bmws. controls are straightforward, and the mix of performance and luxury is really well done. my other evs lacked a sun roof, so having one on the i5 is a big plus. the only real downside is the awful carplay audio behavior: most of the time i need the radio volume at max just to hear normally, then an incoming call can be super loud and the whole system ends up blaring because it is already turned up. lots of people online describe the same issue, and while some suggested fixes help for a while, the low volume problem keeps coming back.

the maple creek dealership basically lied about everything. i told them i didn't want the car until 5/21 and only after all the paperwork was signed they suddenly say they can't do that. i gave them a lease to match at 36/10000 and somehow they changed it to 7500. i wanted the camera to record while i am driving, but it only records about 30 seconds. they told me that once the system fully downloaded the feature would work, which was not true. i clearly said not to sell or share my information with sirius xm and they went ahead and did it. what i asked for and what was delivered did not line up. the contract is not the same as the lease i told them to match. their promises turned out to be lies. i won't get another bmw. the car app is poor. the trunk kick-to-open only works around half the time. you also can't remove apps even though they said you could.

it is about as close as you can get to an electric car that still doesnt really appear or feel like an ev. the whole premium feel is intact. the range, though, really has to be improved, right now it is simply not good enough. on top of that there are some irritating design details. 1. the seat belts bang into plastic if you dont consciously pull them fully up. 2. the small hooks in the trunk for groceries cant actually hold a bag handle. 3. the door handles are oddly placed, so people who dont know the car cant locate them in the dark. 4. the trunk lid needs a very firm pull to shut correctly, which again is hard for people unfamiliar with the car. 5. since clever is a major player in denmark, it is pretty frustrating that their charging card isnt integrated in the infotainment, so the charging guidance is basically unusable in denmark. supposedly that will be sorted.

i'm really happy with my new bmw overall. the one thing that bothers me is trying to learn all the different options on the video screen. i also am not a fan of these door handles and liked the ones on my 2011 bmw 528i much better. another annoyance is that the driver and passenger climate controls don't automatically sync like they did in my old bmw. most of the time i'm driving alone and it's irritating that the cabin temperatures aren't synced by default. if i have someone with me, they can change their own setting, but i feel the automatic sync should be the main preference. i'm still working out how to enter navigation addresses, it was much simpler with the old dial system in my 2011 bmw. i've also found the trunk very hard to open with my foot under the rear of the car; i don't know if there's some trick to it, but it only opens maybe 10% of the times i try.

i've had the car for about 4 months and i'm splitting my thoughts into pros and cons.

pros:
- driving dynamics: really strong acceleration and power delivery, steering is accurate and easy, the car feels nicely planted in corners, and the steering weight is spot on.
- technology: screens have great clarity and quality, ui is fast, apps and info are solid, speakers/sound system are excellent, the iconic sounds are fun, and the mybmw app integration and features plus the ambient lighting are all big positives.
- styling: love the interior dash design and the look of the front fascia, especially the new lights and the kidney grille.

cons:
- brake pedal feel when slowing down isn't right.
- sound insulation around the b pillars is really weak; tyre/road and other cars' noises are way too loud for a 5 series, so the b pillars on both sides need extra deadening.
- rear legroom should be better for a car this long.
- not enough storage: missing rear seat pockets and nothing under the center console.
- rear lights don't look as iconic as the front, and those two silver bits on the lower bumper just seem out of place.

Customer reported that the low profile wheels and tires are causing problems in the New York City area because of potholes. Customer stated he has already had two flat tires in roughly six weeks of ownership, which he did not expect and feels is happening more frequently than he would prefer. Customer compared this with his past experience owning two BMW 3 Series vehicles on three-year leases each, over a total of six years, during which he had no flat tires at all. Customer confirmed that those previous 3 Series models also came equipped with run flat tires.
Customer stated he appreciates that the new vehicle does not have run-flat tires, and specifically mentioned this as an improvement for Dallas road conditions.
Customer stated he appreciates that this vehicle comes without run flats.

Customer reported it is hard to park because the ride height is so tall, and he needs extra room to get the car lined up right. Customer mentioned he would rather have 19-inch wheels instead of the 20-inch wheels, to improve the angle he sees in the camera.

i really like the 5 series bmw and have been buying bmw vehicles since 1999. i still have my 2016 535 xi and it is easily the best car i've owned, both in appearance and in the features it came with. that 2016 has massaging seats, the bmw logo lights up on the inside of the doors, and the wheels look great. overall it's just a gorgeous car.

by comparison, my current 2025 feels very generic. i custom ordered this 2025 and added every option that was available, so it's supposed to be top of the line, yet it's very disappointing. it seems like bmw cut corners on this model. there are no massaging seats, and when i chose the upgraded seats you removed the heated seats in the back. i had a 2024 before and swapped it for the 2025 only because i didn't like the color on the 2024.

back in 2016 and earlier, bmw would send a little gift like a nice keychain or a usb fob shaped like a bmw key. i got nothing with the 2024 or the 2025. the key that came with the 2024 was shiny and attractive, while the 2025 key looks very plain and generic. i don't know why it ended up like that, especially since the 2025 cost more than the 2024. overall, the 2025 has been very disappointing.

i would like to show you a video comparing the 2016 with the 2025 to explain what i mean. i've ordered an m5 and i'm hoping that will turn out better than what i'm driving now. thank you.

for me and my husband, who does most of the driving, the biggest negative is having nearly all the controls on the touch screen. we just can't remember every symbol for everything. a lot of them we still don't recognize and feel like we need to go back to see a genius again. we are also worried that there are no more run flat tires. we still haven't figured out how the tire flat inflator actually works. the sport vs regular gearing feels too far apart. in normal drive, the a/c airflow gets too low whenever we sit in traffic or at a red light, which is hard to deal with in southern florida where it's always hot. on the plus side, the outside and inside look very beautiful. the seats are very comfortable, but we miss having the back seat pockets and spots to store things.
the way it drives is very smooth and comfortable.

my i5m60 is a fantastic car overall. but i do have four complaints. 1) it's really priced too high. you do get a lot of car, yet there's zero discount for choosing an electric. 2) when ordering, i couldn't configure it with anything except summer tires, which is a silly setup for anything but a pure sports car. i've put winter tires on now, but for summer i'd much rather run all-season radials that deal with water better and fit the character of the car more. 3) the removal of physical buttons, like just having a simple switch for the heated steering wheel, is irritating. i honestly hope the eu forces bmw to reverse that choice. 4) in assisted driving the car tends to oversteer on lane changes and then has to correct itself.
i'm a big fan of the bluetooth access, and there are a lot of other things i really like too!

really pleased with how it drives, the tech in it is excellent, the security cameras and speed recognition work great, the close vehicle warning and the yellow alerts on the wing mirrors are very helpful, and it slows down brilliantly when you come off the accelerator. the manual gear shifts on the levers behind the wheel feel really good to use. petrol usage is very eco friendly, and the sport mode sensation is amazing. the location and other monitoring features in the smartphone app are excellent. the car looks amazing, and a few people on the pavements have waved and given a thumbs up as i passed. thanks to the monitoring app and security i managed to get a great insurance deal at a little over £500, as the car is seen as low risk for theft and i can track it myself if it ever did get stolen, thankyou.

i'm happy with the car in general, but it has some surprising problems or design flaws:

1. i am not able to permanently shut off the "start/stop" function, and that makes the ride feel uncomfortable.
2. i also can't lock in the "sync" setting for the heater/ac so it stays on or off, which is irritating.
3. the rear bumper appears a bit loose and makes rattling noises when i turn or go over bumps. when i tapped on it, i could hear rattling, so something inside seems loose or the way it is built is faulty.
4. when i'm stopped at a light and then pull away, there's a click from the front passenger side wheel area. the brakes are probably releasing, but it doesn't feel smooth.
5. while idling, the engine will sometimes shake the car in a way i don't expect.
6. right after starting and driving off, the parking assist usually doesn't come on for the first few minutes, even when obstacles are close. i notice the same thing in parking spaces.

after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

Customer reported she appreciates the move to conventional tires as well as having a spare tire included.
Customer stated that his car is equipped with 21 inch summer tires, and that they have not worked well when driving in a blizzard.

Customer mentioned they would rather have equal-sized wheels instead of the staggered setup in the M-Sport Dynamic Package. Customer stated the staggered layout has bigger wheels in the rear than the front, leading to problems around 12000 to 13000 miles when tire rotation is required, and that identical wheel sizes would simplify rotation.

Customer stated the Hankook tires fitted on his vehicle are extremely noisy. Customer stated he hears a roaring sound while driving the car. Customer stated he would rather have Michelin tires, as he feels they are better tires and do not make as much noise.

this car will not suit everyone. the ride is smooth and quiet, the seats and audio are excellent, and the fuel economy and performance are impressive for such a large vehicle. the accent lighting is something I truly enjoy. the downside is the slightly isolated feel of the ride and some tech that comes across as intrusive. the accelerator pedal has a bit of a sticky feel, and the wave-your-foot trunk opener hardly ever works. the nav system is dreadful. it does not seem set up for americans, and its guidance is often inconsistent and wrong: saying "bear left" when there is no reason, then not saying it when there should be; sending me onto blocked or unfinished roads even though the map later shows them as blocked; telling me to stay on the same road ahead when nothing is actually changing; using bear left/right when you are really turning onto a different road and it should say "turn left onto...". it also does not announce when it is rerouting. there is better technology out there.

Writer stated that answering from the control display should set the audio zone to the front, and accepting the call through the touch command should move the zone to the rear. Writer advised removing the phone in the mobile device menu and pairing it again. Writer stated that re-establishing the Bluetooth connection can sometimes help in situations like this. Writer tried to go over the steps to change the audio zone manually if needed, but the customer already knew how to do that.

Customer stated that the audio volume keeps coming back lower than how he previously set it whenever he gets into the vehicle or after finishing phone calls. Customer stated it seems to occur randomly and, to clear it, he has to get out of the car and then get back in again. Customer stated that this behavior is inconsistent. Customer stated he currently has around 1600 miles on the vehicle. Customer stated he performed a software update in the car last weekend. Customer's vehicle software: G070-25-07-551.
i really like the design, the performance, the audio system and the prestige.

Customer stated the audio in the car keeps glitching. Customer stated it happens when he is using Bluetooth to play downloaded songs from his phone, or when he uses a USB jump drive with music. Customer stated that after driving for a few minutes the sound starts acting up, the music cuts out, and there is a beeping noise like some kind of interference, as if something is trying to break in. Customer stated that FM radio and Sirius XM both work fine without any issues.
Customer stated this only occurs with the USB jump drive or downloaded music on his phone. Customer stated he left the vehicle at the dealership a few days ago, but the dealership was not able to duplicate the problem at first. Customer stated that on the way home from the dealership the glitch started again. Customer stated he brought the car back, and this time the technician confirmed the problem. Customer stated the dealership tried deleting his phone from the system and pairing it again, but that did not resolve it. Writer confirmed the phone is an iPhone 14 PRO, with carrier AT&T and iOS 16.3 installed.
Customer stated he does not use CarPlay.
Follow up: Customer stated the dealership still has his vehicle. Customer stated that even after confirming the malfunction, the dealership has not been able to diagnose it. Customer stated the dealership recorded a video of the issue and forwarded it to BMWNA. Customer stated he then received a text from the dealership saying BMWNA instructed them to reset the master system, and that they would now monitor the car. Customer stated he has been without his vehicle for about 2 weeks and is hoping to get an update from the dealership in the next day or so.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

we absolutely love our i7. it rides so smoothly, looks really elegant, is packed with cool technology, and the real world range is quite good. we use it both for business and personal needs. we shuttle clients, mostly physicians at a clinic, and they are very impressed with the car and really like that it is an ev.

my spouse and i enjoy taking it everywhere. we have put close to 4800 miles on it in about 3 months, and it hardly feels like that much. it is a joy to drive on longer road trips.

there are a couple of things i would change. the subwoofer seems like it should be placed somewhere in the cabin. i think there is an upgraded diamond surround system that might add this. i owned a 2016 m5 before, and the bass in that car was just right. a friend has a 2024 ix, and i was amazed by the sound system in his.

ours is carbon black, so it gets washed often. one thing i noticed is that the rear trunk lid, especially the area under the rear bmw badge, traps a lot of water and it drains slowly. when it finally drains, it runs down onto the rear bumper and leaves water spots. we even use a blow dryer and it still causes some hassle. every car has its quirks, so i am not overly concerned.

also, i feel like the master window controls on the driver door should be moved back about 1-2 inches. even after 3 months, i still end up opening the rear windows when i mean to open the fronts. the placement feels unnatural. i'm 6 feet tall and have never really run into this in another vehicle.

overall, i really love this car and already look forward to owning another one someday. thanks for making such a gem of a vehicle.

the upgraded bowers wilkins stereo is awful and you should give money back to anyone who had to pay for it. in my earlier bmws with the b&w system it was great. you moved the speakers from under the seats and now it is laughable. everyone who rides in the car comments on the stereo and then i tell them it was a $4,800 upgrade... this might end up being my last bmw. when you turn it up there is basically no bass or mid at all. it sounds terrible, everything just disappears, really sad.
also, you cannot keep the ac on air recirculation or keep the whole climate system synced, it resets every single time you shut the car off. luxury should mean you do not have to keep doing things, but i have to spend about a minute every time i get in the car setting up stuff that should stay the same. ac fan level 2 is way too weak and 3 is too strong and loud. bring back proper air vents.
i am not happy with this purchase and this is my 8th 7 series in around 12 years. i will not renew to this again.
