title: G70 Driver profile
requirement_statement: Improve 'Driver profile' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer mentioned he wants his wife's BMW ID to show a nickname instead of her full name. Writer advised that the name on his wife's BMW ID is not able to be modified. Customer added that his wife and children are the main drivers of the vehicle and they would prefer a different name than hers to appear. Writer explained that he and his kids can each set up their own BMW ID and then link it to the car.

Customer stated that when she gets into the vehicle and chooses her profile, the seat does not adjust. Customer added that when she attempts to modify the setting, a message appears saying she must log in with her phone. Writer offered assistance, and customer said she is currently at work and will reach out again when she is with the car.
Customer says the vehicle will sometimes forget his driver profile details and he must log back in agian.

Customer reported his wife's driver profile was not linking to the vehicle when she got in, so she had to enter her PIN each time. Writer guided him through turning on driver recognition for the Digital Key.

Customer stated he is trying to set up his personal profile so that when he gets in the car, the AC temperature and all other settings return to where they were left. Customer mentioned the profile appears on the screen with a welcome message and his name, but the settings are not restored to his previous values. Customer explained that his preferences are not being saved, including the AC and the seat position, and that he has to press seat memory button one again for the seat to go back where it should be. Writer asked if there is another driver involved and whether the customer is using a smartphone or Apple Watch as the key. Customer confirmed he uses a smartphone and is the primary driver about 99 percent of the time. Customer stated his wife does not have a profile set up on the 7 series. Customer stated he plans to visit the dealership when he has time to get assistance with the profile setup. Writer advised the customer to set all settings again, including the seat, make sure they are stored in the profile, and then lock the car upon exiting. Writer verified in Dealer cockpit that the permissions are configured correctly. Writer then asked if the customer also has an Apple Watch or carries the digital key card. Customer confirmed he only has an Apple phone and does not use an Apple Watch. Writer explained that once everything is configured and the vehicle is locked, the system should recognize the profile each time. Writer recommended going to the dealership if the issue continues. Writer also suggested performing an iDrive reboot by moving the car out of the garage, leaving the engine running, and pressing and holding the radio volume button for 70 seconds. Writer explained the screen may turn black as many as three times during that period and instructed the customer to keep holding the button for the full 70 seconds, then allow it to boot up to see if the settings are saved. Writer stated this procedure forces the system to update to the latest version since sometimes it is searching for settings that no longer exist. Customer confirmed he understood all the steps and stated he would try the reboot. Customer then stated he could not stay on the call. Customer stated he would contact the dealership later today or tomorrow to arrange an appointment for next week to address the profile settings concern.

Customer stated that when his wife is driving the car, her profile is not loading properly. Writer advised he should enter the vehicle with only her key, choose her profile, then open settings and link that key to her profile.

Customer reported that at times the vehicle will identify his wife first instead of him, so he needs to manually change the active profile. Customer asked if the vehicle treats his phone, Apple Watch, or key fob differently when recognizing a driver, and whether that would affect which settings load. Writer explained that there is no distinction between those devices, as they all connect to the same driver profile so the same settings will be shown.

Customer stated that when he gets into the car he has to choose his driver profile and then reset his seat position. Writer advised him to connect his profile to the key fob and went over the steps. Customer agreed and asked for an emial to be sent.

Customer stated he would prefer the driver recognition to identify the driver only once the person is seated in the driver seat. Customer stated that when he and his wife get in the vehicle with both key fobs, the system usually picks her profile first because he opens her door and lets her in before he gets in himself. Writer explained that when both key fobs are near the car, the vehicle chooses the profile according to whichever key is detected first. Customer stated the profile should not switch until the actual driver is sitting in the driver seat.

Customer stated that sometimes when beginning a drive, the ambient lighting comes on in white even though it is normally set to a different color. Writer confirmed the Customer has both the key remote and Digital Key set up. Writer advised that it is possible one of those is not assigned to the Customer profile and may be triggering the default profile instead.

Customer mentioned it is difficult to see which settings belong to a specific driver profile and which apply to the entire vehicle. Customer stated that some way to distinguish between them would be helpful.
Customer stated she really likes that the vehicle stores and adjusts the settings automatically depending on who is driving.

Customer stated that when the vehicle was delivered, there was another user profile already stored in the BMW ID system, which had to be deleted by the dealership staff. Writer explained this may have been from technicians using the vehicle to demonstrate features and recorded the concern in the notes.
Customer mentioned he and his wife both have their driver profiles connected to their phone digital keys, and at times the car gets confused when they get in at the same time.
Customer stated that her driver profile prompts for her PIN every single time she gets into the car.

Customer stated the car keeps getting mixed up about which driver is in control. Customer stated that when he is driving, it frequently loads the wrong user profile. Customer stated he is using a key fob, while his wife has her own key fob and also set up the digital key on her phone. Writer explained that the digital key is causing his wife's profile to load. Writer advised that the vehicle will always detect the digital key first and activate the profile associated with that digital key. Writer advised that if his wife disables the digital key on her phone, that should resolve the profile issue.

Customer called for help connecting his key to his driver profile. Customer explained that only his wife's key is currently linked, which makes getting into the vehicle difficult due to her seat position. Writer guided the customer step by step via RVG: open the apps menu, go to BMW ID, manage BMW ID, select his profile, then driver recognition, and add his key under linkage. Customer was able to complete this successfully. Writer also had the customer check the secondary profile to confirm the second key fob was associated, and it was already linked.

Customer reported she would like to change the name on her driver profile in the vehicle instead of using the legal name that currently appears. Writer explained that the profile she is using is probably tied to the vehicle warranty. As a workaround, writer recommended setting up an additional driver profile with her preferred name, using a different email address.
Customer stated she really likes all the personalization options available with the driver profiles.

right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

even though i really love the car itself, my first experiences with it have made me nervous about what owning it long-term will be like. the very first thing that went wrong was a dead 48 volt battery right at vehicle pickup, which meant i couldn't even drive my new $150,000 car home. i ended up waiting about a week while they sourced and installed a new battery.

then at just under 3,000 miles the dcs module failed, which made the brakes almost useless and nearly caused me to be part of a several-car pileup on a local freeway. this happened on december 23rd, during a drive from palm desert to pasadena (roughly 130 miles), and that made it even harder to get a tow truck out to me since i was about 88 miles from home. the wait for the tow was something like 3+ hours.

i've now been in a dealership loaner for over 10 days because the part my car needed was discontinued and replaced by a newer version that still isn't available. i will say bmw emergency service and my service advisors have been responsive, understanding, and sympathetic.

this is my 9th bmw, so i'm familiar with the quirks and issues they tend to develop as they get older, but seeing big problems like this on a brand-new vehicle feels pretty disheartening and discouraging. i waited a long time to be able to buy what i thought was the pinnacle of the bmw lineup, and now that i finally did, i feel somewhat let down.

that said, i truly love the look, the feel, and the way this thing drives; it has met or even exceeded what i expected from a flagship bmw. i'm hopeful that as we go forward my trust in bmw and its craftsmanship will come back. thank you for letting me share all of this.

evidence.quote: Customer reported being very satisfied with the driver assist plus feature on a recent road trip.

Customer asked what the difference is between driving assist and assist plus. Writer advised that driving assist requires the driver to keep hands on the steering wheel every so often, while assist plus allows hands off. Customer confirmed understanding.
Customer mentioned he enjoys using the autonomous driving function when driving on the highway.
Customer mentioned they are excited to use the assisted driving features more, since they regularly go on longer road trips.
Customer stated he avoids using Assisted Driving Plus because the feature appears too complicated to him.

Customer remarked that for a lot of people, it takes some time to get comfortable with the self-driving functions. Customer mentioned that spending more time actually driving the car makes it easier to understand how strong the self-driving systems are and how they behave. Customer noted there is definitely a learning curve with figuring out how the driver assistance features function and respond in different driving scenarios.
Customer stated he appreciates the self drive feature.
Customer stated that he is very pleased with the assisted driving technology when he is traveling on the highway.

Customer stated he was using the highway assistant on the highway when it suddenly stopped functioning and a check light appeared. Customer stated he had to take over and control the car to drive safely. Customer stated this happened at roughly 340 miles and the vehicle now has about 3100 miles. Customer stated he visited the dealership over four times before the ram was finally replaced, and the car is now driving properly.

Customer stated he is very pleased with the Assisted Driving feature. Customer stated he may cover roughly 600 miles in one day. Customer stated he finds the system to be very precise. Customer stated he usually sets the car at 80 MPH. Customer stated he still keeps his hands on the wheel, but by the end of the drive he does not feel exhausted.

Customer stated he really enjoys the handsfree driving, but mentioned the car tends to brake late and very abruptly where a person would start easing off and slowing down sooner. Customer stated he has already set the braking distance to the maximum setting.

Customer stated the prior 7 Series had a feature that kept the car in its lane around curves, but the current one does not do that the same way. Writer compared the 2024 package with his present package and explained the older car had Driving Assistant Pro with Highway Assistant, which is not included on the current vehicle.
Customer stated he appreciates assisted driving plus, noting it helps a lot with lane changes and in stop and go traffic.
Customer stated he likes the Highway Assistant, referring to it as the "self-driving" feature.

Customer stated they really like using the Highway Assistant because it operates completely hands free and this helps take the stress out of their daily commute. Customer added that in their previous vehicle they always had to keep their hands on the steering wheel.
Customer stated he gets prompts to press okay to use Enhanced Driver Assistance and was unsure where to select okay. Writer stated that pressing down on the controller will confirm okay.
Customer commented that having the Highway assistant feature in the vehicle is something he likes.
Customer mentioned the self driving feature and said it is amazing.

Customer reported that while driving from Kentucky down to Tennessee, the driver assistance plus feature refused to switch on. Customer mentioned they suspected dirty sensors again, since that had happened previously, so they cleaned all of them, but the feature still stayed inactive. Customer stated that cruise control would not engage and the front radar distance sensor also did not operate. Customer explained they had to go in and manually disable all the assistance functions, after which they could only use regular cruise control. Customer commented they were unsure if it was some kind of location issue, because the next day back in Kentucky they tried the car and everything worked. Customer stated it has been working perfectly ever since.
Customer stated they would rather have full self-driving than the current adaptive cruise control and wish this car came with it.

Customer stated they like everything about the vehicle and specifically pointed out the autopilot feature as a standout aspect they are enjoying. Customer mentioned they drive frequently, and the autopilot assists them during their regular driving.
Customer indicated he is pleased with the self-driving capabilities of the vehicle.

Customer called asking how to turn on the assisted driving modes. Writer explained to first switch on cruise control, then press mode to pick the desired system. Customer reported that when he does this, it shows the system is ready but he is unsure how to start it. Writer advised again to press mode, select the system he wants, and allow it to activate.
Customer stated they really love the driving assistant.

Customer stated he had a Tesla before purchasing this vehicle. Customer stated that BMW's assisted driving systems are far better than Tesla's. Customer stated these assisted driving functions make long journeys more pleasant and help lessen driver fatigue.

Customer stated that the highway assistant is not available on all roads and that he primarily drives in rural parts of South Carolina. Customer stated it would be nice if this feature covered more roads.
Customer stated he loves that the car can essentially drive itself on the highway and adjust to the speeds of surrounding traffic. Customer stated all of the assisted driving features are great.

Customer stated he really likes the automatic driving feature because he does not have to think about anything while it is active, and it even adjusts the speed going around corners and handles everything.

Customer asked how long he is able to drive with the highway assistant switched on continuously. Writer advised that, to his knowledge, there is no specific time limit. Customer then stated the assisted driving package feels more complicated to operate than on their 2019 X5.
Customer stated they really apreciate the hands-free driving function and like how the system behaves and gives driving assistance.
Customer stated he tried out the self driving function on the way to his second home on a winding road and it worked very well.

Customer stated the assisted driving feature feels a little scary to him. Customer stated that at times it will flash red and then hand control back over to the driver. Writer questioned whether this was happening while the customer was driving around sharp curves or heading into the sun. Customer stated he has not really noticed if curves or sun are the cause. Customer stated the vehicle will sometimes swerve when it detects something, and he is not ready for that sudden swerve when it occurs.
Customer stated he likes using the highway assistant.
Customer indicated he would like the vehicle to offer full autonomous driving capability similar to what Tesla provides.

Customer reported that with Highway Assistant on max following distance, if the vehicle ahead brakes hard, his car waits until it is closer, then brakes very sharply. Customer commented he would prefer the car to detect traffic further ahead and ease into braking more like a human driver.
Customer stated she appreciates the driver assistance systems, particularly in heavy traffic, as they help make driving easier.

Customer inquired whether the highway assistant works only on highways or could take her all the way to the navigation destination. Writer advised it only operates on mapped highways and once off those the customer must continue driving to the destination. Customer then asked if she could upgrade it to do this, and writer advised that is not available.

Customer stated the dashboard interface is a bit challenging because the display screen sits far enough to the right that, when he looks at it in normal use, the driver distraction warning comes on in automated driving mode. Customer commented that the level five driving works very well overall, but the distraction monitoring seems overactive and frequently registers when he looks at the navigation or radio during regular driving. Customer noted he understands the idea of someone taking their eyes off the road for a long stretch, yet the system appears to trigger so quickly that it becomes difficult to even glance at the instruments. Customer suggested it likely would not trigger so much if the display were closer to the center or shown in the heads up display.

this is a newly released model and it still has some bugs that need to be sorted out. the tech is quite overwhelming, and i am repeatedly having to reset things. the interior lighting setting i prefer keeps changing by itself to a different color. whenever i use the idrive selection tool, it drops down a presets screen each time i touch it, so when i try to choose a new radio station it pulls up those presets instead. the driving assistance functions are hard to locate and adjust, you have to hop from one screen to another. there should be a simple way to temporarily disable these features for things like traffic or going through a car wash. a basic alarm cancel or silence button would be very helpful. the seat controls on the dashboard are awkward to use because you have to lean forward to make adjustments. putting the controls on the seat or the door would be better and would let you sit properly while you fine-tune your seating position.

title: G70 Parking Assistant
requirement_statement: Improve 'Parking Assistant' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 17 respondents complain and 10 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer noted they really like the self-parking.
Customer commented that he enjoys using the parking assistant, especially when doing parallel parking.
Customer stated he enjoys some of the fun gimmicks on the vehicle, such as its capability to park itself.

Customer stated she was told she can record the way she drives into her garage so the car will later repeat that maneuver automatically. Writer stated to first drive to the desired starting point, then press the Parking Assistant button near the gear selector, then tap the "Record new path" option on the touchscreen, drive the vehicle into her garage, and when the car is stopped press "Save recording". Writer stated that the next time she is close to that starting point, the vehicle will ask if she wants it to automatically follow this recorded path for her.
Customer stated he only recently started using the parking assistant because his parking space is very tight, but so far he realy likes it.
Customer commented that even though the vehicle is quite large, it is still easy to drive and to park. Customer added that the self-parking function is very helpful.

Customer stated she used parking assist twice to pull into her garage and it failed both times, and she believes the garage may be too small. Writer advised the system requires adequate space on each side so it can maneuver safely.
I had a problem with Active parking assistance - DTU: "System wakes up, requests a destination, then fails to carry out the task."
Customer stated the parking assistant is excellent. Customer stated it self parks the vehicle and leaves equal space around all sides of the car.

Customer inquired about using the automatic parking function. Writer advised Customer to start by pressing the parking camera button, and explained that in the upper right portion of the display a searching area appears where the system scans for parking lines along the passenger side while driving slowly through a parking lot. Writer further explained that after the system identifies a space and the vehicle has already passed it, the car verifies the spot is large enough, and the display in that searching area will prompt the driver to choose a maneuver option such as reverse parking or pulling straight in. Customer acknowledged they now understand how to activate and use the parking assist feature.

Customer was confused about what triggers the parking assistant. Writer explained it relies on finding two open spaces between objects instead of reading parking lines. Customer acknowledged they were unaware and said they will remember that.

During an RVG appointment, customer asked how to turn on Automatic Parking for perpendicular spaces. Writer explained that when getting ready to look for a spot, customer should press the parking assistance key on the center console, the one marked with a P and three lines. Customer confirmed the button was located. Writer explained this switches iDrive into the Parking view, where the vehicle begins scanning for suitable spaces. Writer stated the iDrive display will show which spots are detected in the searching area of the screen, and customer will then pick the desired space and parking style. Writer advised that iDrive will then instruct the customer to release the brake pedal so the vehicle can start the self-parking maneuver. Writer added that once the automatic parking is finished, iDrive will show that the procedure has ended and will shift the vehicle into park. Customer acknowledged the explanation.

Customer asked whether the vehicle includes Automatic Parking, and writer confirmed it does. Customer added he has not tried using it yet. Customer stated the light comes on to show it has detected a spot, but he is unsure what to do at that point. Writer explained that once the light appears, shift into reverse, then turn on the turn signal and press and hold the Park Assist button. Writer noted that directions will appear on the iDrive display and advised to keep the button pressed until the maneuver is done. Writer also stated that touching the brake or moving the steering wheel will cancel the process.
Customer stated his driveway is too long to record as a single Maneuver Assistant move. Customer stated he wishes longer maneuvers could be saved.
Customer stated the Genius showed her how to operate the Automatic Parking Assistant, and Customer stated she now really loves using it.

Customer inquired about the best way to operate the parking assistant feature specifically for parallel parking. Writer explained that when the customer is approaching a potential parking spot, they should press the camera button located on the center console so the vehicle can begin searching for an appropriate space. Writer further advised that, once a space is identified and meets the necessary requirements, an option will appear on the right side of the iDrive display. Customer was told to select that option so the vehicle can carry out the automatic parking. Customer acknowledged the instructions.

Customer explained he had stored a path into his garage for the maneuver assistant so that he can get out of the car and complete the parking process from his iPhone. Customer stated that ever since saving this route, the vehicle will notify him when he reaches the activation point, but the alert will not stop once it has started. Customer stated the gong keeps sounding repeatedly until he has driven roughly 2 miles and is well past the activation point. Writer asked if this occurs every time and customer confirmed it does. Customer also stated there is no way to remove any recorded paths from the menu. Writer asked if he can see the stored paths in the parking assistant, and customer said yes, but when he selects one there is no option to delete it. Writer asked whether the camera view stays on while driving or if only the alert continues. Customer stated that the display switches off once he reaches a certain speed and returns to the main iDrive screen, but the gong alert keeps going. Customer stated he has already updated apps and services in the vehicle and performed an iDrive reboot, yet the problem remains. Customer stated he intends to drop the vehicle off with service at the end of this week. Writer arranged a follow up call. Customer stated the vehicle has about 210 miles on it. Writer called again to check on the repair status, but the customer did not answer. No DCS or AIR Notes.
Customer said they have not tested the recording path function yet, but intend to try it on their driveway and are a bit anxious about how it will manage getting into the garage.
Customer reported that the Parking Assistant is his top feature on this car.

Customer reported that while using the parking assistant the vehicle came to a very sudden stop as it pulled into a space, and he briefly thought it had hit the wall, but it had not. Writer explained that the vehicle is equipped with PDC sensors which assist it in maneuvering into a parking spot. Customer acknowledged this information.
Customer advised that she appreciates having many different options now for parking the vehicle.
Customer stated they are very pleased with the self-parking feature and make use of it frequently.
I had a minor problem with Active parking assistance - DTU: "it is not easy to precisely choose the exact space where you want the car to park."

I had a minor problem with Active parking assistance - Not working/inaccurate/inconsistent: "At times, when I return to a parking spot that was already saved, the auto-park option does not show up. For the same location at night, it acts like it needs a new option created, as if the saved setting was dropped and I had to set it up again."

Customer stated he still has not figured out the self parking feature on the vehicle. Writer explained how to operate the feature, including how it detects spaces and that he should use the P button to search for them.

Customer asked how to use parking assistant. Writer explained to slowly drive past parked cars until the vehicle indicates a suitable spot, then select it and the car will automatically park. Customer acknowledged.

Customer stated the person who originally went over the car with him never pointed out the self-parking feature. Customer stated that recently he pulled up next to a spot to parallel park and suddenly a prompt appeared asking if he wanted the car to park on its own. Customer asked whether this is a comfortable system to rely on and whether it is straightforward to use. Writer explained the operation of the parking assistants and how to use them.

evidence.quote: i would really have liked the option of a manual gearbox, and that would have pushed my rating higher, but as with many brands it seems bmw no longer offers this to buyers. overall the car is great fun to drive when you are not manoeuvring. a few small niggles: still no intermittent setting for the windscreen wipers when they are not in auto mode; the driver seatbelt cannot be adjusted for height so i am always fiddling with it while driving; the driver seat could go lower to give extra headroom when getting in; software updates wipe out settings, especially autohold being turned on. before purchase i would have appreciated a brochure clearly listing the equipment on each model so i could compare, and when reading the handbook, to know whether my car is supposed to have a given feature. also, comfort access does not include foot boot opening even though it was shown in the app before delivery.

overall i'm satisfied with the car and it stacks up well against the different 3 series models i've owned before. i'm generally very pleased with the tech, but it still feels like it needs some fine tuning. three times the tailgate has suddenly closed by itself while either my wife or i were standing behind the car, and on one occasion the locking catch actually hit me on the head. there have also been occasions where the car has locked with me standing right next to it. another problem is with the warnings: i keep getting a message saying the rear right light cluster has failed, even though it is actually working. my bmw dealer is looking into this and i'm waiting for spare parts - all of this on a new car.

as a small car it is excellent overall. plenty of space, comfortable and quick off the mark, with very smooth pull through the gears and really strong grip and cornering behaviour. the keyless boot release can be a bit unreliable. the digital key setup can also be frustrating at times: with my iphone and apple watch the car unlocks as i walk up, but if i open the boot to load it, by the time i've shut it and gone round to the driver door it has locked again and i need to stand for a moment until it opens. the mirrors do not always fold when locking, and the instrument cluster sometimes drops my personal layout. aside from those small digital issues, everything else is perfect.

there are a couple of things i feel i am missing with the car.....a button inside to shut the boot would be ideal, i was honestly shocked that there isn't one. i'd also really like a proper paper handbook, even if it seems old fashioned, because there is so much tech that i'm sure lots of us never really use properly. i dont really know what connected drive actually is, i've just been told it needs renewing soon and right now it just appears like something that will end up costing me more. it would help to have someone explain what happens if i exceed the mileage allowance under the pcp agreement. like most people, i had more questions once i got the car home.....i do think the after sales support, preferably via email, has been very good considering what the car costs, even with everything i've mentioned the car itself is fine. hope this is of use.

i'm very pleased with my new car overall. it fits what i need and comes with lots of extra features. the performance is excellent and i really like the interior and all the functions. my favourite bits are the heated seats, the heated steering wheel, the different drive modes and being able to personalise things like the ambient lighting. the parking camera works really well, and there were plenty of choices when buying it new. on the downside, i would have rated it even higher. i paid extra to have an electric boot fitted. the car has only done around 500 miles, and i don't think i'd actually used the electric boot up to that point. i walked up to the car, pressed the boot open button on the key, and there was nothing around me, then i heard a loud bang. when i checked, the parcel shelf clearly hadn't been fitted properly, had come loose while driving, got wedged, and the auto boot mechanism snapped the clips. i took it back to the dealer, but they couldn't assist, only telling me it would be £280 to get a new parcel shelf. #really

it might not just be this particular car, but there are several points where i do not recomend bmw.

the door locking and unlocking works inconsistently, sometimes it responds and sometimes it doesn't. the tailgate kick opening is almost useless. radio reception on the highway basically doesn't happen, which support has confirmed and is very disappointing. the auto-cruise has stopped functioning while on the move. when i downshift with the paddles, the delay before engine braking comes in is far too long, and the emblem is almost pointless. the auto brake hold can't be turned on and off with a single touch. the engine start feature is treated as a subscription. the usb is only good for charging. the auto wipers don't activate at sensible times. the paid digital premium content feels very poor. the bmw app has failed to pick up driving data three times in the roughly three months since buying the car; i force a reset every time but it never fixes the root cause.
other
it was delivered about 2 months later than the original date, with no progress updates. the way the dealer handles things is no different from japanese car dealers apart from the look of the building and the drinks, and the actual service is weak for an expensive car purchase.

Customer called asking what steps to follow when a Remote Software update appears. Customer mentioned seeing the notification both in the My BMW App and in the car, and was unsure how to handle it or confirm it went through correctly. Writer explained that once the message shows up, it first has to be downloaded, and asked which option the customer had used. Customer replied he did the update through the My BMW App. Writer clarified that the update in the app must download from the app to the phone, and after that it will upload to the vehicle using wifi. Customer then asked if the vehicle itself needed to be connected to something for this, and writer advised that it does not. Writer stated the phone must be connected to a wifi network, not using mobile data, in order to upload the update to the car. Customer indicated he understood. Writer further explained there are certain preconditions that must be satisfied or the Remote Software Upgrade will not complete properly. Writer went over that the customer needs to make sure the download is finished, the vehicle is not on an incline, is in park, and the engine is switched off. Customer confirmed all of those were true and that the Remote Software Upgrade had already been completed successfully, and said he had only been curious about the process.

Customer asked if the My BMW App would alert him when a new remote software update is available. Writer advised that he would receive a notification there and also see it in the vehicle. Writer explained that if it appears in the app, he should download it to his phone first and then transfer it to the vehicle to install. Customer acknowledged.

I had a serious problem with Over-the-air vehicle software update problem: "i had to bring the car to the dealer for an update, since i never got any OTA update notification.". Which problem with RSU?: Other

Customer inquired about RSU and how they would be notified of them. Writer advised that both the vehicle itself and the myBMW app will alert them when an RSU becomes available. Writer advised that the driver can choose to install the update through their mobile device and then sync it to the vehicle later, or they can perform the installation directly in the vehicle, which takes roughly 20 minutes.

with this purchase i had very high expectations of the bmw brand. choosing the 530i online edition through bmw financial lease was something i thought would make us into long-term brand customers, not just one-time consumers. right now though, i am facing serious inconvenience when using android auto. we keep having the same problem where music will not play correctly when starting tmap or other navigation apps, and it is not a random glitch but a recurring, structural issue. this is clearly not just my own case either. the same complaints are constantly coming up in major communities, such as a large online cafe called 'bmw driver club' (around 650,000 members), and even though many users are reporting the same inconvenience, bmw has provided no official explanation of the cause, no plan for improvement, and no proper guidance for customers. the issue itself matters, but the way bmw is handling it feels even more disappointing. these customer inconveniences have been building up for a long time, and i think the lack of active response and communication is something that can really damage trust in a premium brand. in my view, a premium brand is defined not only by how complete its products are, but also by how it reacts when problems come up. in the present situation, trust in the brand is inevitably shaken, even if the vehicle itself is satisfying. i feel that a clear analysis of the cause, a concrete improvement plan, and formal guidance to customers are absolutely needed. instead of treating it as just a minor technical error, i strongly ask for a proactive response that looks at the whole customer experience. my survey score here is not only showing dissatisfaction, but also my expectation that bmw will improve. i hope this point is considered very carefully.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

Customer stated the Climate Control in this model works differently than in earlier cars, but is easy to get used to. Customer stated she appreciates having the Climate Control settings accessible through the touchscreen.

Customer stated the climate controls are a bit hard to use since he is so used to having real buttons. Writer advised that with time he should adjust to using the touchscreen, and the customer agreed.

Customer stated they like to have the air conditioning set to a cool temperature while running the seat heating with the massage on, and they cannot manage this easily in this vehicle without a lot of fiddling. Customer stated that in their prior 7 series this was very simple because the seat settings were not tied into the climate controls. Now they have to push the seat heat to a very high level to get it to come on, but then it is too hot, and in manual mode they find themselves constantly changing the fan and then the temperature, which is all too much for them. Customer stated this feels like a downgrade and a loss of a feature compared to their previous vehicle.

Customer asked how to adjust the passenger-side air flow direction.
Writer explained that the ventilation is managed via the slider located beneath the control panel.
Writer also recommended using the IPA to handle climate control settings.
Customer stated he strongly prefers having physical tactile buttons instead of touchscreen controls, specifically wanting knobs and levers for adjusting the temperature.

Customer asked if the car had a setting so the fan would first go to maximum by itself and then reduce the speed automatically. Writer explained that in the climate menu the customer can choose Auto to activate that function.
Customer reported he appreciates having the climate controls all grouped on the iDrive Control Display, rather than a bunch of separate physical buttons spreading across and cluttering the dashboard.

title: G70 Charge high-voltage battery
requirement_statement: Improve 'Charge high-voltage battery' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated they remembered being told in the past that batteries should be run down quite low before charging again and asked if that was still necessary. Writer explained that the vehicle uses a battery pack made up of many cells and advised that charging to the recommended 80% allows the system to balance the charge across all cells efficiently, so the customer does not need to worry about discharging it low first.

Customer asked if BMW has any specific charging guidelines compared with her Tesla, explaining she mainly wants to preserve the Battery's life. Writer advised that BMW recommends keeping the Battery level between about 10% and 80% and avoiding regular charges to 100%. Writer added she can charge to 100% when necessary, just not every time. Customer acknowledged this information.
Customer stated he appreciates that he can charge this vehicle at home using his own solar panels.

Customer stated they are unhappy with the present charging speeds when using public charging stations for both their i7 and iX vehicles. Customer mentioned they know about the recent announcement regarding access to the Tesla Supercharger network and intend to try that option.

Customer stated he has a regular one way drive of about 190 miles, and has to stop to charge one or two times, losing roughly 20-30 minutes per session. Customer stated he can always earn more money but he cannot gain back time, and he does this trip every month. Customer stated the car tops out at 190 watts of power and asked if it could go higher. Writer advised he should be able to open the apps menu, then charging, then ac limit, and there adjust the current limit. Customer stated that setting was already at its maximum. Writer checked and noted this vehicle is limited to 195 kw, and relayed that to the customer. Customer acknowledged this and thanked the writer.

Customer mentioned it is simple to come home each day and just plug the car in to charge. Customer mentioned he usually lets it charge overnight to about 80%, and with that he is set for roughly a week.

it is a nice car but charging the battery is a major downside. when i see tessaro charging stations it makes me feel like my car is junk. for what i paid, i should have a much better charging setup. our charging stations are totally mickey mouse compared to theirs. i usually wait well over half an hour just in line, and then about another 30 minutes to actually charge. around half the time the charging speed is slowed down due to maintenance. it is a huge hassle. i will tell everyone i know that i hate this car, and i want to return it if that is possible.

Customer asked whether the seat massage function is supplied by the high-voltage battery. Writer confirmed that both the seat comfort features and the climate control draw power from the high-voltage battery.
Customer stated he is still getting used to the idea of charging this BEV instead of filling up a fuel tank at a gas station.

Customer inquired about the charging duration for the car. Writer explained it may take about 12 hours for a full charge, or roughly 3-4 hours on a level 2 charger. Customer said he asked because it seemed like the vehicle was taking a long time to charge.

Customer asked whether he is supposed to limit charging to 80 percent. Writer confirmed that this is correct. Writer explained that charging only up to 80 percent helps the battery function better over a longer period of time.

Customer stated he was unsure how the electric motor charges on longer drives and thought the battery would automatically fully recharge. Writer explained that only a small amount of charging happens during braking and coasting, giving just a few miles of range, and that a full charge requires plugging in. Customer stated he had seen that he might gain a couple of miles which then drop again and thanked the writer for explaining this is normal. Customer asked if it is okay to leave the car overnight without charging. Writer advised that this is fine, but noted the preconditioning feature will not operate without charge.

Customer stated he would prefer a shorter charging time, as right now it takes around 10 to 11 hours to fully charge the battery with a 220-volt charger installed at his home a few years ago for electric vehicles. Customer stated he assumed using 220 volts would result in a much quicker charge. Customer mentioned his wife used to have a fully electric Mercedes that needed about 11 to 12 hours to charge, and he is seeing similar charging duration now despite having a much smaller range.

right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings

on top of that, ota software updates arrive very late, which is disappointing versus other luxury makers. more timely updates would really help the overall ownership experience.

right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

title: G60 Digital Key
requirement_statement: Improve 'Digital Key' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 15 respondents complain and 13 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the dealer representative told them they would not need the key fob once the phone was set up with the app and digital key. Customer explained that on one occasion they went to the garage with the key fob left upstairs and were unable to unlock the car using the app. Customer expressed concern about potentially being stuck in a shopping center parking lot if they relied on not bringing the key fob and then could not unlock the vehicle. Customer stated the digital key works inconsistently and, although it has worked at times, they expect it to function every time. Customer mentioned they still carry the key fob because they do not trust the digital key fully, and that the wallet version of the key is less reliable than the app. Writer explained that Samsung Wallet or Apple Wallet may require an authentication step before the key is active, which can lead to inconsistent operation. Writer recommended using the key fob as a backup. Writer explained that if the vehicle is in sleep or standby mode, it may need to be awakened by holding the phone near the door handle. Writer acknowledged the customer wants the digital key to behave like the key fob, unlocking on approach and locking when walking away with complete reliability. Writer confirmed this feedback would be documented.
Customer mentioned his nephew showed him the digital key that lets him use his phone as a key, but he did not have both key fobs with him at that moment. Customer said he thinks that is very cool.

Customer asked how the car detects the Digital Key Card, Digital Key Plus, and the key fob, and which one is prioritized. Writer advised that the Digital Key Plus ultra wideband signal is recognized first, while the Digital Key Card uses Near Field Communication with a range of roughly 1-2 cm.
Customer stated he has the new digital key and feels it is pretty cool.
Customer stated they are pleased with the digital key plus.

Customer explained she brought the car to a car wash and left her phone inside, since taking the phone out makes the doors lock. Customer stated she got out of the car, then the car wash attendant got in, stepped on the brake, and the car turned off. Customer mentioned she changed over to the service card and that setup worked. Customer commented she now knows she needs to switch to the valet key when she gets out before letting someone else drive it, and once the car wash is finished she gets back in and turns her own setting back on.
Customer stated their phone-as-key feature is very useful.

Customer stated he would like to be able to have two phones set up as car keys, because when he is driving his wife's phone ends up overriding his own settings. Writer explained that the main digital key owner can share it, even though she is on iPhone and he is on android. Writer advised she should open Apple Wallet, tap the three dots, select share, and then follow the prompts. Customer stated they will review this.

Customer stated her dealership provided a credit card-style item with the vehicle and asked what its purpose was. Writer explained this is a digital key card that functions like the digital key on a phone. Writer advised that it needs initial activation and that placing the card in the mobile device tray will prompt an activation request on the touchscreen. Customer indicated she understood.
Customer stated he appreciates being able to use the digital key and that he does not have to carry a physical key for the vehicle.

Customer stated he did not understand what the BMW Card he received is used for. Writer explained the card serves as an additional key for the vehicle, another method to access the vehicle if necessary. Customer acknowledged.
Customer stated she really likes that she does not need to bring a physical key anymore since she uses the Digital Key on her phone.
Customer stated they use the digital key via Apple Wallet and are pleased with how it works.

Customer reported that he exclusively uses the Digital Key for this vehicle. Customer stated that if he unlocks the car and then sits inside for several minutes without pressing the "Start" button, the vehicle appears to time out and powers down completely. Customer stated that at that point he needs to open and close the door again for the car to detect that he is inside, and then he can start the vehicle as usual. Customer commented that it would be better if the display stayed on longer after he enters the car, before he hits the "Start" button.

Customer asked about the purpose of the Digital Key Card. Writer stated it can be used instead of the key fob. Writer stated that holding the card to the door handle will lock or unlock the vehicle. Writer stated to place the card in the tray, press the brake, then press the Start/Stop button.
Customer stated that they appreciate being able to use their phone as a key.

every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

evidence.quote: Customer stated the Highway Assistant tends to be somewhat jerky when going through a bend, particularly in situations where the vehicle has to reduce speed before entering the corner.

Customer remarked they are very happy with the self driving function. Customer noted they drive to work four days a week and spend a lot of time on highways and longer trips, so the feature is very helpful for them.

Customer reported that at first the hands-free Driver Assist Plus feature would not operate, even though the standard driver assist continued to function reliably. Customer then noted that the hands-free feature began working on its own without any software updates. Writer explained that the feature only works on controlled access freeways and confirmed that it is currently operating properly.
Customer stated he really likes the highway assist feature and said it works great for his long commute to work.
Customer stated he tested the hands-free driving on the highway and found it very relaxing. Customer said it helped him feel comfortable in the vehicle for a few minutes.
Customer mentioned that he is pleased with the highway assistant feature.
Customer commented that the self-driving feature is absolutely unbelievable.

Customer reported trouble with the Driving Assist Plus, mainly the attention camera. Customer said the steering wheel was adjusted too low so the camera could not see their eyes, which turned the feature off. Customer found in the owners manual that wheel height impacts the camera and solved it by moving the wheel higher.
Customer stated the auto drive feature on the freeway is fantastic and expressed strong appreciation for the automated driving functions during highway trips.
Customer stated they enjoy the updated self-driving that is totally hands off and commented that it is really cool.

Customer reported that Highway Assistant does not behave well when coming up to an exit while in the carpool lane. Customer explained he feels the system gets mixed up by the carpool lane lines compared to the regular lane markings and the car tries to move over into the normal lanes. Customer indicated he typically grabs the steering wheel himself when he is exiting the carpool lane.
Customer stated he needed help with autonomous driving mode and settings. Writer walked him through the instructions.
Customer stated the Highway Assistant, which lets him use semi-autonomous driving up to 85 mph, is state of the art and stated he uses it daily on the highway.
Customer stated when Highway assistant shows ready, they were unsure if they needed to do anything else or if it meant it was active. Wrtier confirmed that ready means it is ready to use.
Customer reported that he is pleased with the driver's assistant systems in the vehicle, and noted in particular that he especially appreciates the self drive function.

Customer stated they used to drive a Model Y, and the main thing they really appreciate on the i5 is driving assist plus, which they feel is more accurate than autopilot. Customer stated they feel safer using it in this vehicle than in the Tesla because of glitches they experienced with the Tesla, and they feel more safe and confident in this system.
Customer stated they really love using the highway assistant.
Customer commented that he would like the highway assistant to function while wearing polarized sunglasses.
Customer stated that the highway assistance feature has worked very well for him.
Customer mentioned the self driving feature works really well.
Customer stated the hands-off function performs better than on their 3 Series, with higher speed capability.

Customer reported using the highway assistant quite a lot due to regularly driving long-distance trips and confirmed it has been very convenient. Customer mentioned this is one of their favorite features and it is used on a daily basis.
Customer stated he is very happy with the automatic cruise control.
Customer stated likes that Highway Assistant is included as a feature in the vehicle.
Customer mentioned she enjoys using the assisted driving function.

Customer stated that the automated driving feature on the highway is new to him but very nice to have. Customer stated he is experiencing this technology for the first time and considers it a valuable feature for highway trips.

Customer stated his only complaint with the Highway assistant is the driver distraction detected warning, which he feels is overly touchy and sensitive. Customer stated that even when he is staring straight ahead at the road it will sometimes pop up, and if he glances for a moment at the rearview mirror or the side view mirror it comes on, which he finds annoying. Customer stated the system is too sensitive.
Customer stated the highway assistant is sometimes hard to work with, as it keeps warning that his eyes are off the road even when he is actually looking ahead.
Customer stated he values the hands free driving function since he regularly travels on the highway for his job.
Customer stated he really enjoys the automatic lane change feature with the highway assistant.

Customer stated Assisted Driving Plus was functioning well during the first few weeks of ownership on highway trips, but then suddenly became unavailable on the same routes under similar conditions. Customer stated this change occurred after an RSU. Writer guided the customer through a system reboot and checked the settings. System settings were reset and the customer will try the feature again on the next highway drive. Writer advised visiting the dealership if the problem remains.

Customer stated the vehicle allows hands free driving on the interstate up to around 80 or 85 miles per hour, but it still flashes for the driver to take the wheel after the hands have been off for a certain time. Customer asked if this is how it is supposed to work and mentioned his wife noticed the same thing when driving on the interstate between two nearby cities. Customer noted his wife does not like to leave her hands off the steering wheel. Writer provided information on the highway assistant and advised that the vehicle will periodically require the steering wheel to be held.
Customer stated the primary reason for buying the car was the Driver Assistance Professional with hands-free self-driving, and overall it has worked very well and met the needed expectations.

Customer expressed confusion about the highway assistant and questioned how useful the self-driving function is when it demands constant attention and issues warnings or disengages if the driver looks at their phone. Customer said they would prefer more autonomous behavior that lets them look away from the road. Writer clarified that highway assistant is meant as a driver aid rather than full self-driving and confirmed it still requires the driver to keep eyes on the road for safety.
Customer reported their first use of highway-assisted driving was a positive experience.

Customer stated they had trouble fully understanding the two-level adaptive driving system. Writer went over what the first level does and then explained the second level highway assistant functions. Customer also mentioned confusion about how the system follows speed limits in adaptive mode. Writer explained how the speed is ajusted in that mode.

Customer stated the vehicle should be capable of more autonomous functions and hopes BMW will develop it so it can stop at traffic lights and make turns at intersections, since the car can already detect the lights, show a red light status on the screen, and read road signs, so he feels the technology is already in place.
Customer stated that Highway Assistant can take a while to toggle on and start working at times when he wants to engage it or switch it on quickly.

Customer stated the interior becomes extremely hot after the vehicle sits in the sun for roughly 10 minutes. Customer reported the cabin temperature reaches around 110 degrees and that the dashboard gets hot enough to burn when touched. Customer stated this level of heat is higher than in any other car brand they have owned. Customer mentioned they do not live in a desert climate and expressed worry about how the vehicle might perform in even hotter regions. Customer acknowledged this suggests the interior is tightly insulated and sealed, but stated the severity of the heat buildup is unacceptable for a vehicle costing about 75000 dollars. Customer further stated they believe this is not a one-off case and that all vehicles of this model likely experience the same issue.
Customer commented that the interior color is fantastic, specifically the BMW Individual leather 'Merino' Copper Brown/Atlas Grey.
Customer stated he was accustomed to having more leather inside the cabin, and that in this vehicle the interior feels more like plastic to him.
Customer stated they like the vehicle's interior and specifically mentioned enjoying the design and layout of the dash.
Customer stated he likes the interior design, specifically because of the veganza.
Customer stated he appreciates the refreshed layout compared to his earlier BMW models.
Customer stated the color combo looks great, specifically the Black Perforated Veganza.
Customer stated he really prefers the interior design on this vehicle, especially when he compares it to the electric cars he owned before.
Customer stated the interior design and overall layout are very appealing and that they prefer it over the Audi they had before.

Customer stated the interior materials do not feel quite as nice compared to his previous M340i and M440i Grand Coupe, and commented that BMW seems to be undergoing a major transition in both styling and material quality. Customer noted that visible stitching is disappearing everywhere, and although the doors and dashboard are padded, there is no stitching, which makes the interior appear very plain and minimalistic. Customer further stated there is far too much piano black used throughout the interior and exterior, and mentioned that it easily shows fingerprints, dust, and scratches.
Customer stated that the overall setup of the vehicle is very appealing.
Customer stated the interior of the car is very beautiful.
Customer stated he likes the interior design and feels it has a cool look.
Customer stated he would prefer a different finish for the interior materials, as the current glossy surface keeps noticeable fingerprints anywhere he touches it.
Customer stated that they really like the mocha brown/chocolate interior combined with the black accent pieces.

Customer commented that she loves the overall interior look and feels the whole package fits together nicely. Customer stated the ambient lights are less bothersome than in her previous 2023 5 series because they do not create the same light reflections in the windows at night.
Customer stated the interior feels more luxurious compared to his last BMW.
Customer stated his wife specifically requested a white exterior with a matching white interior.

Customer stated the interior looks gorgeous, specifically the Smoke White. Customer stated the standard interior quality on both 2026 models is greatly improved. Customer stated he has always selected the luxury interior upgrade on his past BMWs, but with the 530i he did not feel it was necessary because the standard interior is already beautiful.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function.

in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate.

the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues.

i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix.

2. homelink garage door opener
the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then.

most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.
