bmw support feels weak. the car is pretty new in terms of electronic car evolution, so maybe bmw does not yet predict the problems customers run into. i put in a wall box (over $600) and, using bmw's instructions, the wall box would not work. it turned out the instructions were wrong, and a very experienced electrician had to come back and spend more than three hours on the phone with the bmw dealership, who at first had no idea how to fix it and basically guessed for three hours. that extra visit cost me another $250, which is ridiculous.

the manual is massive in length and still not helpful.

overall i feel like i bought an electronic vehicle from bmw a few years too early; my friends with an electric mercedes and a tesla don't face these kinds of issues.

evidence.quote: Customer stated that at times when he gets out of the car the radio keeps playing. Writer advised this can occur if it is still connected to his phone, then walked him through iDrive to apps, vehicle, doors and windows, lock and unlock, to choose the option for the car to power down after the door is opened. Writer also advised that once parked with the engine off, if the customer unfastens the seatbelt before opening the door it should shut everything off, and if it is still playing he can hold the volume button in for about 3 seconds to turn all electronics off. Customer stated he was not aware of this and thanked the writer.

Customer inquired about having the radio shut off after turning off the engine. Writer outlined the steps for the automatic idle state feature: go to the apps menu, then vehicle apps, then doors and windows, then lock/unlock, and select turn off after opening door. Customer acknowledged the guidance.

Customer stated the radio keeps playing after the vehicle is switched off, even though the door setting is set to turn everything off on exit. Writer advised that idle mode can be disabled by holding the volume button for about 5 seconds and noted that any weight on the seats makes the car think a passenger is still inside. Customer acknowledged.

Customer stated that after turning the engine off and walking away, his phone would remain connected to the vehicle and he could not use siri normally. He figured out that locking the vehicle makes the operating system shut down so his phone disconnects. Writer advised that this is one solution, and that the customer can also go to Doors and Windows, Unlock/Lock, and toggle on turn off after opening door so the vehicle powers everything down once a door is opened. Writer further advised that if there is a passenger in the front seat, the passenger also needs to open their door for everything to turn off. Customer acknowledged.

Customer mentioned she feels like she must be doing something wrong whenever she gets out of the car. Customer said that if she has a passenger and wants to keep the vehicle running for their comfort, the car switches itself off anyway. Customer said she plans to go back to her Genius to learn how to stop this from happening. Writer explained she is not doing anything incorrectly. Writer explained this is a built-in safety function. Writer noted that when the driver unbuckles the seat belt and opens the driver door, the vehicle will power down automatically. Writer noted this is intended to stop the car from rolling over someone and also works as an anti-theft measure. Writer advised that if she wants to leave someone inside and keep them comfortable, she should activate preconditioning when she exits, which keeps the cabin comfortable for around 15 minutes. Writer clarified that preconditioning keeps the interior pleasant but does not leave the vehicle in a driver ready state.
Customer mentioned he is pleased with the automatic idle state feature because the radio turns itself off once the doors are opened.

Customer stated that when they switch the car off, the radio does not immediately shut down and only turns off after the vehicle has been off for a while, and commented there should be a way for the radio to power down as soon as the car is turned off. Customer acknowledged this was a bit of nitpicking. Writer explained there is a setting in the doors and windows menu under the unlock and lock section, and directed Customer to open that menu while in the car. Writer noted the option is located all the way at the bottom and that, when enabled, everything will turn off when the driver door is opened. Writer suggested activating this feature would probably make Customer very satisfied. Customer expressed appreciation for having something new to play with later and remarked that this was fantastic.

Customer stated he would prefer the vehicle to remain on after opening the door like his Tesla Model 3 did. Customer stated the Tesla stayed on about 10-15 minutes without pressing the start stop button so he could get out, grab something, and keep the air conditioning going.

Customer reported that at times the radio remains on even after opening the door. Writer instructed the Customer to enable the automatic idle state, with the following path: apps menu, vehicle apps, doors and windows, lock/unlock, then select turn off after opening door. Customer confirmed understanding.

Customer stated he does not like that the vehicle powers down shortly after opening the door and would prefer it to stay on when stepping out quickly. Writer advised that using sports mode stops this from occurring. Customer stated he already knows about that option.

Customer stated that when she closes the door and walks away from the car, the music keeps playing for a while and the light strip inside stays on as well. Writer explained that this is the auxiliary resting state and that the vehicle will keep the audio running for roughly 15 minutes before it switches off. Customer acknowledged this information.

Customer stated he is unsure how to keep the engine running when he steps out to collect his mail. Writer advised there is no direct way to leave it running while exiting. Writer stated that switching the vehicle to Sport Mode should keep the engine on while stopped, and also recommended disabling the "Turn off vehicle after opening door" setting in the Apps menu under Doors/Windows.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

the car is fantastic for comfort and road handling. there are a couple of things that need attention: the tow cover pops off too easily and then i end up having to buy another one, which is not what i expect after paying over $130k for this car. when the flat screen is lowered i have to rely only on the side mirrors, and i feel a rear camera would be a better solution. also, when the rear window screen is down you cant see through it, so again you are forced to use the side mirrors. there is a lot of technology in this vehicle and i just hope it is built to last for many miles and years.

car is overall very good but there are a few things that really need work. the air conditioning feels weak and you can't aim it right at one person. the charger setup is awful and charging takes way too long. i do like the "hey bmw" function, but when you have to say the same command 3 times it becomes frustrating. you're not able to close the trunk with a button from inside, even though there are all kinds of ways to close the doors, which doesn't make sense. the tv screen that drops down in back completely blocks the driver's view. they should let the rearview mirror switch to a camera image so you can still see behind. the car ought to start out in efficient mode instead of one that burns more miles. the seat heating doesn't get really warm and the cooling is also weak. the moon roof lights are tied to the lights on the side panels and can't be separated, and it should be possible to mix those colors.

Customer questioned how to prevent the passenger side mirror from tilting downward in reverse. Via RVG writer stated to tap the button for the driver's side exterior mirror. Writer stated that once that button is illuminated, the passenger side will not tilt. Writer confirmed the driver side mirror does not tilt.

Customer indicated she would like the exterior mirrors to fold in when the vehicle is locked. Writer explained to go into the Apps Menu, choose Doors and Windows, then Lock/Unlock, and turn on "Fold mirrors on lock/unlock". Customer followed these steps and was able to activate the feature.

Customer reported receiving 'mirror is not recognized' messages while driving, especially when changing lanes. Customer stated this behavior began after a recent software update and was not present beforehand. Writer advised performing an iDrive refresh. Writer also indicated they will follow up on Monday so the customer has time to drive the vehicle and determine whether the reset resolved the concern.

Customer stated the exterior rearview mirrors look as though water is leaking into or behind the mirror assemblies. Customer noted he has already contacted the dealer about this. Customer said he plans to take the vehicle to the dealer for diagnosis after the holidays. Writer requested RVG or mirror photos, but the customer did not have the vehicle available to provide them.
Customer stated he likes that the side mirrors can fold in so they are less likely to be hit or damaged.

Customer stated that when he took delivery he noticed the driver side exterior mirror looks like it has a heavy film over it. Customer stated he already mentioned this to his salesperson, but the car has not gone into service yet to have that mirror replaced. Customer stated the mirror looks like it needs to defrost, almost like there is condensation on the glass, and at night it becomes really hard to see anything in that mirror. Writer asked if he was by the vehicle so pictures could be captured with RVG. Customer stated he is not with the car right now and will not be for a few days due to driving a truck for a living. Writer advised he will send an email and asked the customer to respond with some photos of the mirror.{

i am happy with the new car. it is clearly more comfortable and in general more interesting than the older series i had. still, there are some drawbacks i really cannot ignore: - once the speed goes past about 110-120 km/h, the car is not well insulated anymore, wind noise becomes obvious and disturbing even though it has the special package. - at night, the driver's main rearview mirror gives a blurry picture, lights from cars behind and strong light sources look smeared, vertical lines show up and this makes driving harder. - the air conditioning will not run when the ignition is switched off. - there is no way to turn off the lights while the car is on (for example if you just want the ac working in a parking lot). - every single time you start driving you have to switch on the battery conservation function again. - the driver has no glove compartment now. before it was located to the left of the steering wheel. there is also no smaller extra glovebox like on the f01. - the driver's joystick/control stick feels very rigid when choosing left/right/up/down. - the driver's seat fails to go back to where it was before the car was shut down. - the cup holders do not offer cooling or heating at all.

title: G70 Manage / pair mobile device (Bluetooth)
requirement_statement: Improve 'Manage / pair mobile device (Bluetooth)' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: I had a minor problem with Built-in Bluetooth system - Frequent pairing/connectivity issues: "Display shows a message saying the blue tooth is outdated". Describe Bluetooth Problem: Won't find/authorize my mobile phone/device

Customer mentioned she would like the audio to start playing again when a call is made private and moved to her phone, so passengers are not left in silence. Customer noted her Chrysler Pacifica manages this perfectly.
Customer reports that their Samsung phone has trouble establishing a connection with the vehicle's interface.

I had a very minor problem with Built-in Bluetooth system - Frequent pairing/connectivity issues: "Every so often the eSim starts trying to connect and then the bluetooth acts up so I have to manually reset the display controls."

Customer explained they want to place calls with voice commands by saying hey BMW call and then a contact name, but the system is not picking up those contact names. Customer said they can only make calls by manually entering the phone number, and when trying commands like call Laura Mobile the system could not finish the request. Writer asked whether Apple CarPlay or Android Auto was in use, and customer replied they have an iPhone but were not using CarPlay, only the built-in BMW system. Writer advised removing and reconnecting the device and checking that all permissions are granted. Customer reported that the calling function was working again afterward.

Customer stated his Bluetooth shut off and then would not reconnect for a few days. Customer stated he removed his phone from the system and paired it back, and it has worked fine since. Writer confirmed the phone is an iPhone 14 Pro with Verizon and software version 16.3. Writer suggested updating iOS, rebooting the phone fully, un-pairing the phone and deleting it from iDrive before re-pairing, rebooting iDrive by holding the radio power button for 30 seconds, and visiting the dealership.

Customer stated there was a technology problem with the phone connecting soon after they took delivery. Customer explained the phone paired at first but then disconnected and they were unable to get it to connect again. Customer mentioned they happened to be close to the dealership when this occurred. Writer confirmed the phone was not connecting. Customer stated the dealership went into the system and programmed what had to be programmed. Customer explained it was something in the system they were not familiar with and could not provide any further details.

I had a very minor problem with Built-in Bluetooth system - Frequent pairing/connectivity issues: "every so often the Bluetooth wont see my phone, and I have to run through pairing again to get it connected". Describe Bluetooth Problem: Won't find/authorize my mobile phone/device

Customer reported he has not been able to get Bluetooth to connect correctly and feels there could be an issue with it. Writer advised that if it seems to be a mechanical problem, he should reach out to the dealer for assistance.
Customer states the audio volume is low when the device is connected through Bluetooth. Writer did not have a chance to follow up because the customer needed to end the call.

the electronics are awful. whenever i switch my phone on or off, i have to redo the bluetooth pairing in the car and spend ages getting the phone to talk to the car again. my phone is fairly new, so this shouldn't be happening on a $140,000 car. my last four cars were two audi a8 models and two s-class mercedes, and i never once had trouble with the phone connection in those.

Customer stated that inbound calls are coming through extremely muffled, so they end up hanging up and calling the person back. Customer noted that call quality on outbound calls is fine. Customer's phone is a Samsung Galaxy S22+ on Android 14 with Verizon. Customer mentioned they are using eSIM, do not use Android Auto, and that the issue has been present since they took delivery. Customer added they are waiting for the dealer to contact them once a loaner vehicle is available.
Customer mentioned they really appreciate being able to have both of their cell phones connected to the car at the same time.

Customer stated the Bluetooth audio is not functioning well. Customer stated that during phone calls the volume is very low. Customer stated he attempted to change the sound levels on both his phone and the vehicle, but the issue remained. Customer stated this is another reason the vehicle is currently in for service. Writer tried to collect phone details, but customer was at work and did not have much time to share information.

Customer stated that when she walks up to the car, her phone will sometimes connect and then disconnect. Customer stated that when she pulls into the driveway, her husband's phone automatically connects to her car even though her settings should give her phone first priority. Customer stated she can hear her husband's phone conversation through her car when he is on a call in the garage using his AirPods.

Customer reported his mobile device was no longer connecting to the system after he had turned off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and it would not reconnect. Customer went out to the vehicle. Writer activated RVG and, using iDrive, advised selecting Home > Menu > Mobile Devices > Driver's preferred phone, then verifying the phone was checked to make calls. Customer found it was unchecked, selected it, and then stated the phone audio was playing through the system.

I had a minor problem with Massaging seat - DTU: "Getting it to massage the exact area you want can take a while."

1) front fascia needs to be improved, i really dont understand how the current front design got signed off by the design and management teams.
2) i have asked several times if i could try out new car tech, see design changes and give feedback on upcoming bmw models, but nobody has ever replied.
3) packaging info should be clearer, rear massaging seats were not obvious. front seats yes, but we only realized the rear seats did not have massage when my family tried them.
4) please add a zone in the front windshield where toll tags and parking garage sensors work properly, basically a blank spot so the readers can detect them.
5) make the front side pillars slimmer so visibility improves. no brand has done this yet, can bmw be the first?
6) mercedes and lucid already offer massaging seats with reclining and bottom sections, bmw might want to match that.
7) for 7 series flagship buyers, offer new ambient interior light patterns every now and then, while still keeping it classy.
8) give me an amazing deal on the 2027 760 when it launches, i am excited for the updated front fascia. otherwise i could be drawn to the refreshed 2027 s class, and the deal has to be mind blowing if you know what i mean.
8) bmw has finessed the air suspension better than the current s class, but they might catch up on power and suspension with their refresh.

I still cannot manage to keep my favorite sirius/xm stations set on the radio, even though send works great. my other 7s had a massage function in the driver seat, but for some reason that feature is gone now, and oddly the salesperson said they had never heard of it.

such a fantastic car, it gives an amazing driving experience every time. it is fully loaded with equipment and has three driving modes; i have not used the economy setting yet, but will do soon as my daily commute mileage is about to increase a lot. for my needs it is ideal, the interior and exterior build quality feel truly top class, backed up by advanced electronics and security systems. the two year service intervals are a real plus, and the my bmw app is excellent. i have only owned it for a couple of months, it has just finished running in and now it is ready for some proper fun. the drive chain and gearbox are incredibly smooth, and the way it grips the road is superb, always giving me confidence on the twisty country lanes where i live. i do still wish the new regulations did not affect the exhaust sound, as i love the noise from the m series, but sadly my car does not have that same exhaust note.

it really is a great car. practical for the whole family, yet quick enough when i want a solo blast. the cabin quality is far ahead of the fast toyotas i have had. fuel economy is excellent, over 40mpg is doable and even with harder driving it stays pretty good. my only gripe, and the reason it did not get 10 stars, is the sound. i would like sport mode to let the exhaust really speak, but it stays too muted. i know eu rules play a part in that, but if i keep it long term i would end up looking at an aftermaket exhaust.

the sensor for unlocking the doors feels too insensitive, and roughly one out of five times the lock wont react even when touching the handle. as soon as you open the door, the audio system powers up. if you step away from the car briefly while the engine is left running, the horn starts blaring, so you basically cant use the ot-lock feature. when setting a navigation destination by voice, only a small number of options is shown and one gets picked automatically, so you are unable to choose from several candidates. with the engine running at night you cant switch on the lights, so i would at least like them to be smaller. the rear gate opener also reacts poorly, probably because that sensor isnt very sensitive either. the remote key needs to be quite close for the doors to lock, the effective distance is short.

overall i am very pleased with my new vehicle. after around three months i am gradually getting used to the technology built into it. there are a few aspects of the idrive options i would prefer to be different. first, i would like the ability to turn off the auto headlights. at the moment the lights can only be switched off while the car is in standby, and once the engine is running the auto lights are active again. there is a control on the lighting stalk but it does not actually disable them. second, there is no way to switch off the front daytime running lights, even though i am sure they could be accessed if needed. third, both the 12v supply (cigar lighter socket) and the usb c charging points stay powered for about 5 minutes after the vehicle is shut down, which keeps my dashcam running and leads to battery discharge.

it might not just be this particular car, but there are several points where i do not recomend bmw.

the door locking and unlocking works inconsistently, sometimes it responds and sometimes it doesn't. the tailgate kick opening is almost useless. radio reception on the highway basically doesn't happen, which support has confirmed and is very disappointing. the auto-cruise has stopped functioning while on the move. when i downshift with the paddles, the delay before engine braking comes in is far too long, and the emblem is almost pointless. the auto brake hold can't be turned on and off with a single touch. the engine start feature is treated as a subscription. the usb is only good for charging. the auto wipers don't activate at sensible times. the paid digital premium content feels very poor. the bmw app has failed to pick up driving data three times in the roughly three months since buying the car; i force a reset every time but it never fixes the root cause.

i'd like to point out a couple of negative things. when reversing uphill from a stop it feels really awkward - the way the throttle responds, with the engine and mild hybrid motor together, seems wrongly tuned at times. it can jump from no power to way too much in a tiny band, which has already led to some near misses and makes me overly cautious when trying to get up over curbs into tight roadside parking spots. coming from a 430i that had the best adaptive cupholders i've used to these ones, which are probably the worst i've had, is just awful. i get that different models have cost savings, but surely cupholders aren't a big expense. with these, any drink that isn't a perfect fit feels like it might tip and spill all over the centre console. really terrible.

i had an f40 m135i before and that car was much better. this f70 feels down on bhp and torque, more like an f40 128ti wearing the wrong badge. it just feels like a regular 1 series and has no real punch to justify the m badge. the exhaust sound is terrible. with no cockpit buttons it is really awkward to change settings while driving and i really do not like that setup. i also got an email saying i must pay for digital premium?? i have no clue what that even includes, and your website makes it hard to figure out, so i am not paying extra. the car turned up with 18" wheels instead of the 19" i ordered, though the dealer did fix that. in my view it should have about 320bhp, 450 torque and the proper bmw sound, and i now wish i had just kept the f40 for another 2 years ??

No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.

the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

I had a very serious problem with Power plug/USB port - Charges too slowly: "when i put the phone on the left charging tray, which is the only one that actually charges, it might go up just 1-5% on an hour drive, or even drop below the starting level, even though the screen keeps saying it is charging. feels ridiculously underpowered."
I had a minor problem with Power plug/USB port - DTU/poorly located: "Putting it inside a shut glove box is stupdi."

I had a problem with Not enough power plugs/USB ports: "my 2021 had additional USB ports that were inside the console. I play music from an iPod and used to keep it tucked inside the console. now it has to plug in outside, so the cord and iPod sit out in the open and clutter up the console space."
Customer stated that when he plays music from a USB and some tracks are quieter, it would be nice if the car could detect that and automatically turn the volume up for those recordings.

Customer stated he had exported his music from his 2015 4 Series onto a thumb drive, but when he plugs that thumb drive into his 2024 5 Series the system reports no audio files found. Writer advised that the original music files need to be copied onto a thumb drive directly. Writer further advised that it is not possible to move the encrypted data from one vehicle to another device.
Customer stated he does not like the USB port being placed beside the cupholders. Customer stated it seems like he could accidentally break off the USB plug.

you can sense the refined build quality that isn't showy, very much in line with bmw overall. there are lots of new functions, and coming over from a g21, i'm quite pleased with the different, supple and soft ride. it's a very good car. on the flip side, one big minus is that the idle stop cancellation function has effectively been removed, even though that feature matters a lot to buyers, and the audio controls feel worse when i use a usb flash drive. that part is really disappointing. in particular, i strongly wish they would update the os so the idle stop cancellation that was available up through id8.0 could be added back in id8.5 as a selectable idle stop cancellation option for each trip.

Customer stated he would prefer additional space to charge her Android phone instead of relying only on the wireless charging pad. Customer stated she and her husband often need to charge at the same time and she wanted another place to plug in, like she can in her other vehicle. Writer advised where the type C ports are located in the center console for charging. Customer acknowledged the explanation.

Customer asked why all of the USB connections are the newer smaller style instead of the regular USB A size, since that is what his older storage devices use. Writer explained that USB C is able to charge more quickly and that most newer phone cables come as USB C. Customer mentioned he had to purchase a converter for his music device.

my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

the car is very comfortable and feels up to date, but i have had way too many issues in a short period. i like the interior styling, yet a lot of the nice features are buried and take forever to access. there really should be simple buttons to open and close all doors. the lower door switch on the driver side is placed horribly, my knee has hit it multiple times and the door has popped open while driving. the fuel door refused to open when i was around 340 miles from home, and bmw roadside told me to just tear it off because they had no other solution. i have also gotten warning lights for the emergency contact system with no cause the dealer could identify. all of this has happened within the 3 months i have owned the car. my 2020 740ix had both keys quit working when i was roughly 70 miles from home, and nobody could explain why. i currently own 3 bmw and lease 2 more, and i am starting to lose faith in your products.

evidence.quote: Customer stated that when saving FM stations, they appear to store the first song that is playing as the station name instead of the station call letters, and that name then stays. Customer stated this has happened on every 7 series he has owned. Customer stated the car also does not reliably resume the last station or even the same media type, like radio presets versus Sirius. Customer stated this often occurs after not using the vehicle for several hours or around a day, and during that span it will start up muted, but when returning from the store it is back on the same station and volume.

Customer inquired about setting preset stations on Sirius XM. Writer provided a link to RVG and, using RVG, advised to tap the Music Menu > Sirius XM, then on the right side select Save to Favorites, and on the left side tap Favorites. Customer was able to set up the radio presets successfully.

Customer stated that if the radio is playing and he tries to place a phone call through the iDrive system, the radio keeps playing while he is speaking to the Voice Assistant and stays on until the other person answers. Customer stated this is annoying and he wants the radio to switch off while he is attempting to make a phone call.

the auto time zone adjustment just does not function. the radio also fails to quiet when i give carplay voice commands. with a 291 mile range, the actual distance i can use is heavily cut because i only charge between 20% and 80%. right now the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available. every leg of a trip easily ends up with an extra hour added for each charging stop. i still dont know for sure, but if the battery life really proves to be just 8 years then this purchase will have been a poor investment. my insurance premium has shot up by about 200% even though the car has all this safety equipment. the explanation given is that repairing that safety tech after a crash costs a lot more, and the insurers claim there is not enough data yet to justify lowering the rates. sun glare or heavy rain seem to mess with the cameras trying to read the surroundings, and then the system basically chooses to shut itself off because it sees too much risk. when i drive on a road running parallel to train tracks, and a side street that crosses those tracks comes up, the railroad crossing lights aimed at the train get misread by the car as a stop light intended for my parallel road. there is also one set of traffic signals that the car reads as if they were a yield sign. the navigation does not let me set a preference for electrify america chargers when the planned distance exceeds the current charge; it just picks the first charger it finds. for at least the first 3 years, that electrify america selection option really should be there.

I still cannot manage to keep my favorite sirius/xm stations set on the radio, even though send works great. my other 7s had a massage function in the driver seat, but for some reason that feature is gone now, and oddly the salesperson said they had never heard of it.

the sensor for unlocking the doors feels too insensitive, and roughly one out of five times the lock wont react even when touching the handle. as soon as you open the door, the audio system powers up. if you step away from the car briefly while the engine is left running, the horn starts blaring, so you basically cant use the ot-lock feature. when setting a navigation destination by voice, only a small number of options is shown and one gets picked automatically, so you are unable to choose from several candidates. with the engine running at night you cant switch on the lights, so i would at least like them to be smaller. the rear gate opener also reacts poorly, probably because that sensor isnt very sensitive either. the remote key needs to be quite close for the doors to lock, the effective distance is short.

reg dn75jlu goes well and looks very good, but the door panels feel really flimsy, they almost push in when i'm washing it. there is a small rough patch on the inner edge of the front door and i can't tell if it came from the factory like that or if the garage did it when they were preparing it for handover. i'm not happy that there were no printed hand books, i ended up paying just over £70 to get hard copies. i purchased the car from a dealer in northbrook as they offered a strong price, but it's more than 100 miles away so it's been awkward getting the answers i asked for. this is the bmw 1 series 123xdrive m sport and i'm let down there are no m sport seat belts and no m sport badges on the front wings. i would appreciate hearing your reply. many thanks mark turner.

as a small car it is excellent overall. plenty of space, comfortable and quick off the mark, with very smooth pull through the gears and really strong grip and cornering behaviour. the keyless boot release can be a bit unreliable. the digital key setup can also be frustrating at times: with my iphone and apple watch the car unlocks as i walk up, but if i open the boot to load it, by the time i've shut it and gone round to the driver door it has locked again and i need to stand for a moment until it opens. the mirrors do not always fold when locking, and the instrument cluster sometimes drops my personal layout. aside from those small digital issues, everything else is perfect.

too many issues
1. the rubber gasket on the rear door, even though it is a new car, was already damaged and leaking.
2. the mirrors on this new car make a squeaky noise whenever opening or closing.
3. the key that should lock the car automatically when you walk away only works maybe 1 time out of 10.
4. the digital display also goes dark: first the navigation screen on the left side blacks out, then the speedometer side goes black while driving.
5.
when that happened, i called the bmw emergency center. they asked if there was a warning light, but with the display black i cant see any warning light.
in the end they said it was fine to keep driving
...
hey, i cant see my speed, but if i get caught they will just say it was my choice to keep going.
6. at the one month check for the water leak (and the squeaking when opening/closing), the auto lock and door mirrors,
even though i mentioned it to the dealer several times, all they did was put oil on the door mirror.
3 days later it is squeaking again!
none of the other problems have improved.
7.
even though its a brand new car, its already been back to the workshop three times.

would i recommend it?? not sure??

(im debating posting this online), but i can see the dealer is at least trying to fix it.
for now just waiting and watching.

pros - the fresh design is very attractive, the interior quality is excellent and there is some new standard kit, plus the engine with its electric boost is very efficient both in economy and performance. the new infotainment is generally very good, apart from one missing feature. cons - after having 3 118i's i really miss the rotary controller and the shortcut buttons, and finding that standard air recirculation to the rear has been removed is dissapointing. (i even checked with the dealer, thinking it was a mistake, only to be told it is now part of a package) my main disappointment is the media system. when cars lost cd players years ago i copied lots of cds onto a port memory stick and could access them via the media, which is now not possible. however, it is still a very nice car.

i am very happy with my bmw 120 m sports, this is actually my second 1 series. the first one was my wife's, i used to drive her bmw while she drove my jaguar e pace that was the top version. after my wife passed away i sold the jaguar, let my daughter have the original bmw 1, and then got this one. the car has lots of extras, but i feel some of the fun is spoiled by silly cost-cutting, like the indicator feeling really cheap and nasty, same with the car key. they took away the round control button too, just to push voice control and shave costs. you would be amazed how little things like that can influence whether you buy a car or not. i still chose it because it is small, compact, has a 360 degree camera and an opening glass sunroof, which very few small cars offer. i was looking for a small luxury car that did not trigger the luxury band road tax.

i'm very much a bmw person, i still have faith in their quality and technology, at least for the moment. it was already hard to find a follow-up to my last car, since i didnt want to go fully electric yet and the hybrid size classes felt kind of bulky and big while the electric-only driving was only for quite short kilometers. i hope there will later be a "small" handy all-electric car that can cover at least 500 km on one charge. for now i ended up choosing the self-charging hybrid 120.

the m135x drive feels like a great all-rounder for its size, but it doesnt really give that big grin. the engine/exhaust sound isnt very inspiring, and when you slow down it tends to change down, so when you go to accelerate again it isnt ready and drops 1 or 2 gears, making the engine revvy and the car a bit jerky on re-acceleration. that said, on uk a and b roads its a lot of fun, no need to thrash it, just hold it in the higher rev band for a steady, manageable pace. id really like to experience how the x-drive with the dct gearbox behaves on slippery surfaces. nice car??

blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: we have owned bmws for many years, so we are disappointed with our latest 120i m sport, first registered april 2025. we added extra optional kit on top of the standard packages. we have made numerous calls to the dealership about the exterior door handle lighting that is fitted, as we cannot get it programmed and the dealer says they cannot assist. we have found a matching 2025 car without the comfort package where the handles have no lights at all, which makes me think our lights were never coded from new. we have also seen, in certain sunlight, tiny speckles across the front windscreen. we asked about this and were told the dealer needs to view it, but for reasons beyond our control we have not managed to go. we will look forward to your reply.

overall this m135 is a big step down from my old 128ti, nowhere near as good. it just isnt as nice to drive, it tends to understeer and is awkward to manoeuvre slowly, especially parking, because the transmission feels very jerky. getting rid of the i-drive knob and all the physical heating buttons is backwards and i see it as a safety problem. the dashboard reflects off the windscreen, worse at night. the centre console actually flexes when you press the my modes button, which feels cheap. there is lots of wind noise from the wing mirrors on the motorway. the 128ti had door handle lights, m-sport pin stripes on the seat belts, coloured edging on the floor mats, red brake calipers and built-in digital services like spotify, all of which made it feel special, and the m135 lacks all of that. in the end the m135 feels disappointing and not worth the money.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.

the m135x drive feels like a great all-rounder for its size, but it doesnt really give that big grin. the engine/exhaust sound isnt very inspiring, and when you slow down it tends to change down, so when you go to accelerate again it isnt ready and drops 1 or 2 gears, making the engine revvy and the car a bit jerky on re-acceleration. that said, on uk a and b roads its a lot of fun, no need to thrash it, just hold it in the higher rev band for a steady, manageable pace. id really like to experience how the x-drive with the dct gearbox behaves on slippery surfaces. nice car??

i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

for a car at this price point, it really should come with leather seats and trim. the interior doors, seats, and center console all feel cheap. the range is not very good, and i do not understand why the ix would have better range. the car takes a long time to cool down, and with no cooled seats that problem is even worse. the brakes could be stronger for a vehicle of this size and weight. some of the center console buttons stick or do not always respond when you press them. the door lock switch is awkward to use and sometimes does not register a press, and since it is a solid piece you cannot easily tell if it actually worked.

i'm pleased overall but not as thrilled as i thought i would be. a few small tweaks would really help.

air conditioned seats: i can tell the car not to turn on seat heat by default, but i can't do the same for the cooling. having a cold butt is uncomfortable for me, i don't want it at all and end up switching it off every single drive. on hot days that makes me dislike the car a bit.

- garage door openers: with such a smart car, it should use geofencing to automatically open gates and garage doors as you arrive. my old model s did that and it was extremely convenient.

- alarm: again with geofencing, the car should be able to stay unlocked and disarmed automatically when parked at home. not for everyone, but it would be easy to add as a menu option so in a safe garage you don't risk setting off the alarm or hunting for a key to open the trunk.

one-pedal driving: i use aggressive energy recovery and really like it, but i'd prefer if it brought the car all the way to a stop instead of continuing to creep.

auto hold: when auto hold releases in traffic or at lights, even with a very gentle press on the pedal the car snaps out of the hold and lurches slightly. it's annoying and should be much smoother.

on the positive side, the audio system and in-car phone are excellent. i especially value the speakerphone performance.

for an ev it truly still handles like a bmw, and i'm glad for that.

- garage door openers: with such a smart car, it should use geofencing to automatically open gates and garage doors as you arrive. my old model s did that and it was extremely convenient.

- alarm: again with geofencing, the car should be able to stay unlocked and disarmed automatically when parked at home. not for everyone, but it would be easy to add as a menu option so in a safe garage you don't risk setting off the alarm or hunting for a key to open the trunk.

one-pedal driving: i use aggressive energy recovery and really like it, but i'd prefer if it brought the car all the way to a stop instead of continuing to creep.

auto hold: when auto hold releases in traffic or at lights, even with a very gentle press on the pedal the car snaps out of the hold and lurches slightly. it's annoying and should be much smoother.

on the positive side, the audio system and in-car phone are excellent. i especially value the speakerphone performance.

for an ev it truly still handles like a bmw, and i'm glad for that.

i really like the 5 series bmw and have been buying bmw vehicles since 1999. i still have my 2016 535 xi and it is easily the best car i've owned, both in appearance and in the features it came with. that 2016 has massaging seats, the bmw logo lights up on the inside of the doors, and the wheels look great. overall it's just a gorgeous car.

by comparison, my current 2025 feels very generic. i custom ordered this 2025 and added every option that was available, so it's supposed to be top of the line, yet it's very disappointing. it seems like bmw cut corners on this model. there are no massaging seats, and when i chose the upgraded seats you removed the heated seats in the back. i had a 2024 before and swapped it for the 2025 only because i didn't like the color on the 2024.

back in 2016 and earlier, bmw would send a little gift like a nice keychain or a usb fob shaped like a bmw key. i got nothing with the 2024 or the 2025. the key that came with the 2024 was shiny and attractive, while the 2025 key looks very plain and generic. i don't know why it ended up like that, especially since the 2025 cost more than the 2024. overall, the 2025 has been very disappointing.

i would like to show you a video comparing the 2016 with the 2025 to explain what i mean. i've ordered an m5 and i'm hoping that will turn out better than what i'm driving now. thank you.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

this is my 5th bmw vehicle.
all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:
550i
540i
740i
550i
now a 530i
i realize i am now in the regular 5 series, which i chose because, in my view, quality and functionality have gone backwards overall. that is not just about this 530 compared to those older cars.
my issues are:
run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series
2) air conditioning feels downgraded and not strong enough for south texas heat
3) ac/vent fan is too noisy except on the lowest level. with the fan high, you basically cant talk on the phone.
4) auto stop/start, but the driver does not have simple, effective full control to switch it off.
5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced
6) not enough storage. the small latched compartment by the driver is gone, there is a phone charging pad instead of extra storage depth (should be removable), and the glove box is limited and does not work well.
7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

evidence.quote: we have been buying bmw cars for at least twenty years and i always feel very safe in them. i drive about 25 miles or so every day and usually replace the car every three years. this one is very comfortable and the visibility is excellent, which is one of my essential requirements. i really like the white interior, but it is not as nice as my last car where everything inside was light cream, so i was very disappointed. i even went to look at mercedes and audi to compare their interiors and was actually about to write the deposit cheque for a mercedes before changing my mind. learning all the new systems like the heating is taking me a while, probably because i am seventy one. we prefer a spacious car with good room for passengers. the boot is big and the saloon feels very secure as we travel often and do not want anything left visible. i also wonder why you removed the sleeves on the backs of the front seats, now there is no storage there.

overall the car feels basically well built, but the price is still too high for what you actually get. there are several areas where it seems things have been pared back compared to what you would expect as obvious. it is not just about the equipment list you can read through (which you really have to study carefully, because it is very hard to understand exactly what the car has as standard). in terms of perceived quality, for example, the carpet in the boot and the standard radio have clearly been economised, which is far below what you expect from a premium brand. there are also obvious gaps in the standard equipment that ought to be a given and cost nothing, like the fact there is no cigar lighter socket in the trunk. you can see lines in the doors bulging slightly where the inner plate meets the edges, which feels far under the standard you would expect and becomes a daily irritation when you notice it. in the middle of the bonnet you can see a row of marks that look like spot welds from underneath. so in the end i actually regret buying it, even though in many ways it is a nice car.

the way this car rides is incredibly smooth, my family even calls it a "magic carpet" ride. i also really like the interior lighting and the hand gesture controls, they are both super convenient and cool. i did not give it 10 stars because i really wish i could bring up the reverse view whenever i want like i could on my old car, instead of only when the car is actually in reverse. that function was very useful and convenient, but this car sadly does not have it, and it also lacks self-closing doors, which i consider a must with kids.

Customer stated that they are no longer able to locate the interior lights easily and commented that the lights are hard to see.

On top of that, the buttons aren't raised at all, it's just a flat shiny panel with touch activation, which makes it even more awkward to use."

Customer reported the passenger-side reading light will randomly switch on while driving. Customer said it tends to happen when they wave their hand around the cabin during a conversation. Customer stated he really likes that there is now lighting on the rear speakers. Customer commented this look was something Mercedes had been doing, so he was pleased to see BMW use it as well.

1) front fascia needs to be improved, i really dont understand how the current front design got signed off by the design and management teams.
2) i have asked several times if i could try out new car tech, see design changes and give feedback on upcoming bmw models, but nobody has ever replied.
3) packaging info should be clearer, rear massaging seats were not obvious. front seats yes, but we only realized the rear seats did not have massage when my family tried them.
4) please add a zone in the front windshield where toll tags and parking garage sensors work properly, basically a blank spot so the readers can detect them.
5) make the front side pillars slimmer so visibility improves. no brand has done this yet, can bmw be the first?
6) mercedes and lucid already offer massaging seats with reclining and bottom sections, bmw might want to match that.
7) for 7 series flagship buyers, offer new ambient interior light patterns every now and then, while still keeping it classy.
8) give me an amazing deal on the 2027 760 when it launches, i am excited for the updated front fascia. otherwise i could be drawn to the refreshed 2027 s class, and the deal has to be mind blowing if you know what i mean.
8) bmw has finessed the air suspension better than the current s class, but they might catch up on power and suspension with their refresh.

4) please add a zone in the front windshield where toll tags and parking garage sensors work properly, basically a blank spot so the readers can detect them.
5) make the front side pillars slimmer so visibility improves. no brand has done this yet, can bmw be the first?
6) mercedes and lucid already offer massaging seats with reclining and bottom sections, bmw might want to match that.
7) for 7 series flagship buyers, offer new ambient interior light patterns every now and then, while still keeping it classy.
8) give me an amazing deal on the 2027 760 when it launches, i am excited for the updated front fascia. otherwise i could be drawn to the refreshed 2027 s class, and the deal has to be mind blowing if you know what i mean.

this car is outstanding. the interior feels very high end, with the unique swarovski and leather package. the audio system is brilliant, and the seating is very spacious, better than most touring sedans. the dashboard size feels right, and the minimalist approach to the console and hand controls keeps everything elegant. the exterior looks fantastic: black-on-black paint, blue calipers, crystal eyebrows and that huge grill really stand out. power comes on instantly, and the tight turning radius is a big advantage. the remote app features make it more convenient. overall, it delivers bentley-level quality at bmw pricing. well done.

this is probably my 7th or 8th 7 series. while the exterior styling is interesting, the comfort and ergonomics are not at the level of the earlier one. everything has to be operated through the center console, which i do not find safe while driving. the cost-cutting on this kind of vehicle feels ridiculous: the sunroof is gone without any prior notice, the little "pocket" on the left of the steering wheel is gone, the "comfort plus" setting has disappeared, and the seats are much less comfortable with fewer adjustments (for example, the headrest no longer properly supports anything). it is also very disappointing to see the v8 removed and to be forced into a hybrid petrol v6 that does not deliver driving pleasure, etc....

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

title: G70 Luggage compartment
requirement_statement: Improve 'Luggage compartment' for G70 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 13 respondents complain and 6 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer mentioned that luggage ends up crammed in the rear, though he feels it is still manageable.
Customer mentioned he would prefer trunk capacity closer to that of the Lincoln Towncar he owns. Customer commented that the Towncar's trunk is significantly deeper than the trunk on the BMW.

Customer stated there are two metallic units located under the mat in the trunk area, describing one as a larger square box and the other as smaller, and noted they appear permanently mounted and unlike anything seen in other cars. Writer initially thought Customer might be talking about the tire repair kit, but Customer confirmed it was not the tire repair kit. Writer asked if Customer was currently at the vehicle and offered to start a BMW Blitz video call to view what Customer was referencing. Writer sent a text message link for the video call and confirmed they could see what the phone was pointed toward. Customer stated they were walking to the trunk and then the call disconnected before the matter was resolved.

Customer stated he would prefer the trunk to be slightly larger, as the current space does not meet his needs. Customer mentioned he basically sometimes wishes he had gone with an X7 because he wants the extra room. Customer noted that, from a design standpoint, the trunk area is the only part he is not happy with. Writer acknowledged his comments and stated she would forward them to the design team for possible future improvement.
Customer stated he would like an enclosed storage compartment in the rear cargo area where he can keep small items stowed away.

Customer stated the trunk undercarriage appears unfinished. RVG captured the upper trunk area that, per Customer, looks unfinished. Customer stated he has observed this same thing on other BMW models and on Mercedes models as well. Customer stated he would like the felt material used on the bottom of the trunk to also be the lining on the top.
Customer stated the vehicle rides slightly higher and is somewhat longer, which results in a little more trunk room that they felt was needed.

Customer stated he wishes the trunk opening were about 2-3 inches wider. Customer stated his daughters wheelchair does not go in as easily as it does in his Mercedes S 580. Customer stated he has to slide the wheelchair in at an odd angle and shift it around to get it to fit.

Customer stated that when he is outside the vehicle with the bass turned up on the Bowers & Wilkins Diamond Surround Sound System, he hears a rattling sound from the passenger-side rear exterior area. Customer stated he is unsure which exact part is rattling. Customer stated something on the outside may be loose. Customer stated the noise is not audible from inside the cabin. Customer stated he has not yet informed his dealer about this.
Customer reports the trunk cargo space is laid out so it will not hold two golf bags unless they are positioned diagonally.
Customer stated he would prefer an even larger cargo space. Customer also noted there used to be a small hidden storage compartment in the trunk.
Customer noted that the trunk space in this car is much larger compared to the trunk space in his previous 2018 740i.
Customer commented that he likes how the trunk is larger than some of the competing vehicles.
Customer commented that the trunk offers plenty of room.

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

evidence.quote: the m135 xdrive is a joy to drive, powerful and feels safe. it is a very good looking car and extremely comfortable inside. i've had lots of different cars over the years but this one is definitely the best.

this 1 series is my first ever bmw and i'm really impressed with the power, the fuel economy and how comfortable it is. the amount of standard kit is great, and the safety features make me feel confident and are a big help, especially when parking. the seats are extremely comfortable and the cabin is very quiet, so it is a very enjoyable car to drive. the materials used inside feel high quality and the os9 instruments are very detailed with lots of different display options. i would happily recommend the 1 series and i expect to stay with bmw for many years.
