i sent this over to the gm at skyline bmw and still haven't heard back.

dear jordan merrick,

i recently bought a new bmw 530i from skyline bmw, expecting a premium experience that fits the brand's reputation. instead, what happened has raised some serious concerns that i feel need attention.

a few days after taking delivery, i noticed a scuff on the front headlight and paint chips on the hood. when i told my sales rep, he said they would take care of it. when i brought the car back, the paint chips were touched up, but the scuff on the headlight was still there. when i pointed that out, i was told the dealership does a pre-delivery inspection, basically suggesting the damage couldn't have been there before i bought it.

while i understand new cars go through inspections, i have reason to suspect my vehicle might have been used by someone else prior to my purchase. the car already had over 120 miles on it when i bought it, and when i connected my phone to apple carplay, i found that another device had been registered before.

because of all this, i don't feel sure that i actually received a brand-new vehicle in the condition i expected. i purchased this car for my business and had been planning on additional vehicles for my family, but this situation has made me question that decision.

i believe resolving this in a fair and professional way would reflect well on your dealership and help rebuild my confidence in your focus on customer satisfaction. it would not only restore my trust, but also reinforce my thinking about future purchases for my wife and daughter. excellent service stands out, and i am more than willing to share a positive story if this is handled properly.

please let me know how we can address this matter at your earliest convenience. i look forward to hearing from you.



regards,

marcus delaine
delaine capital, llc

a few days after taking delivery, i noticed a scuff on the front headlight and paint chips on the hood. when i told my sales rep, he said they would take care of it. when i brought the car back, the paint chips were touched up, but the scuff on the headlight was still there. when i pointed that out, i was told the dealership does a pre-delivery inspection, basically suggesting the damage couldn't have been there before i bought it.

while i understand new cars go through inspections, i have reason to suspect my vehicle might have been used by someone else prior to my purchase. the car already had over 120 miles on it when i bought it, and when i connected my phone to apple carplay, i found that another device had been registered before.

because of all this, i don't feel sure that i actually received a brand-new vehicle in the condition i expected. i purchased this car for my business and had been planning on additional vehicles for my family, but this situation has made me question that decision.

i believe resolving this in a fair and professional way would reflect well on your dealership and help rebuild my confidence in your focus on customer satisfaction. it would not only restore my trust, but also reinforce my thinking about future purchases for my wife and daughter. excellent service stands out, and i am more than willing to share a positive story if this is handled properly.

please let me know how we can address this matter at your earliest convenience. i look forward to hearing from you.



regards,

marcus delaine
delaine capital, llc

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

overall i really like my new 540i xdrive, and as i'm still figuring out all the features, i'm very pleased with the size, styling, and overall design. i picked the msport package and love the sportier, more aggressive look, especially the way the lines on the front hood flow up to the bmw badge. i've been using personal mode most of the time and wish there were a more comfort-oriented setting within personal mode. i often need the car to stay running with the a/c on while i quickly go into the office or a grocery store, and i still haven't found a way to keep it on and locked without leaving the key inside. fit and finish, with the tight tolerances, are so far what i expect from bmw. the steering feels a bit lighter than the traditional bmw dna. all in all, i'm satisfied with the car so far.

even though i love how the car handles, there are a few things you took away that my 2021 had and i just don't get why. you removed the pockets on the back of the seats. maybe that cut production costs, but without those pockets i have to dump stuff like umbrellas and the kids' things on the rear floor. the worst part, and honestly a deal breaker when my lease is up, is the trunk size. i can't fit my grandchild's stroller in there, or a full food shop, or my mother's walker. i also dislike the silver/chrome 5s on the rear windows, it's a luxury vehicle and i don't need it shouting that it's a 5 series. the glove box is smaller now, same with the door wells, and i really don't like that i can't leave anything in the console tray since i'm no longer able to cover it. i'm forced to look away from the road to manage the controls because the knobs are gone and everything is flat. with the fan vents hidden and streamlined, i can't adjust the airflow direction anymore. i could keep going, but i'm sure the team who came up with this very modern car is pleased with what they made. for me, if these things aren't changed by the time my lease ends, i'll most likely move to another luxury brand. i genuinely hope you take this feedback on board. when i checked reviews afterwards, i saw these issues weren't just mine, a lot of people felt the same way. i really believe i'm exactly the kind of customer you target, so i hope you treat my comments seriously. my whole family drives bmws and nobody from about 35 to 70 is happy with the new design. it feels very clunky and not sleek anymore. i've already told my sales person all of this. again, i hope you truly take in and value my feedback.
anna kerr

the car is very comfortable to sit in and drive, and the handling is quite responsive. i haven't had a vehicle this large for many years, but this one drives and turns almost like a smaller car. the acceleration is excellent, and i don't feel any need for the m version's extra power. the suspension is also excellent, which makes every ride enjoyable, though i'd prefer an air suspension like i've experienced in the audi q8 etron or what bmw offers on the i7. the range is very good, but with the limited fast charging along my usual routes to nj on the delmarva peninsula, i find myself wishing it could go more like 450-500 miles; for long out-of-state trips we rely on a gas vehicle. for driving around virginia the range works fine and is better than my previous ev, the vw id4. the technology in this car can be overwhelming, but i'm learning it and the infotainment bit by bit. it feels solid on the road, always composed and responsive. i do miss a spare tire, and the idea of using the provided flat repair system worries me since i've never done that before; it might help if the dealer walked me through it so i'd feel less anxious. overall, i really enjoy being behind the wheel of this car, it's the best i've owned.

we swapped a 2021 530 and a 2022 530 for two 2026 530s, and the new cars feel similar in overall quality, ride, and cabin noise. we are still learning our way around the touch screens and the menu structure, and i figure we will get the hang of it over time. i am still trying to convince myself that touch screens are truly as convenient as the old knobs and buttons, since they demand more visual attention instead of simple finger feel. the mapping functions and the heads-up display are better than before, and i really like the route graphics, especially how a real-time camera view pops up when approaching an intersection where you need to turn. nobody was able to tell me why run flat tires are no longer standard equipment. there are two letdowns for me: the removal of the small compartment to the left of the steering wheel, which used to be an ideal spot for sunglasses, and the redesign of the door storage areas into an odd shape, unlike the previous design that could hold an extra drink container. i tried the complimentary feature that lets the car pull itself into a saved parking spot, but i did not feel it was accurate enough to guide the car into my garage without risking contact with the wall on one side or the other vehicle on the opposite side.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

this is my fourth bmw, and this 530ix really does not let me down. the tech makes it easier to drive and adds safety with things like lane warning, blind spot alerts and the little beepers. the ride itself is very smooth.
my last sedan was a 2013 535ix, so a lot of the differences stand out. for one, the doors on this car feel much lighter than before. i liked the heavier doors, and these new ones sound kind of hollow. the audio system also powers up as i walk up to the car, whether it is sirius or pandora from my phone. i am old school, i always turn the radio off before shutting the car, so this is annoying. plus, when other people get in, they might end up hearing something that is not appropriate for them.
then there is the auto start/stop, which in my opinion cuts in way too quickly. after just an instant of being stopped the engine shuts off, and with summer heat that drop in a/c feels uncomfortable. turning it off every single time i start the car is really inconvenient.
lastly, i have to admit i did not pay much attention to the trim level when i ordered this one, and i miss a few of the features that came with the nicer package on my previous car. since this one is leased i will probably just hand it back at the end and go for an upgraded model. i love my cars, the dealership, and the service department/manager, and i do not see myself switching to somewhere else.

i really enjoy how the car rides. but bmw has a lot of room to improve when it comes to tech and charging. on the tech side, bmw should really take a look at what hyundai offers, especially since their cars cost a lot less. lane assist needs to be much better, keeping the car truly centered in the lane and handling corners properly for the whole trip. the "cruise control" also needs an upgrade so it adjusts correctly for the following distance the driver selects, and can bring the car all the way to a stop when the car in front stops. the driver alerts like lane departure and car proximity warnings also need to function more reliably.

for charging, bmw should finish up a deal with tesla so bmw owners can use the tesla fast chargers, or else team up with other brands in a joint venture to build a competing fast charging network. right now the non-tesla chargers are not dependable, and even the ones that show up on the bmw map sometimes are not actually there.

the car is really fantastic overall. it has the best ride of any vehicle i've owned, and i really like the acceleration. the level 2 driving *mostly* works very well, though i haven't really played with the self-parking yet.

my issue with the self driving is that it reacts too slowly when another car moves into or out of the lane ahead. once a slower car pulled into my lane and then had to brake because of traffic. the bmw 550e kept going at a higher speed as that car merged, and when they hit their brakes my car had to slam on the brakes hard. i honestly thought i was going to crash, but luckily it didn't happen.

the hybrid setup is great because it cuts my fuel costs a lot. the downside is that if the destination is a fair distance away, the car uses *all* the available battery to get there, so you can't then precondition the car for the drive back.

while i did have the money to buy it, i still feel it's a bit on the pricey side, and that makes me less willing to recommend a somewhat overpriced car to friends.

overall the experience has been very positive, the tech feels solid and the highway "self-driving" is much better than the last generation. i would like finer control over the sport mode settings. i also want clearer guidance on how to use the engine when coming off battery mode, including proper warm up time. on long drives, i'd like to hold back some battery for later while still using a bit during the trip for boost, but the current programming does not seem to support that. i realize that means more complexity and instructions, but i think many bmw owners are fine with that, and i want to get the most out of how the battery and engine work together. i came from an n63, now with a b58, and while i know they are different, the b58 sometimes sounds like it's really working even when i'm not revving it much. is that extra sound being pumped in, and is that really what i want to be hearing? i'd rather hear a confident engine than one that sounds like it's straining. also, instead of having to pay for an esim subscription, why can't the car just use my phone's hotspot for things like the youtube app.

Customer explained this is her first electric car, so she is not sure what to do if she leaves the car parked for a while. Writer advsied that for shorter periods the battery should stay around 30%-50% and that the vehicle should not be left with the charge completely depleted. Writer also advised that if the vehicle will sit for about 3 months or more she should reach out to her local service center.

the vehicle is fantastic overall, but there are a few things i feel could be improved.

on the front passenger side, the seat belt is set up so that the buckle ends up resting and vibrating against the side of the car if the belt gets twisted, and this was already an issue on my earlier 5 series.

when i spray the windshield washer, the water now runs down from the top of the windscreen, which did not happen on my old 5 series.

the steering wheel buttons are much too tiny, the previous design was better.

there is no indication when the battery preheating is actually on.

i would like more options to switch off atc etc, before there used to be a button for that.

and yes, buttons are great :-d

this is my first time driving a fully electric car, and getting used to the battery took me around a month and a half. cold january temps plus two motors and wide tires mean the battery drops fast, which i initially hated. a friend talked me into giving it a fair shot, and now the driving experience is incredible, hard to picture anything better. the tech is fun to use and works well. i do wish the charging flap were powered so it opened and closed on its own, it feels a bit low-tech on such a high-tech vehicle. the battery still drains quickly, but i'm learning to live with it.

overall it is an outstanding car. there are just a couple of things that really feel like cost cutting, and i honestly do not get why those choices were made. the biggest one is that the car cannot acclimatize while on the ice and instead will only use the main hybrid battery, which makes absolutely no sense. it comes across like somebody just did not bother to push the right software update. that behavior also hurts the practicality for people who commute. you are forced to drive in a way that saves enough of the main battery so you can still use the acclimatization settings before your next trip.

the other irritation is that you cannot unlock the car using the rear passenger door handles. at close to $80,000, it feels like they could have added two more touch sensors to make locking and unlocking simpler. overall the experience is great, but there are definitely a few things that make you wonder if they were driven by engineering or by a bean counter.

i am worried that if i travel somewhere away from home, for example on a ski trip, i would not be able to leave the car outside for a week without driving it, because the battery would end up drained.

the power, the quick response and the way this car drives are all exceptional. a trip in this m60 would probably convert even a hardcore skeptic who doubts how strong an electric car can be. i am absolutely satisfied with the cabin and with how it drives.

sadly, i placed the order without ever seeing an m60 live. i am let down by how the front grille looks. i much prefer the more "classic bmw" front of the normal i5 edrive40 models - i wanted the m60 for the all wheel drive and the dual battery setup, but i really do not care for the odd grille design. if it were possible, i would change it.

my earlier i5 had massaging seats, and that is not offered on these electric versions. that is a big disappointment because that was a feature i enjoyed a lot on my last bmw.

title: G70 Comfort Access
requirement_statement: Improve 'Comfort Access' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated that at times she leaves her Key Fob inside the vehicle in her purse and when her husband walks away from the car with his Key Fob, the car will lock with her Key Fob still inside. Writer stated the vehicle might not be detecting her Key Fob since it is buried in her purse. Writer stated it is also possible the Key Fob battery is weak. Writer stated the dealer can further diagnose whether her Key Fob battery is low.

Customer stated that because she has only one Key Fob, when she hands that Key Fob to a valet, they will leave it inside the vehicle, and then the doors end up locking the Key Fob in the car when she walks away carrying her Digital Key. Writer stated that to stop the Digital Key from locking the doors in this situation, she can turn off "Passive Entry" in Apple Wallet by tapping the BMW Digital Key, then tapping the lowercase "i" in the top-right of the phone screen, and toggling off "Passive Entry". Writer stated this keeps the Digital Key on her phone, and "Passive Entry" can be easily switched back on after she picks up the car from the valet. Writer stated another option is to activate the Service Card by placing it on the smartphone tray and following the activation prompt on the Control Display, then giving the valet the Service Card to use as the key for the vehicle.

Customer stated he has enabled the option on his car to exclude his home address from the comfort access feature. Customer reported that when he goes into his pantry or walks near the garage, he can still hear the car locking and unlocking within about 10 feet of the car. Customer notced this repeatedly.

we really enjoy the car overall. a couple of small things we would tweak though: the trunk only opens with the foot motion sometimes, and closing the doors from outside isn't always easy because the button could be more visible and simpler to reach.

Customer agreed.
Customer stated the iPhone digital key can be troublesome when he is just walking by the car and not actually using it.

Customer reported an issue with her key fob, stating the car is no longer automatically unlocking when she approaches it. Customer then placed the writer on hold and the call dropped before additional questions could be asked.

Customer reported that he has turned on the exclude home option for comfort access but that he has several home locations. Customer would like, in the future, to have the feature allow multiple home addresses.

evidence.quote: Customer inquired about the function of the button on the center console that shows a vehicle with three lines. Writer used RVG to verify the button the customer was referencing. Writer advised it serves as a quick access button for the driver assistance settings. Customer acknowledged.

my 2024 760i xdrive is just fantastic. it looks amazing, rides incredibly well, and all the tech is there without feeling too complicated. i recently drove about 220 miles and got a bit over 26 mpg overall, with 31.1 mpg for roughly the first 160 miles where the speed limit was 55 mph. the driver assist plus is a great feature, it really makes highway trips feel safer and more relaxed for me and my wife. the only two downsides i have are kind of trivial... 1) there is no spot specifically for my sunglasses, and 2) i would really prefer the hvac to stay on sync by default unless i manually change it. aside from those small things, i absolutely love this car and am already excited for my next ultimate driving experience in it. thank you!

this is a newly released model and it still has some bugs that need to be sorted out. the tech is quite overwhelming, and i am repeatedly having to reset things. the interior lighting setting i prefer keeps changing by itself to a different color. whenever i use the idrive selection tool, it drops down a presets screen each time i touch it, so when i try to choose a new radio station it pulls up those presets instead. the driving assistance functions are hard to locate and adjust, you have to hop from one screen to another. there should be a simple way to temporarily disable these features for things like traffic or going through a car wash. a basic alarm cancel or silence button would be very helpful. the seat controls on the dashboard are awkward to use because you have to lean forward to make adjustments. putting the controls on the seat or the door would be better and would let you sit properly while you fine-tune your seating position.

1. it makes no sense not to have a sunglass holder. my old 740 had one, and in about three months with this car i've already broken two pricey pairs of sunglasses because of this bad design.
2. the app is moody and only seems to work when it feels like it, which is extremely irritating. i plug the car in, ride the garage elevator down, then the office tower elevator up, and the app tells me the car isn't charging. so i head back down the office building, up the garage elevator to the car, and it actually is charging. then i go back down the garage elevator, up the high rise again to my office, call bmw assist, and they say i have to return to the car to troubleshoot…meaning sitting in a hot garage while they poke around and doing the elevator shuffle twice more. forget it…click…that was me ending the call.
3. the air conditioning layout is very unfriendly to use.

the car itself drives well, but there are some things that are just not acceptable, especially the sunglasses issue you've been hearing about for years. if the next one shows up without a sunglass holder, my time at that dealer will be very short before i walk out. the charging quirks are a nuisance and waste my time, so i'll probably just end up guessing when it's actually done charging.

Customer stated that at times the Active Driving Assistant shuts off and tells him to take over, even though he has both hands on the steering wheel. Customer stated that when this happens several times in a row, the Active Driving Assistant becomes unavailable for a while. Customer stated he is confident his hands remain on the wheel and that no hands-on-wheel warning appears before the system stops. Customer stated this typically happens on highway drives and that the Driver Attention Camera in the Instrument Cluster is not blocked. Customer stated the car does not attempt to pull to the shoulder, it only instructs him to resume control, with a noticeable shake and slight slowing when it does so. Customer stated he has not contacted the dealer. Writer advised that if he feels the feature is malfunctioning, he should have the dealer diagnose it.

title: G60 Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation
requirement_statement: Improve 'Brake Energy Regeneration / recuperation' for G60 customers.
warnings: Mixed evidence: 11 respondents complain and 5 praise this topic. Read the quotes.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer expressed being impressed by the regenerative braking, noting it recovers about 2 miles of range while braking.
Customer stated that after the most recent Remote Software Upgrade, the Regenerative Braking has become much smoother when it engages.
Customer stated that they appreciate the regen braking.
Customer stated he would like the vehicle to retain B Mode as the default setting.

Customer stated that with this EV he was surprised by how much the car begins to slow when he lets off the accelerator, and that this feels quite different compared to an ICE vehicle. Writer explained that a big part of that sensation is energy recuperation, or regenerative braking. Writer advised the vehicle starts converting kinetic energy and charging the battery as soon as the accelerator is released. Customer stated the explanation at purchase could have been better and that this new feel is going to take a little getting used to.

Customer asked if using the turn signal would cause increased regenerative braking when approaching a corner. Writer advised that brake regeneration is not impacted by the signal itself, but can change based on how the brake pedal is applied and which engine is being used during the drive. Customer then asked if regeneration is strongest in sport mode, and writer advised that it is best in sport mode.

Customer stated he is seeing significantly less brake dust on this vehicle because he mostly relies on brake regeneration. Customer stated with his prior X4 that did not offer this regeneration feature, he was washing the car multiple times each week. Customer stated with this one he can stretch the time between washes, which he finds nice.

Customer explained that the regenerative braking on the i5 feels quite different from the iX. Customer stated that on the iX, regen kicks in immediately when you lift off the accelerator, at any speed or in any situation. Customer stated the i5 instead uses adaptive regenerative braking, changing its behavior depending on the vehicle speed, surroundings, and location. Customer mentioned that at times the i5 will coast unexpectedly. Customer reported it has been challenging to adjust to how the i5's regenerative braking operates compared to the iX. Customer said it would be preferable if there were some way to fine-tune how the adaptive regenerative braking functions. Customer added that overall they do think adaptive regenerative braking is better, but it remains difficult to get used to after being accustomed to the iX setup.

Customer stated it was hard to get used to Adaptive Recuperation. Customer stated he normally expects the car to coast when he releases the accelerator, but in this vehicle it feels like it is braking when he expects coasting. Writer stated Adaptive Recuperation is designed to recover some of the energy that would be lost while the vehicle is coasting and use that energy to charge the battery. Writer stated that if the customer does not like Adaptive Recuperation, he can reduce the strength by going to the Apps menu, then Driving Settings, Drivetrain and chassis, Adaptive Recuperation, and selecting the desired setting.

Customer mentioned they are not happy with how quickly the car slows when they lift off the accelerator, so they keep the regeneration at low. Customer stated that at times it switches back to the highest regen setting. Writer asked if the same profile was being used, and customer replied the same person could be driving.

Customer mentioned his prior BMW had a regenerative braking function and asked if his new 2025 550e supports something similar. Writer went over how the system operates and informed the Customer that it will not perform automatic braking, but it does recover energy.

Customer mentioned that the B mode is excellent and that it feels better than when they drive their Tesla. Customer also commented that they appreciate being able to move from D to B at any time without restriction.

Customer stated that in the regenerative braking mode, even the setting meant for slower braking makes the car stop too abruptly and he does not think his lights come on. Customer stated that on a trip, people behind honked when he slowed, he felt nearly hit, and will not use that mode again.

Customer reported that the adaptive braking behavior is confusing to him in terms of how consistently it works. Customer described that when he is driving and coming up to a street light or a stop sign, or when he turns on the blinker, the vehicle will begin to brake for him even before he actually presses the brake pedal. Customer stated that when he uses the blinker the way the car brakes seems logical in relation to how far away he is from the turn he is about to make, and the system then applies braking. Customer explained it took him some time to get used to this, because he feels like he should be doing the braking himself and now, when he is braking and the car is braking at the same time, it can feel a bit jolty. Customer commented that he has to plan for the adaptive braking that is going to occur.
Customer noted that sometimes at a stop sign or street light the car clearly detects the stop sign or light, because it will show a small symbol of a stop sign or street light in the heads-up display, but he said that does not happen very frequently. Customer estimated that at a stop sign maybe around 20% of the time the system will recognize it and display it in the heads-up display, but most of the time it does not, which he finds confusing. Customer stated it is similar for street lights, and that he has only seen it show a red light symbol in the heads-up display once or twice when he comes up to a red light, while the vast majority of the time that symbol does not appear.
Customer stated that when the car takes over braking in some situations but not in other situations, it is a bit unsettling for him, and he would prefer to understand what the underlying logic is and to know more consistently what the car is going to do and what it is not going to do. Customer added that the amount of adaptive braking the car applies without him touching the brakes does not feel consistent as he approaches stop signs or street lights. Customer said the system seems more predictable when he turns on the blinker, and in those cases he can better anticipate how much braking the car will do adaptively, and he has adjusted his own braking to account for that.
Writer asked whether he was in any kind of driver assistance mode when he noticed the traffic light symbol. Customer replied that he was not, that he never changed the mode, and that he has only used the assisted driving mode on the freeway one time, which is not what he is referring to in this situation. Writer shared from her personal experience that she has seen the little icons appear for a red light or stop sign when she was approaching a red light and was not slowing down quickly enough, and that is when she saw them pop up. Writer explained that if she is already slowing down adequately, then the symbols do not show up to give a quick alert. Customer responded that this might make sense and suggested that maybe the few times he has seen the symbols were when the car did not think he was slowing down fast enough and
Customer indicated he would prefer the car to default to B Mode at startup.

Customer asked which setting to use among Adaptive, High, Medium, or Low. Writer used RVG to confirm what the customer was looking at. Writer explained that these options control the brake regeneration. Writer advised that Adaptive varies the amount of regeneration with driving conditions, while the other levels keep the regeneration at a fixed level.

after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

evidence.quote: heated steering wheel feature. That is the one thing I love most about the interior of my vehicle.

i chose this as a replacement car while the previous one was being inspected, after taking it out for a test drive. it has good space and comfort, and the stability is solid, though it does leave me feeling tired. considering its total length, it takes corners well. the lcd screen is simple to read and to use. the traditional change lever is gone, and the cleaner design is a plus. i'm pleased with the other functions too. since the paddle switch turns along with the steering wheel, i wonder if it is hard to make it stay fixed.

Customer stated the steering keeps pulling toward the driver side. Customer stated he believes the wheel tow alignment is off. Customer stated he has not gone to the dealer about this yet but may go this upcoming weekend. Writer recommended contacting and visiting the dealer.

this is easily one of the best cars ive owned, super smooth and very luxurious, everything about it just makes sense. my only suggestion is that integral active steering should come on all 7 series, because without it u-turns and steering in tight spots are really tough. aside from that, its basically perfect.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings

1) front fascia needs to be improved, i really dont understand how the current front design got signed off by the design and management teams.
2) i have asked several times if i could try out new car tech, see design changes and give feedback on upcoming bmw models, but nobody has ever replied.
3) packaging info should be clearer, rear massaging seats were not obvious. front seats yes, but we only realized the rear seats did not have massage when my family tried them.
4) please add a zone in the front windshield where toll tags and parking garage sensors work properly, basically a blank spot so the readers can detect them.
5) make the front side pillars slimmer so visibility improves. no brand has done this yet, can bmw be the first?
6) mercedes and lucid already offer massaging seats with reclining and bottom sections, bmw might want to match that.
7) for 7 series flagship buyers, offer new ambient interior light patterns every now and then, while still keeping it classy.
8) give me an amazing deal on the 2027 760 when it launches, i am excited for the updated front fascia. otherwise i could be drawn to the refreshed 2027 s class, and the deal has to be mind blowing if you know what i mean.
8) bmw has finessed the air suspension better than the current s class, but they might catch up on power and suspension with their refresh.

i am both a bmw fan and a driving enthusiast. over roughly the last 50 years i have been lucky enough to own a variety of mercedes and bmw vehicles, including several s classes and several 7 series. i had a '22 760i that i really loved, and i originally ordered it with the autobahn package. bmw ended up deleting that package, but i still accepted delivery of the car. i already knew how good ars is because i had an '05 750i where ars was standard equipment, and that remains one of the best driving and riding cars i have ever owned. once bmw brought the autobahn package back, i felt i had to get it, and i have absolutely no regrets. the change in ride, handling, and steering response is very clear and noticeable, and this is honestly one of the best cars i have had. i just came back from a trip of a bit over 2000 miles and the car performed flawlessly. the way it combines ride comfort with handling is remarkable, with the suspension staying composed over all the different surfaces on i-95. i have taken that same drive many times in my other cars, and this one is the best "road" car so far. my only real comment is that i wish bmw would push acoustic control further. even though the car is already very quiet, i think adding true acoustic glass with an acoustic interlayer and proper labeling, together with active noise cancellation, could provide an extra 2-4db of noise reduction. i do not quite see why this has not been done yet, especially considering the rolls royce experience. maybe these features could be bundled into an "acoustic package". i am looking forward to the lci version expected in 2027. thank you, and please keep making great cars!

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.

with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

cons: the hvac could cool better, likely because of the hidden vents, and it only got a bit better after i put clear uv tint on the windows. you also can't set sport mode as the default, even though i drive in sport most of the time. i can't remove the red and blue colors on the display and interactive bar, and i'm not a fan of those colors. the steering feels a little soft and not as connected to the road as my previous cars. it's a big car, and adding about 5" more length wasn't a good thing. the styling is just okay; i actually think my 2017 740i looks better.

title: G60 Engine acoustics / engine sound
requirement_statement: Review mixed feedback on 'Engine acoustics / engine sound' for G60 customers.

blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.

evidence.quote: the tech in this car can feel a bit too much. i really don't like that the radio, lights and other systems turn on just from opening a door, even when i'm not getting in to start the engine. it feels like an energy waste that it takes so long for everything to power down after a door is opened. i wish there were more interior storage, for example some kind of pocket behind the front seats. i understand the goal of a "clean" appearance, but there isn't enough space in the front console, so why not use the rear seat area. the recessed section on the dash in front of the steering wheel is pointless to me, and i'm worried the texas sun would bake anything left there. i was also caught off guard that there is no usb port, so i'd need an adapter for music stored that way. and there is a port on the back of the front seats that needs an expensive accessory to be useful, which makes me wonder why they chose that setup.

really like the tech in the car and the overall fit and finish. i keep wishing there were an i4 variant that felt this quiet and this smooth (i really enjoy the i5 but it is a little on the big side for my daily commute - i chose it because it is much more comfortable. i have driven the i4 a lot and enjoy it, but it feels more like a sport car). my single design gripe is that at night the interaction light bar throws a reflection onto the driver side window, right across the line of sight to the driver side mirror - this clearly feels like an oversight. i now run the light bar at its lowest brightness at night so the problem is just bearable. the drive modes are nice, but i would really like a way to hide or delete some of the silly ones (like expressive or artistic) to make it simpler to pick the few i actually use. overall though, it is a gorgeous car and i am genuinely happy to be driving a bmw again!

every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.
Customer stated that he really loves how quiet the engine is. Customer stated the engine is so smooth and quiet that he cannot even feel it shifting when it does so.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

title: G70 Interior acoustics
requirement_statement: Preserve 'Interior acoustics' for G70 customers.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: Customer stated he appreciates the calm, quiet interior of the car.
Customer stated he really likes the vehicle and especially appreciates how quiet it is.

honestly, getting this car was a mistake. the build quality is terrible for what it costs. i figured bmw's top end six figure model would give me a really high quality experience, but the main problem is the wind and cabin noise. on the freeway it sounds like the windows are a bit open or like driving straight through a wind storm, even when it's calm outside. the wind noise is insanely loud. i've ridden in other bmws and even cheaper cars and none of them had this level of wind sound. when other cars pass by you hear all of it, like there's missing insulation or something. the plastic glowing trim along the dash and doors feels super cheap too, it creaks and cracks over every bump, and the trim on the passenger door just rattles all the time. there are a few other little rattles and the vent controls are kind of awkward to use, but those are small compared to the wind noise. i bought this thing for a quiet, ultra luxury experience and it's the total opposite. i've been in lots of cars, even budget hondas and similar, and never had wind noise like this. my last car, a 2019 m550, was totally vault quiet at speed, so i dont know what happned here. very disappointing, i'm absolutely never going to buy or recommend a bmw again.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

i really enjoy this car. the ride quality is excellent and the cabin stays very quiet. the 760 has more than enough power and the tech in it is impressive. the one thing i'd change is the way the menus are laid out for the controls. i end up digging around through a bunch of apps on the screen just to find basic functions.

my other issue is that when i spec'd and ordered the car, i assumed the 760 came with active cruise and all the parking assists like my previous m850 and m5 had. it was a letdown to find out later those systems were actually part of a big option package that i hadn't realized i needed to add. my wife's lexus rx350 has all of that included as standard equipment for about half the cost.

it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.

1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.

2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.

3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.

4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.

5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.

6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.

7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.

8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.

9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.

10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.

i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
 michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

the performance jump in electric mode is spectacular, apparently from having a second gear there. the bigger battery gives a huge mileage gain: our previous 740e and 745e averaged about 51 mpg over their lives with driving around northern virginia, while the 750e is running over 141 mpg under the same conditions. all three have had the individual interior, which still looks stunning, though I miss the little mini glove box on the left side. the seats are more comfortable than in the 740e and 745e, and the trunk space is clearly larger, which I really appreciate. we get more regular "like your car" remarks from strangers now, with the standard 19" wheels and brooklyn grey with xpel stealth, though I wish frozen bluestone had been an option. I like the automatic doors, even if they are a touch quirky. the voice assistant is better now and really helps make up for the lack of buttons. the interior lighting is excellent, and the ride and handling are outstanding. the child proofing is smartly done; the rear seat car seat flap is the best approach I have seen, and the voice assistant blocks window operation.

the 120 m sport is a joy to drive and you really feel connected to it on the road. there is a small hesitation when pulling away in normal drive, but switching to s mode fixes that and that is my preferred setting. the cabin is cozy and the view backwards through the side and rear mirrors is very good. the reversing camera makes parking easy. with the pro pack the car's appearance is boosted and the styling stands out even more. the main screen menu and all its options take a bit of time to learn, but it is actually enjoyable to figure it out. i used to have a 320 sport diesel which i was very fond of, and this new 120 m sport feels even more rewarding and fun to drive. the dynamic handling is very accurate and really encourages good driving. i absolutely love it.

i am very happy with my bmw 120 m sports, this is actually my second 1 series. the first one was my wife's, i used to drive her bmw while she drove my jaguar e pace that was the top version. after my wife passed away i sold the jaguar, let my daughter have the original bmw 1, and then got this one. the car has lots of extras, but i feel some of the fun is spoiled by silly cost-cutting, like the indicator feeling really cheap and nasty, same with the car key. they took away the round control button too, just to push voice control and shave costs. you would be amazed how little things like that can influence whether you buy a car or not. i still chose it because it is small, compact, has a 360 degree camera and an opening glass sunroof, which very few small cars offer. i was looking for a small luxury car that did not trigger the luxury band road tax.

this feels like a big step up from my old bmw 120. the seating is far more comfortable, and the steering is lighter and reacts better. as a mild hybrid the fuel use is much improved, i get more mpg which makes it cheaper to run. the standard reverse parking camera is brilliant, it really helps make parking safer and simpler in tight spots. i also love the vehicle warning lights in the side mirrors on the motorway, another very useful standard feature that makes driving and overtaking safer. overall i'm really pleased with the new car, bmw definitely seem to have upgraded the 120 m sport. it's small but still has plenty of punch. i did knock off 1 point because the central screen is tricky to use while on the move, i'm right handed so actually hitting the correct button first go can be a bit hit and miss.

my issue is that i find modern technology hard to cope with. it all feels very complicated. it ended up taking about 3 months before i got an owner's handbook, and that only arrived after i kept on at the dealer repeatedly. it had been 11 years since i last bought a bmw, so a lot has changed. i found not having a traditional handbrake quite frightening. if i had received the handbook on the first day, that would have been far more useful. i did consider a mercedes a class, but the privacy glass in the rear window put me off. the staff at bmw wakefield were helpful. the difficulty was that i was so overwhelmed by all the new functions that it stopped me from truly enjoying the new car. the reception desk at wakefield and the parking attendant are both really good. i am beginning to like the car more now, but i still feel slightly scared of it. younger relatives would probably love it.

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!

i asked the dealership to swap my old 1 series for something as close as possible, just adding a reversing camera. instead they put me into a car smaller than my previous 1 series, with no electric seats, no heated steering wheel, no electric boot opening, much less room inside, no glove compartments and no phone charging cradle. i see this as fundamentally dishonest sales staff simply pushing a new model rather than a second hand one. bmw's customer treatment has been absolutely useless, and next time we will probably go for a mercedes.

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.

the inability to properly control the driving modes is really annoying. the disappearance of buttons and the idrive wheel to manage things is a pain. the touch screen itself is very good, but it pulls your attention away too much. a simple button to turn off start stop would do, instead it's awkward to use. i want to set off, not waste time searching through menus. the centre console buttons are hard to distinguish so you have to look down, there's barely any separation. the steering wheel is excessively thick and an option for a slimmer one would be preferable. with no audible exhaust note it becomes boring to drive. you pay a high price only to be asked to pay again for premium infotainment options soon after. i only want the spotify app. the cabin is beautiful and a pleasant environment. i feel like i'm managing a machine rather than actually driving. fantastic car, no character at all.

evidence.quote: i have had this one for about three months now, but i still don't really remember the feeling of sliding in the same model as before. what stands out is how simple it is to control and how it can cruise calmly even when i'm going fast. the price of the car itself feels quite high though. i picked this model because i was willing to pay more in order to get a comfortable drive. originally i chose a 116i f20 for my wife, and the steering on that is outstanding, you can really sense what the driver is feeling. after that, i bought a lexus is as a replacement for a 435i and that was excellent too. then came the 116i m135, which is also strong in power and easy to manage, and now i'm on an x3m competition. i use the m135 around town and the x3mc when i'm going at high speeds.

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.

i really like this car overall, but there are definitely ups and downs.   pros: the way it drives in general; the new style seats are really comfy; and you can feel that classic bmw engineering in every part of this m sport 1 series.    cons: the active-lane-keeping-assistant feels dangerous on narrow roads and on uk cars you can't permanently switch it off. all the tech being buried in the screen menus and not just on a simple button is frustrating; and the turning circle is way bigger than my old mercedes so it needs a lot more steering work.

Customer reported a rattle from the right rear wheel area when driving around 30mph on rough roads. Customer reported that on smooth highway there is no rattle. Customer added it sounds like it is coming from the bottom of the shock absorber and that he will bring the car to the dealer in April.
Customer stated the ride quality of the vehicle is very smooth. Customer stated their local roads have a lot of potholes and the vehicle has handled those rough conditions extremely well.

Customer stated he deliberately chose the 19-inch wheels instead of the 20-inch wheels because of concerns about his back and finds the ride very nice and comfortable. Customer noted this setup was specifically selected to maximize comfort.
Customer stated he appreciates the overall quality of the ride.

Customer stated he would like the option to raise and lower the suspension height, like on the X5 where the suspension can be adjusted up or down. Customer stated he specifically wants to lift the suspension so the rear of the car does not scrape on his girl friends drive way.

Customer stated the updated suspension setup in this car deals with potholes much better than their old 530i, and they notice less jarring impact and less impact noise when driving over rough Texas roads.
Customer stated the vehicle's suspension system provides a comfortable ride.

Customer stated he thinks there might be a suspension issue, but he is not certain yet as he has only driven the vehicle briefly. Customer stated the car went into service after about 5 days due to exterior paint damage. Customer stated that when he gets the vehicle back he will have the dealership inspect the suspension concern.

great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.
