i really do like this car: the way it puts the power down, the handling, the ride, how it soaks up rough patches, the stance and style, and the excellent paint. but there are a few things that need rethinking. the multimedia/infotainment setup is overly complicated, like the software team did it just because they could. complexity isn't what defines luxury; real luxury should be easy to use, and this bmw system isn't. there's also a quality issue on the dash that jumps out at me whenever the sun hits it, making me wonder about bmw's qc on that part. then there's the brutal, eye-burning glare from the gloss black on the center console. did nobody drive this in bright daylight? i'm seriously thinking about having it wrapped in matte vinyl to calm it down. since nothing else inside is gloss black, i keep asking myself, why do it there? and why are there no pockets on the backs of the front seats? those are very useful and should have been included. it feels like a bean counter cut them, and that was a bad decision.

i really enjoy how this car drives, and that was the main reason i chose it. i also like the updated exterior look. still, i was close to going with something else instead: a genesis, an audi allroad wagon, or a mercedes wagon. the genesis appealed because its interior finish seemed better than the bmw, the audi wagon because i prefer wagons and have already owned three audi avant wagons, and if audi still sold the avant i would have gone for that. the mercedes wagon was ruled out because the lease was too expensive. with this 540, the interior has been a letdown, as my previous 540 felt more upscale inside. this one makes me feel like i am sitting at an apple laptop, and it really bothers me that the retractable lid over the cup holder area is gone. without it, that spot looks like a random catch-all and ruins the console's previously nice look. the material covering the top of the dash also seems cheaper.

the car handles incredibly well. it feels very responsive and nimble, and the ride quality is good,
even when driving in wet weather.
i also appreciate the overall size of the vehicle - there is generous interior room in both the front and back, and the trunk is quite large.
for future upgrades, the in-car clock is really tiny - a bigger display would be better for us older drivers. also, the direction indicator (showing north, south, east, west) only appears off and on. in the cadillac i traded in, the clock face was a comfortable size and the direction display was visible all the time.
i have also found parts of the tech for the radio/sirius/spotify and car play to be difficult and a bit hard to figure out.

this is my fourth bmw since my first one back in 2016, and just when i think the standards have peaked, suddenly there are all these new features and the car basically performs better than ever for what you need. i'm still figuring out everything the 520i can do, but every trip so far has been a real pleasure behind the wheel. even though many of our roads are awful with potholes, once you are on the motorway the car is an absolute dream to drive and unmatched by anything else in its class. i did try a used 7 series on a test drive and almost went for it, but when the new 520i came out it felt like having a 7 series anyway, with plenty of space, luxury and majesty. a fantastic car and, in my view, the best in its class.

i really enjoy the overall driving environment, but the storage space frustrates me. my previous car was a 2012 528i, and with the back seats folded it had almost station-wagon-like room. this 530i is a letdown in that regard: the trunk is smaller and the pass-through is narrower, so larger items are harder to carry. on top of that, there is no bmw or oem trailer hitch option, which means we can't take our bikes unless i risk damaging the sky lounge roof or trunk lid with a bike rack. the online bmw configurator also confused me, and i ended up thinking both the 530i and 540i had a hybrid electric motor to boost mileage and performance. if i had known the difference, i probably would have chosen the 540i.

1. i paid extra for the remote parking option, but it often refuses to work. out of 10 attempts it seems to fail about half the time. especially in tight spaces it just won't allow remote parking at all, whether that's because of a sensor error or something else. honestly, i'd like to get my money back for this feature.

2. the body size is bigger than a mercedes-benz e-class or an audi a6, which makes it inconvenient when trying to park or drive through narrow streets. if the body is that large, the cabin should feel more spacious, but the interior doesn't really seem any bigger.

3. the hazard light button is a touch type, so you can't easily tell if it has actually been pressed. when you're in a rush, it's hard to switch it on, which raises the chance of an accident.

4. the bsi engine oil change interval is too long. i'd prefer replacing it every year or at around 15,000 km, but they set it at 20,000 km. trying to save money like that just seems like it will hurt people's impression of how durable the car is.

5. as soon as you approach the vehicle, the side mirrors fold out, which makes it awkward to squeeze between cars in a cramped parking lot. it would be better if the mirrors only opened when the door is actually opened or once the driver gets in.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

the auto time zone adjustment just does not function. the radio also fails to quiet when i give carplay voice commands. with a 291 mile range, the actual distance i can use is heavily cut because i only charge between 20% and 80%. right now the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available. every leg of a trip easily ends up with an extra hour added for each charging stop. i still dont know for sure, but if the battery life really proves to be just 8 years then this purchase will have been a poor investment. my insurance premium has shot up by about 200% even though the car has all this safety equipment. the explanation given is that repairing that safety tech after a crash costs a lot more, and the insurers claim there is not enough data yet to justify lowering the rates. sun glare or heavy rain seem to mess with the cameras trying to read the surroundings, and then the system basically chooses to shut itself off because it sees too much risk. when i drive on a road running parallel to train tracks, and a side street that crosses those tracks comes up, the railroad crossing lights aimed at the train get misread by the car as a stop light intended for my parallel road. there is also one set of traffic signals that the car reads as if they were a yield sign. the navigation does not let me set a preference for electrify america chargers when the planned distance exceeds the current charge; it just picks the first charger it finds. for at least the first 3 years, that electrify america selection option really should be there.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

i have a 750e 2026, and this is my second 7 series model. from the very first day, the car has been making a repeating knocking sound from the right rear passenger side, very much like the automatic door lock noise (da-da). the dealership has been supportive, understanding, and professional while trying to track it down, and they have traced it to a valve that is supposed to push gas vapors toward the engine when a certain buildup level is reached.
this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

the car is just incredible in every respect and i really love it. i only want to highlight two things that, although clearly intended well, are flawed. first, the front passengers don't have truly adjustable ac vents. there's a tiny on knob under the vent panel to tweak the airflow a bit, but the range of adjustment is extremely limited. i understand the sleek look of a dash without the usual vents, but here it feels like form winning over function, and the ac function suffers a lot because of that choice. second, the driver's side open door button is a problem. i tend to lean my left leg against the driver door while i'm driving, and very often my knee hits that open button and the door pops open even as the car is moving. that's really frightening and unsafe. it doesn't do it when the door is locked and the speed is over roughly 10 mph, but it happens below that speed. those are the only two points i have that i think would make the car safer and better for the driver.

so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

Customer stated that rattles are much more noticeable in BEVs and that this vehicle has several distinct rattles, most noticeable in the 40-60kHz range. Customer stated the rattling has been present from day one and occurs primarily when playing music at certain tones, but also at times when driving over bumps. Customer stated the areas affected include the back deck behind the passenger seats, the panel between the rear dome light and rear brake light near the roof, the sunroof control panel, and the air vents with small flaps by the subwoofer in the trunk. Writer advised having the service center inspect these specific spots to verify that all parts and panels are installed as intended. Customer acknowledged.

evidence.quote: Customer stated he has been eagerly waiting for a BMW wireless vehicle charging system, saying it would provide a more seamless experience for EV and PHEV models.
Customer stated the vehicle is simple for him to charge at home.

Customer reported at first she was unable to charge the vehicle with her home charger because she was using the wrong adapter and was not aware there was a second one. Customer stated there are two different adapters, one meant for Superchargers and one for a level two charger. Customer stated she went to the dealer and a few people there also did not realize this until one of the Geniuses said they thought there might be another adapter and then they sorted it out.
Customer stated that charging the vehicle at home is working very well.

Customer reported that the first time he tried to charge at home with his tesla wall box using an adapter at 60 AMPS, the vehicle indicated it would need 3 days to complete the charge. Customer stated he looked into the matter and realized he needed to change the AC settings in the app. Customer stated that after making that adjustment, the vehicle has been charging properly.

Customer stated the electric powertrain offers major economic advantages because their home solar panels generate more electricity than needed and send the extra back to the grid. Customer explained that the i5 uses this surplus from their solar system, which lets them operate the vehicle basically at no cost, with no cash outlay required for charging.

the manual is massive in length and still not helpful.

overall i feel like i bought an electronic vehicle from bmw a few years too early; my friends with an electric mercedes and a tesla don't face these kinds of issues.

title: G60 Impression of safety

evidence.quote: over the years i have owned a few bmws and with this 2024 one i am running into more problems than before. i am a huge bmw fan, always arguing with some of my friends that bmw is way superior to mercedes, especially when it comes to having a fun yet safe car. on this car though, i have had several issues. 1. the right side door had a rattling sound from day one. that was taken care of and after roughly 3 weeks at the dealer it finally got fixed. 2. the big problem that keeps coming back is the hood, which seems defective or just poor quality. the hood started to show random dents, so i kept bringing it to my body shop. they tried paintless dent removal and managed to fix a few of them, but the dents keep returning. this is mainly because the hood is aluminum and the glue points between the hood frame and the outer hood panel were not done right. every hot day or whenever the car sits in the sun, the aluminum hood expands and these dents pop back up. i have been dealing with this since day one and it has completely driven me crazy at this stage so i cannot enjoy this gorgeous car fully. the dealer did a great job fixing the rattling door, but i do not think they can really solve the hood situation. i honestly do not feel this lives up to bmw standards, especially for a 5 series that is close to 70k. hoping this complaint actually reaches somebody.

i got my first 5 series back in about 2001 and this is basically the only kind of vehicle i've driven. now i'm on my 5th 5 series and it's the best handling car i've had, which is why i rated it a 10. however, the tech is distracting and most of it i won't end up using. safety matters most to me and going into the screen takes my eyes off the road. my earlier cars were more basic, and that's what i actually like. i'm really upset that the cd player is gone. i spent just under $950 on the upgraded speakers and then found out the cg player was taken out, and the sales person never told me. i know there are other ways to play music, but i want to choose for myself. in short the car is fantastic, but it's also kind of a nuisance. less is more.

title: G70 Dealer
requirement_statement: Improve 'dealer' for G70 customers.
warnings: Groundedness is below 70%; human validation is required.
Topic and polarity come from keyword rules, not BMW labels.
blindspots: No dated observations; 30-day velocity is unknown.
No validated synthetic sales take-rate causality score.
No validated competitor two-year ROI score.

evidence.quote: i've had this car since around mid december 2024 and it's already in the shop for the second time. i really do enjoy the car and it's a joy to drive, but this is my first bmw after many years sticking with mercedes, and i'm not happy. i know cars can have problems, but this one is new, and the hassle and time of going to the dealer twice in about 3 months makes me not want to recommend it to anyone, which is unfortunate.
brand-new car already going back to the dealer for yet another alert problem.

the car itself is fantastic, super comfortable, really luxurious and very powerful. even though i rated it 10/10, i'm still disappointed that neither the dealer nor bmw gave me any merch or lifestyle items with my roughly $130k purchase. i recently bought a porsche 911 and porsche north america sent a full welcome package with lifestyle goodies, key chains and similar stuff. that's where i feel bmw falls short, i would really like some floating center caps and at least a keychain or something.
- vehicle had a breakdown on the day it was supposed to ship / dealer branch manager shows no proper work / dealer branch manager misled the customer and went back on the promise
fantastic dealer, i honestly wouldnt purchase from any other place.

ongoing issues and i could not get into the dealer when needed. the dealership basically brushed me off. the problems started right at delivery. i ended up selling the car at a big loss. bmw should give me a new replacement for my trouble and for positive publicity.

the car quit on me in the middle of traffic on october 3, 2023 and it has been sitting in the dealer's service department ever since that day. this easily could have turned into an accident, but i was lucky enough to coast over into a parking lot instead. very scarry experience, and i want a replacement car.

i bought my first brand new 2023 740i in december 2022, and about two weeks later, when I was trying to head home, the car would not start. it completely shut down and had to be towed to the dealer. they could not explain why it happened, so they put me into another brand new 2023 740i. i have had this second one for around two months, and on 3/12/2023, after dinner when I was ready to leave, that car also would not start and was again towed to the dealership that night. now, two days after that, neither they nor I know what is wrong with this model. this whole situation has been extremely stressful, very disappointing, and honestly alarming. i feel like I ended up with two lemons, and I would never want my family or friends to go through what I am dealing with. the dealership has given me two loaner cars and they seem just as concerned as I am about the problems with this bmw model.

i got my car thru manhatten bmw. do i have to go to one specific dealer for proper service? i went to other service places and they kept asking if i bought the car from them. is this really a thing? feels like they ignored a lot of the questions i had.

was really excited to get behind the wheel of this bmw flagship. on the freeway a chassis setting warning came up telling me to pull over urgently, around the second week of my lease. took it to the dealership and they spent about 2 months on it before saying it couldn't be fixed. ended up returning the car and still losing money on payments and insurance for a car that sat at the dealer for those 2 months. really left a bad taste, so i'm not leasing or buying this now, maybe will revisit in a few years. hope others who own or plan to get one don't go through this.
exceptional quality and customer service from the seaside bay dealer!
i paid around $140k for this bmw and the whole purchase experience was so poor that i cant recommend either the dealer or the vehicle.
i did not buy a bmw 740i from the bmw dealer in riverside california. i do not live in california. you have the wrong email, please update it to the proper person.

dealer support from both before and after the sale has been unacceptable.
this being my first bmw purchase has turned into a major disappointment. I have owned multiple luxury cars before and have never encountered such poor treatment from any of those brands.

shoddy constrution
dealer is terrble

If there was one comment (positive or negative) about your new vehicle that you would allow us to share with your vehicle's manufacturer, what would you want to say to them?
: "I am kind of a technological dinosaur and I needed support for EV things, like finding an electrician to put a plug in my garage, signing up with ElectrifyAmerica for the free electricity that comes with the car, and learning how commercial charging stations work. I ended up finding the electrician totally on my own and I still have not been able to sign up or figure out the public charging. Qmerit was completely useless. I really like my dealer, but they did nothing to help on the EV education side. I love my i7, yet I am nervous about taking it too far away from home, which is disappointing because I am not getting all the enjoyment from the car that I should."

I had a very serious problem with Other Exterior Problem(s): "About a week after I got the car, the automatic rear trunk closer failed and the trunk wouldn't shut.  The car was towed to the dealer, and they ended up replacing an electronic trunk closure unit."

the bmw dealer team was fantastic -  the finance consultant who found the best financial option. the sales lead and her team who matched the best bmwi7 for our business with all the bells and whistles -  the person who patiently went through all the details with us. the product specialist who carefully explained how the entire car works to all of my fleet drivers so everyone understands it. the workshop crew who did an excellent job with the campaigns. and the service advisor who spotted opportunities, guided us, and convinced us that this car needed to be part of our fleet. the dealer principal who was involved at the handover every step of the way - - the bmw team - you guys feel like a family and we will keep supporting your dealership.  - we have already purchased 3 bmw's and plan to buy many more

there is a nonstop popping sound coming from the climate control area. the dealer has had my car for about 5 weeks now and still cannot figure out how to repair it. bmw is currently contacting me to purchase the car back. apparently there are two other vehicles in the metro chicago region with the same set of options that are experiencing the identical issue.

the car already feels like it is falling apart only three months after delivery.
a lot of functions are not working and the trunk cover is hanging off its base.
the vehicle has been at a local bmw dealer since 01/05/2026 and is still there.
that is not a pleasant feeling when you paid about $150,000.00 for it.

the sky lounge glass started cracking less than 2 months after i bought the car. i reported this to the dealer. they determined it was a defect in the glass and that the warranty covers it. but the dealer still has not been able to tell me when they will actually repair the vehicle. on top of that, the loaner they gave me is not a 760, so i feel i am not receiving the level of value i paid for my 760. it has now been about three weeks since i dropped it off (around june 15th), and even after several follow-ups with the dealer they still cannot give me any repair date. this has been a very frustrating experience with the dealership and with owning a bmw 760. at this stage, i am thinking about contacting the better business bureau and/or saying the car is a lemon that needs to be replaced.

maria from the dealer in bayview, fl was incredibly helpful. she is a real asset for both the dealership and us customers. i am from a generation where anything involving the internet is difficult, but with maria it has not been an issue.

1) front fascia needs to be improved, i really dont understand how the current front design got signed off by the design and management teams.
2) i have asked several times if i could try out new car tech, see design changes and give feedback on upcoming bmw models, but nobody has ever replied.
3) packaging info should be clearer, rear massaging seats were not obvious. front seats yes, but we only realized the rear seats did not have massage when my family tried them.
4) please add a zone in the front windshield where toll tags and parking garage sensors work properly, basically a blank spot so the readers can detect them.
5) make the front side pillars slimmer so visibility improves. no brand has done this yet, can bmw be the first?
6) mercedes and lucid already offer massaging seats with reclining and bottom sections, bmw might want to match that.
7) for 7 series flagship buyers, offer new ambient interior light patterns every now and then, while still keeping it classy.
8) give me an amazing deal on the 2027 760 when it launches, i am excited for the updated front fascia. otherwise i could be drawn to the refreshed 2027 s class, and the deal has to be mind blowing if you know what i mean.
8) bmw has finessed the air suspension better than the current s class, but they might catch up on power and suspension with their refresh.

the auto doors are cool, but they really need to react quicker in terms of the delay before they move, and be more consistent. this clearly needs a software update.

the auto driving sensors are not fully dependable, especially once the weather is anything less than ideal.

in auto cruise, the automatic braking when coming up on slower or stopped traffic is not trustworthy at all; if you just let it go, it will basically plow into the other car even though it clearly knows the car is there. that is ridiculous and needs fixing.

with navigation, the voice will sometimes ask something like, "is this the final destination or an intermediate destination?" and when you answer with "intermediate destination" or something almost word-for-word from what it asked, it replies "i don't know what that means." that is obviously dumb.

auto park is too complicated just to have it locate and park in a simple spot, and yes, i do understand how to use it.

sport mode offers too few speedometer display choices.

ar guidance showing where to turn should have a green arrow on the road surface.

the way auto cruise decides how much to slow for corners is all over the place. it over-slows some bends and attacks others like an f1 car.

major problem: auto speed control won't reduce speed until after the posted limit changes and you press the set button. clearly the car should be able to adjust speed ahead of the sign, so there must be an option to anticipate upcoming lower limits.

i also need clearer visual feedback that the air suspension has raised the car and that i'm actually driving with it raised.

overall i'm pretty satisfied with it. i'd be happy to send more comments by email. i have several high-end vehicles, and this is my second 740.

evidence.quote: its a really good car, definitely feels like an upgrade over my old f40 118i m sport. engine is strong and the mild hybrid gives a nice extra shove and helps with efficiency. it corners and rides very well and im getting better fuel economy than with the f40. some of the cabin materials feel a bit flimsier than before, not a big deal but i did notice. the new cabin layout looks great and all the digital stuff behaves properly. a few oddities though: the keyless entry/exit reacts way too easily, and sometimes the car systems seem to randomly reset, so auto hold ends up switched off in the menu even though i had it on. the speed warning feature is just irritating, even if i can switch it off each trip here in the uk.

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.

with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.

overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.

the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.

the car is enjoyable to drive and uses less petrol than i expected. on the downside it is overcomplicated, with far too much reliance on the display screen where proper physical buttons would be safer and more practical. there are two temperature sliders that stay permanently synced, which makes one of them pointless and irritating. there is also a software issue where the recommended tyre pressures keep changing, apparently because the tyre information is not stored correctly. the car was delivered without an owner's handbook; after getting one later, i find it very poor, with no clear way to see which parts apply to my specific car. it wastes space on general 'principle' sections instead of clearly explaining how features operate and how to control them. finally, the door mirrors stick out too far and add unnecessary width, they could definitely be smaller.

i would really have liked the option of a manual gearbox, and that would have pushed my rating higher, but as with many brands it seems bmw no longer offers this to buyers. overall the car is great fun to drive when you are not manoeuvring. a few small niggles: still no intermittent setting for the windscreen wipers when they are not in auto mode; the driver seatbelt cannot be adjusted for height so i am always fiddling with it while driving; the driver seat could go lower to give extra headroom when getting in; software updates wipe out settings, especially autohold being turned on. before purchase i would have appreciated a brochure clearly listing the equipment on each model so i could compare, and when reading the handbook, to know whether my car is supposed to have a given feature. also, comfort access does not include foot boot opening even though it was shown in the app before delivery.

it is a comfortable place to sit, even if it is not exactly glamorous. driving is mostly good. the sunroof is a let-down though, i would have preferred a larger one. the fact that you push forward for reverse and pull back for drive feels completely crazy to me, i dont understand why anyone would set it up like that. the display isnt great either, everything is tiny, and i only just noticed i was almost out of fuel because it is so hard to see the fuel level. i have almost finished setting up the heating and cooling, but working out where the air actually goes is awkward and there are loads of little controls to fiddle with. i absolutely hate the parking and reversing assist, the car is constantly yelling at me, with margins that seem far too wide. it keeps making warning sounds for no reason i can figure out, and the car has already cut out twice and then would not go either backwards or forwards. i am now about to take it in to be checked.

i would recommend this car to people whose sitting height is low, because it is really a lot of fun to drive.

but for those with a taller sitting height, i would not recommend it and think it should make you stop and reconsider.

the reason is the rearview mirror is oversized, it blocks the left side view and makes the left corner dangerous.

i loved the m2 i had up until last month, but even then the visibility at the left corner was dangerous.
if the rearview mirror design is not improved, i will not purchase this model again.

bmw mirrors are made very large because they are integrated with etc, and on many cars the left visibility is dangerously poor.

bmws drive very well and are great fun, but i will hold off buying another one until the bad visibility from the rearview mirror is fixed.

please, compare the mirrors with other makers and improve the rearview mirror.

i have owned many porsche 911s and caymans before, and i am still waiting for a porsche arriving this month, but their left corner visibility is very good.

in terms of driving enjoyment, bmw is more fun than porsche for me, so the mirror issue is really unfortunate.

i want to keep buying bmw in the future.
best regards.

after swapping my old 71 plate 1 series for this one after roughly 3 years, i was really looking forward to an updated model and hassle free, enjoyable driving. instead my new car, now a 120 rather than the 1.8 sport, feels like a much lower spec than what i had before. the seats are now basic, they do have heating but no lumbar support, there is no drivers dimming rear-view mirror, and unlike three cars ago i can no longer move it up and down with a switch. the side mirrors no longer adjust when parking, and it came with no high beam assist, which i then had to pay about £10 to get added. even the hey bmw assistant has been changed from a female voice to a male. i realise some of this can be bought as extras, but i already had these features on my previous cars, so why pay again. the car should include all that and even more, but in my view it just doesn't.

the car is generally reasonable to drive. it is my first time owning an automatic and i am still getting used to it, noticing both advantages and disadvantages with the change. being a brand new model there are some appealing improvements, but in my view there are one or two design issues (in fact i have found three, though whether others agree is just opinion). the visual warning for another vehicle in the blind spot seems like a great new idea, yet in practice it appears, at least on the nearside, to work very inconsistently. the internal light display reflects too much onto the windscreen at night and becomes a distraction. and having the fog lamp button on the indicator stalk feels odd and tends to cause accidental switching on.

for us this is a major step up from the previous f40 version. the ride is noticeably smoother and the cabin much quieter, with a handy increase in acceleration performance as well. fuel economy is significantly better, the regenerative braking really shines, and together with the bigger fuel tank it gives a very useful gain in overall range. the curved screen setup for driver info, sat nav, climate and so on works really well, and in our view is far better than similar systems in many other cars.

the one negative so far is the "puddle lights" in the outer door handles, which currently do not operate, even though they are fitted in the handles. these were standard and fully working on our previous 118i m sport, so why not on this one? apart from that, the car drives exactly how a bmw should and gives the impression of being a much larger model. we absolutely love it.

over the last few years i have owned several 5 series models, the latest being an m5 that i have had for 8 years. that m5 has a head up display and physical knobs for most of the controls, and it is a superb car to drive. i bought this 1 series for my wife, and it comes with a touchscreen. i find that touchscreen frankly dangerous, and when i drive it i would never try to change anything on that screen while the car is moving. i took it from stock because i did not want to wait for one with a head up display, which turned out to be a bad decision. my wife also dislikes the touchscreen and therefore dislikes the car. the touchscreen feels like a solution looking for a problem, whereas in my m5 your eyes stay on the road and your left hand learns where the knobs are so you do not need to look down. it is a shame, because the car itself is great to drive.

i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

this is the 6th bmw i have owned, a mix of new and used, and i've liked every single one of them. i feel this particular model is the best yet, it is a pleasure to drive. i was hesitant about going for an automatic at first, but i wanted this model so i went ahead, and i have absolutely no regrets. it comes with all the technology i realistically need, even though i know there are extra options available beyond what i have. the car responds quickly when you ask it to, is comfortable, and the interior layout is very well thought out. the boot is big enough to carry my band gear without issues. i picked the midnight thunder paint and friends and family often comment on how distinctive it looks. the only downside was one time when the software hadn't updated properly and i had to carefully coax the car back home, luckily i was close by and an engineer sorted it out. now i always keep an eye on the app for that.

from the first drive home from the dealer in my new bmw120 i felt at ease in the car. the seats are excellent, the steering is very precise, and the general feel of the interior is one of quality. the extras that come as standard are very complete. i find bmw idrive straightforward to operate, and the control display always seems to react well to what i do. this is the 5th bmw i have owned and it is the one i enjoy driving the most. only a few gripes: i am unhappy that there is no physical owners manual. i do have a pdf on my laptop and i can use the bmw app for tutorials, but i would still like a paper copy to look at. the material on the door pockets seems lower grade than the rest of the cabin. these are minor issues really, otherwise everything is good!

this feels like a big step up from my old bmw 120. the seating is far more comfortable, and the steering is lighter and reacts better. as a mild hybrid the fuel use is much improved, i get more mpg which makes it cheaper to run. the standard reverse parking camera is brilliant, it really helps make parking safer and simpler in tight spots. i also love the vehicle warning lights in the side mirrors on the motorway, another very useful standard feature that makes driving and overtaking safer. overall i'm really pleased with the new car, bmw definitely seem to have upgraded the 120 m sport. it's small but still has plenty of punch. i did knock off 1 point because the central screen is tricky to use while on the move, i'm right handed so actually hitting the correct button first go can be a bit hit and miss.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.

the car itself has attractive lines and drives well, but the support from the dealership before the purchase and after collection was not acceptable. i had to go back several times with complaints before the car became easier to live with. the greater reliance on the car systems is positive, but you cant realistically grasp everything at the handover. buyers need better guidance so the advantages and joy of a new model are real, not just promised. for instance, the video they give shows a left-hand-drive car even though in the uk we drive right-hand-drive, which is confusing. i am hoping over the next few months i will learn more about the systems and use them properly, so i can get the comfort and the full experience of driving what is otherwise a remarkable car.

the 120 m sport is a joy to drive and you really feel connected to it on the road. there is a small hesitation when pulling away in normal drive, but switching to s mode fixes that and that is my preferred setting. the cabin is cozy and the view backwards through the side and rear mirrors is very good. the reversing camera makes parking easy. with the pro pack the car's appearance is boosted and the styling stands out even more. the main screen menu and all its options take a bit of time to learn, but it is actually enjoyable to figure it out. i used to have a 320 sport diesel which i was very fond of, and this new 120 m sport feels even more rewarding and fun to drive. the dynamic handling is very accurate and really encourages good driving. i absolutely love it.

overall this m135 is a big step down from my old 128ti, nowhere near as good. it just isnt as nice to drive, it tends to understeer and is awkward to manoeuvre slowly, especially parking, because the transmission feels very jerky. getting rid of the i-drive knob and all the physical heating buttons is backwards and i see it as a safety problem. the dashboard reflects off the windscreen, worse at night. the centre console actually flexes when you press the my modes button, which feels cheap. there is lots of wind noise from the wing mirrors on the motorway. the 128ti had door handle lights, m-sport pin stripes on the seat belts, coloured edging on the floor mats, red brake calipers and built-in digital services like spotify, all of which made it feel special, and the m135 lacks all of that. in the end the m135 feels disappointing and not worth the money.

my new 120 m sport has a nice colour and is a tidy little car. before this i had 5 new 3 series tourings, the last one a 330i m sport which was lovely, and the 120 is not in the same league. i notice the road noise gets quite loud once you are over about 50 mph, which makes the radio hard to hear. i also can't get my i pod to show info on the screen via usb, it only works over bluetooth now. the automatic gearbox doesn't feel as good or as smooth as the 330i's. the tech in this car is very hard to get used to for me as a retired older driver. i asked for an owners manual when the car was delivered but, roughly 3 months later, still haven't had one, first time i've had a new car without a handbook included. the 120 is a strong little car and i'm happy with how it performs. overall i'd give it 7 out of 10.

this car ticks almost all the boxes for me. the key thing is that it is genuinely fun to drive. on top of that, the purchase price felt competitive and the overall value for a new car seemed good.

the downside is the complexity of the technology. it is not straightforward to learn, and making it simpler would be a very good objective.

the big negative so far has been getting the driver seat adjusted so i do not end up with serious pain in my lower right back and right knee. i spent hours trying to find a position that worked. my son had to set the seat for me again this week, the second time, and now i can drive for about 30 minutes without pain. i am hoping that will also hold up for my regular 2 hour trips. over the last roughly 35 years i have had teslas and e class mercedes and never ran into this problem. my last mercedes had multi contour seats. my i5 has the upgraded seat package, but i just cannot get it dialed in, there are simply too many adjustments. the current e class mercedes offers an electronic assistant to help the driver find a seat position, and maybe bmw should add something like that too.

the car handles incredibly well. it feels very responsive and nimble, and the ride quality is good,
even when driving in wet weather.
i also appreciate the overall size of the vehicle - there is generous interior room in both the front and back, and the trunk is quite large.
for future upgrades, the in-car clock is really tiny - a bigger display would be better for us older drivers. also, the direction indicator (showing north, south, east, west) only appears off and on. in the cadillac i traded in, the clock face was a comfortable size and the direction display was visible all the time.
i have also found parts of the tech for the radio/sirius/spotify and car play to be difficult and a bit hard to figure out.

this is a very good drivers car, but it definitely comes up short on some luxury items compared with a mercedes.
things like massage seats, automatic shades, reclining rear seats, air suspension and so on are big omissions.
i've had around half a dozen benzs over the past decade, and moving to this car is still a welcome change.
the highway assist is an outstanding feature and really pushed me toward choosing the 5 series.
that said, in terms of luxury it still leaves plenty to wish for, starting from the overall design to some of the features.

really like the tech in the car and the overall fit and finish. i keep wishing there were an i4 variant that felt this quiet and this smooth (i really enjoy the i5 but it is a little on the big side for my daily commute - i chose it because it is much more comfortable. i have driven the i4 a lot and enjoy it, but it feels more like a sport car). my single design gripe is that at night the interaction light bar throws a reflection onto the driver side window, right across the line of sight to the driver side mirror - this clearly feels like an oversight. i now run the light bar at its lowest brightness at night so the problem is just bearable. the drive modes are nice, but i would really like a way to hide or delete some of the silly ones (like expressive or artistic) to make it simpler to pick the few i actually use. overall though, it is a gorgeous car and i am genuinely happy to be driving a bmw again!

the car is very comfortable to sit in and drive, and the handling is quite responsive. i haven't had a vehicle this large for many years, but this one drives and turns almost like a smaller car. the acceleration is excellent, and i don't feel any need for the m version's extra power. the suspension is also excellent, which makes every ride enjoyable, though i'd prefer an air suspension like i've experienced in the audi q8 etron or what bmw offers on the i7. the range is very good, but with the limited fast charging along my usual routes to nj on the delmarva peninsula, i find myself wishing it could go more like 450-500 miles; for long out-of-state trips we rely on a gas vehicle. for driving around virginia the range works fine and is better than my previous ev, the vw id4. the technology in this car can be overwhelming, but i'm learning it and the infotainment bit by bit. it feels solid on the road, always composed and responsive. i do miss a spare tire, and the idea of using the provided flat repair system worries me since i've never done that before; it might help if the dealer walked me through it so i'd feel less anxious. overall, i really enjoy being behind the wheel of this car, it's the best i've owned.

overall the experience has been very positive, the tech feels solid and the highway "self-driving" is much better than the last generation. i would like finer control over the sport mode settings. i also want clearer guidance on how to use the engine when coming off battery mode, including proper warm up time. on long drives, i'd like to hold back some battery for later while still using a bit during the trip for boost, but the current programming does not seem to support that. i realize that means more complexity and instructions, but i think many bmw owners are fine with that, and i want to get the most out of how the battery and engine work together. i came from an n63, now with a b58, and while i know they are different, the b58 sometimes sounds like it's really working even when i'm not revving it much. is that extra sound being pumped in, and is that really what i want to be hearing? i'd rather hear a confident engine than one that sounds like it's straining. also, instead of having to pay for an esim subscription, why can't the car just use my phone's hotspot for things like the youtube app.

my first bmw was a 2015 bmw i3 rex, and since then the material quality, attention to detail, and level of service with each bmw i have bought have only improved. that first car came from bmw dallas east, and the others from bmw of south austin, yet the service has stayed the same. even when my i3 rex needed work at bmw of laredo, the service was flawless. because of rising prices from covid, kids graduating, and that year we would all rather forget, i had to go with cheaper non-bmw cars for a while. as soon as i could, i called my bmw store and leased my 5th bmw. i tell everyone about the dealership, my service manager and his great mechanics, and the sales staff that knows exactly what i am after and helps me get a price i can live with. if i have any say in it, i will never own anything but a bmw again. at this price point, nothing really compares.

this is my first time driving a fully electric car, and getting used to the battery took me around a month and a half. cold january temps plus two motors and wide tires mean the battery drops fast, which i initially hated. a friend talked me into giving it a fair shot, and now the driving experience is incredible, hard to picture anything better. the tech is fun to use and works well. i do wish the charging flap were powered so it opened and closed on its own, it feels a bit low-tech on such a high-tech vehicle. the battery still drains quickly, but i'm learning to live with it.

positives: the car drives very smoothly and feels great on the road. it has plenty of space, and with the right options selected it is very comfortable. the self driving related tech works quite well. the harmon kardon audio sounds good.
negatives: the turning circle is really bad. when a passenger gestures with their hand while talking, it ends up activating the gesture control. i don't understand why the display has to jump from the navigation map to digital art whenever i switch into eco mode. i also can't set which driving mode the car should start in each time, so i have to turn eco driving on manually on every trip. i don't get why the youtube app demands an esim even though the car is already connected to my phone through carplay or bluetooth and could use that data. and even though i paid for the led headlight animation upgrade, the animation hasn't changed at all.

i really enjoy how this car drives, and that was the main reason i chose it. i also like the updated exterior look. still, i was close to going with something else instead: a genesis, an audi allroad wagon, or a mercedes wagon. the genesis appealed because its interior finish seemed better than the bmw, the audi wagon because i prefer wagons and have already owned three audi avant wagons, and if audi still sold the avant i would have gone for that. the mercedes wagon was ruled out because the lease was too expensive. with this 540, the interior has been a letdown, as my previous 540 felt more upscale inside. this one makes me feel like i am sitting at an apple laptop, and it really bothers me that the retractable lid over the cup holder area is gone. without it, that spot looks like a random catch-all and ruins the console's previously nice look. the material covering the top of the dash also seems cheaper.

the car itself drives really nicely. i would rate it higher if two things were different: they took away the acc button for toggling on and off, and also removed the drive assist distance control button from the steering wheel. on top of that, the software pushes way too much onto the screen, so trying to do stuff while driving feels unsafe. i could list a lot more complaints, but it seems pointless since it won't change any of my dissatisfaction. for example, this roughly $80k car can't adjust the climate from the rear seats, while my about $50k x3 can. the front seat backs are hard so there are no pockets anymore. the connector on the back of the front seats is almost useless because there are hardly any accessories for it. i would much rather just have the old pockets.

my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

i am worried that if i travel somewhere away from home, for example on a ski trip, i would not be able to leave the car outside for a week without driving it, because the battery would end up drained.

the car is extremely smooth and quiet, unlike my earlier bmws. controls are straightforward, and the mix of performance and luxury is really well done. my other evs lacked a sun roof, so having one on the i5 is a big plus. the only real downside is the awful carplay audio behavior: most of the time i need the radio volume at max just to hear normally, then an incoming call can be super loud and the whole system ends up blaring because it is already turned up. lots of people online describe the same issue, and while some suggested fixes help for a while, the low volume problem keeps coming back.

the power, the quick response and the way this car drives are all exceptional. a trip in this m60 would probably convert even a hardcore skeptic who doubts how strong an electric car can be. i am absolutely satisfied with the cabin and with how it drives.

sadly, i placed the order without ever seeing an m60 live. i am let down by how the front grille looks. i much prefer the more "classic bmw" front of the normal i5 edrive40 models - i wanted the m60 for the all wheel drive and the dual battery setup, but i really do not care for the odd grille design. if it were possible, i would change it.

my earlier i5 had massaging seats, and that is not offered on these electric versions. that is a big disappointment because that was a feature i enjoyed a lot on my last bmw.

the power, the quick response and the way this car drives are all exceptional. a trip in this m60 would probably convert even a hardcore skeptic who doubts how strong an electric car can be. i am absolutely satisfied with the cabin and with how it drives.
